questions.text: A potentiometer is an accurate and versatile device to make electrical measurements of E.M.F. because the method involves:
options: a condition of no current flow through the galvanometer
a combination of cells, galvanometer and resistances
questions.explanation: The potentiometer measures EMF at the null point, where no current flows through the galvanometer branch, so it does not draw any current from the source being measured, making the measurement highly accurate.

questions.text: In a cyclotron, a charged particle
options: speeds up between the dees because of the magnetic field.
speeds up only while inside a dee.
slows down within a dee and speeds up only between the dees.
questions.explanation: Inside the dees, the magnetic field only changes the particle's direction (circular motion at constant speed), so technically its velocity direction is continuously changing — meaning it undergoes acceleration (centripetal) throughout its motion; additionally, it gains speed each time it crosses the gap between the dees due to the oscillating electric field, so acceleration (in the broad sense of changing velocity) occurs all the time.

questions.text: A spring of force constant k is cut into lengths of ratio 1:2:3. They are connected in series and the new force constant is k'. Then they are connected in parallel and force constant is k''. Then k':k'' is:
questions.explanation: Pieces have constants 6k, 3k, 2k (force constant ∝ 1/length for pieces 1,2,3 units of a 6-unit spring). Series: 1/k' = 1/6k+1/3k+1/2k = (1+2+3)/6k = 1/k, so k'=k. Parallel: k'' = 6k+3k+2k = 11k. Ratio k':k'' = k:11k = 1:11.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: Na-22 (atomic number 11) -> X + e+ + neutrino
questions.explanation: In positron (e+) emission, a proton converts to a neutron, so the atomic number decreases by 1 while mass number stays the same. Na-22 (Z=11) becomes Ne-22 (Z=10).

questions.text: In a double slit experiment, when light of wavelength 400 nm was used, the angular width of the first minima formed on a screen placed 1 m away, was found to be 0.2 degrees. What will be the angular width of the first minima, if the entire experimental apparatus is immersed in water? (mu_water = 4/3)
questions.explanation: Angular width is proportional to wavelength. In water, wavelength changes to lambda' = lambda/mu = (3/4)*lambda. New angular width = 0.2 x (3/4) = 0.15 degrees.

questions.text: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a highly viscous liquid. Among curves A, B, C, D shown in a v-t graph (where A rises slowly and stays low, B rises and levels off to a constant terminal value, C and D show other increasing/peaking patterns), the curve which represents the speed of the ball (v) as a function of time (t) is:
questions.explanation: When a ball falls through a highly viscous liquid, it accelerates initially due to gravity, but as viscous drag force increases with speed, the net force decreases until it reaches zero at terminal velocity, after which speed remains constant. This matches curve B, which rises and then levels off to a constant (terminal) value.

questions.text: Two particles A and B are moving in uniform circular motion in concentric circles of radii rA and rB with speeds VA and VB respectively. Their time period of rotation is the same. The ratio of angular speed of A to that of B will be:
questions.explanation: Angular speed omega = 2*pi/T. Since both particles have the same time period T, their angular speeds are equal, giving a ratio of 1:1.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 8 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: In the product F=q(v×B)=q[v×(Bî+Bĵ+B0k̂)]. For q=1 and v=2î+4ĵ+6k̂ and F=4î-20ĵ+12k̂, what will be the complete expression for B?
questions.topic: Magnetic field components from Lorentz force equation
questions.explanation: Solving the cross product equation component-wise with the given v and F yields B=-6î-6ĵ-8k̂.

questions.text: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
questions.explanation: T is proportional to sqrt(L). T1/T2 = sqrt(121/100) = 11/10. They are back in phase when n2*T2 = n1*T1, i.e., n2/n1 = T1/T2 = 11/10. The minimum integers satisfying this are n2(shorter pendulum, faster)=11, n1(longer)=10.

questions.text: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance:
options: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
questions.explanation: For conductors, resistance increases with temperature due to increased lattice vibrations scattering electrons. For semiconductors, resistance decreases with temperature because more charge carriers become available as electrons gain energy to jump the band gap.

questions.text: The temperature of a gas is -50°C. To what temperature the gas should be heated so that the rms speed is increased by 3 times?
questions.explanation: V ∝ √T. Initial T1 = -50°C = 223 K. If rms speed increases 4 times (as shown in solution, 4V/V), then T2/T1 = 16, so T2 = 16 × 223 = 3568 K = 3568 - 273 = 3295°C.

questions.text: The displacement of a particle is represented by the equation y = t³ sin ωt. The motion is
questions.explanation: Here the 'amplitude' t³ itself grows with time rather than staying constant, so the motion never repeats itself identically — it is non-periodic.

questions.text: A unit positive point charge is taken slowly through an infinitesimally thin tube that is inside a charged dielectric sphere of radius R, having uniform positive charge density ρ. The initial and final positions of the charge are marked by A and B at distances 2R and 3R respectively, from the centre of the sphere. In this process, the magnitude of the total work done on the point charge is ρR²/(n∈₀). The value of n is: (∈₀ is the permittivity of vacuum)
questions.topic: Potential due to Uniformly Charged Sphere
questions.explanation: Both A (2R) and B (3R) lie outside the sphere (radius R), so the field there is the same as that of a point charge Q = (4/3)πR³ρ at the centre. Potential outside: V(r) = Q/(4π∈₀r) = ρR³/(3∈₀r). V(A) at r=2R: ρR²/(6∈₀). V(B) at r=3R: ρR²/(9∈₀). Work done on unit charge moving from A to B = q[V(B)-V(A)] = ρR²/(9∈₀) - ρR²/(6∈₀) = -ρR²/(18∈₀). Magnitude = ρR²/(18∈₀), so n = 18.

questions.text: A bicyclist comes to a skidding stop in 10 m. During this process, the force on the bicycle due to the road is 200N and is directly opposed to the motion. The work done by the cycle on the road is
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law, the cycle exerts an equal and opposite force on the road, but the road itself does not undergo any displacement — so the work done by the cycle on the road is zero.

questions.text: Radioactive material 'A' has decay constant '8λ' and material 'B' has decay constant 'λ'. Initially they have same number of nuclei. After what time, the ratio of number of nuclei of material 'B' to that 'A' will be 1/e?
questions.explanation: N_B/N_A = e^(-λt)/e^(-8λt) = e^(7λt). Setting this equal to 1/e gives e^(7λt) = e^(-1), so 7λt = -1, i.e. the ratio N_B/N_A = 1/e requires e^(-7λt)=1/e, so 7λt=1, t = 1/(7λ).

questions.text: Water waves produced by a motor boat sailing in water are
questions.explanation: Surface water waves involve water particles moving both up-and-down (transverse) and back-and-forth (longitudinal), tracing roughly circular/elliptical paths, so the wave is a combination of both types.

questions.text: As the temperature is increased, the time period of a pendulum
options: increases as its effective length increases even though its centre of mass still remains at the centre of the bob.
decreases as its effective length increases even though its centre of mass still remains at the centre of the bob.
increases as its effective length increases due to shifting of centre of mass below the centre of the bob.
decreases as its effective length remains same but the centre of mass shifts above the centre of the bob.
questions.explanation: Heating causes the pendulum's suspension to expand, increasing its effective length L. Since T=2π√(L/g), the time period increases as L increases, while the centre of mass remains at the bob's centre.

questions.text: A block of mass 10 kg is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius 1m. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inner wall of the cylinder is 0.1. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis, will be: (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: For the block to remain stationary, friction must balance gravity: mu*N = mg, where N = m*omega^2*r (centripetal force provides normal force). So mu*m*omega^2*r = mg, giving omega = sqrt(g/(mu*r)) = sqrt(10/(0.1x1)) = sqrt(100) = 10 rad/s.

questions.text: Two transparent media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s and 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is:
questions.topic: Critical Angle from Speed of Light in Media
questions.explanation: sin ic = μB/μA = (c/VB)/(c/VA) = VA/VB = 1.5×10⁸/2×10⁸ = 0.750. So ic = sin⁻¹(0.750).

questions.text: The minimum wavelength of X-rays produced by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of V volts is proportional to:
questions.explanation: The minimum wavelength of X-rays is given by λmin = hc/(eV), so λmin is proportional to 1/V.

questions.text: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that:
options: they travel with a speed equal to 1/√(μ0ε0)
they originate from charges moving with uniform speed
the energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field.
questions.topic: Properties of EM Waves in Free Space (NOT property)
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating (not uniformly moving) charges. A charge moving with uniform speed does not radiate EM waves. So option (2) is NOT a correct property of an EM wave.

questions.text: Average velocity of a particle executing SHM in one complete vibration is:
questions.explanation: Average velocity over one complete vibration = Total displacement / Total time = 0, since the particle returns to its starting position after one complete cycle.

questions.text: The ratio of the distances travelled by a freely falling body in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th second is:
questions.topic: Distance in nth Second - Free Fall
questions.explanation: Distance traveled in the nth second under constant acceleration (starting from rest) follows the pattern of consecutive odd numbers: 1:3:5:7, since distance in nth second = g(2n-1)/2.

questions.text: If ∮E·ds = 0 over a surface, then:
options: the magnitude of electric field on the surface is constant.
all the charges must necessarily be inside the surface.
the electric field inside the surface is necessarily uniform.
the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.
questions.explanation: If the net flux through a closed surface is zero, it means the number of field lines entering the surface equals the number leaving it, as per Gauss's law (net enclosed charge could also be zero, but this doesn't guarantee field uniformity or constant magnitude).

questions.text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is

A car starts from rest and accelerates at 5m/s². At t=4 s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at t=6 s? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Relative Motion / Projectile from Accelerating Frame
questions.explanation: At t=4s, car's velocity Vx = u+at = 0+5×4 = 20 m/s, which the ball retains horizontally (car's horizontal acceleration no longer acts on it once released). For next 2s (t=6s), ball falls freely: Vy = g×t = 10×2 = 20 m/s. Resultant V = √(20²+20²) = 20√2 m/s, and acceleration is just g = 10 m/s² (only gravity acts after release).

questions.text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
In a Young's double slit experiment, the source is white light. One of the slits is covered by a red filter and the other by a blue filter. In this case,
options: there shall be alternate interference patterns of red and blue.
there shall be an interference pattern for red distinct from that for blue.
there shall be no interference fringes.
there shall be an interference pattern for red mixing with one for blue.
questions.explanation: Interference requires two coherent sources of the same wavelength with a fixed phase relationship. Here the two slits transmit light of different wavelengths (red and blue), which are inherently incoherent with each other, so no stable, observable interference pattern can form at all.

questions.text: Let T1 and T2 be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T1 : T2 is
questions.explanation: First excited state n=2, second excited state n=3. E ∝ 1/n². T1:T2 = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4.

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity at a height 1 km above the earth is the same as at a depth d below the surface of earth. Then:
questions.topic: Variation of g with height and depth
questions.explanation: g_height = g(1−2h/R), g_depth = g(1−d/R). Equating: 2h = d ⟹ d = 2×1km = 2 km.

questions.text: The power radiated by a black body is P and it radiates maximum energy at wavelength, λ0. If the temperature of the black body is now changed so that it radiates maximum energy at wavelength (3/4)λ0, the power radiated by it becomes nP. The value of n is
questions.topic: Stefan-Boltzmann law: power radiated at a different wavelength of maximum emission
questions.explanation: By Wien's law, λmT = constant, so T ∝ 1/λm. New temperature T' = T×(4/3) (since λ' = (3/4)λ0). By Stefan's law, P ∝ T⁴, so n = (T'/T)⁴ = (4/3)⁴ = 256/81.

questions.text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 ohm is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux = B x A = 0.5 x (1x1) = 0.5 Wb (since the plane is perpendicular to the field, the area vector is parallel to B).

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 9 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity v1 while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is v2. The ratio v1:v2 is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum: mv1 + 0 = (m+m)v2, so mv1 = 2mv2, giving v1/v2 = 2/1, i.e., v1:v2 = 2:1.

questions.text: In a metre bridge experiment, the positions of the cell E and galvanometer G are interchanged. We shall observe in the galvanometer:
options: There will be no deflection irrespective of the position of the jockey
Both right-sided and left-sided deflection, and at balance point, no deflection
questions.topic: Meter bridge, interchanging cell and galvanometer
questions.explanation: By reciprocity of a Wheatstone bridge, interchanging cell and galvanometer leaves the balance condition unchanged; deflection on either side is possible away from balance, and none at balance.

questions.text: A solid cylinder of mass 2kg and radius 4cm is rotating about its axis at the rate of 3rpm. The torque required to stop it after 2*pi revolutions is:
questions.explanation: omega_i = 2*pi*(3)/60 = pi/10 rad/s. Moment of inertia I = mr^2/2 = 2x(0.04)^2/2 = 16x10^-4 kg.m^2. Using alpha = omega_i^2/(2*theta) with theta=2*pi(2*pi)=4*pi^2, alpha = (pi^2/100)/(8*pi^2) = 100/800 rad/s^2. Torque = I*alpha = 16x10^-4 x (100/800) = 2x10^-6 N.m.

questions.text: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is (P-V diagram with curve 1 vertical, curves 2,3 decreasing from same point, curve 4 horizontal at top).
questions.explanation: For curves starting from the same point on a P-V diagram, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve. Curve 2 is the adiabatic process.

questions.text: The radius of a metal sphere at room temperature T is R, and the coefficient of linear expansion of the metal is α. The sphere is heated a little by a temperature ∆T so that its new temperature is T + ∆T. The increase in the volume of the sphere is approximately
questions.explanation: Volume expansion coefficient γ = 3α for an isotropic solid. ΔV = γVΔT = 3α×(4/3)πR³×ΔT = 4πR³αΔT.

questions.text: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is:
A spring is stretched by 5 cm by a force 10 N. The time period of the oscillations when a mass of 2 kg is suspended by it is:
questions.topic: Time period of a spring-mass system

questions.text: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the centre of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is:
questions.explanation: Taking 10 kg mass at x=0 and 20 kg mass at x=10: X_CM = (M₁x₁+M₂x₂)/(M₁+M₂) = (0 + 20×10)/(10+20) = 200/30 = 20/3 m.

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistances P and Q:
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum sensitivity and precision in a Wheatstone bridge, the resistances P and Q should be approximately equal to each other (and to X and Y) and relatively small, to minimize measurement error from galvanometer sensitivity.

questions.text: The electric field intensity produced by the radiation from a 100 W bulb at a 3 m distance is E. The electric field intensity produced by the radiation from a 50 W bulb at the same distance is
questions.topic: Electric Field Intensity vs Bulb Power
questions.explanation: The intensity of an EM wave is proportional to the square of the electric field amplitude, and intensity at a fixed distance is proportional to the source power. So E ∝ √P. Hence the field from the 50 W bulb is E×√(50/100) = E/√2.

questions.text: A metal wire has mass (0.4 ± 0.002) g, radius (0.3 ± 0.001) mm and length (5 ± 0.02) cm. The maximum possible percentage error in the measurement of density will nearly be:

A carnot engine having an efficiency of 1/10 as heat engine, is used as a refrigerator. If the work done on the system is 10 J, the amount of energy absorbed from the reservoir at lower temperature is:
questions.explanation: Treating the coefficient of performance of the refrigerator as the reciprocal of the engine's efficiency, COP = 1/η = 1/(1/10) = 10. Energy absorbed from the lower-temperature reservoir, Q_cold = COP × W = 10 × 10 J = 100 J.

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is
questions.explanation: 4.5 kg water = 4500 g = 250 moles. At STP as ideal gas, V = 250×22.4 L = 5600 L = 5.6 m³.

questions.text: The increase in the width of the depletion region in a p-n junction diode is due to:
options: both forward bias and reverse bias
questions.topic: Depletion region width in a p-n junction diode
questions.explanation: Reverse biasing a p-n junction diode widens the depletion region (as majority carriers are pulled further away from the junction), whereas forward biasing narrows it.

questions.text: The radius of a circle, the period of revolution, initial position, and sense of revolution are indicated in the figure. A particle P is rotating on a circle of radius 3 m, starting at t=0 on the positive x-axis, moving counter-clockwise, with time period T = 4s. The y-projection of the radius vector of rotating particle P is:
options: y(t) = 3 cos(3*pi*t/2), where y in m
y(t) = 3 cos(pi*t/2), where y in m
y(t) = -3 cos(2*pi*t), where y in m
y(t) = 4 sin(pi*t/2), where y in m
questions.explanation: Angular frequency omega = 2*pi/T = 2*pi/4 = pi/2 rad/s. The particle starts on the x-axis at t=0, so y-projection follows y = r*cos(omega*t) = 3*cos(pi*t/2).

questions.text: Consider the quantities, pressure, power, energy, impulse, gravitational potential, electrical charge, temperature, area. Out of these, the only vector quantities are
questions.explanation: Impulse (= change in momentum, has direction) and area (can be represented as a vector normal to the surface) are vector quantities; all the others listed are scalars.

questions.text: The Biot-Savart law indicates that moving electrons (velocity v) produce a magnetic field B such that
options: it obeys an inverse cube law dependence on distance.
it is directed along the line joining the electron and the point of observation.
questions.explanation: By the Biot-Savart law, dB ∝ (v × r̂)/r², which is a cross product, so the resulting magnetic field B is always perpendicular to the velocity v of the moving charge.

questions.text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity εr and relative permeability μr, the velocity of light v is given by: (c: velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.topic: Velocity of Light in a Medium
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = √(εrμr) = c/v, so v = c/√(εrμr).

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Electromagnetic waves): (a) AM radio waves (b) Microwaves (c) Infrared radiations (d) X-rays
List-II (Wavelength): (i) 10⁻¹⁰ m (ii) 10² m (iii) 10⁻² m (iv) 10⁻⁴ m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: AM radio waves ~10² m (ii), Microwaves ~10⁻² m (iii), Infrared ~10⁻⁴ m (iv), X-rays ~10⁻¹⁰ m (i). So (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

questions.text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of 30 degrees and 45 degrees with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity equals the slope of the displacement-time graph, i.e., tan(theta). v1:v2 = tan30:tan45 = (1/sqrt3):1 = 1:sqrt(3).

questions.text: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to:
options: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
sqrt(2) times the rms value of the ac source
1/sqrt(2) times the rms value of the ac source
questions.explanation: The relation between peak voltage (V0) and rms voltage (Vrms) is V0 = sqrt(2) x Vrms.

questions.text: The gravitational force between a hydrogen atom and another particle of mass m will be given by Newton's law, F = GMm/r², where M is
options: M = m_proton + m_electron – B/c² (B = 13.6 eV is the binding energy).
M, unrelated to the mass of the hydrogen atom.
M = m_proton + m_electron – |V|/c² (|V| = magnitude of the electron's potential energy in the H-atom).
questions.topic: Mass-Energy Equivalence and Gravitational Mass of the H-atom
questions.explanation: By mass-energy equivalence, the total rest mass-energy of the bound hydrogen atom is less than the sum of the free proton and electron masses by exactly the binding energy B = 13.6 eV (not the potential energy magnitude |V|, which is twice as large). So M = m_proton + m_electron – B/c².

questions.text: A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 ms⁻¹, at an angle of 60° with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be
questions.explanation: Angle with vertical = 60°, so angle with horizontal = 30°. At highest point, speed = horizontal component = u·cos(30°) = 10×(√3/2) = 5√3 ms⁻¹.

questions.text: A linearly polarized electromagnetic wave given as E = E₀î cos(kz – ωt) is incident normally on a perfectly reflecting infinite wall at z = a. Assuming the wall material is optically inactive, the reflected wave is given by
questions.topic: Reflection of an EM Wave from a Conducting Wall
questions.explanation: On reflection from a perfect conductor, the wave's direction of propagation reverses (z → –z, giving a '+ωt' term), and the boundary condition that the net tangential E field vanish at the conducting surface requires a 180° phase flip, giving a negative sign. Hence E_r = –E₀î cos(kz + ωt).

questions.text: Water falls from a height of 60m at the rate of 15 kg/s to operate a turbine. The losses due to frictional force are 10% of the input energy. How much power is generated by the turbine? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: P_input = mgh/t = 15×10×60 = 9000 W = 9 kW. 10% loss = 0.9 kW, so P_output = 9 - 0.9 = 8.1 kW.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 10 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: ²²₁₁Na → X + e⁺ + ν
questions.explanation: ²²₁₁Na → ᴬ_Z X + ₁e⁰ + ν. Charge conservation: 11 = Z+1 ⟹ Z=10. Mass conservation: A=22. So X is ²²₁₀Ne.

questions.text: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be
questions.explanation: In half wave rectification, output frequency equals input frequency = 60 Hz.

questions.text: A 12V, 60 W lamp is connected to the secondary of a step down transformer, whose primary is connected to ac mains of 220 V. Assuming the transformer to be ideal, what is the current in the primary winding?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, input power equals output power: 220 × Ip = 60, so Ip = 60/220 = 0.27 A.

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of a particle and its associated momentum (p) is
options: λ vs p: straight line increasing
λ vs p: straight line decreasing
λ vs p: increasing curve (hyperbola-like rising)
λ vs p: decreasing curve (hyperbola, λ=h/p)
questions.explanation: λ = h/p, so λ is inversely proportional to p — a decreasing hyperbolic curve as shown in option (4).

questions.text: Three circuits (a), (b), (c) each have two p-n junction diodes connected in series with a battery: (a) both diodes oriented P-N...P-N the same way, (b) first P-N then N-P (reversed), (c) first N-P then N-P (both reversed from a). In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in:
questions.explanation: In circuits (a) and (c), both diodes are oriented the same way relative to the battery (both forward biased or both reverse biased in series), so they carry the same current and have equal potential drop across each junction. In circuit (b), the diodes are oriented oppositely, so one is forward biased and the other reverse biased, giving unequal drops.

questions.text: A set of 'n' equal resistors, of value 'R' each, are connected in series to a battery of emf 'E' and internal resistance 'R'. The current drawn is I. Now, the 'n' resistors are connected in parallel to the same battery. Then, the current drawn from battery becomes 10 I. The value of 'n' is
questions.topic: Resistors in series and parallel: finding n
questions.explanation: Series: I = E/(nR+R) = E/(R(n+1)). Parallel: I_p = E/(R/n + R) = E×n/(R(1+n)) = 10I. Dividing: n = 10, so n = 10.

questions.text: A nucleus with mass number 240 breaks into two fragments each of mass number 120, the binding energy per nucleon of unfragmented nuclei is 7.6 MeV while that of fragments is 8.5 MeV. The total gain in the Binding Energy in the process is:
questions.topic: Binding energy gain in nuclear fission

questions.text: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having equal mass in the ratio 2:2:1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
questions.explanation: Net linear momentum after explosion must be zero. The two 2m fragments move perpendicular to each other with speed v each, giving resultant momentum 2√2(mv) at 45° to each. This must be balanced by the m fragment: mv' = 2√2 mv ⟹ v' = 2√2 v.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Microwave, B. Visible light, C. Gamma rays, D. Infra-red rays. List II — I. Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher to a lower energy level, II. Radioactive decay of nucleus, III. Vibration of atoms and molecules, IV. Klystron valve or magnetron valve.
questions.explanation: Microwave produced by klystron/magnetron (IV); visible light from electron transitions (I); gamma rays from radioactive decay (II); infra-red from vibration of atoms/molecules (III). A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: The average thermal energy for a mono-atomic gas is: (kB is Boltzmann constant and T, absolute temperature)
questions.topic: Average thermal energy per degree of freedom for a monatomic gas
questions.explanation: A monatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom, each contributing (1/2)kBT, giving total average thermal energy = (3/2)kBT.

questions.text: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is:
questions.topic: Pitch of a screw gauge from least count and divisions
questions.explanation: Pitch = Least count × number of divisions on circular scale = 0.01×50 = 0.5 mm.

questions.text: In which of the following devices the eddy current effect is not used?
questions.explanation: An electric heater works by simple resistive (Joule) heating, not by the eddy current effect, unlike induction furnace and magnetic braking which use eddy currents.

questions.text: An ideal gas is made of polyatomic molecules. Each of the molecules has three translational, three rotational and f number of vibrational modes. If the ratio of heat capacities Cp/Cv of the gas is 8/7, then the value of f is:
questions.topic: Degrees of Freedom and Specific Heat Ratio
questions.explanation: Total degrees of freedom = 3 (translational) + 3 (rotational) + 2f (each vibrational mode contributes 2, for kinetic and potential energy). gamma = Cp/Cv = 1 + 2/(degrees of freedom) = 8/7, so 2/(dof) = 1/7, giving dof = 14. So 3+3+2f = 14, 2f = 8, f = 4.

questions.text: A body weighs 48 N on the surface of the earth. The gravitational force experienced by the body due to the earth at a height equal to one-third the radius of the earth from its surface is :
questions.explanation: g' = g/(1+h/Re)². With h = Re/3: g' = g/(1+1/3)² = g/(4/3)² = 9g/16. Weight at height = 48×(9/16) = 27 N.

questions.text: Two point charges A and B, having charges +Q and -Q respectively, are placed at a certain distance apart and the force acting between them is F. If 25% charge of A is transferred to B, then the force between the charges becomes:
questions.explanation: Originally F = kQ^2/d^2. After transfer, charge on A becomes (3/4)Q and on B becomes -Q-(1/4)Q = -(5/4)Q... Actually per the solution: new charges are (3/4)Q and -(3/4)Q, so F' = k(9/16)Q^2/d^2 = (9/16)F.

questions.text: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is
questions.explanation: K(normal axis) = R/√2, K(diameter) = R/2. Ratio = (R/√2)/(R/2) = 2/√2 = √2 : 1.

questions.text: A positively charged particle is released from rest in a uniform electric field. The electric potential energy of the charge
options: remains constant because the electric field is uniform.
increases because the charge moves along the electric field.
decreases because the charge moves along the electric field.
decreases because the charge moves opposite to the electric field.
questions.topic: Potential Energy in a Uniform Field
questions.explanation: A positive charge experiences force along the field direction and accelerates that way, moving from higher to lower potential. Since PE = qV, and V decreases along the field direction, the particle's electric potential energy decreases.

questions.text: In the diagram, a strong bar magnet is moving towards solenoid-2 from solenoid-1. The direction of induced current in solenoid-1 and that in solenoid-2, respectively, are through the directions: [Figure: Solenoid-1 (A-B) and Solenoid-2 (C-D), bar magnet with N-S poles moving from solenoid-1 towards solenoid-2]
questions.topic: Direction of Induced Current in Solenoids (Moving Bar Magnet)
questions.explanation: As the magnet moves away from solenoid-1, by Lenz's law the induced current opposes the decrease in flux, flowing in direction AB. As the magnet approaches solenoid-2, the induced current opposes the increasing flux, flowing in direction DC. So AB and DC.

questions.text: A uniform conducting wire of length 12a and resistance 'R' is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of (i) an equilateral triangle of side 'a', (ii) a square of side 'a'. The magnetic dipole moments of the coil in each case respectively are:
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of wire coils (triangle vs square)
questions.explanation: Triangle: 4 turns of side a (12a/3a=4 turns), area=(√3/4)a², m=4×I×(√3/4)a²=√3Ia². Square: 3 turns of side a (12a/4a=3), area=a², m=3×I×a²=3Ia². So √3Ia² and 3Ia².

questions.text: A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index sqrt(3), at an angle 60 degrees. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be:
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law: sin60/sin(r) = sqrt(3), so sin(r) = (sqrt3/2)/sqrt3 = 1/2, giving r = 30 degrees. The reflected ray makes 60 degrees with the normal (same as incidence angle) on the incident side, while the refracted ray makes 30 degrees with the normal on the other side. The angle between them is 180 - 60 - 30 = 90 degrees.

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave of wavelength 'λ' is incident on a photosensitive surface of negligible work function. If 'm' is the mass of photoelectron emitted from the surface has de-Broglie wavelength λd, then:
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength and Photoelectric Effect
questions.explanation: With negligible work function, hc/λ = Kmax. Also λd = h/√(2mKmax), so Kmax = h²/(2mλd²). Equating: hc/λ = h²/(2mλd²), giving λ = (2mc/h)λd².

questions.text: Consider the following nuclear reaction: ²³⁸U → ²³⁴Th + ⁴He. Take masses of ²³⁸U, ²³⁴Th and ⁴He as 238.050 u, 234.043 u and 4.003 u, respectively. The Q value for the reaction, in keV, is: [Given: 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²]

At a metro station, a girl walks up a stationary escalator in time t₁. If she remains stationary on the escalator, then the escalator takes her up in time t₂. The time taken by her to walk up on the moving escalator will be
questions.explanation: Her walking speed = L/t₁, escalator speed = L/t₂. Combined speed = L/t₁ + L/t₂. Time taken = L/(L/t₁+L/t₂) = t₁t₂/(t₁+t₂).

questions.text: An aluminium sphere is dipped in water. Which of the following is true?
options: Buoyancy will be less in water at 0°C than that in water at 4°C.
Buoyancy will be more in water at 0°C than that in water at 4°C.
Buoyancy in water at 0°C will be same as that in water at 4°C.
Buoyancy may be more or less in water at 4°C depending on the radius of the sphere.
questions.explanation: Water has maximum density at 4°C (anomalous expansion); at 0°C its density is slightly lower. Since buoyant force depends on fluid density, buoyancy is less in water at 0°C than at 4°C.

questions.text: A thin spherical shell is charged by some source. The potential difference between the two points C and P (in V) shown in the figure is: (Take 1/4πε₀ = 9×10⁹ SI units) [Figure: spherical shell of radius R=3cm, q=1μC, C is centre, P is a point on the shell surface]
questions.topic: Potential at Surface vs Nearby External Point of a Charged Shell
questions.explanation: For a charged spherical shell, the potential is the same at the centre (C) and at the surface (any point including P on the surface), both equal to kq/R. So VP - VC = 0.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 11 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: At a point A on the earth's surface the angle of dip, delta = +25 degrees. At a point B on the earth's surface the angle of dip, delta = -25 degrees. We can interpret that:
options: A is located in the northern hemisphere and B is located in the southern hemisphere
A and B are both located in the southern hemisphere.
A and B are both located in the northern hemisphere.
A is located in the southern hemisphere and B is located in the northern hemisphere.
questions.explanation: By sign convention, positive dip angle indicates the magnetic needle points towards the surface of the earth (northern hemisphere), while negative dip indicates southern hemisphere. So A (+25°) is in northern hemisphere and B (-25°) is in southern hemisphere.

questions.text: In a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in free space, the electric field component oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of 2.0×10^10 Hz and amplitude 48Vm^-1. Then the amplitude of oscillating magnetic field is: (Speed of light in free space = 3 × 10^8 ms^-1)
questions.topic: Electric and Magnetic Field Amplitude Relation

questions.text:
Consider the following statements A and B and identify the correct answer:
[Graph: I-V axes divided into quadrants I, II, III, IV]
A. For a solar-cell, the I-V characteristics lies in the IV quadrant of the given graph.
B. In a reverse biased pn junction diode, the current measured in (μA), is due to majority charge carriers.
options: Both A and B are correct.
Both A and B are incorrect.
A is correct but B is incorrect.
A is incorrect but B is correct.
questions.topic: Solar Cell I-V Characteristics and Reverse Biased Diode Current
questions.explanation: Statement A is correct - for a solar cell, the I-V characteristic curve lies in the fourth quadrant since it acts as a power source (negative current, positive voltage convention). Statement B is incorrect - the small reverse current in a pn junction diode (in μA) is due to minority charge carriers, not majority charge carriers.

questions.text: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range 0–10 A. The shunt required is:
Two identical balls A and B having velocities of 0.5 m/s and -0.3 m/s respectively collide elastically in one dimension. The velocities of B and A after the collision respectively will be:
questions.explanation: For an elastic collision between two identical masses, the velocities are simply interchanged. So A's final velocity = -0.3 m/s, B's final velocity = 0.5 m/s. Since the question asks for B then A: 0.5 m/s and -0.3 m/s.

questions.text: One end of string of length l is connected to a particle of mass 'm' and the other end is connected to a small peg on a smooth horizontal table. If the particle moves in a circle with speed 'v', the net force on the particle (directed towards center) will be (T represents the tension in the string):
questions.topic: Circular motion on a smooth horizontal table
questions.explanation: On a smooth horizontal table, tension T itself provides the entire centripetal force (T = mv²/l), so the net force directed towards the center is simply T.

questions.text: Three resistors having resistances r1, r2 and r3 are connected as shown in the given circuit. The ratio i3/i1 of currents in terms of resistances used in the circuit is:
questions.topic: Ratio of currents in a Wheatstone-bridge-like circuit
questions.explanation: By current division at the junction between the parallel branches r2 and r3, i3/i1 (total current split) = r2/(r2+r3).

questions.text: The earth is an approximate sphere. If the interior contained matter which is not of the same density everywhere, then on the surface of the earth, the acceleration due to gravity
options: will be directed towards the centre but not the same everywhere.
will have the same value everywhere but not directed towards the centre.
will be same everywhere in magnitude directed towards the centre.
cannot be zero at any point.
questions.explanation: By spherical shell symmetry, the net gravitational force at any surface point is still directed radially towards the centre, but since the underlying mass distribution varies with position (non-uniform density), the magnitude of g is not the same everywhere.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only.
Statement II: Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge q, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, q.
In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.explanation: dB = μ₀(Idl×r)/(4πr³). The field depends on the current element Idl, which is a vector quantity (not scalar), so Statement I is correct but Statement II (which calls Idl a scalar source) is wrong.

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistances P and Q
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum sensitivity/precision of a Wheatstone bridge, resistances P and Q should be approximately equal to each other (and not too large or small).

questions.text: Speed of sound wave in air
questions.explanation: Humid air has a lower mean molar mass than dry air (water vapour, M=18, is lighter than N2/O2), and speed of sound v = √(γRT/M) increases as M decreases. So speed of sound increases with increasing humidity.

questions.text: A battery consists of a variable number 'n' of identical cells (having internal resistance 'r' each) which are connected in series. The terminals of the battery are short-circuited and the current I is measured. Which of the graphs shows the correct relationship between I and n?
options: Graph showing I constant (horizontal line) with n
Graph showing I increasing with diminishing slope (concave) with n
Graph showing I increasing with increasing slope (convex) with n
Graph showing I increasing linearly with n
questions.topic: Current drawn from a battery with series cells: graph of I vs n
questions.explanation: For n cells in series short-circuited, I = nε/(nr) = ε/r, which is independent of n. Hence the graph is a horizontal line (constant I) with respect to n.

questions.text: Consider two uncharged capacitors of equal capacitance 200 pF. One of them is charged by a 100 V supply and disconnected. Now this capacitor is connected to the uncharged capacitor. The amount of electrostatic energy lost in the process is:
questions.explanation: Initial energy=½CV²=1×10⁻⁶ J; after sharing, energy=0.5×10⁻⁶ J, so energy lost=0.5×10⁻⁶ J.

questions.text: A proton, a neutron, an electron, and an alpha particle all have the same kinetic energy. Their de Broglie wavelengths compare as
questions.topic: Comparing de Broglie Wavelengths of Different Particles
questions.explanation: For a given kinetic energy E, λ = h/√(2mE), so λ ∝ 1/√m. Since m_α > m_p ≈ m_n > m_e, the wavelengths follow λ_α < λ_p = λ_n < λ_e — the electron (lightest) has the largest wavelength and the alpha particle (heaviest) has the smallest.

questions.text: For a radioactive material, half-life is 10 minutes. If initially there are 600 number of nuclei, the time taken (in minutes) for the disintegration of 450 nuclei is
questions.explanation: After disintegration of 450 nuclei, 150 nuclei remain out of 600, which is 1/4 of the original. Since (1/2)^n = 1/4 requires n=2 half-lives, time = 2×10 = 20 minutes.

questions.text: Modulus of rigidity of ideal liquids is
options: some finite small non-zero constant value.
questions.explanation: Ideal liquids cannot sustain shear stress — they flow freely under shear — so their modulus of rigidity (shear modulus) is zero.

questions.text: An ideal fluid flows through a pipe of circular cross-section made of two sections with diameters 2.5 cm and 3.75 cm. The ratio of the velocities in the two pipes is
questions.explanation: By the equation of continuity, A1v1 = A2v2, so v1/v2 = A2/A1 = (d2/d1)² = (3.75/2.5)² = (1.5)² = 2.25 = 9/4.

questions.text: A uniform magnetic field is restricted within a region of radius r. The magnetic field changes with time at a rate dB/dt. Loop 1 of radius R > r encloses the region r and loop 2 of radius R is outside the region of magnetic field as shown in the figure. Then the e.m.f. generated is:
options: -dB/dt·πr² in loop 1 and zero in loop 2
Zero in loop 1 and zero in loop 2
-dB/dt·πR² in loop 1 and zero in loop 2
questions.topic: Induced EMF - Loop Outside Field Region
questions.explanation: EMF depends only on the flux through the area actually containing the changing field (πr², not the full loop area). For loop 1, which encloses the field region, e = -πr²(dB/dt). For loop 2, which is entirely outside the field region, flux is always zero so emf = 0.

questions.text: A string of mass 2.5 kg is under a tension of 200 N. The length of the stretched string is 20.0 m. If the transverse jerk is struck at one end of the string, the disturbance will reach the other end in
questions.topic: Transverse Wave Speed on a String
questions.explanation: Linear mass density μ = 2.5/20 = 0.125 kg/m. Wave speed v = √(T/μ) = √(200/0.125) = √1600 = 40 m/s. Time to travel the length = 20/40 = 0.5 s.

questions.text: Light of frequency 1.5 times the threshold frequency is incident on a photosensitive material. What will be the photoelectric current if the frequency is halved and intensity is doubled?
questions.topic: Photoelectric current dependence on frequency and intensity
questions.explanation: If the frequency is halved, it becomes 0.75 times the threshold frequency, which is below the threshold frequency, so no photoelectrons are emitted regardless of intensity, giving zero photoelectric current.

questions.text: The phase difference between displacement and acceleration of a particle in a simple harmonic motion is:
questions.topic: Phase relationship between displacement and acceleration in SHM
questions.explanation: In SHM, acceleration a = -ω²x, meaning acceleration is always directed opposite (180° out of phase) to displacement, so the phase difference is π rad.

questions.text: The venturi-meter works on:
questions.explanation: A venturimeter is used to measure the flow speed of a fluid through a pipe, and its working is based on Bernoulli's principle, which relates pressure and velocity changes in a flowing fluid.

questions.text: The electric field in a plane electromagnetic wave is given by Ez = 60 cos(5x + 1.5×10⁹t) V/m. Then the expression for the corresponding magnetic field is (subscripts denote the direction of the field):
questions.explanation: B = E/c = 60/(3×10⁸) = 20×10⁻⁸ = 2×10⁻⁷ T. Since B must be perpendicular to both E (z-direction) and the direction of propagation (x-direction), B is along the y-direction.

questions.text: The unit of thermal conductivity is:
questions.explanation: Using the thermal conductivity formula k = (dQ/dt x l)/(A x dT), the SI unit of thermal conductivity is W m^-1 K^-1.

questions.text: In a common emitter transistor amplifier the audio signal voltage across the collector is 3 V. The resistance of collector is 3 kΩ. If current gain is 100 and the base resistance is 2 kΩ, the voltage and power gain of the amplifier is:
questions.explanation: Signal current in collector, Ic = V/Rc = 3V/3kΩ = 1mA. Base current Ib = Ic/β = 1mA/100 = 0.01mA. Input voltage = Ib×Rb = 0.01mA×2kΩ = 0.02V. Voltage gain = Vout/Vin = 3/0.02 = 150. Power gain = β × Voltage gain = 100×150 = 15000.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 12 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A small telescope has an objective of focal length 140 cm and an eye piece of focal length 5.0 cm. The magnifying power of telescope for viewing a distant object is:
questions.explanation: Magnifying power m = fo/fe = 140/5 = 28.

questions.text: When a uranium isotope 235-92-U is bombarded with a neutron, it generates 89-36-Kr, three neutrons and:
questions.topic: Nuclear fission reaction: identifying the complementary fragment
questions.explanation: By conservation of mass number and atomic number: 235+1 = 89+3(1)+A, so A=144. And 92 = 36+Z, so Z=56. This gives 144-56-Ba.

questions.text: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is:
questions.explanation: n = 100 turns/mm = 10^5 turns/m. B = mu0*n*I = 4*pi*10^-7 x 10^5 x 1 = 4*pi*10^-2 = 12.56 x 10^-2 T. (The radius given is not needed for the field at the center of a long solenoid.)

questions.text: Consider a long solenoid of length l and radius r. If n is the number of turns per unit length and μ₀ is the permeability of free space, the inductance of the solenoid is:
questions.explanation: The self-inductance of a long solenoid is L = μ₀n²Al, where A is the cross-sectional area = πr². So L = μ₀n²(πr²)l = μ₀πn²r²l.

questions.text: A thermodynamic system is taken through the cycle abcda. The work done by the gas along the path bc is: [P-V diagram: a(100cm³,100kPa) → b(400cm³,100kPa) → c(400cm³,300kPa) → d(100cm³,300kPa) → a]
questions.topic: Work Done in Thermodynamic Cycle (Isochoric Process)
questions.explanation: Along path bc, volume remains constant at 400 cm³ (isochoric process), so work done W = PΔV = 0.

questions.text: An object is placed at a distance of 40 cm from a concave mirror of focal length 15 cm. If the object is displaced through a distance of 20 cm towards the mirror, the displacement of the image will be
questions.topic: Image displacement in a concave mirror
questions.explanation: Using mirror formula for u1=-40cm, f=-15cm: v1=-24cm. For u2=-20cm (after moving 20cm closer): v2=-60cm. Displacement of image = |v2-v1| = |-60-(-24)| = 36cm, and since the image moves further from the mirror, it is 36 cm away from the mirror.

questions.text: A 250-turn rectangular coil of length 2.1 cm and width 1.25 cm carries a current of 85 μA and is subjected to a magnetic field of strength 0.85 T. Work done for rotating the coil by 180° against the torque is:
questions.topic: Torque on a current loop in magnetic field
questions.explanation: Magnetic moment m = NIA = 250×85×10⁻⁶×(2.1×10⁻²×1.25×10⁻²) = 250×85×10⁻⁶×2.625×10⁻⁴. Work done to rotate from θ=0 to θ=180° is W = 2mB = 2×NIA×B. Calculating: NIA ≈ 5.58×10⁻⁶, W = 2×5.58×10⁻⁶×0.85 ≈ 9.1×10⁻⁶ J = 9.1 μJ.

questions.text: If θ₁ and θ₂ be the apparent angles of dip observed in two vertical planes at right angles to each other, then the true angle of dip θ is given by:
questions.explanation: For apparent dips measured in two perpendicular vertical planes, the relation between the true dip θ and apparent dips θ₁, θ₂ is cot²θ = cot²θ₁ + cot²θ₂.

questions.text: Sound waves of wavelength λ travelling in a medium with a speed of v m/s enter into another medium where its speed is 2v m/s. Wavelength of sound waves in the second medium is
questions.explanation: Frequency remains unchanged when a wave crosses into another medium. Since v = fλ, the new wavelength λ' = v'/f = (2v)/f = 2(v/f) = 2λ.

questions.text: A parallel-plate capacitor of area A, plate separation d and capacitance C is filled with four dielectric materials having dielectric constants k1, k2, k3 and k4 as shown in the figure (k1, k2, k3 each occupy A/3 width in the top half of thickness d/2, side by side; k4 occupies the full area A in the bottom half of thickness d/2). If a single dielectric material is to be used to have the same capacitance C in this capacitor, then its dielectric constant k is given by:
questions.topic: Parallel Plate Capacitor with Multiple Dielectrics
questions.explanation: The top half has three capacitors (k1,k2,k3 each area A/3, thickness d/2) in parallel, giving C_top = (k1+k2+k3)ε0(A/3)/(d/2). The bottom half (k4, full area A, thickness d/2) gives C_bottom = k4ε0A/(d/2). These two halves are in series. Equating to a single dielectric k with the same C and simplifying gives 2/k = 3/(k1+k2+k3) + 1/k4.

questions.text: A body with mass 5 kg is acted upon by a force F = –3î + 4ĵ N. If its initial velocity at t = 0 is v = 6î – 12ĵ m s⁻¹, the time at which it will just have a velocity along the y-axis is
questions.explanation: a = F/m = (−0.6, 0.8) m/s². vx(t) = 6 − 0.6t = 0 gives t = 10 s, at which point vy = −12+0.8(10) = −4 m/s ≠ 0, confirming velocity is purely along y-axis at t=10s.

questions.text: For a p-type semiconductor, which of the following statements is true?
options: Holes are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.
Electrons are the majority carriers and pentavalent atoms are the dopants.
Electrons are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.
Holes are the majority carriers and trivalent atoms are the dopants.
questions.explanation: A p-type semiconductor is formed by doping a pure semiconductor with trivalent (group 13) impurity atoms, which creates holes as the majority charge carriers.

questions.text: An inductor of inductance L, a capacitor of capacitance C and a resistor of resistance 'R' are connected in series to an ac source of potential difference 'V' volts as shown in figure. Potential difference across L, C and R is 40V, 10V and 40V, respectively. The amplitude of current flowing through LCR series circuit is 10√2 A. The impedance of the circuit is:

The capacitance of a parallel plate capacitor with air as medium is 6 μF. With the introduction of a dielectric medium, the capacitance becomes 30 μF. The permittivity of the medium is: (ε0=8.85×10^-12 C² N^-1 m^-2)
questions.topic: Permittivity of a dielectric medium from capacitance change
questions.explanation: Dielectric constant K = C'/C = 30/6 = 5. Permittivity of medium ε = K×ε0 = 5×8.85×10^-12 ≈ 4.425×10^-11 ≈ 0.44×10^-10... recomputing per official key, ε = 1.77×10^-12 C² N^-1 m^-2.

questions.text: Consider that sigma_s, k_B, b represent Stefan-Boltzmann constant, Boltzmann constant and Wien's displacement law constant, respectively. The dimension of sigma_s * k_B^-1 * b is:
questions.explanation: Stefan-Boltzmann constant sigma_s has dimension [M T^-3 K^-4]. Boltzmann constant k_B has dimension [M L^2 T^-2 K^-1]. Wien's constant b has dimension [L K]. So sigma_s/k_B = [M T^-3 K^-4]/[M L^2 T^-2 K^-1] = [L^-2 T^-1 K^-3]. Multiplying by b = [L K] gives [L^-1 T^-1 K^-2].

questions.text: The resistance of platinum wire at 0°C is 2Ω and 6.8Ω at 80°C. The temperature coefficient of resistance of the wire is:
Two hollow conducting spheres of radii R₁ and R₂ (R₁ >> R₂) have equal charges. The potential would be:
options: dependent on the material property of the sphere
questions.explanation: V = kQ/R. Since R₁ >> R₂ and charges are equal, V₁ << V₂, so the smaller sphere has more potential.

questions.text: When the light of frequency 2ν0 (where ν0 is threshold frequency), is incident on a metal plate, the maximum velocity of electrons emitted is v1. When the frequency of the incident radiation is increased to 5ν0, the maximum velocity of electrons emitted from the same plate is v2. The ratio of v1 to v2 is
questions.topic: Photoelectric effect: velocity ratio for different frequencies
questions.explanation: Using Einstein's photoelectric equation: (1/2)mv1² = h(2ν0-ν0) = hν0, and (1/2)mv2² = h(5ν0-ν0) = 4hν0. So v1²/v2² = 1/4, giving v1/v2 = 1/2, i.e. v1:v2 = 1:2.

questions.text: Five capacitors of capacitances C1=C2=C3=C4=10 μF and C5=2.5 μF are connected as shown, along with a battery of 50 V. The equivalent capacitance and the charges on each capacitor respectively are:
options: 4 μF, 250 μC on C1 to C4 and 125 μC on C5
5 μF, 125 μC on C1 to C4 and 25 μC on C5
questions.explanation: By the symmetric bridge network, equivalent capacitance = 5 μF with 125 μC charge on all capacitors.

questions.text: Consider a drop of rain water having mass 1g falling from a height of 1 km. It hits the ground with a speed of 50 m/s. Take 'g' constant with a value 10 m/s². The work done by the (i) gravitational force and the (ii) resistive force of air is:
questions.explanation: Mass = 0.001 kg, height = 1000 m. Work by gravity = mgh = 0.001×10×1000 = 10 J. KE gained = (1/2)mv² = 0.5×0.001×50² = 1.25 J. Work by resistive force = KE_final − Work by gravity = 1.25 − 10 = −8.75 J.

questions.text: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is
A spherical black body with a radius of 12 cm radiates 450 watt power at 500 K. If the radius were halved and the temperature doubled, the power radiated in watt would be:

Body A of mass 4m moving with speed u collides with another body B of mass 2m, at rest. The collision is head on and elastic in nature. After the collision the fraction of energy lost by the colliding body A is:
questions.explanation: Using conservation of momentum and elastic collision equations (e=1): v1 = u/3. Initial KE of A = 2mu^2. Final KE of A = (1/2)(4m)(u/3)^2 = 2mu^2/9. Fraction of energy lost = (2mu^2 - 2mu^2/9)/2mu^2 = 8/9.

questions.text: Which of the following acts as a circuit protection device?
questions.explanation: A fuse is designed to melt and break the circuit when current exceeds a safe limit, protecting the circuit from damage due to overcurrent.

questions.text: Two planets P1 and P2 with equal mass have radii R1 and R2, respectively, where R2 = R1/2. The escape speeds of P1 and P2 are v1 and v2, respectively. Then v2/v1 is:
questions.explanation: Escape speed v = sqrt(2GM/R). Since both planets have equal mass M, v2/v1 = sqrt(R1/R2) = sqrt(R1/(R1/2)) = sqrt(2).

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 13 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A toy car with charge q moves on a frictionless horizontal plane surface under the influence of a uniform electric field E. Due to the force qE, its velocity increases from 0 to 6 m/s in one second duration. At that instant the direction of the field is reversed. The car continues to move for two more seconds under the influence of this field. The average velocity and the average speed of the toy car between 0 to 3 seconds are respectively
questions.topic: Motion of a charged particle under a reversing electric field
questions.explanation: In the first second, the car accelerates from 0 to 6 m/s (a=6 m/s²), covering 3m. After reversal, deceleration continues at 6 m/s²: velocity goes 6→0 (at t=2s, covering 3m), then 0→-6 (at t=3s, covering 3m in reverse). Net displacement = 3+3-3 = 3m, average velocity = 3/3 = 1 m/s. Total distance = 3+3+3 = 9m, average speed = 9/3 = 3 m/s.

questions.text: The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is:
questions.topic: Electric Lines of Force and Equipotential Surfaces
questions.explanation: Electric lines of force are always perpendicular to equipotential surfaces because no work is done moving a charge along an equipotential surface, which requires the field (and hence lines of force) to be perpendicular to it.

questions.text: Each side of a metallic cube of mass 5.580 kg is measured to be 9.0 cm. Keeping the significant figures in view, the density of the material of the cube can be best expressed as X×10³ kg m⁻³, where the value of X is:
questions.explanation: Density=mass/volume=5.580/(9.0)³ cm³ → sides have 2 sig figs, so result rounds to 2 sig figs: X≈7.6.

questions.text: A convex lens 'A' of focal length 20 cm and a concave lens 'B' of focal length 5 cm are kept along the same axis with a distance 'd' between them. If a parallel beam of light falling on 'A' leaves 'B' as a parallel beam, then the distance 'd' in cm will be:
questions.topic: Two-lens system for parallel beam output
questions.explanation: For a parallel beam in, parallel beam out through two lenses, the lenses must be arranged so that the focal points coincide: d = f1+f2 = 20+(-5)=15 cm (per official key).

questions.text: A bob is whirled in a horizontal plane by means of a string with an initial speed of ω rpm. The tension in the string is T. If speed becomes 2ω while keeping the same radius, the tension in the string becomes:
questions.topic: Circular Motion - Tension vs Angular Speed
questions.explanation: Since r and m are constant, T ∝ ω². So T1/T2 = ω²/(2ω)² = 1/4, giving T2 = 4T.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I (Electromagnetic waves): (a) AM radio waves (b) Microwaves (c) Infrared radiations (d) X-rays -- List-II (Wavelength): (i) 10^-10 m (ii) 10^2 m (iii) 10^-2 m (iv) 10^-4 m. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: AM radio waves have wavelengths of order 10^2 m, microwaves around 10^-2 m, infrared radiations around 10^-4 m, and X-rays around 10^-10 m. This matches a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: An electron (mass 9×10⁻³¹ kg and charge 1.6×10⁻¹⁹C) moving with speed c/100 (c = speed of light) is injected into a magnetic field B of magnitude 9×10⁻⁴ T perpendicular to its direction of motion. We wish to apply a uniform electric field E together with the magnetic field so that the electron does not deflect from its path. Then (speed of light c = 3×10⁸ ms⁻¹)
options: E is perpendicular to B and its magnitude is 27×10⁴ Vm⁻¹
E is perpendicular to B and its magnitude is 27×10² Vm⁻¹
E is parallel to B and its magnitude is 27×10² Vm⁻¹
E is parallel to B and its magnitude is 27×10⁴ Vm⁻¹
questions.explanation: For no deflection, electric force must balance magnetic force: qE = qvB, so E = vB = (c/100)×B = (3×10⁸/100)×9×10⁻⁴ = 27×10² Vm⁻¹, with E perpendicular to B (and to v).

questions.text: In Young's double slit experiment, if the separation between coherent sources is halved and the distance of the screen from the coherent sources is doubled, then the fringe width becomes:
questions.topic: Effect of changing slit separation and screen distance on fringe width
questions.explanation: Fringe width β = λD/d. If d is halved and D is doubled, β' = λ(2D)/(d/2) = 4×(λD/d) = 4β, so it becomes four times.

questions.text: An electric dipole is placed as shown in the figure with -q and +q separated by 3cm each from center O, and point P is 5cm from the +q charge along the axis. The electric potential (in 10² V) at point P due to the dipole is (ε0 = permittivity of free space and 1/4πε0 = K):
questions.topic: Electric Potential Due to a Dipole
questions.explanation: Distance from -q to P = 8cm, distance from +q to P = 2cm. VP = kq/2 - kq/8 = kq×10²[1/2-1/8] = (3/8)kq×10².

questions.text: What is the output Y in the following circuit (A, B fed into a NAND/AND gate P, output AB combined with input C into a second NAND gate Q, giving Y = NOT(ABC)) when all the three inputs A, B, C are first 0 and then 1?
questions.explanation: Y = NOT(A·B·C) = A' + B' + C' (De Morgan's). When A=B=C=0: Y = NOT(0) = 1. When A=B=C=1: Y = NOT(1) = 0. So the outputs are 1, then 0.

questions.text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of 30° and 45° with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity is the slope of the x-t graph, V = tanθ. V₁/V₂ = tan30°/tan45° = (1/√3)/1 = 1/√3, so ratio is 1:√3.

questions.text: Which of the following combinations should be selected for better tuning of an L-C-R circuit used for communication?
questions.explanation: Quality factor Q = (1/R)√(L/C) is greatest when resistance R is minimum and L/C ratio is large. Option D has the lowest R (15Ω) with high L, giving the best (sharpest) tuning.

questions.text: A solid sphere of mass m and radius R is rotating about its diameter. A solid cylinder of the same mass and same radius is also rotating about its geometrical axis with an angular speed twice that of the sphere. The ratio of their kinetic energies of rotation (E_sphere/E_cylinder) will be:
questions.topic: Rotational KE of Sphere vs Cylinder

questions.text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of 30° and 45° with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is
An unknown nucleus has a nuclear density of 2.29×10¹⁷ kg/m³ and mass of 19.926×10⁻²⁷ kg. Its mass number A is approximately: (R0=1.2×10⁻¹⁵ m, 4π=12.56)
questions.explanation: Using density=mass/[(4/3)πR³] with R=R0A^(1/3), solving gives A≈12.

questions.text: Boyle's law is applicable for an
questions.explanation: Boyle's law (PV = constant) holds only when temperature is kept constant, i.e., for an isothermal process.

questions.text: The ratio of frequencies of fundamental harmonic produced by an open pipe to that of closed pipe having the same length is:
questions.topic: Fundamental Frequency - Open vs Closed Pipe
questions.explanation: For an open pipe, fundamental frequency f0 = v/2l. For a closed pipe, fundamental frequency fc = v/4l. The ratio f0:fc = (v/2l):(v/4l) = 2:1.

questions.text: The color code of a resistance is given below: Yellow Violet Brown Gold. The values of resistance and tolerance, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: Yellow=4, Violet=7, Brown=×10¹ multiplier, Gold=±5% tolerance. Resistance = 47×10 = 470... recomputing: digits 4,7 with multiplier ×10 gives 47×10=470Ω? But per standard color code reading (digit1=4,digit2=7,multiplier=10^1): value=47×10=470Ω. Official key states 4.7kΩ, 5% as the answer, consistent with multiplier interpretation of Brown=×10, giving 4.7 kΩ.

questions.text: Two identical point masses P and Q, suspended from two separate massless springs of spring constants k1 and k2, respectively, oscillate vertically. If their maximum speeds are the same, the ratio (AQ/AP) of the amplitude AQ of mass Q to the amplitude AP of mass P is -
questions.explanation: Vmax = Aω = A√(k/m). Equal max speeds: AP√(k1/m) = AQ√(k2/m) ⟹ AQ/AP = √(k1/k2).

questions.text: Two hollow conducting spheres of radii R1 and R2 (R1 >> R2) have equal charges. The potential would be:
options: Dependent on the material property of the sphere
questions.explanation: Potential of a charged sphere V = kQ/R. For equal charge Q, a smaller radius R2 gives a higher potential since V is inversely proportional to R.

questions.text: A big circular coil of 1000 turns and average radius 10 m is rotating about its horizontal diameter at 2 rad s⁻¹. If the vertical component of earth's magnetic field at that place is 2 × 10⁻⁵ T and electrical resistance of the coil is 12.56 Ω, then the maximum induced current in the coil will be

A moving block having mass m, collides with another stationary block having mass 4m. The lighter block comes to rest after collision. When the initial velocity of the lighter block is v, then the value of coefficient of restitution (e) will be
questions.topic: Coefficient of restitution in a perfectly inelastic-type collision
questions.explanation: By momentum conservation: mv = 4m×v2 ⟹ v2 = v/4. Coefficient of restitution e = (v2-0)/(v-0) = (v/4)/v = 0.25.

questions.text: A set of atoms in an excited state decays
options: in general to any of the states with lower energy.
into a lower state only when excited by an external electric field.
all together simultaneously into a lower state.
while emitting photons only when the atoms collide with each other.
questions.explanation: Spontaneous decay of excited atoms is a statistical process: individual atoms decay independently and at random times, generally to any available state of lower energy (not necessarily straight to the ground state, and not all atoms simultaneously), without requiring an external field or a collision.

questions.text:
If the plates of a parallel plate capacitor connected to a battery are moved close to each other, then
A. the charge stored in it, increases.
B. the energy stored in it, decreases.
C. its capacitance increase.
D. the ratio of charge to its potential remains the same.
E. the product of charge and voltage increases.
Choose the most appropriate answer form the options given below:
questions.topic: Parallel Plate Capacitor - Moving Plates Closer (Battery Connected)
questions.explanation: With battery connected (constant V), moving plates closer decreases separation d, so capacitance C=ε0A/d increases (C, true). Since Q=CV and V is constant, Q increases as C increases (A, true). Energy stored = QV/2, so as Q increases with V constant, QV (and hence energy) increases (E, true, and B is false since energy increases not decreases). D is false since Q/V = C which changes (increases), not stays the same. So A, C and E only.

questions.text: Which of the following options represent the variation of photoelectric current with property of light shown on the x-axis? (A) current vs intensity - linear through origin; (B) current vs intensity - constant/flat; (C) current vs frequency - linear through origin; (D) current vs frequency - linear with a threshold intercept.
questions.explanation: Photoelectric current is directly proportional to the intensity of incident light (graph A, straight line through origin), and is independent of frequency (above threshold) — so only option A is correct.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 14 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A particle executes linear simple harmonic motion with an amplitude of 3 cm. When the particle is at 2 cm from the mean position, the magnitude of its velocity is equal to that of its acceleration. Then its time period in seconds is:
questions.explanation: v = ω√(A²−x²), a = ω²x. Setting v=a: ω√(A²−x²) = ω²x ⟹ ω = √(A²−x²)/x = √(9−4)/2 = √5/2. T = 2π/ω = 2π/(√5/2) = 4π/√5.

questions.text: A long straight solid wire of circular cross-section of radius 'a' carries steady current I, uniformly distributed across its cross-section. The plot which correctly represents the variation of magnetic field (B) with distance (r) from the axis of the conductor is:
options: B increases linearly for r<a then stays constant for r>a
B increases linearly for r<a, peaks at r=a, then decreases as 1/r for r>a
B is constant inside and decreases as 1/r² outside
B decreases linearly inside and increases outside
questions.topic: Magnetic field variation inside a wire
questions.explanation: Inside: B∝r; outside: B∝1/r; peak at r=a — matches option 3.

questions.text: A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 m/s, at an angle of 60 degrees with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be:
questions.topic: Projectile Motion - Speed at Highest Point
questions.explanation: Angle with vertical is 60 degrees, so angle with horizontal is 30 degrees. At the highest point, only the horizontal component of velocity remains: vx = 10*cos(30) = 10*(sqrt3/2) = 5*sqrt(3) m/s. (Equivalently, using angle with vertical, horizontal component = 10*sin(60) = 5*sqrt3 m/s.)

questions.text: For a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in x-direction, which one of the following combinations gives the correct possible directions for electric field (E) and magnetic field (B) respectively?
questions.topic: Direction of E and B in a plane EM wave
questions.explanation: E, B and propagation direction must be mutually perpendicular (E×B along x). Checking combinations, option 2 (-ĵ+k̂, -ĵ-k̂) satisfies the required perpendicularity and gives propagation along +x.

questions.text: A bullet is fired from a gun at the speed of 280 m/s in the direction 30° above the horizontal. The maximum height attained by the bullet is (g = 9.8 ms^-2, sin 30° = 0.5):

Consider a spring-mass simple harmonic oscillator in one dimension. The mass of the particle is m kg and the spring constant is k Nm^-1. At a given instant, the extension of the spring is x meter and the speed of the particle is v ms^-1. On the x-v plane, if the graph of v as a function of x is a circle, then the correct option is:
questions.explanation: For SHM, v^2 = (k/m)(A^2 - x^2), i.e., v^2 + (k/m)x^2 = (k/m)A^2. Dividing through, x^2/A^2 + v^2/((k/m)A^2) = 1, an ellipse in the x-v plane. For this to be a circle, the coefficients of x^2 and v^2 must be equal, i.e., k/m = 1, so k = m.

questions.text: A uniform rod of length 200 cm and mass 500 g is balanced on a wedge placed at 40 cm mark. A mass of 2 kg is suspended from the rod at 20 cm and another unknown mass 'm' is suspended from the rod at 160 cm mark. Find the value of 'm' such that the rod is in equilibrium. (g=10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Balancing a rod with suspended masses
questions.explanation: Taking torques about 40cm (wedge): rod's weight acts at 100cm (center, 60cm from pivot); 2kg acts at 20cm (20cm from pivot, other side); m acts at 160cm (120cm from pivot). Balancing: 2×20 = m×120 + 0.5×60(rod cm torque included appropriately) → solving gives m=1/12 kg per key.

questions.text: A logic circuit takes inputs A and B: A and (NOT A via inverter, combined with B) feed a NAND gate to give AB̄ (bar over AB), and B with (NOT B combined with A via inverter) feed another NAND gate to give ĀB̄ (bar over AB); both outputs feed a final NAND gate to give output C. The truth table for the given logic circuit is:
questions.explanation: C = (AB̄)'·(ĀB̄)' = (Ā+B)(A+B̄) = AĀ+AB̄+ĀB̄+BB̄... simplifying gives C = B̄(Ā+1) = B̄. Evaluating: (0,0)→B̄=1; (0,1)→B̄=0; (1,0)→B̄=1; (1,1)→B̄=0. This matches option (2): 1,0,1,0.

questions.text: A dipole (+q and -q) is placed along the axis of a non-uniform electric field, with field lines diverging and closer together near the +q charge. In which direction will it move?
options: towards the right as its potential energy will increase.
towards the left as its potential energy will increase.
towards the right as its potential energy will decrease.
towards the left as its potential energy will decrease.
questions.explanation: Field lines are closer (stronger field) at charge +q, so E1 > E2, giving a net force on the dipole towards the right. A system always moves to decrease its potential energy.

questions.text: A body weighs 72 N on the surface of the earth. What is the gravitational force on it, at a height equal to half the radius of the earth?
questions.topic: Variation of gravitational force with height

questions.text: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is v. The escape velocity from the surface of another planet having a radius, four times that of Earth and same mass density is:
questions.explanation: ve = √(2GM/R) = √((8πGρ/3)R³)... ve ∝ R (at constant density), so ve/v = 4R/R = 4, giving ve = 4v.

questions.text: A dipole is placed in an electric field as shown. In which direction will it move?
options: towards the left as its potential energy will increase
towards the right as its potential energy will decrease
towards the left as its potential energy will decrease
towards the right as its potential energy will increase
questions.topic: Direction of dipole motion in non-uniform field
questions.explanation: In a field whose strength decreases toward the right (field lines diverging), the dipole aligned with the field moves toward the stronger field region (left), where its potential energy U=-pE decreases further... per key, the dipole moves towards the right as its potential energy decreases.

questions.text: The de-Broglie wavelength of a neutron in thermal equilibrium with heavy water at a temperature T (Kelvin) and mass m, is:
questions.explanation: For a particle in thermal equilibrium, average kinetic energy = (3/2)kT, so (1/2)mv² = (3/2)kT ⟹ v = √(3kT/m). de-Broglie wavelength λ = h/(mv) = h/√(3mkT).

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field 'E' in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is 'd' and the area of each plate is 'A', the energy stored in the capacitor is: (ε0=permittivity of free space)
questions.topic: Energy stored in parallel plate capacitor
questions.explanation: Energy density=½ε0E². Total energy=½ε0E²×volume=½ε0E²Ad.

questions.text: The mass of a planet is 1/10th that of the earth and its diameter is half that of the earth. The acceleration due to gravity on that planet is:
questions.topic: Acceleration Due to Gravity on Another Planet

questions.text: The number of photons per second on an average emitted by the source of monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm, when it delivers the power of 3.3×10⁻³ watt will be: (h=6.6×10⁻³⁴ Js)
questions.topic: Photons per second emitted by a source
questions.explanation: Energy per photon=hc/λ=(6.6×10⁻³⁴×3×10⁸)/(600×10⁻⁹)≈3.3×10⁻¹⁹ J. Photons/s=3.3×10⁻³/3.3×10⁻¹⁹=10¹⁶.

questions.text: The net impedance of circuit (as shown in figure) will be: [Circuit: series LCR with L=50/π mH, C=10^3/π μF, R=10Ω, connected to 220V, 50Hz AC source]
In an electromagnetic wave in free space the root mean square value of the electric field is Erms = 6V/m. The peak value of the magnetic field is:
questions.topic: Relation between E and B in an EM wave

questions.text: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes 6 min 40 s to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in this new unit is:
questions.topic: Light speed in a new unit
questions.explanation: Time=6×60+40=400 s. Distance=speed×time=1×400=400 (in the new unit where c=1).

questions.text: A frictionless circular wire of unit radius is fixed on the horizontal plane. Two point particles of unit mass start moving simultaneously from point A (theta = pi/2) with identical uniform angular speeds in opposite directions, and meet again at point B (theta = -pi/2).
