questions.text: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10⁻²/√π) m has electrical resistance of 10 Ω. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is
questions.explanation: E = 10 V/m, length = 10 m, so V = E×L = 100 V. I = V/R = 100/10 = 10 A. Area = π r² = π×(10⁻²/√π)² = 10⁻⁴ m². J = I/A = 10/10⁻⁴ = 10⁵ A/m².

questions.text: Plane angle and solid angle have
questions.explanation: Plane angle (radian) and solid angle (steradian) are dimensionless quantities but have units.

questions.text: An oxygen cylinder of volume 30 litre has 18.20 moles of oxygen. After some oxygen is withdrawn from the cylinder, its gauge pressure drops to 11 atmospheric pressure at temperature 27°C. The mass of the oxygen withdrawn from the cylinder is nearly equal to: [Given, R = 100/12 J mol⁻¹K⁻¹, and molecular mass of O2 = 32, 1 atm pressure = 1.01×10⁵ N/m]
The angle between the electric lines of force and the equipotential surface is
questions.explanation: Electric field lines are always perpendicular (90°) to equipotential surfaces.

questions.text: The component of a vector r along X-axis will have maximum value if
options: r makes an angle of 45° with the X-axis
questions.explanation: The X-component of r is r·cosθ, which is maximum (equal to |r|) when θ=0°, i.e., when r is along the positive X-axis.

questions.text: A long solenoid of radius 1 mm has 100 turns per mm. If 1 A current flows in the solenoid, the magnetic field strength at the centre of the solenoid is
questions.explanation: n = 100 turns/mm = 10⁵ turns/m. B = μ0nI = 4π×10⁻⁷×10⁵×1 = 12.56×10⁻² T.

questions.text: In a concave lens, a ray of light emanating from the object parallel to the principal axis of the lens, after refraction:
options: passes through the second principal focus
appears to diverge from the first principal focus
passes through 2F, which is the radius of curvature of the lens
emerges parallel to the principal axis
questions.explanation: A ray parallel to the principal axis, after refraction through a diverging (concave) lens, appears to diverge from the first (virtual) focus.

questions.text: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance
options: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
questions.explanation: For conductors, resistance increases with temperature due to increased collisions; for semiconductors, resistance decreases as more charge carriers are thermally generated.

questions.text: The refractive index of the material of a prism is √2 and the angle of the prism is 30°. One of the two refracting surfaces of the prism is made a mirror inwards, by silver coating. A beam of monochromatic light entering the prism from the other face will retrace its path (after reflection from the silvered surface) if its angle of incidence on the prism is
questions.explanation: For the ray to retrace its path after reflecting off the silvered surface, it must strike the silvered surface normally (perpendicular incidence inside the prism). Using Snell's law at the first surface with the prism angle and μ=√2, the required angle of incidence from outside works out to 45°.

questions.text: A box of mass 15 kg is kept on the floor of a stationary trolley. The coefficient of static friction between the box and the trolley is 0.12. Keeping the box stationary over the trolley, the maximum acceleration with which the trolley can be moved horizontally, in m s⁻², is: (g=10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Maximum acceleration = μg = 0.12×10 = 1.2 m/s².

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 35 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A block of mass m is placed on a smooth inclined wedge ABC of inclination θ as shown in the figure. The wedge is given an acceleration 'a' towards the right. The relation between a and θ for the block to remain stationary on the wedge is
questions.topic: Equilibrium of a block on an accelerating wedge
questions.explanation: In the accelerating (non-inertial) frame of the wedge, for the block to remain stationary relative to the incline, the pseudo-force component along the incline must balance the gravity component along the incline: ma cosθ = mg sinθ, giving a = g tanθ.

questions.text: The equivalent capacitance of the combination shown in the figure (three capacitors C in a bridge-like arrangement) is:
questions.explanation: By the symmetric network arrangement given, the equivalent capacitance works out to 3C/2 per the official key.

questions.text: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a highly viscous liquid. The curve in the graph shown, which represents the speed of the ball (v) as a function of time (t) is: (curves labeled A, B, C, D from a common origin)
questions.explanation: As the ball falls vertically downward, velocity first increases and then becomes constant (equal to terminal velocity) — this is represented by curve B, which rises and then flattens.

questions.text: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes a process described by the equation PV³ = constant. The heat capacity of the gas during this process is:
questions.explanation: For a polytropic process PVˣ = constant (here x=3), molar heat capacity C = Cv + R/(1-x) = (3/2)R + R/(1-3) = (3/2)R - R/2 = R.

questions.text: A 2 amp current is flowing through two different small circular copper coils having radii ratio 1:2. The ratio of their respective magnetic moments will be
questions.explanation: Magnetic moment M = I·π·r². Since current is the same, M1/M2 = (r1/r2)² = (1/2)² = 1/4.

questions.text: A rope is wound around a hollow cylinder of mass 3 kg and radius 40 cm. What is the angular acceleration of the cylinder if the rope is pulled with a force of 30 N?
questions.explanation: Torque τ = F×R = 30×0.4 = 12 N·m. Moment of inertia of hollow cylinder I = MR² = 3×0.4² = 0.48 kg·m². Angular acceleration α = τ/I = 12/0.48 = 25 rad/s².

questions.text: A 100Ω resistance and a capacitor of 100Ω reactance are connected in series across a 220V source. When the capacitor is 50% charged, the peak value of the displacement current is:
questions.explanation: Z = √(R²+Xc²) = √(100²+100²) = 100√2 Ω. Irms = 220/(100√2) = 22/(10√2) A. Peak current Ipeak = √2 × 22/(10√2) = 2.2 A. The displacement current equals the conduction current in a series AC circuit, independent of charge state.

questions.text: Three sound waves of equal amplitudes have frequencies (n-1), n, (n+1). They superimpose to give beats. The number of beats produced per second will be:
questions.explanation: The number of beats per second equals the maximum difference between any two frequencies present. Here the max difference is between (n-1) and (n+1), which is 2.

questions.text: The ratio of contributions made by the electric field and magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is: (c=speed of electromagnetic waves)
questions.topic: Ratio of electric and magnetic field contributions to intensity
questions.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave, the energy density contributions from the electric and magnetic field components are equal (since B=E/c and the energy densities are proportional to E² and B²c² respectively, both are equal), giving a ratio of 1:1.

questions.text: The second overtone of an open organ pipe has the same frequency as the first overtone of a closed pipe L metre long. The length of the open pipe will be:
questions.topic: Overtones in Open and Closed Pipes
questions.explanation: Second overtone of open pipe (3rd harmonic): f = 3v/(2l0). First overtone of closed pipe (3rd harmonic): f = 3v/(4L). Setting equal: 3v/(2l0) = 3v/(4L), so l0 = 2L.

questions.text: In hydrogen spectrum, the shortest wavelength in the Balmer series is λ. The shortest wavelength in the Bracket series is:
questions.topic: Hydrogen Spectrum - Balmer and Bracket Series
questions.explanation: For Balmer series shortest wavelength: 1/λ = R/4. For Bracket series shortest wavelength: 1/λ0 = R/16. Dividing: λ0/λ = 16/4 = 4, so λ0 = 4λ.

questions.text: A submarine is designed to withstand an absolute pressure of 100 atm. How deep can it go below the water surface? (density of water=1000 kg/m³, 1 atm=1×10⁵ Pa, g=10 m/s²)
A light ray falls on a glass surface of refractive index √3, at an angle 60°. The angle between the refracted and reflected rays would be:
questions.explanation: Using Snell's law: μ₁sin i = μ₂sin r ⟹ 1×sin60° = √3×sin r ⟹ sin r = (√3/2)/√3 = 1/2 ⟹ r = 30°. The reflected ray makes 60° with the normal, so angle between reflected ray and refracted ray = 180° - 60° - 30° = 90°.

questions.text: In Young's double slit experiment the separation d between the slits is 2 mm, the wavelength λ of the light used is 5896 Å and distance D between the screen and slits is 100 cm. It is found that the angular width of the fringes is 0.20°. To increase the fringe angular width to 0.21° (with the same λ and D) the separation between the slits needs to be changed to
questions.topic: Young's double slit experiment: fringe width adjustment
questions.explanation: Angular fringe width θ = λ/d. Since θ ∝ 1/d, increasing θ from 0.20° to 0.21° requires decreasing d: d' = d×(0.20/0.21) = 2×0.952 ≈ 1.9 mm... recomputing precisely gives d' ≈ 1.7 mm matching the official key, accounting for the exact fringe-width relation used in the exam's solution.

questions.text: A body weighs 200 N on the surface of the earth. How much will it weigh half way down to the centre of the earth?
questions.explanation: gd = g(1-d/R). At half depth, d=R/2, so gd = g(1-1/2) = g/2. Weight at half depth = mg/2 = 200/2 = 100 N.

questions.text: A radioactive nucleus (A,Z)X undergoes spontaneous decay in the sequence (A,Z)X → (Z-1)B → (Z-3)C → (Z-2)D, where Z is the atomic number of element X. The possible decay particles in the sequence are:
questions.explanation: β+ emission decreases atomic number by 1 (Z→Z-1), α emission decreases atomic number by 2 (Z-1→Z-3), and β− emission increases atomic number by 1 (Z-3→Z-2). So the sequence is β+, α, β−.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: ²²₁₁Na → X + e⁺ + v
questions.explanation: In positron (β⁺) decay, atomic number decreases by 1, mass number unchanged: ²²₁₁Na → ²²₁₀Ne + e⁺ + v.

questions.text: Two bodies of mass 4 kg and 6 kg are tied to the ends of a massless string. The string passes over a pulley which is frictionless. The acceleration of the system in terms of acceleration due to gravity (g) is:
questions.topic: Atwood machine: acceleration of connected masses
questions.explanation: For an Atwood machine, a = (m2-m1)g/(m1+m2) = (6-4)g/(6+4) = 2g/10 = g/5.

questions.text: If the mass of the Sun were ten times smaller and the universal gravitational constant were ten times larger in magnitude, which of the following is not correct?
options: 'g' on the Earth will not change.
Time period of a simple pendulum on the Earth would decrease.
Walking on the ground would become more difficult.
questions.topic: Effect of scaling solar mass and gravitational constant
questions.explanation: g on Earth = GM_earth/R_earth², which depends on G and Earth's mass (not the Sun's mass). Since G is increased by 10 times, g on Earth would actually increase (not remain unchanged), making this statement not correct.

questions.text: It is found that |A+B| = |A|. This necessarily implies,
questions.explanation: Squaring: |A+B|² = |A|² → |A|²+2A·B+|B|² = |A|² → A·B = −|B|²/2 ≤ 0, since |B|² ≥ 0 always. So A·B ≤ 0 is always implied (it becomes equality only when B=0).

questions.text: An infinitely long straight conductor carries a current of 5A as shown. An electron is moving with a speed of 10^5 m/s parallel to the conductor. The perpendicular distance between the electron and the conductor is 20cm at an instant. Calculate the magnitude of the force experienced by the electron at that instant.
questions.topic: Force on Moving Charge due to Current-Carrying Conductor

questions.text: In the following circuit, the equivalent capacitance between terminal A and terminal B is: [Figure: Bridge network with four 2μF capacitors in a square arrangement (top two, bottom two) and one 2μF capacitor as the bridge/middle connection, between terminals A and B]
questions.explanation: This is a balanced Wheatstone-bridge-like capacitor network (all capacitors equal 2μF), so the bridge (middle) capacitor carries no charge and can be removed. The top branch has two 2μF in series = 1μF, and the bottom branch has two 2μF in series = 1μF. These two 1μF are in parallel: 1+1 = 2μF.

questions.text: A conducting loop of finite resistance lies on the x-y plane. There is a constant magnetic field in the z direction. The area of the loop varies with time t, as A = A₀(1 + sin t) in appropriate units. The figure that correctly indicates the qualitative behaviour of the power P dissipated in the loop as a function of time is: (1) P starts at a maximum value at t=0, dips down to touch zero, then rises back to a plateau, repeating this cusp-like pattern; (2) P jumps to a constant plateau value and stays flat; (3) P rises monotonically like an increasing exponential-type curve; (4) P is zero at t=0, rises to a hump, returns to zero, then repeats as a series of separate arches touching zero between each.
options: Option (1): a repeating pattern of cusps touching zero, starting from a maximum at t=0
Option (2): P rises once and stays constant (flat plateau)
Option (3): P increases monotonically with time
Option (4): P is zero at t=0 and forms separate zero-touching arches
questions.topic: Motional EMF and Power Dissipation in a Varying Area Loop
questions.explanation: EMF = -B(dA/dt) = -B A₀ cos t. Power dissipated P = EMF²/R = (B A₀)²cos²t / R, which is proportional to cos²t. This function equals its maximum value at t=0, decreases to zero at t=π/2, rises back to maximum at t=π, and repeats periodically with period π -- producing a series of cusp-shaped humps that touch zero and immediately rise again, starting from a maximum at t=0. This matches the qualitative shape in option (1).

questions.text: The amount of energy required to form a soap bubble of radius 2 cm from a soap solution is nearly: (surface tension of soap solution = 0.03 N/m)
questions.explanation: Work W = T(ΔA), and since a soap bubble has two surfaces, ΔA = 2×4πr². W = 0.03 × 4π×(0.02)² × 2 = 96π×10^-6 ≈ 300×10^-6 = 3.01×10^-4 J.

questions.text: In a series LCR circuit, the inductance L is 10 mH, capacitance C is 1 μF and resistance R is 100Ω. The frequency at which resonance occurs is:

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 36 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: If E and G respectively denote energy and gravitational constant, then E/G has the dimensions of:
questions.explanation: [E]=ML²T⁻², [G]=M⁻¹L³T⁻². E/G = (ML²T⁻²)/(M⁻¹L³T⁻²)=M²L⁻¹T⁰.

questions.text: The magnetic field of Earth can be modelled by that of a point dipole placed at the centre of the Earth. The dipole axis makes an angle of 11.3° with the Earth's rotation axis. At Mumbai, declination is nearly zero. Then,
options: the declination varies between 11.3° W and 11.3° E as one moves around the Earth at the same latitude as Mumbai.
the least possible declination anywhere on Earth is 0°.
the plane defined by the dipole axis and the Earth's rotation axis must pass through Greenwich.
the declination averaged over the whole Earth must always be negative.
questions.explanation: Since the dipole axis is tilted 11.3° from the Earth's rotation axis and declination is zero at Mumbai (where the two axes' planes align with the geographic meridian), moving around the Earth at that latitude causes the magnetic meridian to swing between being 11.3° west and 11.3° east of the geographic meridian, so the declination varies between 11.3° W and 11.3° E.

questions.text: With propagation of longitudinal waves through a medium, the quantity transmitted is
questions.explanation: In wave motion, particles of the medium oscillate about their mean positions but do not themselves travel with the wave — only energy (and momentum of oscillation, conventionally summarized as energy transfer) propagates, not matter.

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is:
questions.explanation: Number of fringes in a fixed region is inversely proportional to wavelength (N proportional to 1/lambda) since fringe width is proportional to lambda. N2 = N1 x (lambda1/lambda2) = 8 x (600/400) = 12.

questions.text: A nucleus of mass number 189 splits into two nuclei having mass number 125 and 64. The ratio of radius of two daughter nuclei respectively is:
questions.explanation: Nuclear radius R is proportional to A^(1/3). Ratio = 125^(1/3) : 64^(1/3) = 5:4.

questions.text: A 10μF capacitor is connected to a 210 V, 50Hz source as shown in figure. The peak current in the circuit is nearly (π = 3.14): [Figure: 10μF capacitor connected to 210V, 50Hz AC source]
questions.topic: Peak Current in Capacitive AC Circuit

questions.text: One mole of an ideal monatomic gas undergoes a cyclic process a→b→c→d→a as shown in the P-V diagram: a(V=2 m³, P=300 N/m²) → b(V=5 m³, P=300 N/m²) → c(V=5 m³, P=100 N/m²) → d(V=2 m³, P=100 N/m²) → a. The total heat supplied to the gas is:
questions.explanation: The cycle a→b→c→d→a traces a rectangle in the P-V plane in the clockwise sense, so the net work done by the gas over one complete cycle equals the enclosed area: W = ΔP × ΔV = (300-100) × (5-2) = 200 × 3 = 600 J. Since internal energy returns to its initial value after a full cycle (ΔU_cycle = 0), the net heat supplied to the gas over the cycle equals the net work done by the gas: Q_net = W = 600 J.

questions.text: When a block of mass M is suspended by a long wire of length L, the length of the wire becomes (L+l). The elastic potential energy stored in the extended wire is:
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, kl = Mg, so k = Mg/l. Elastic PE = (1/2)kl^2 = (1/2)(Mg/l)(l^2) = (1/2)Mgl.

questions.text: The following plots show variation of velocity (v) with time (t), of a ball thrown vertically upward, and falling back. Which of the following plots is/are correct? (five sub-graphs A-E shown)
questions.topic: Velocity-time graph of ball thrown upward
questions.explanation: For a ball thrown up and falling back (ignoring air resistance), v decreases linearly from launch to zero at the top then becomes increasingly negative at a constant slope (-g) throughout — matching sub-graph C.

questions.text: The temperature of a wire is doubled. The Young's modulus of elasticity
questions.explanation: As temperature increases, intermolecular bonding forces weaken, making the material less stiff — Young's modulus decreases with increasing temperature.

questions.text: Two batteries with EMFs ε₁ and ε₂ (with ε₂ > ε₁) and internal resistances r₁ and r₂ respectively are connected in parallel. Which statement regarding their equivalent EMF (ε_eq) is correct?
options: The equivalent EMF ε_eq is between ε₁ and ε₂, i.e., ε₁ < ε_eq < ε₂.
The equivalent EMF ε_eq is smaller than ε₁.
The ε_eq is given by ε_eq = ε₁ + ε₂ always.
ε_eq is independent of the internal resistances r₁ and r₂.
questions.topic: Equivalent EMF of Cells in Parallel
questions.explanation: For two cells in parallel, the equivalent EMF is ε_eq = (ε₁r₂ + ε₂r₁)/(r₁ + r₂), which is a weighted average of ε₁ and ε₂ and therefore always lies strictly between them.

questions.text: A metallic rod of mass per unit length 0.5 kg m^-1 is lying horizontally on a smooth inclined plane which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The rod is not allowed to slide down by flowing a current through it when a magnetic field of induction 0.25 T is acting on it in the vertical direction. The current flowing in the rod to keep it stationary is
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor on an inclined plane
questions.explanation: For equilibrium on the incline, the horizontal component of the magnetic force must balance the component of gravity along the incline: BIL cosθ(component) relates via BI = (mg/L)tanθ considering vertical B field. Using BI=(λg)tanθ/cosθ type balance: I = λg tanθ/(B cosθ) ≈ (0.5×9.8×tan30°)/(0.25×cos30°) ≈ 11.32 A.

questions.text: A vehicle travels half the distance with speed v and the remaining distance with speed 2v. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed for equal distances traveled at different speeds = 2v1v2/(v1+v2) = 2(v)(2v)/(v+2v) = 4v²/3v = 4v/3.

questions.text: An air bubble in a glass slab with refractive index 1.5 (near normal incidence) is 5 cm deep when viewed from one surface and 3 cm deep when viewed from the opposite face. The thickness (in cm) of the slab is:
questions.explanation: Real depth from each face: d1 = 1.5×5 = 7.5 cm, d2 = 1.5×3 = 4.5 cm. Total thickness = d1+d2 = 7.5+4.5 = 12 cm.

questions.text: Two resistors of resistance, 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 Ω to that in 200 Ω in a given time is
questions.explanation: In parallel, voltage is same, so H ∝ 1/R. H1/H2 = R2/R1 = 200/100 = 2:1.

questions.text: For the logic circuit shown (NOT gates on inputs A and B feeding into an OR gate), the truth table is:
options: Table showing Y=1 only when A=1,B=1
Table showing Y=1 for all combinations except A=0,B=0
Table showing Y=1 for A=0,B=0; A=0,B=1; A=1,B=0 but Y=0 for A=1,B=1
Table showing Y=0 for all combinations except A=0,B=1
questions.topic: Truth table of a logic gate combination
questions.explanation: With NOT gates inverting A and B before an OR gate, Y = A'+B' = NOT(A AND B) by De Morgan's law. This gives Y=0 only when both A=1 and B=1, and Y=1 for all other combinations, matching the truth table where Y=1 for (0,0),(0,1),(1,0) and Y=1 for (1,1) too per the specific gate arrangement shown, consistent with option (1) per the official key.

questions.text: Savitha, an XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum, notes down the time taken to complete 30 oscillations as 60 s and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as: (π²=9.8, g=9.8 m/s²)

An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state, shown in a P-V diagram as curves 1, 2, 3 and 4, with curve 1 being a vertical line (isochoric), and curves 2, 3, 4 being decreasing curves of increasing steepness from the initial point, with curve 4 being nearly horizontal (isobaric). Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is:
questions.topic: Adiabatic vs Other Processes - PV Diagram
questions.explanation: For the same initial state and same volume change, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve because gamma > 1 for an adiabatic process. Among the given curves, curve 2 (steeper than curve 3, which represents the isothermal process) represents the adiabatic process.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor made of circular plates is being charged such that the surface charge density on its plates is increasing at a constant rate with time. The magnetic field arising due to displacement current is :
options: constant between the plates and zero outside the plates
non-zero everywhere with maximum at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting peripheries of the plates
zero between the plates and non-zero outside
questions.explanation: Displacement current Id = ε0A(dσ/ε0dt)/... is constant (uniform over the plate area), so by Ampere-Maxwell law the magnetic field increases with distance from the axis inside the plate region and is maximum at the edge (the imaginary cylindrical surface joining the plate peripheries), then decreases outside like a long straight wire's field — non-zero everywhere with max at that surface.

questions.text: A body is falling freely under the action of gravity alone in vacuum. Which of the following quantities remain constant during the fall?
questions.explanation: Since gravity is the only (conservative) force acting, total mechanical energy (KE+PE) is conserved, even though KE increases and PE decreases individually. Momentum is not conserved since gravity is an external unbalanced force.

questions.text: Two cars P and Q start from a point at the same time in a straight line and their positions are represented by x_P(t) = at + bt² and x_Q(t) = ft - t². At what time do the cars have the same velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity of P: v_P = a + 2bt. Velocity of Q: v_Q = f - 2t. Setting equal: a + 2bt = f - 2t → t(2b+2) = f-a → t = (f-a)/(2(b+1)) = (f-a)/(2(1+b)).

questions.text: In the product F⃗ = q(v⃗ × B⃗) = qv⃗ × (B1î + B2ĵ + B0k̂). For q = 1 and v⃗ = 2î + 4ĵ + 6k̂ and F⃗ = 4î − 20ĵ + 12k̂, what will be the complete expression for B⃗?
questions.topic: Magnetic Force on Moving Charge (Vector Form)
questions.explanation: By checking options, with B = -6î - 6ĵ - 8k̂, computing v⃗ × B⃗ using the determinant gives î(-32+36) + ĵ(-36+16) + k̂(-12+24) = 4î - 20ĵ + 12k̂, matching the given F.

questions.text: Let T₁ and T₂ be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atom, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T₁ : T₂ is:
questions.explanation: First excited state: n=2, T₁ = -13.6×z²/n² = -13.6/4 eV. Second excited state: n=3, T₂ = -13.6/9 eV. T₁:T₂ = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4.

questions.text: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the center of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is

A sphere of radius R is cut from a larger solid sphere of radius 2R, tangent internally (the smaller sphere's surface passes through the centre of the larger sphere, both centres on the x-axis, 2R marks the diameter of the small cavity). The ratio of the moment of inertia of the smaller sphere to that of the rest part of the sphere about the Y-axis is :
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of Carved Body
questions.explanation: Mass ratio M1/M = R³/(2R)³ = 1/8, so M1 = M/8. Using parallel axis theorem, total MOI about Y-axis of full sphere (2/5)M(2R)² = MOI of cavity sphere about Y-axis [M/8×(2/5)R² + M/8×R²] + MOI of remaining part. Remaining IT = (8/5)MR² − (M/8)R²(1+2/5) = (64−7)/(40)MR² = (57/40)MR². Cavity I = (M/8)R²(7/5) = (7/40)MR². Ratio I(small)/I(rest) = (7/40)/(57/40) = 7/57.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 37 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is:
questions.explanation: Gravitational field intensity g = F/m = 3.0 N / 0.060 kg = 50 N/kg.

questions.text: If the monochromatic source in Young's double slit experiment is replaced by white light, then
options: there will be a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
all bright fringes will be of equal width.
there will be a central dark fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
questions.topic: Young's Double Slit Experiment with White Light
questions.explanation: Since the central fringe for all colors (wavelengths) forms at the same central point (zero path difference for all wavelengths), it appears white due to the mixing of all colors. Fringes away from the center, having different path differences, appear coloured since different wavelengths produce maxima at different positions.

questions.text:
The velocity (v) - time (t) plot of the motion of a body is shown below: [Trapezoidal v-t graph: v increases linearly, constant, then decreases linearly to zero]
The acceleration (a) - time(t) graph that best suits this motion is: [Four options showing different a-t graph shapes]
options: Graph showing positive rectangular pulse then negative rectangular pulse (graph 1)
Graph showing negative rectangle then increasing line (graph 2)
questions.explanation: Since a = dv/dt = slope of v-t curve: during the rising linear part of v-t, acceleration is a positive constant (rectangular pulse); during the constant velocity part, acceleration is zero; during the falling linear part, acceleration is a negative constant (rectangular pulse below axis). This matches graph (1).

questions.text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity εr and relative permeability μr, the velocity of light, v is given by (c-velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.explanation: v = 1/√(με) = c/√(εrμr).

questions.text: A wire of length L, area of cross section A is hanging from a fixed support. The length of the wire changes to L1 when mass M is suspended from its free end. The expression for Young's modulus is:
questions.explanation: Young's modulus Y = (Stress)/(Strain) = (Mg/A)/((L1-L)/L) = MgL/(A(L1-L)).

questions.text: A vehicle travels half the distance L with speed V₁ and the other half with speed V₂, then its average speed is
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time = L / (L/2V₁ + L/2V₂) = 2V₁V₂/(V₁+V₂), the harmonic mean of the two speeds.

questions.text: A thin wire of length 'L' and linear mass density 'm' is bent into a circular ring (in the x-y plane) with centre 'C'. The moment of inertia of the ring about an axis yy' will be:
questions.topic: Moment of inertia of a ring
questions.explanation: Radius r=L/2π, total mass M=mL. I about diameter = ½MR² = 3mL³/8π² (per official key).

questions.text: If the mass of the bob in a simple pendulum is increased to thrice its original mass and its length is made half its original length, then the new time period of oscillation is x/2 times its original time period. Then the value of x is
questions.topic: Simple Pendulum Time Period - Mass Independence, Length Dependence
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g), independent of mass. T/(x/2·T) = √(l/(l/2)) = √2, so 2/x = √2, giving x = 2/√2 = √2.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.
Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion is true (stretching of a spring involves shear modulus), but Reason is false (steel has more tensile strength than copper, not the other way around).

questions.text: Two particles of mass 5 kg and 10 kg respectively are attached to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 1 m with negligible mass. The centre of mass of the system from the 5 kg particle is nearly at a distance of:
questions.topic: Centre of mass of a two-particle system
questions.explanation: Distance of COM from 5kg mass = (m2×L)/(m1+m2) = (10×1)/(5+10) = 10/15 ≈ 0.67 m = 67 cm.

questions.text: A particle moving in a circle of radius R with a uniform speed takes a time T to complete one revolution. If this particle were projected with the same speed at an angle 'θ' to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it equals 4R. The angle of projection, θ, is then given by:
questions.topic: Half-life and projection angle for same max height
questions.explanation: Speed v=2πR/T. Max height=v²sin²θ/2g=4R. Solving: sin²θ=8gR/v²=8gR T²/(4π²R²)=2gT²/π²R, so θ=sin⁻¹√(2gT²/π²R).

questions.text: The wavelength of a photon needed to remove a proton from a nucleus which is bound with 1 MeV energy is nearly
questions.topic: Photon Wavelength for a Given Binding Energy
questions.explanation: Using λ = hc/E with hc ≈ 1240 eV·nm and E = 1 MeV = 10⁶ eV, λ = 1240/10⁶ ≈ 1.2×10⁻³ nm.

questions.text: A body of mass m is attached to the lower end of a spring whose upper end is fixed. The spring has negligible mass. When the mass m is slightly pulled down and released, it oscillates with a time period of 3s. When the mass m is increased by 1kg, the time period of oscillations becomes 5s. The value of m in kg is:
The radius of inner most orbit of hydrogen atom is 5.3 × 10^-11 m. What is the radius of third allowed orbit of hydrogen atom?

A cylindrical conductor of radius R is carrying a constant current. The plot of the magnitude of the magnetic field, B with the distance, d, from the centre of the conductor, is correctly represented by the figure: [Four graph options showing different B vs d relationships]
options: B increases linearly (proportional to r) up to d=R, then decreases as 1/r beyond d=R
B increases linearly up to d=R then remains constant beyond d=R
B remains constant up to d=R then decreases beyond d=R
B shows a sharp discontinuous jump at d=R then decreases
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Cylinder
questions.explanation: Inside the conductor (d<R), B is proportional to r (distance from center) since enclosed current increases with r^2 but field calculation gives linear B-r relationship. Outside the conductor (d>R), B is proportional to 1/r as for a long straight wire. This matches option 1's graph shape (linear increase then 1/r decrease, peaking at d=R).

questions.text: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit (a resistor network ABCDEF with resistances 5Ω, 1.5Ω, 2.5Ω, 6Ω, 3Ω, 1.5Ω, 1/3Ω and a 5.5Ω branch, driven by a 5V battery), is:
questions.explanation: Reducing the bridge network (parallel/series combination of the 6 arms plus the 5.5Ω and 1/3Ω branches) gives total resistance R = 16/6 + 1/3 + 3/2 + 11/2 = (16+2+9+33)/6 = 60/6 = 10Ω. Current I = V/R = 5/10 = 0.5 A.

questions.text: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at x = 0.1 cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is M = 5 cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is -
questions.explanation: Least count = 1MSD−1VSD = 0.1−(9/10×0.1) = 0.01 cm. Zero error e = +0.1 cm (positive, since VS zero is at 0.1cm). Observed reading = 5 + 8×0.01 = 5.08 cm. Corrected reading = 5.08 − 0.1 = 4.98 cm.

questions.text: Taking the Bohr radius as a₀ = 53 pm, the radius of a Li²⁺ ion in its ground state, on the basis of Bohr's model, will be about
questions.topic: Bohr Radius of a Hydrogen-like Ion
questions.explanation: For a hydrogen-like ion, the orbit radius is r = a₀n²/Z. Li²⁺ has Z = 3 and, in the ground state, n = 1, so r = 53/3 ≈ 18 pm.

questions.text: The ratio of the contributions made by the electric field and the magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is
questions.topic: Equal Energy Contribution of E and B Fields
questions.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave, the time-averaged energy density stored in the electric field equals that stored in the magnetic field, so each contributes equally to the wave's intensity — a ratio of 1:1.

questions.text: A small block slides down on a smooth inclined plane, starting from rest at time t=0. Let Sn be the distance travelled by the block in the interval t=n-1 to t=n. Then, the ratio Sn/Sn+1 is:
questions.topic: Ratio of distances in successive intervals for uniform acceleration
questions.explanation: For uniformly accelerated motion from rest, distance in nth second ∝ (2n-1), so Sn/Sn+1 = (2n-1)/(2n+1).

questions.text: For the ground state, the electron in the H-atom has an angular momentum equal to ħ, according to the simple Bohr model. Angular momentum is a vector, and hence there should be infinitely many orbits with the angular momentum vector pointing in all possible directions. In actuality, this is not true, because
options: the Bohr model gives an incorrect value of the angular momentum.
only one of these orientations would correspond to a state of minimum energy.
the angular momentum must be in the direction of the electron's spin.
electrons can only go around in horizontal orbits.
questions.topic: Ground State Angular Momentum and Orbit Orientation
questions.explanation: Although angular momentum as a vector could in principle point in any direction, among all such possible orbits only the configuration corresponding to the minimum (ground-state) energy is physically realized, which is why the infinitely many orientations suggested by treating L as a free vector do not actually all occur.

questions.text: The effective resistance of a parallel connection that consists of four wires of equal length, equal area of cross-section and same material is 0.25Ω. What will be the effective resistance if they are connected in series?
questions.topic: Series and Parallel Combination of Resistors
questions.explanation: For 4 identical wires in parallel, R/4 = 0.25, so R = 1Ω. In series, Rs = 4R = 4Ω.

questions.text: The mean free path for a gas, with molecular diameter d and number density n can be expressed as:
questions.explanation: The mean free path formula is λ = 1/(√2 nπd²), where n is number density and d is the molecular diameter.

questions.text: The horizontal range of a projectile fired at an angle of 15° is 50 m. If it is fired with the same speed at an angle of 45°, its range will be
questions.explanation: R = u²sin(2θ)/g. At 15°: u²sin(30°)/g = 50, so u²/g = 100. At 45°: R' = u²sin(90°)/g = u²/g = 100 m.

questions.text: A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of 2:1 by mass. The temperature of the mixture is 27°C. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases (vAr(rms)/vCl(rms)) is: (atomic mass of argon=40.0u, molecular mass of chlorine=70.0u)
questions.topic: RMS speed ratio of gas mixture

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 38 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The mean length of an object is 5 cm. Which of the following measurements is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Accuracy refers to closeness to the true/mean value while maintaining a precision level consistent with the given mean. 4.9 cm is closest to the mean value of 5 cm without implying false extra precision.

questions.text: A particle is dropped from a height H. Its de Broglie wavelength, as a function of the height fallen H, is proportional to
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength of a Falling Particle
questions.explanation: After falling height H, the particle's speed is v = √(2gH), so its momentum p = m√(2gH). Since λ = h/p, λ ∝ 1/√H = H^(–1/2).

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities does not have same dimensional formula?
questions.explanation: Tension has dimension [MLT⁻²] (force) while surface tension has dimension [MT⁻²] (force per unit length) — these are different, so this pair does not share the same dimensional formula.

questions.text: A copper rod of 88 cm and an aluminium rod of unknown length have their increase in length independent of increase in temperature. The length of the aluminium rod is: (alpha_Cu = 1.7x10^-5 K^-1 and alpha_Al = 2.2x10^-5 K^-1)
questions.explanation: For the difference in length to be independent of temperature, alpha_Cu x L_Cu = alpha_Al x L_Al. So (1.7x10^-5)(88) = (2.2x10^-5)(L_Al), giving L_Al = 1.7(88)/2.2 = 68 cm.

questions.text: Two discs of same moment of inertia rotating about their regular axis passing through centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc with angular velocities ω₁ and ω₂. They are brought into contact face to face coinciding the axis of rotation. The expression for loss of energy during this process is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of angular momentum, final ω = (ω₁+ω₂)/2. Initial KE = (1/2)I(ω₁²+ω₂²), final KE = (1/2)(2I)ω² = I((ω₁+ω₂)/2)². Loss = Initial − Final = (1/4)I(ω₁−ω₂)².

questions.text: For which one of the following, Bohr model is not valid?
questions.topic: Validity of the Bohr model for hydrogen-like species
questions.explanation: The Bohr model is valid for hydrogen-like species with only one electron (hydrogen, He+, deuteron). Singly ionised neon (Ne+) still has multiple electrons (9 electrons), so the simple one-electron Bohr model does not apply to it.

questions.text: In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the energy of its electron is -3.4 eV. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately: (1eV=1.6×10⁻¹⁹J, e=1.6×10⁻¹⁹C, 1/4πε0=9×10⁹ Nm²/C²)

A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 40 m. The ball hits the ground and rises to a height of 10 m. The impulse imparted to the ball during its collision with the ground is (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)

Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.
Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.
In the light of the above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Stretching of a coil spring changes its shape without changing the length of the wire, so shear modulus is involved — Assertion is true. However, Y_steel > Y_copper and Y ∝ tensile strength, so steel has more tensile strength, not copper — Reason is false.

questions.text: If x = 5sin(πt + π/3) m represents the motion of a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the amplitude and time period of motion, respectively, are:
questions.topic: SHM Equation - Amplitude and Time Period
questions.explanation: Comparing x = 5sin(πt + π/3) with standard SHM equation x = A sin(ωt + φ): Amplitude A = 5 m, angular frequency ω = π rad/s, so time period T = 2π/ω = 2π/π = 2 s.

questions.text: A solid sphere is rotating freely about its symmetry axis in free space. The radius of the sphere is increased keeping its mass same. Which of the following physical quantities would remain constant for the sphere?
questions.topic: Conservation of angular momentum for a changing-radius spinning sphere
questions.explanation: In free space, with no external torque acting on the sphere, its angular momentum (L = Iω) remains conserved even as the radius (and hence moment of inertia) changes, causing a corresponding change in angular velocity.

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is:
questions.explanation: Moles of water = 4500 g / 18 g/mol = 250 mol. If intermolecular forces vanish, water molecules would behave as an ideal gas at STP, occupying volume = 250 mol x 22.4 L/mol = 5600 L = 5.6 m^3.

questions.text:
If c is the velocity of light in free space, the correct statements about photon among the following are:
A. The energy of a photon is E = hν.
B. The velocity of a photon is c.
C. The momentum of a photon, p = hν/c.
D. In a photon-electron collision, both total energy and total momentum are conserved.
E. Photon possesses positive charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation: A photon has energy E=hν (A, true), travels at velocity c (B, true), has momentum p=hν/c (C, true), and in photon-electron collisions both energy and momentum are conserved (D, true). A photon is chargeless/neutral, not positively charged (E, false). So A, B, C and D only.

questions.text: When a disc rotates with uniform angular velocity, which of the following is not true?
options: The sense of rotation remains same.
The orientation of the axis of rotation remains same.
The speed of rotation is non-zero and remains same.
The angular acceleration is non-zero and remains same.
questions.explanation: Uniform angular velocity means ω is constant, so angular acceleration (rate of change of ω) must be zero, not non-zero. Statement (d) is therefore not true.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only.
Statement II: Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge q, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, q.
In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because Idl is actually a vector source and charge q is a scalar source — this is reversed in the statement.

questions.text: A horizontal bridge is built across a river. A student standing on the bridge throws a small ball vertically upwards with a velocity 4 ms^-1. The ball strikes the water surface after 4s. The height of bridge above water surface is (Take g=10 ms^-2):

Match List-I with List-II: List-I: (a) Gravitational constant (G) (b) Gravitational potential energy (c) Gravitational potential (d) Gravitational intensity -- List-II: (i) [L^2T^-2] (ii) [M^-1L^3T^-2] (iii) [LT^-2] (iv) [ML^2T^-2]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: G has dimensional formula [M^-1L^3T^-2] (ii). Gravitational PE has formula [ML^2T^-2] (iv). Gravitational potential (PE per unit mass) has formula [L^2T^-2] (i). Gravitational intensity (force per unit mass) has formula [LT^-2] (iii). So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

questions.text: Light with an energy flux of 20 W/cm² falls on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence. If the surface has an area of 30 cm², the total momentum delivered to the surface (assuming complete absorption) during 30 minutes is
questions.explanation: Total energy absorbed U = flux × area × time = 20 × 30 × 1800 = 1.08×10⁶ J. For complete absorption, momentum p = U/c = 1.08×10⁶ / (3×10⁸) = 3.6×10⁻³ = 36×10⁻⁴ kg·m/s.

questions.text: A capacitor is charged by a battery. The battery is removed and another identical uncharged capacitor is connected in parallel. The total electrostatic energy of resulting system:
questions.topic: Capacitors connected in parallel; energy stored
questions.explanation: Charge Q is shared equally between the two identical capacitors (charge conserved), so each gets Q/2. Final energy = 2×(Q/2)²/(2C) = Q²/(4C), which is half the initial energy Q²/(2C). So energy decreases by a factor of 2.

questions.text: An iron rod of susceptibility 599 is subjected to a magnetising field of 1200 A/m. The permeability of the material of the rod is: (μ0=4π×10^-7 T m A^-1)
questions.explanation: Relative permeability μr = 1+χ = 1+599 = 600. Permeability μ = μ0×μr = 4π×10^-7×600 = 2400π×10^-7 = 2.4π×10^-4 T m A^-1.

questions.text: A bullet from a gun is fired on a rectangular wooden block with velocity u. When bullet travels 24 cm through the block along its length horizontally, velocity of bullet becomes u/3. Then its further penetrates into the block in the same direction before coming to rest exactly at the other end of the block. The total length of the block is:
questions.explanation: Using v²=u²-2a(2×24): (u/3)²=u²-48a, giving a=u²/54. The block ends when v=0: 0=u²-2a·d, so d=u²/(2a)=u²/(2×u²/54)=27cm.

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10H, capacitance 10 μF, resistance 50 Ω is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200 sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is ν₀ and the frequency of the ac source is ν then:
questions.explanation: Resonant frequency ν₀ = 1/(2π√LC) = 1/(2π√(10×10⁻⁵)) = 1/(2π×10⁻²) = 100/2π = 50/π Hz. Comparing V=V₀sinωt with ω=100: ν = ω/2π = 100/2π = 50/π Hz. So ν₀ = ν = 50/π Hz.

questions.text: A physical quantity P is related to four observations a,b,c and d as follows: P = a³b²/(c√d). The percentage errors of measurement in a,b,c and d are 1%, 3%, 2% and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity P is -

Two cars moving in opposite directions approach each other with speed of 22 m/s and 16.5 m/s respectively. The driver of the first car blows a horn having a frequency 400 Hz. The frequency heard by the driver of the second car is [velocity of sound 340 m/s]:
questions.explanation: Apparent frequency f' = f×(v+v_observer)/(v-v_source) = 400×(340+16.5)/(340-22) = 400×356.5/318 ≈ 448 Hz.

questions.text: A horizontal force 10 N is applied to a block A as shown in figure. The mass of blocks A and B are 2 kg and 3 kg, respectively. The blocks slide over a frictionless surface. The force exerted by block A on block B is: [Figure: F=10N applied to block A (2kg) pushing block B (3kg), both on frictionless surface]
questions.explanation: Common acceleration a = F/m = 10/5 = 2 m/s². Force on B from A: N = m_B × a = 3 × 2 = 6 N.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 39 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Unpolarised light is incident from air on a plane surface of a material of refractive index 'μ'. At a particular angle of incidence 'i', it is found that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. Which of the following options is correct for this situation?
options: Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector parallel to the plane of incidence
Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector perpendicular to the plane of incidence
questions.explanation: This is Brewster's angle condition. At this angle, the reflected ray is completely plane polarised, with its electric vector oscillating perpendicular to the plane of incidence (tan i = μ gives the angle, not the polarisation direction option here).

questions.text: A ball of mass 0.15 kg is dropped from a height 10m, strikes the ground and rebounds to the same height. The magnitude of impulse imparted to the ball is (g = 10 m/s²) nearly:

A student measured the diameter of a small steel ball using a screw gauge of least count 0.001 cm. The main scale reading is 5 mm and zero of circular scale division coincides with 25 divisions above the reference level. If screw gauge has a zero error of -0.004 cm, the correct diameter of the ball is
questions.topic: Screw gauge measurement with zero error
questions.explanation: Reading = Main scale + (circular scale division × least count) = 0.5cm + (25×0.001cm) = 0.525cm. Correct reading = observed reading - zero error = 0.525 - (-0.004) = 0.529 cm.

questions.text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of V volt. If the de Broglie wavelength of the electron is 1.227×10^-2 nm, the potential difference is:
questions.explanation: Using λ = 1.227/√V nm (standard formula with V in volts, λ in nm): 1.227×10^-2 = 1.227/√V, so √V = 100, V = 10^4 V.

questions.text: A ray of light with wavelength λ is incident on three different photo-electric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelengths of these photo-electric cells are λ₁, λ₂, and λ₃ respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are V₁, V₂ and V₃ respectively. The relation between λ and threshold wavelengths are λ₁ < λ, λ₂ > λ and λ₃ >> λ. The correct option is:
questions.topic: Photoelectric Effect - Threshold Wavelength and Stopping Potential
questions.explanation: Photoemission occurs only when the incident wavelength is less than the threshold wavelength (λ < λ_threshold), i.e., photon energy exceeds the work function. For cell 1: λ₁ < λ means the threshold wavelength is smaller than incident wavelength, so no photoemission occurs and V₁ = 0. For cell 2: λ₂ > λ, so photoemission occurs with some stopping potential V₂ > 0. For cell 3: λ₃ >> λ, so the incident photon energy far exceeds the work function, giving a much larger stopping potential V₃ >> V₂ > 0. Hence V₁ = 0 and V₂ < V₃.

questions.text: A rigid ball of mass m strikes a rigid wall at 60° and gets reflected without loss of speed as shown in the figure (incoming and outgoing velocity V each making 60° with the wall's normal/horizontal). The value of impulse imparted by the wall on the ball will be:
questions.explanation: Only the component of velocity perpendicular to the wall reverses; components parallel to the wall cancel. Change in momentum (impulse) = 2mV cos60° = 2mV×(1/2) = mV.

questions.text: An electron falls from rest through a vertical distance h in a uniform and vertically upward directed electric field E. The direction of electric field is now reversed, keeping its magnitude the same. A proton is allowed to fall from rest in it through the same vertical distance h. The time of fall of the electron, in comparison to the time of fall of the proton, is
questions.topic: Electron and proton falling under a reversed electric field
questions.explanation: Since the electron has a much smaller mass than the proton, the acceleration a=eE/m experienced by the electron under the same force is much larger, so the electron falls through the same distance h in a much smaller time compared to the proton.

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 microF, resistance 50 ohm is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is v0 and the frequency of the ac source is v, then:
questions.explanation: Resonant angular frequency omega0 = 1/sqrt(LC) = 1/sqrt(10 x 10x10^-6) = 1/sqrt(10^-4) = 100 rad/s, so v0 = 100/(2*pi) = 50/pi Hz. From V=200sin(100t), omega=100 rad/s, so v = 100/(2*pi) = 50/pi Hz. Hence v0 = v = 50/pi Hz.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Atoms are electrically neutral as they contain equal number of positive and negative charges.
Statement II: Atoms of each element are stable and emit their characteristic spectrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.topic: Atomic Neutrality and Stability of Atoms
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct - atoms are electrically neutral due to equal numbers of protons and electrons, and stable atoms of each element emit a characteristic line spectrum.

questions.text: Which of the following measurements require 'index correction'?
options: Measurement of gravitational acceleration using simple pendulum
Measurement of focal length of lenses using optical bench
Measurement of speed of sound using resonance tube
Measurement of resistance of a wire using meter bridge
questions.explanation: Index correction (also called the index error or bench error correction) is applied in optical bench experiments for determining the focal length of lenses/mirrors, because the index needles (pointers) used to locate positions on the bench do not exactly coincide with the optical centre of the lens, introducing a systematic offset that must be corrected for.

questions.text: Let T1 and T2 be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T1:T2 is:
questions.topic: Bohr Model - Energy of Excited States
questions.explanation: Energy in nth state E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV. First excited state is n=2, second excited state is n=3. T1:T2 = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4.

questions.text: A body of mass 60g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is:

A tuning fork is used to produce resonance in a glass tube. The length of the air column in this tube can be adjusted by a variable piston. At room temperature of 27°C two successive resonances are produced at 20 cm and 73 cm of column length. If the frequency of the tuning fork is 320 Hz, the velocity of sound in air at 27°C is
questions.topic: Resonance tube experiment: finding velocity of sound
questions.explanation: The distance between two successive resonances equals half the wavelength: λ/2 = 73-20 = 53 cm, so λ = 106 cm = 1.06 m. Velocity v = fλ = 320×1.06 ≈ 339 m/s.

questions.text: A mass m is attached to a thin wire and whirled in a vertical circle. The wire is most likely to break when:
options: the mass is at the lowest point
inclined at an angle of 60 degrees from vertical
the mass is at the highest point
questions.explanation: At the lowest point of the vertical circle, tension T = mu^2/l + mg is maximum (both the centripetal force requirement and gravity act in the same direction relative to tension), making the wire most likely to break there.

questions.text: Consider that an electron is revolving in an excited state of a Hydrogen atom with velocity √25.6 × 10⁵ ms⁻¹. The radius of the orbit is x × 10⁻⁹ m. The value of x is: [Take the mass of electron to be 9×10⁻³¹ kg, charge of electron = −1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C and 1/(4πε₀) = 9×10⁹ N m² C⁻²]
questions.explanation: For a circular Bohr orbit, the Coulomb force provides centripetal force: ke²/r² = mv²/r, so r = ke²/(mv²). Here v² = 25.6×10¹⁰ = 2.56×10¹¹ (ms⁻¹)². ke² = 9×10⁹ × (1.6×10⁻¹⁹)² = 9×10⁹×2.56×10⁻³⁸ = 2.304×10⁻²⁸. mv² = 9×10⁻³¹×2.56×10¹¹ = 2.304×10⁻¹⁹. r = 2.304×10⁻²⁸/2.304×10⁻¹⁹ = 1×10⁻⁹ m. So x = 1.

questions.text: A potentiometer is an accurate and versatile device to make electrical measurements of E.M.F. because the method involves:
options: a condition of no current flow through the galvanometer
a combination of cells, galvanometer and resistances
questions.explanation: The potentiometer measures EMF at the null point, where no current flows through the galvanometer branch, so it does not draw any current from the source being measured, making the measurement highly accurate.

questions.text: In a cyclotron, a charged particle
options: speeds up between the dees because of the magnetic field.
speeds up only while inside a dee.
slows down within a dee and speeds up only between the dees.
questions.explanation: Inside the dees, the magnetic field only changes the particle's direction (circular motion at constant speed), so technically its velocity direction is continuously changing — meaning it undergoes acceleration (centripetal) throughout its motion; additionally, it gains speed each time it crosses the gap between the dees due to the oscillating electric field, so acceleration (in the broad sense of changing velocity) occurs all the time.

questions.text: A spring of force constant k is cut into lengths of ratio 1:2:3. They are connected in series and the new force constant is k'. Then they are connected in parallel and force constant is k''. Then k':k'' is:
questions.explanation: Pieces have constants 6k, 3k, 2k (force constant ∝ 1/length for pieces 1,2,3 units of a 6-unit spring). Series: 1/k' = 1/6k+1/3k+1/2k = (1+2+3)/6k = 1/k, so k'=k. Parallel: k'' = 6k+3k+2k = 11k. Ratio k':k'' = k:11k = 1:11.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: Na-22 (atomic number 11) -> X + e+ + neutrino
questions.explanation: In positron (e+) emission, a proton converts to a neutron, so the atomic number decreases by 1 while mass number stays the same. Na-22 (Z=11) becomes Ne-22 (Z=10).

questions.text: In a double slit experiment, when light of wavelength 400 nm was used, the angular width of the first minima formed on a screen placed 1 m away, was found to be 0.2 degrees. What will be the angular width of the first minima, if the entire experimental apparatus is immersed in water? (mu_water = 4/3)
questions.explanation: Angular width is proportional to wavelength. In water, wavelength changes to lambda' = lambda/mu = (3/4)*lambda. New angular width = 0.2 x (3/4) = 0.15 degrees.

questions.text: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a highly viscous liquid. Among curves A, B, C, D shown in a v-t graph (where A rises slowly and stays low, B rises and levels off to a constant terminal value, C and D show other increasing/peaking patterns), the curve which represents the speed of the ball (v) as a function of time (t) is:
questions.explanation: When a ball falls through a highly viscous liquid, it accelerates initially due to gravity, but as viscous drag force increases with speed, the net force decreases until it reaches zero at terminal velocity, after which speed remains constant. This matches curve B, which rises and then levels off to a constant (terminal) value.

questions.text: Two particles A and B are moving in uniform circular motion in concentric circles of radii rA and rB with speeds VA and VB respectively. Their time period of rotation is the same. The ratio of angular speed of A to that of B will be:
questions.explanation: Angular speed omega = 2*pi/T. Since both particles have the same time period T, their angular speeds are equal, giving a ratio of 1:1.

questions.text: In the product F=q(v×B)=q[v×(Bî+Bĵ+B0k̂)]. For q=1 and v=2î+4ĵ+6k̂ and F=4î-20ĵ+12k̂, what will be the complete expression for B?
questions.topic: Magnetic field components from Lorentz force equation
questions.explanation: Solving the cross product equation component-wise with the given v and F yields B=-6î-6ĵ-8k̂.

questions.text: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
questions.explanation: T is proportional to sqrt(L). T1/T2 = sqrt(121/100) = 11/10. They are back in phase when n2*T2 = n1*T1, i.e., n2/n1 = T1/T2 = 11/10. The minimum integers satisfying this are n2(shorter pendulum, faster)=11, n1(longer)=10.

questions.text: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance:
options: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
questions.explanation: For conductors, resistance increases with temperature due to increased lattice vibrations scattering electrons. For semiconductors, resistance decreases with temperature because more charge carriers become available as electrons gain energy to jump the band gap.

tests.title: JEE Main Physics Practice Test 40 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Physics practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The temperature of a gas is -50°C. To what temperature the gas should be heated so that the rms speed is increased by 3 times?
questions.explanation: V ∝ √T. Initial T1 = -50°C = 223 K. If rms speed increases 4 times (as shown in solution, 4V/V), then T2/T1 = 16, so T2 = 16 × 223 = 3568 K = 3568 - 273 = 3295°C.

questions.text: The displacement of a particle is represented by the equation y = t³ sin ωt. The motion is
questions.explanation: Here the 'amplitude' t³ itself grows with time rather than staying constant, so the motion never repeats itself identically — it is non-periodic.

questions.text: A unit positive point charge is taken slowly through an infinitesimally thin tube that is inside a charged dielectric sphere of radius R, having uniform positive charge density ρ. The initial and final positions of the charge are marked by A and B at distances 2R and 3R respectively, from the centre of the sphere. In this process, the magnitude of the total work done on the point charge is ρR²/(n∈₀). The value of n is: (∈₀ is the permittivity of vacuum)
questions.topic: Potential due to Uniformly Charged Sphere
questions.explanation: Both A (2R) and B (3R) lie outside the sphere (radius R), so the field there is the same as that of a point charge Q = (4/3)πR³ρ at the centre. Potential outside: V(r) = Q/(4π∈₀r) = ρR³/(3∈₀r). V(A) at r=2R: ρR²/(6∈₀). V(B) at r=3R: ρR²/(9∈₀). Work done on unit charge moving from A to B = q[V(B)-V(A)] = ρR²/(9∈₀) - ρR²/(6∈₀) = -ρR²/(18∈₀). Magnitude = ρR²/(18∈₀), so n = 18.

questions.text: A bicyclist comes to a skidding stop in 10 m. During this process, the force on the bicycle due to the road is 200N and is directly opposed to the motion. The work done by the cycle on the road is
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law, the cycle exerts an equal and opposite force on the road, but the road itself does not undergo any displacement — so the work done by the cycle on the road is zero.

questions.text: Radioactive material 'A' has decay constant '8λ' and material 'B' has decay constant 'λ'. Initially they have same number of nuclei. After what time, the ratio of number of nuclei of material 'B' to that 'A' will be 1/e?
questions.explanation: N_B/N_A = e^(-λt)/e^(-8λt) = e^(7λt). Setting this equal to 1/e gives e^(7λt) = e^(-1), so 7λt = -1, i.e. the ratio N_B/N_A = 1/e requires e^(-7λt)=1/e, so 7λt=1, t = 1/(7λ).

questions.text: Water waves produced by a motor boat sailing in water are
questions.explanation: Surface water waves involve water particles moving both up-and-down (transverse) and back-and-forth (longitudinal), tracing roughly circular/elliptical paths, so the wave is a combination of both types.

questions.text: As the temperature is increased, the time period of a pendulum
options: increases as its effective length increases even though its centre of mass still remains at the centre of the bob.
decreases as its effective length increases even though its centre of mass still remains at the centre of the bob.
increases as its effective length increases due to shifting of centre of mass below the centre of the bob.
decreases as its effective length remains same but the centre of mass shifts above the centre of the bob.
questions.explanation: Heating causes the pendulum's suspension to expand, increasing its effective length L. Since T=2π√(L/g), the time period increases as L increases, while the centre of mass remains at the bob's centre.

questions.text: A block of mass 10 kg is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius 1m. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inner wall of the cylinder is 0.1. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis, will be: (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: For the block to remain stationary, friction must balance gravity: mu*N = mg, where N = m*omega^2*r (centripetal force provides normal force). So mu*m*omega^2*r = mg, giving omega = sqrt(g/(mu*r)) = sqrt(10/(0.1x1)) = sqrt(100) = 10 rad/s.

questions.text: Two transparent media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s and 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is:
questions.topic: Critical Angle from Speed of Light in Media
questions.explanation: sin ic = μB/μA = (c/VB)/(c/VA) = VA/VB = 1.5×10⁸/2×10⁸ = 0.750. So ic = sin⁻¹(0.750).

questions.text: The minimum wavelength of X-rays produced by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of V volts is proportional to:
questions.explanation: The minimum wavelength of X-rays is given by λmin = hc/(eV), so λmin is proportional to 1/V.

questions.text: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that:
options: they travel with a speed equal to 1/√(μ0ε0)
they originate from charges moving with uniform speed
the energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field.
questions.topic: Properties of EM Waves in Free Space (NOT property)
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating (not uniformly moving) charges. A charge moving with uniform speed does not radiate EM waves. So option (2) is NOT a correct property of an EM wave.

questions.text: Average velocity of a particle executing SHM in one complete vibration is:
questions.explanation: Average velocity over one complete vibration = Total displacement / Total time = 0, since the particle returns to its starting position after one complete cycle.

questions.text: The ratio of the distances travelled by a freely falling body in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th second is:
questions.topic: Distance in nth Second - Free Fall
questions.explanation: Distance traveled in the nth second under constant acceleration (starting from rest) follows the pattern of consecutive odd numbers: 1:3:5:7, since distance in nth second = g(2n-1)/2.

questions.text: If ∮E·ds = 0 over a surface, then:
options: the magnitude of electric field on the surface is constant.
all the charges must necessarily be inside the surface.
the electric field inside the surface is necessarily uniform.
the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.
questions.explanation: If the net flux through a closed surface is zero, it means the number of field lines entering the surface equals the number leaving it, as per Gauss's law (net enclosed charge could also be zero, but this doesn't guarantee field uniformity or constant magnitude).

questions.text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is

A car starts from rest and accelerates at 5m/s². At t=4 s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at t=6 s? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Relative Motion / Projectile from Accelerating Frame
questions.explanation: At t=4s, car's velocity Vx = u+at = 0+5×4 = 20 m/s, which the ball retains horizontally (car's horizontal acceleration no longer acts on it once released). For next 2s (t=6s), ball falls freely: Vy = g×t = 10×2 = 20 m/s. Resultant V = √(20²+20²) = 20√2 m/s, and acceleration is just g = 10 m/s² (only gravity acts after release).

questions.text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
In a Young's double slit experiment, the source is white light. One of the slits is covered by a red filter and the other by a blue filter. In this case,
options: there shall be alternate interference patterns of red and blue.
there shall be an interference pattern for red distinct from that for blue.
there shall be no interference fringes.
there shall be an interference pattern for red mixing with one for blue.
questions.explanation: Interference requires two coherent sources of the same wavelength with a fixed phase relationship. Here the two slits transmit light of different wavelengths (red and blue), which are inherently incoherent with each other, so no stable, observable interference pattern can form at all.

questions.text: Let T1 and T2 be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T1 : T2 is
questions.explanation: First excited state n=2, second excited state n=3. E ∝ 1/n². T1:T2 = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4.

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity at a height 1 km above the earth is the same as at a depth d below the surface of earth. Then:
questions.topic: Variation of g with height and depth
questions.explanation: g_height = g(1−2h/R), g_depth = g(1−d/R). Equating: 2h = d ⟹ d = 2×1km = 2 km.

questions.text: The power radiated by a black body is P and it radiates maximum energy at wavelength, λ0. If the temperature of the black body is now changed so that it radiates maximum energy at wavelength (3/4)λ0, the power radiated by it becomes nP. The value of n is
questions.topic: Stefan-Boltzmann law: power radiated at a different wavelength of maximum emission
questions.explanation: By Wien's law, λmT = constant, so T ∝ 1/λm. New temperature T' = T×(4/3) (since λ' = (3/4)λ0). By Stefan's law, P ∝ T⁴, so n = (T'/T)⁴ = (4/3)⁴ = 256/81.

questions.text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 ohm is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux = B x A = 0.5 x (1x1) = 0.5 Wb (since the plane is perpendicular to the field, the area vector is parallel to B).

questions.text: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity v1 while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is v2. The ratio v1:v2 is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum: mv1 + 0 = (m+m)v2, so mv1 = 2mv2, giving v1/v2 = 2/1, i.e., v1:v2 = 2:1.

questions.text: In a metre bridge experiment, the positions of the cell E and galvanometer G are interchanged. We shall observe in the galvanometer:
options: There will be no deflection irrespective of the position of the jockey
Both right-sided and left-sided deflection, and at balance point, no deflection
questions.topic: Meter bridge, interchanging cell and galvanometer
questions.explanation: By reciprocity of a Wheatstone bridge, interchanging cell and galvanometer leaves the balance condition unchanged; deflection on either side is possible away from balance, and none at balance.

questions.text: A solid cylinder of mass 2kg and radius 4cm is rotating about its axis at the rate of 3rpm. The torque required to stop it after 2*pi revolutions is:
questions.explanation: omega_i = 2*pi*(3)/60 = pi/10 rad/s. Moment of inertia I = mr^2/2 = 2x(0.04)^2/2 = 16x10^-4 kg.m^2. Using alpha = omega_i^2/(2*theta) with theta=2*pi(2*pi)=4*pi^2, alpha = (pi^2/100)/(8*pi^2) = 100/800 rad/s^2. Torque = I*alpha = 16x10^-4 x (100/800) = 2x10^-6 N.m.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 1 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2 + HBr, (C6H5CO)2O2 [peroxide]
questions.topic: Major product of alkene with HBr (peroxide effect)
questions.explanation: In presence of peroxide, HBr adds via anti-Markovnikov (Kharasch effect), giving Br on the terminal carbon: (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-Br.

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction, showing a horizontal line y vs x at constant temperature T. The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are:
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t-half)
questions.topic: Zero and First Order Reaction Graphs
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, rate is constant regardless of concentration, so plotting rate (y) vs concentration (x) gives a horizontal line. For a first order reaction, the half-life (t-half) is independent of initial concentration, so plotting t-half (y) vs concentration (x) also gives a horizontal line.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: a hexane chain with Cl on C2, a methyl branch on C3, OH on C4 (counting to give lowest locants), and Br on C6 (terminal carbon): CH3-CHCl-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-Br
questions.explanation: Numbering from the end nearer to the OH group (principal characteristic group, suffix -ol gets lowest locant) and naming substituents alphabetically (bromo, chloro, methyl): 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: Heating NaCl with concentrated H2SO4 and MnO2 results in oxidation of Mn.
Statement-II: Heating NaI with concentrated H2SO4 and MnO2 results in reduction of Mn.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
questions.topic: Oxidizing Action of MnO2 with Halide Salts and Conc. H2SO4
questions.explanation: In both reactions, NaX + H2SO4 generates HX, which is then oxidized to X2 by MnO2; in this process MnO2 acts as the oxidizing agent and Mn is itself REDUCED from +4 to +2 (not oxidized). So Statement-I, which claims 'oxidation of Mn', is incorrect. Statement-II correctly states that heating NaI with conc. H2SO4 and MnO2 results in reduction of Mn (as MnO2 oxidizes I⁻ to I2), which is correct. So Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state. Statement II: Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: benzenediazonium salt is indeed prepared from aniline + NaNO2/HCl at 273-278K and is unstable/decomposes in dry form; and direct iodination of benzene is difficult, so iodobenzene is made via the Sandmeyer-type reaction of the diazonium salt with KI.

questions.text: The right option for the statement 'Tyndall effect is exhibited by', is:
questions.topic: Identifying a colloid that shows the Tyndall effect
