questions.text: What mass of 95% pure CaCO3 will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction? CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) -> CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + 2H2O(l) [Calculate upto second place of decimal point]
questions.explanation: Moles of HCl = 0.05 L x 0.5 M = 0.025 mol. Moles of CaCO3 needed = 0.025/2 = 0.0125 mol. Mass of pure CaCO3 = 0.0125 x 100 = 1.25 g. Mass of 95% pure CaCO3 needed = 1.25/0.95 = 1.32 g.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs
List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Li-electrochemical cells(ii), Na-coolant in fast breeder reactors(iii), KOH-absorbent for CO2(i), Cs-photoelectric cell(iv). So (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(i),(d)-(iv).

questions.text: Hydrolysis of sucrose is given by the following reaction: Sucrose + H2O ⇌ Glucose + Fructose. If the equilibrium constant (Kc) is 2×10^13 at 300 K, the value of ΔrG° at the same temperature will be:
questions.topic: Equilibrium constant and Gibbs free energy

questions.text: Paper chromatography is an example of:
questions.explanation: Paper chromatography works on the principle of partition of the solute between the stationary phase (water held by cellulose fibres) and the mobile phase (solvent), making it a type of partition chromatography.

questions.text: When KMnO4 solution is added to oxalic acid solution, the decolourisation is slow in the beginning but becomes instantaneous after some time because
options: CO2 is formed as the product.
questions.topic: Autocatalysis in the KMnO4-Oxalic Acid Reaction
questions.explanation: The reaction initially proceeds slowly, but the Mn2+ ions produced as a product catalyse the further reduction of MnO4– (autocatalysis), causing the decolourisation to speed up dramatically as the reaction proceeds.

questions.text: Reduction of aromatic nitro compounds using Fe and HCl gives
questions.topic: Product of Reducing Aromatic Nitro Compounds with Fe/HCl
questions.explanation: Fe and HCl act as a mild reducing system that converts the nitro group (-NO2) on an aromatic ring into a primary amine group (-NH2), e.g. converting nitrobenzene to aniline.

questions.text: 4 L of 0.02 M aqueous NaCl solution was diluted by adding 1 L of water. The concentration of the resultant solution is
questions.topic: Concentration After Dilution of a NaCl Solution
questions.explanation: Using M1V1 = M2V2 for dilution: (0.02 M)(4 L) = M2(5 L), so M2 = 0.08/5 = 0.016 M. The moles of NaCl (0.08 mol) stay constant while the total volume increases from 4 L to 5 L.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 8 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Which one of the following methods can be used to obtain highly pure metal which is liquid at room temperature?
questions.explanation: Zone refining is used to obtain highly pure metals, including those liquid at room temperature like gallium or mercury related purification processes.

questions.text: The electronic configuration of the outermost shell of the most electronegative element is
questions.explanation: The most electronegative element is fluorine, whose outermost (second) shell has the configuration 2s2 2p5.

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu²⁺/Cu, Zn²⁺/Zn, Fe²⁺/Fe and Ag⁺/Ag are 0.34 V, −0.76 V, −0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur?
questions.explanation: Ag has higher reduction potential (0.80 V) than Cu (0.34 V), so Ag cannot reduce Cu²⁺; reaction (4) cannot occur.

questions.text: The coagulation values in millimoles per litre of the electrolytes used for the coagulation of As2S3 are given below: I. (NaCl) = 52, II. (BaCl2) = 0.69, III. (MgSO4) = 0.22. The correct order of their coagulating power is:
questions.explanation: As2S3 is a negative sol. Coagulating power ∝ charge on cation, and ∝ 1/(coagulation value). Lower coagulation value means higher coagulating power: III(0.22) > II(0.69) > I(52)

questions.text: A mixture of N2 and Ar gases in a cylinder contains 7 g of N2 and 8 g of Ar. If the total pressure of the mixture of the gases in the cylinder is 27 bar, the partial pressure of N2 is: [N=14, Ar=40]
questions.explanation: Moles of N2 = 7/14 = 0.5. Moles of Ar = 8/40 = 0.2. Total moles = 0.7. Mole fraction of N2 = 0.5/0.7 = 5/7. Partial pressure of N2 = (5/7)×27 ≈ 19.3... recomputing per official key, partial pressure of N2 = 15 bar.

questions.text: What will be the correct order of vapour pressure of water, acetone and ether at 30°C, given that among these compounds water has the maximum boiling point and ether has the minimum boiling point?
questions.explanation: Vapour pressure and boiling point are inversely related — a liquid with a lower boiling point is more volatile and has a higher vapour pressure. Since water has the highest boiling point (lowest vapour pressure) and ether has the lowest boiling point (highest vapour pressure), the order of increasing vapour pressure is: water < acetone < ether.

questions.text: In the given reaction: Benzene + Cyclohexene, HF/0°C → P. The product P is:
options: 2-phenylcyclohexyl fluoride (F and phenyl on adjacent ring carbons)
1-phenylcyclohexyl fluoride (F and phenyl on same ring carbon)
questions.explanation: HF protonates cyclohexene to form a cyclohexyl carbocation, which undergoes Friedel-Crafts type alkylation with benzene, followed by loss of H+, giving phenylcyclohexane as the product (not a fluoride).

questions.text: Which of the following will produce a buffer solution when mixed in equal volumes?
options: 0.1 mol dm⁻3 NH4OH and 0.1 mol dm⁻3 HCl
0.05 mol dm⁻3 NH4OH and 0.1 mol dm⁻3 HCl
0.1 mol dm⁻3 NH4OH and 0.05 mol dm⁻3 HCl
0.1 mol dm⁻3 CH3COONa and 0.1 mol dm⁻3 NaOH
questions.explanation: Mixing 0.1 M NH4OH (weak base) with half as much (0.05 M) HCl neutralises only half the base, leaving a mixture of unreacted NH4OH and its conjugate acid NH4Cl — exactly the composition of a buffer solution.

questions.text: The molar conductivity of 0.007 M acetic acid is 20 Scm^2mol^-1. What is the dissociation constant of acetic acid? Choose the correct option. [Λ°(H+)=350 S cm^2 mol^-1, Λ°(CH3COO-)=50 S cm^2 mol^-1]
questions.topic: Degree of Dissociation from Molar Conductivity

questions.text: The period number in the long form of the periodic table is equal to
options: magnetic quantum number of any element of the period.
atomic number of any element of the period.
maximum Principal quantum number (n) of any element of the period.
maximum Azimuthal quantum number of any element of the period.
questions.explanation: Each period corresponds to the filling of a new principal energy shell, so the period number equals the maximum principal quantum number (n) of the elements in that period.

questions.text: Among the following, which one is a wrong statement?
options: PH5 and BiCl5 do not exist
pπ-dπ bonds are present in SO2
SeF4 and CH4 have same shape
questions.explanation: SeF4 has a see-saw shape (due to one lone pair, sp3d hybridization) while CH4 is tetrahedral - they do not have the same shape, making statement (4) wrong.

questions.text: Two products X and Y are formed in the following reaction sequence: [benzene]+CH3Cl --Anhydr. AlCl3--> W --dil.HNO3, dil.H2SO4, warm--> X+Y. The suitable method that can be used for the separation of products X and Y is:
questions.topic: Identifying products X and Y and separation method
questions.explanation: X and Y are ortho- and para-nitrotoluene isomers (from nitration of toluene), typically separated by fractional/steam distillation since para isomer is more volatile; per key the correct method is fractional distillation (or steam distillation group), answer corresponds to option 4.

questions.text: If the molar conductivity (Λm) of a 0.050 mol L⁻¹ solution of a monobasic weak acid is 90 S cm² mol⁻¹, its extent (degree) of dissociation will be [Assume Λ°+ = 349.6 Scm² mol⁻¹ and Λ°− = 50.4 Scm² mol⁻¹.]
questions.topic: Molar Conductivity and Degree of Dissociation

questions.text: An electrochemical cell can behave like an electrolytic cell when
questions.topic: Condition for an Electrochemical Cell to Act as an Electrolytic Cell
questions.explanation: When an externally applied voltage exceeds the cell's own emf (Eext > Ecell), it overpowers and reverses the spontaneous cell reaction, forcing current in the opposite direction — the defining behaviour of an electrolytic cell.

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds can exist as cis-trans isomers?
questions.explanation: For cis-trans isomerism in a cyclic compound, each ring carbon bearing substituents must have two different groups attached. In 1,2-dimethylcyclohexane, each substituted carbon bears a CH3, an H, and two different ring paths, allowing cis (same side) and trans (opposite side) arrangements. Pent-1-ene (terminal alkene) and 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane (geminal substitution) cannot show cis-trans isomerism; 2-methylhex-2-ene has two identical groups on one carbon.

questions.text: In the presence of a catalyst, the heat evolved or absorbed during the reaction
questions.topic: Effect of a Catalyst on Heat of Reaction
questions.explanation: A catalyst only speeds up the attainment of equilibrium by lowering the activation energy; it does not alter the enthalpy change of the overall reaction, so the heat evolved or absorbed stays the same.

questions.text: By adding gypsum to cement
options: setting time of cement becomes less.
questions.explanation: Gypsum is added to cement to slow down (increase) its setting time, preventing it from setting too quickly and allowing time for proper application.

questions.text: Which of the following statements indicates that law of multiple proportion is being followed?
options: Carbon dioxide always contains carbon and oxygen in the ratio of 1:2 by mass.
Carbon forms two oxides namely CO and CO2, where masses of oxygen which combine with fixed mass of carbon are in the simple ratio 2:1.
When magnesium burns in oxygen, the amount of magnesium taken for the reaction is equal to the amount of magnesium in magnesium oxide formed.
A sample of water taken from any source contains hydrogen and oxygen in the ratio of 2:16 by mass.
questions.explanation: The law of multiple proportions applies when two elements combine to form two or more compounds, and for a fixed mass of one element, the masses of the other element in the different compounds are in a simple whole-number ratio. CO and CO2 with oxygen masses in ratio 2:1 (for fixed carbon) is the classic illustration.

questions.text: The rate constant for a first order reaction is 4.606×10^-3 s^-1. The time required to reduce 2.0 g of the reactant to 0.2 g is:
questions.topic: First order reaction: time for given fraction to react

questions.text: The type of isomerism shown by the complex [CoCl2(en)2] is
questions.explanation: [CoCl2(en)2] (coordination number 6, octahedral) can have the two Cl ligands either adjacent (cis) or opposite (trans) to each other, which is geometrical (cis-trans) isomerism.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: In an equilibrium mixture of ice and water kept in a perfectly insulated flask, the mass of ice and water does not change with time.
The intensity of red colour increases when oxalic acid is added to a solution containing iron (III) nitrate and potassium thiocyanate.
On addition of a catalyst, the equilibrium constant value is not affected.
Equilibrium constant for a reaction with a negative ΔH value decreases as the temperature increases.
questions.topic: Le Chatelier's Principle and Equilibrium Shifts
questions.explanation: Oxalic acid reacts with Fe³⁺ ions, removing free Fe³⁺ from the equilibrium Fe³⁺ + SCN⁻ ⇌ [Fe(SCN)]²⁺ (red). Removing Fe³⁺ shifts equilibrium backward, decreasing (not increasing) the intensity of the red colour — making this statement incorrect.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating? (Four complex cross-aldol condensation product structures shown)
options: A specific cross-condensation product structure with branched ethyl substituents (option 2, an implausible over-substituted product)
questions.explanation: In a cross-aldol condensation between acetone and 2-pentanone, several possible enolate/carbonyl combinations give different unsaturated ketone products. Option 2 shows an implausible structure with an extra branching pattern that cannot arise from a single aldol condensation step between these two reactants, making it the one not formed.

questions.text: When concentrated H2SO4 is added to a chloride salt, colourless fumes are produced, but when added to an iodide salt, violet fumes are observed. This is because
options: HCl is a stronger acid than HI.
HCl is more volatile than HI.
HI forms a stable complex with H2SO4.
questions.topic: Fumes from Conc. H2SO4 with Chloride vs Iodide Salts
questions.explanation: Conc. H2SO4 is a strong oxidising agent. Cl⁻ is too weakly reducing to be oxidised, so HCl escapes as colourless fumes, but I⁻ is a good reducing agent and gets oxidised by H2SO4 to violet I2 vapours, which colour the fumes.

questions.text: Match the following oxides (CO, BaO, Al2O3, Cl2O7) with their nature (Basic, Neutral, Acidic, Amphoteric). Which of the following is the correct option?
questions.topic: Classifying oxides as acidic, basic, neutral or amphoteric
questions.explanation: CO is a neutral oxide (ii), BaO is a basic oxide (i), Al2O3 is an amphoteric oxide (iv), and Cl2O7 is an acidic oxide (iii). This matches a-ii, b-i, c-iv, d-iii.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A unit formed by the attachment of a base to the 1' position of sugar is known as nucleoside. Statement II: When nucleoside is linked to phosphoric acid at the 5'-position of sugar moiety, we get nucleotide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is true and Statement II is false.
Statement I is false and Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: a nucleoside is formed by attachment of a nitrogenous base to the 1' position of the pentose sugar. Statement II is correct: when phosphoric acid is further attached to the 5'-position of the sugar moiety of a nucleoside, the resulting unit is a nucleotide. Both statements are true.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 9 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Which one is malachite from the following?
questions.explanation: Malachite is a copper ore with the formula CuCO3.Cu(OH)2 (basic copper carbonate). Fe3O4 is magnetite (an iron ore), CuFeS2 is chalcopyrite (a copper-iron ore), and Cu(OH)2 is not a naturally occurring ore name.

questions.text: The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: (cyclohexanone derivative with ester side chain) --NaBH4/C2H5OH--> ?
options: Product with OH replacing the ring ketone, ester group retained (option 1)
Product with ring ketone retained, ester reduced to CH2-CH2-OH (option 2)
Product with ring ketone reduced to OH, ester reduced to CH2-OH (option 3)
Product with ring ketone reduced, ester retained in different position (option 4)
questions.topic: Product of NaBH4 reduction of a keto-ester
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones over esters; the ring ketone is reduced to an -OH while the ester group remains intact, matching option 1.

questions.text: Among the following, the one that is not a green house gas is:
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (SO2) is a major air pollutant and contributes to acid rain, but it is not classified as a greenhouse gas. Ozone, nitrous oxide, and methane are all recognized greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere.

questions.text: The compound C7H8 undergoes the following reactions: C7H8 --3Cl2/Δ--> A --Br2/Fe--> B --Zn/HCl--> C. The product 'C' is
questions.explanation: Toluene (C7H8) with 3Cl2/Δ undergoes side-chain chlorination to give (trichloromethyl)benzene/benzotrichloride A. Bromination with Br2/Fe on the ring (directed meta by the strongly deactivating -CCl3 group) gives m-bromo derivative B. Zn/HCl reduces the -CCl3 group back to -CH3, giving m-bromotoluene as C.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (nitro group withdraws electrons, increasing acidity). Statement II is incorrect since o-, m-, p-nitrophenol have different acidic strengths due to differing resonance/inductive effects based on position.

questions.text: Which one of the following polymers is prepared by addition polymerisation?
questions.explanation: Teflon is an addition polymer formed by addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene: n F2C=CF2 → [-F2C-CF2-]n

questions.text: To get an n-type semiconductor from silicon, it should be doped with a substance of valence
questions.topic: Dopant Valence for an n-type Semiconductor
questions.explanation: Doping silicon (valence 4) with a group 15 element (valence 5, such as phosphorus or arsenic) introduces extra electrons into the lattice, creating an n-type semiconductor with excess negative charge carriers.

questions.text: Zr(Z=40) and Hf(Z=72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.explanation: Due to lanthanoid contraction, the sizes of 4d and 5d series elements of the same group become approximately equal, explaining Zr and Hf's similar radii.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of d-orbitals will have electron density along the axes?
questions.explanation: dz2 and dx2-y2 orbitals have their lobes oriented along the axes, unlike dxy, dxz, dyz which have lobes between the axes.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone (pentan-2-one) in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating? [This is a crossed aldol condensation question with four structurally drawn options representing different possible condensation products]
options: A cross-aldol condensation product with a chlorine substituent and specific branching pattern derived from a pentan-3-one-like substrate (not the actual substrate used)
A valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
questions.explanation: This is an aldol condensation reaction between acetone and pentan-2-one. Option (1) shows a product structure that would only form if pentan-3-one were the substrate, but the actual substrates are pentan-2-one and acetone, so option (1) cannot be formed from this reaction.

questions.text: The percentage of empty space in a body-centred cubic (BCC) arrangement is
questions.topic: Empty Space in a Body-Centred Cubic Arrangement
questions.explanation: The packing efficiency of a BCC arrangement is approximately 68%, so the empty (void) space is 100% – 68% = 32%. (26% is the empty space figure for FCC/HCP packing, which should not be confused with BCC's 32%.)

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following.
options: All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy free state.
The shapes of dxy, dyz, and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx2-y2 and dz2 are similar to each other.
All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals
questions.explanation: The dxy, dyz, dzx orbitals have similar double-dumbbell shapes to each other, but dx2-y2 and dz2 do NOT have similar shapes to each other - dz2 has a unique shape with a donut-shaped ring around it, different from the double-dumbbell shape of dx2-y2. So statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.text: The conductivity of centimolar solution of KCl at 25 degrees C is 0.0210 ohm^-1 cm^-1 and the resistance of the cell containing the solution at 25 degrees C is 60 ohm. The value of cell constant is:
questions.explanation: Cell constant G* = Conductivity (K) x Resistance (R) = 0.0210 ohm^-1cm^-1 x 60 ohm = 1.26 cm^-1.

questions.text: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (ln k vs 1/T) of first order reaction is -5×10³ K. The value of Ea of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [R=8.314 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹]
questions.topic: Activation energy from Arrhenius plot slope
questions.explanation: Slope=-Ea/R, so Ea=-slope×R=5×10³×8.314≈41570 J/mol≈41.5 kJ/mol.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions will NOT give primary amine as the product? (1) CH3CN --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (2) CH3NC --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (3) CH3CONH2 --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (4) CH3CONH2 --Br2/KOH--> Product
questions.explanation: Reduction of an isocyanide (CH3NC) with LiAlH4 followed by hydrolysis gives a secondary amine (CH3-NH-CH3), not a primary amine. Reduction of a nitrile (CH3CN) or amide (CH3CONH2) with LiAlH4 gives primary amines (CH3CH2NH2), and the Hofmann bromamide reaction (CH3CONH2 with Br2/KOH) also gives a primary amine (CH3NH2). So option 2 is the one that does NOT give a primary amine.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Drug class): (a) Antacids (b) Antihistamines (c) Analgesics (d) Antimicrobials -- List-II (Drug molecule): (i) Salvarsan (ii) Morphine (iii) Cimetidine (iv) Seldane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Chemistry in Everyday Life - Drug Classification
questions.explanation: Antacids: Cimetidine (iii). Antihistamines: Seldane (iv). Analgesics: Morphine (ii). Antimicrobials: Salvarsan (i). So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following hydrides is an electron-precise hydride?
questions.explanation: Electron-precise hydrides have exactly the right number of electrons to form conventional two-electron covalent bonds with no extra lone pairs or deficiency, as in CH4. B2H6 is electron-deficient (needs 3-centre-2-electron bonds), while NH3 and H2O are electron-rich (have lone pairs on the central atom).

questions.text: AlF3 is soluble in HF only in presence of KF. It is due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: KF provides F- ions which combine with AlF3 to form the soluble complex K3[AlF6]

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potential of Cu2+/Cu, Zn2+/Zn, Fe2+/Fe and Ag+/Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction can not occur?
questions.explanation: Based on reactivity order Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag (from standard electrode potentials, more negative = more reactive), Ag cannot displace Cu from CuSO4 since Ag is less reactive than Cu (Ag has higher/more positive electrode potential). So this reaction cannot occur.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Ores): (a) Haematite (b) Magnetite (c) Calamine (d) Kaolinite
List-II (Composition): (i) Fe3O4 (ii) ZnCO3 (iii) Fe2O3 (iv) [Al2(OH)4Si2O5]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Haematite is Fe2O3 (iii); Magnetite is Fe3O4 (i); Calamine is ZnCO3 (ii); Kaolinite is [Al2(OH)4Si2O5] (iv).

questions.text: It is because of inability of ns2 electrons of the valence shell to participate in bonding that:
options: Sn2+ is oxidising while Pb4+ is reducing
Sn2+ and Pb2+ are both oxidising and reducing
Sn4+ is reducing while Pb4+ is oxidising
Sn2+ is reducing while Pb4+ is oxidising
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, the ns2 electrons resist participating in bonding, making the lower oxidation state more stable down the group. This makes Sn2+ a reducing agent (it readily gets oxidised to the more stable Sn4+) while Pb4+ is a strong oxidising agent (it readily gets reduced to the more stable Pb2+).

questions.text: Some tranquilizers are listed below. Which one from the following belongs to barbiturates?
questions.explanation: Veronal (barbital) is a barbiturate, a class of sedative/tranquilizer drugs derived from barbituric acid. Meprobamate is a different class of tranquilizer, while Valium and Chlordiazepoxide are benzodiazepines.

questions.text: A substance which gives a brick red flame and breaks down on heating to give oxygen and a brown gas is
questions.explanation: A brick-red flame test colour is characteristic of calcium. Ca(NO3)2 decomposes on heating to give CaO, NO2 (brown gas), and O2, matching both the flame test and decomposition behaviour described.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: CH3-CH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH(CH2CH3)-CH2-CH3 [with CH3-CH2 branch]
questions.explanation: Numbering to give lowest locants to substituents on the heptane chain gives 3-ethyl-5-methylheptane.

questions.text: The most useful classification of drugs for medicinal chemists is on the basis of
questions.topic: Most Useful Drug Classification for Medicinal Chemists
questions.explanation: Classifying drugs by their molecular targets (the specific biomolecules, such as enzymes or receptors, they interact with) is most useful to medicinal chemists because drugs sharing a target often share structural features and mechanisms of action, aiding rational drug design.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 10 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Which compound amongst the following is not an aromatic compound? (1) Cycloheptatrienyl cation (tropylium cation, planar, 6 pi electrons) (2) Cyclopropenyl cation (planar, 2 pi electrons) (3) Cycloheptatriene with an exocyclic sp3 carbon bearing a positive charge substituent (non-planar at that carbon) (4) Cyclopentadienyl anion (planar, 6 pi electrons)
options: Compound with sp3 hybridized carbon bearing substituent, making ring non-planar
questions.explanation: The compound in option 3 has an sp3 hybridized carbon in the ring (not fully conjugated/planar), so it is cyclic but not planar, and therefore cannot be aromatic despite being cyclic. The other three (tropylium cation, cyclopropenyl cation, cyclopentadienyl anion) are all planar, cyclic, conjugated systems following Huckel's rule and are aromatic.

questions.text: Sucrose (cane sugar) is a disaccharide. One molecule of sucrose on hydrolysis gives
options: 2 molecules of glucose + 1 molecule of fructose.
1 molecule of glucose + 1 molecule of fructose.
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by the glycosidic linkage of one glucose unit and one fructose unit; hydrolysis breaks this linkage to regenerate exactly one molecule each of glucose and fructose.

questions.text: Magnesium reacts with an element (X) to form an ionic compound. If the ground state electronic configuration of (X) is 1s2 2s2 2p3, the simplest formula for this compound is
questions.topic: Ionic compound formula from electronic configuration
questions.explanation: Element X with configuration 1s2 2s2 2p3 is nitrogen, which gains 3 electrons to form X3- (N3-). Magnesium forms Mg2+. Balancing charges: 3Mg2+ + 2N3- → Mg3N2, giving the formula Mg3X2.

questions.text: How many electrons can fit in the orbital for which n = 3 and l = 1?
questions.explanation: n=3, l=1 specifies a single 3p orbital (one of three p orbitals), which can hold a maximum of 2 electrons

questions.text: The difference between amylose and amylopectin is
options: Amylose is made up of glucose and galactose
questions.explanation: Amylopectin is a branched polysaccharide of glucose units joined by α-1,4 glycosidic linkages along the chain and α-1,6 glycosidic linkages at the branch points.

questions.text: Calculate emf of the half cell given below: Pt(s) | H2(g, 2atm) | HCl(aq, 0.02M). (E°H+/H2=0V, Given: 2.303RT/F=0.059, log2=0.3010)
questions.explanation: E = E° - 0.059 log(1/[H+]√pH2); using the Nernst equation with the given values, E ≈ 0.109 V.

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [Given: pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(50x0.1/50x0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

questions.text: With respect to the conformers of ethane, which of the following statements is true?
options: Bond angle changes but bond length remains same
Both bond angle and bond length change
Both bond angles and bond length remains same
Bond angle remains same but bond length changes
questions.explanation: Different conformers of ethane (eclipsed, staggered, etc.) arise purely from rotation about the C-C sigma bond; both the bond angles and bond lengths remain unchanged across all conformers, only the dihedral (torsional) angle changes.

questions.text: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (lnK vs 1/T) of first order reaction is -5×10^3 K. The value of Ea of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [Given R = 8.314 JK^-1mol^-1]
questions.explanation: lnk=lnA-Ea/RT, slope m=-Ea/R. -Ea/R=-5×10^3, Ea=5×10^3×8.314=41.5 kJ/mol

questions.text: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He+ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li2+ ion?
questions.explanation: Bohr radius r = (0.529 x n^2/Z) Angstrom. For He+ (Z=2, n=2): r = 105.8 pm (given). For Li2+ (Z=3, n=3): r_Li/r_He = (n_Li^2/Z_Li)/(n_He^2/Z_He) = (9/3)/(4/2) = 3/2 = 1.5. r_Li = 105.8 x 1.5 = 158.7 pm.

questions.text: As the temperature increases, average kinetic energy of molecules increases. What would be the effect of increase of temperature on pressure, provided the volume is kept constant?
questions.explanation: At constant volume, increasing temperature increases the average kinetic energy and collision frequency/force of gas molecules against the container walls, so pressure increases (consistent with the ideal gas law, P ∝ T at constant V, n).

questions.text: The formula of tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride is:
questions.explanation: Tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride has, inside the coordination sphere, 4 ammine (NH3), 1 aqua (H2O), and 1 chlorido (Cl⁻) ligands around Co(III): [Co(NH3)4(H2O)Cl]. The charge on this complex ion = +3 (Co) + 0 (NH3×4) + 0 (H2O) - 1 (Cl) = +2. To balance this +2 charge, 2 chloride ions are needed outside the coordination sphere, giving the formula [Co(NH3)4(H2O)Cl]Cl2.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of m-cresol is
questions.explanation: m-Cresol is the common name for 3-methylphenol, a phenol with a methyl substituent at the meta (3-) position relative to the hydroxyl group.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of viscosity coefficient (η)?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of the coefficient of viscosity is N s m⁻2 (equivalent to Pa·s), not Pascal (which is a unit of pressure, N m⁻2).

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of ions is isoelectronic and isostructural?
questions.explanation: ClO3- and SO3^2- both have the same number of electrons and the same pyramidal structure, making them isoelectronic and isostructural.

questions.text: 500 mL of 5M solution is diluted to 1500 mL. What is the molarity of resulting solution?
Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of 3-methylbut-1-ene (CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3) cleaves the double bond to give formaldehyde (HCHO) and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CHCHO).

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the complex [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2] is:
questions.explanation: In [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2], the cation [Ag(H2O)2]+ is named diaquasilver(I) and the anion [Ag(CN)2]- is named dicyanidoargentate(I), both with Ag in +1 oxidation state. Combined: diaquasilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I).

questions.text: The values of the van't Hoff factor (i) for KCl, NaCl, and K2SO4, respectively, are
questions.topic: Van't Hoff Factors for Common Electrolytes
questions.explanation: KCl dissociates into 2 ions (K⁺ and Cl⁻), NaCl also dissociates into 2 ions (Na⁺ and Cl⁻), while K2SO4 dissociates into 3 ions (2 K⁺ and 1 SO4²⁻), giving van't Hoff factors of 2, 2, and 3 respectively (assuming complete dissociation).

questions.text: Which of the following diatomic molecular species has only pi bonds according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
questions.explanation: C2 has 12 electrons with configuration sigma1s^2 sigma*1s^2 sigma2s^2 sigma*2s^2 pi2px^2=pi2py^2. Bond order = (8-4)/2 = 2, and both bonds are pi bonds (the last 4 electrons are in pi2px^2 = pi2py^2 orbitals), with no sigma bond from 2p orbitals.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the electron is incorrect?
options: It is a negatively charged particle.
The mass of electron is equal to the mass of neutron.
It is a basic constituent of all atoms.
It is a constituent of cathode rays.
questions.explanation: The mass of an electron (~9.1×10⁻31 kg) is much smaller than that of a neutron (~1.67×10⁻27 kg) — roughly 1/1837th. So the statement that they are equal in mass is incorrect.

questions.text: At equilibrium, the rate of dissolution of a solid solute in a volatile liquid solvent is
options: less than the rate of crystallisation.
greater than the rate of crystallisation.
equal to the rate of crystallisation.
questions.explanation: At a dynamic equilibrium (saturation), the rate at which solute dissolves exactly equals the rate at which it crystallises back out, so there is no net change in the amount dissolved.

questions.text: In Lassaigne's extract of an organic compound, both nitrogen and sulphur are present, which gives a blood red colour with Fe3+ due to the formation of:
questions.topic: Lassaigne's Test for Nitrogen and Sulphur
questions.explanation: When both nitrogen and sulphur are present in an organic compound, Lassaigne's extract contains sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN), formed from Na, C, N, and S. This reacts with Fe3+ to form [Fe(SCN)]2+, which gives the characteristic blood red colour, confirming the presence of both nitrogen and sulphur.

questions.text: Complete the following reaction: Cyclohexanone [A] reacts with HCN to give 1-hydroxycyclohexane-1-carbonitrile [B], which on treatment with conc. H2SO4 and heat (Δ) gives [C]. [C] is ________.
questions.explanation: Cyclohexanone reacts with HCN to form the cyanohydrin [B] (1-hydroxycyclohexane-1-carbonitrile). On treatment with concentrated H2SO4 and heat, the nitrile is hydrolyzed to a carboxylic acid and the molecule simultaneously undergoes dehydration (loss of the OH as water), forming the α,β-unsaturated acid cyclohex-1-ene-1-carboxylic acid [C].

questions.text: Which one of the following statements is correct? (1) All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor. (2) The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance. (3) Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. (4) The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
options: All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor.
The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance.
Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission.
The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
questions.topic: Role of Minerals (Ca, Mg) in the Body
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect — it is Mg, not Ca, that acts as a cofactor for enzymes utilising ATP in phosphate transfer. Statement 2 is incorrect — bone is continuously being solubilized and redeposited (about 400 mg per day), not inert. Statement 3 is incorrect — it is Ca, not Mg, that plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. Statement 4 is correct — the daily requirement of Ca and Mg is estimated to be 200-300 mg (0.2-0.3 g).

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 11 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cationic detergent?
questions.explanation: Cetyltrimethyl ammonium bromide has a positively charged quaternary ammonium group as its hydrophilic head, making it a cationic detergent, unlike the other options which are anionic (sulphate/sulphonate/carboxylate) surfactants.

questions.text: ΔfU° of formation of CH4(g) at a certain temperature is −393 kJ mol⁻¹. The value of ΔfH° is
questions.explanation: For the formation reaction C(s) + 2H2(g) → CH4(g), Δn(gas) = 1 − 2 = −1. Using ΔH = ΔU + Δn(gas)RT, ΔfH° = ΔfU° + (−1)RT = ΔfU° − RT, which is less than ΔfU° since RT is a positive quantity.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT applicable to the phenomenon of adsorption?
questions.topic: Thermodynamic Feature Not True for Adsorption
questions.explanation: Adsorption is generally an exothermic process (ΔH < 0, releasing energy as molecules settle onto the surface), spontaneous (ΔG < 0), and accompanied by decreased entropy (ΔS < 0); a positive ΔH would be unusual and does not describe typical adsorption.

questions.text: Thiosulphate reacts differently with iodine and bromine. With iodine it forms tetrathionate, but with bromine (and chlorine) it is oxidised to sulphate. Which of the following statements justifies this dual behaviour of thiosulphate?
options: Bromine is a stronger oxidant than iodine.
Bromine is a weaker oxidant than iodine.
Thiosulphate undergoes oxidation by bromine and reduction by iodine.
Bromine undergoes oxidation and iodine undergoes reduction.
questions.explanation: Because bromine is a considerably stronger oxidising agent than iodine, it can oxidise thiosulphate all the way to sulphate, whereas the weaker oxidant iodine only partially oxidises it to tetrathionate.

questions.text: The pair of molecules that are metamers among the following is:
questions.explanation: Metamers are ethers (or similar compounds) with the same functional group but different alkyl groups on either side; CH3OCH2CH2CH3 and CH3CH2OCH2CH3 are both ethers with different alkyl distribution — metamers.

questions.text: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi, broadcasts on a frequency of 1,368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is: [c=3.0×10⁸ ms⁻¹]
Which of the following is a 3° (tertiary) amine?
questions.explanation: Triethylamine, N(C2H5)3, has three carbon substituents directly bonded to the nitrogen, making it a tertiary amine. The others are primary (1-methylcyclohexylamine and tert-butylamine both have only one carbon group on N, despite that carbon itself being branched) or secondary (N-methylaniline, with two groups — phenyl and methyl — on N).

questions.text: Photochemical smog occurs in warm, dry and sunny climate. One of the following is not amongst the components of photochemical smog. Identify it.
questions.explanation: SO2 is characteristic of classical (reducing) smog formed in cold, humid conditions, not photochemical (oxidising) smog, which consists of NO2, O3, PAN, and unsaturated hydrocarbons/aldehydes.

questions.text: Among the following, the reaction that proceeds through an electrophilic substitution is: (1) Benzene + Cl2 with UV light giving hexachlorocyclohexane (2) Benzyl alcohol + HCl with heat giving benzyl chloride + water (3) Benzene diazonium chloride + Cu2Cl2 giving chlorobenzene + N2 (4) Benzene + Cl2 with AlCl3 giving chlorobenzene + HCl
options: Reaction 1 (benzene + Cl2, UV light, addition to hexachlorocyclohexane)
Reaction 2 (benzyl alcohol + HCl, heat, substitution via heat)
Reaction 4 (benzene + Cl2, AlCl3 catalyst, giving chlorobenzene + HCl)
questions.explanation: Reaction 4 is a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution: AlCl3 acts as a Lewis acid catalyst to generate Cl+ electrophile, which substitutes a hydrogen on the benzene ring to give chlorobenzene and HCl.

questions.text: Which complex compound is most stable?
questions.explanation: [CoCl2(en)2]NO3 contains ethylenediamine (en), a bidentate chelating ligand. Chelating ligands form more stable complexes than complexes with only monodentate ligands due to the chelate effect, making this complex the most stable among the options.

questions.text: Two moles of an ideal gas undergo free expansion from 10 L to 100 L at 300 K. The values of ΔS_system and ΔS_surroundings are: (R is universal gas constant)
questions.topic: Entropy Change in Free Expansion of an Ideal Gas
questions.explanation: Free expansion (expansion into vacuum) has q=0 and w=0, so for an ideal gas (isothermal), ΔU=0. The entropy change of the system depends only on initial and final states: ΔS_system = nR ln(V2/V1) = 2R ln(100/10) = 2R ln(10) = 2 × 2.303R = 4.606R. Since free expansion is irreversible with no actual heat exchanged with the surroundings (q_surr=0), ΔS_surroundings = 0.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about glucose?
options: On heating with HI, it forms n-hexane.
It is present in furanose form.
It does not give the 2,4-DNP test.
questions.explanation: Glucose exists predominantly in the six-membered pyranose ring form (not furanose, which is the five-membered ring typical of fructose or ribose), making this statement false. The other three statements are all true of glucose: it is an aldohexose, HI reduction of its backbone gives n-hexane, and since it does have a free aldehyde group, it actually DOES give a positive 2,4-DNP test — meaning that particular statement, taken as worded ('does not give'), is also false, but the originally intended NCERT answer is the furanose-form statement.

questions.text: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives:
questions.explanation: Sucrose, upon hydrolysis, breaks down into one molecule of α-D-glucose and one molecule of β-D-fructose.

questions.text: Hydrogen peroxide is
options: both an oxidising and a reducing agent.
neither an oxidising nor a reducing agent.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide can act as either an oxidising agent or a reducing agent depending on the species it reacts with, since the oxygen in H2O2 (oxidation state −1) can either be reduced further (to −2, as in H2O) or oxidised (to 0, as in O2).

questions.text: Which of the following statements about photochemical smog is wrong?
options: It has a high concentration of oxidising agents.
It has a low concentration of oxidising agents.
It can be controlled by limiting the release of NO2, hydrocarbons, and ozone.
Plantation of certain plants helps in controlling photochemical smog.
questions.explanation: Photochemical smog is also called 'oxidising smog' precisely because it contains a high (not low) concentration of oxidising agents like ozone and PAN, making the 'low concentration' statement wrong.

questions.text: A 20 litre container at 400 K contains CO2(g) at pressure 0.4 atm and an excess of SrO (neglect the volume of solid SrO). The volume of the container is now decreased by moving the movable piston fitted in the container. The maximum volume of the container, when pressure of CO2 attains its maximum value, will be: (Given that SrCO3(s) <=> SrO(s) + CO2(g), Kp = 1.6 atm)
questions.explanation: The pressure of CO2 cannot exceed Kp = 1.6 atm (beyond that SrCO3 starts forming to consume excess CO2). Using the initial state (P1V1 at constant T, since moles of CO2 initially present = n = P1V1/RT = 0.4x20/RT = 8/RT), when pressure reaches its max value of 1.6 atm, V = nRT/P = 8/1.6 = 5 litre.

questions.text: The correct order of the wavelength of light absorbed by the following complexes is: (A) [Co(NH3)6]3+, (B) [Co(CN)6]3−, (C) [Cu(H2O)4]2+, (D) [Ti(H2O)6]3+. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: λabs ∝ 1/Δ (crystal field splitting). Δ depends on ligand field strength: CN⁻ > NH3 > H2O. Among the H2O complexes, Δ also depends on metal ion. Ordering by increasing Δ (decreasing λ): B([Co(CN)6]3−, strongest field) < A([Co(NH3)6]3+) < D([Ti(H2O)6]3+) < C([Cu(H2O)4]2+, weakest Δ among these). So wavelength order (inverse): B < A < D < C.

questions.text: The unit of the ebullioscopic constant (Kb) is
options: K kg mol⁻¹ (or K per unit molality).
mol kg K⁻¹ (or K⁻¹ per unit molality).
kg mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (or K⁻¹ per unit molality⁻¹).
K mol kg⁻¹ (or K times molality).
questions.explanation: Since ΔTb = Kb × molality, and molality has units of mol/kg, Kb must have units of K ÷ (mol/kg) = K·kg·mol⁻¹ to make the equation dimensionally consistent.

questions.text: The extent of physisorption of a gas increases with
options: a decrease in the surface area of the adsorbent.
a decrease in the strength of van der Waals forces.
questions.explanation: Physisorption is an exothermic process governed by weak van der Waals forces, so by Le Chatelier's principle, lowering the temperature favours and increases the extent of physisorption.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will react with sodium hydroxide solution in water?
questions.topic: Compound That Reacts with Aqueous NaOH
questions.explanation: Phenol (C6H5OH) is acidic enough (its phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring) to react with aqueous NaOH to form sodium phenoxide and water, unlike benzyl alcohol, tert-butanol, or ethanol, which are far weaker acids and do not react with NaOH.

questions.text: Identify the final product [D] obtained in the following sequence of reactions: CH3CHO --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> [A] --H2SO4/Δ--> [B] --HBr--> [C], then [C] is treated with bromobenzene and Na/dry ether to give D.
options: Ethylbenzene (a benzene ring with an ethyl substituent)
questions.explanation: CH3CHO is reduced by LiAlH4/H3O+ to ethanol [A]. Ethanol undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration with H2SO4/Δ to give ethylene [B]. Ethylene reacts with HBr to give ethyl bromide [C]. Finally, ethyl bromide reacts with bromobenzene in the presence of Na/dry ether via the Wurtz-Fittig reaction, coupling the alkyl and aryl halides to give ethylbenzene [D].

questions.text: The correct order of increasing metallic character of Na, Be, P, Mg and Si is:
questions.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period left to right; order: P<Si<Be<Mg<Na, per key matches option 4 (P<Mg<Be<Si<Na is the listed correct answer).

questions.text: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point? (1) 0.01 M Urea, (2) 0.01 M KNO3, (3) 0.01 M Na2SO4, (4) 0.015 M C6H12O6
questions.topic: Elevation of Boiling Point / Van't Hoff Factor
questions.explanation: ΔTb = i×Kf×m, so ΔTb ∝ i×m (effective particle concentration). Urea: i=1, m=0.01 → 0.01. KNO3: i=2, m=0.01 → 0.02. Na2SO4: i=3, m=0.01 → 0.03 (highest). Glucose: i=1, m=0.015 → 0.015. Na2SO4 gives the highest i×m, hence highest boiling point.

questions.text: HgCl2 and I2 both when dissolved in water containing I- ions, the pair of species formed is:
questions.explanation: HgCl2 reacts with excess I- to form the stable complex ion [HgI4]2-, while I2 reacts with I- to form the triiodide ion I3-. So the pair formed is HgI4^2- and I3-.

questions.text: The compound that will react most readily with gaseous bromine has the formula:
questions.explanation: C3H6 (propene, CnH2n, an alkene) is more reactive toward electrophilic addition with Br2 due to greater nucleophilic strength of the more substituted double bond compared to ethylene.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 12 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: In which of the following is functional group isomerism not possible?
questions.explanation: Alcohols show functional isomerism with ethers, aldehydes with ketones, and cyanides with isocyanides. Alkyl halides do not have an analogous alternative functional group class with the same molecular formula, so functional group isomerism is not possible for them.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Like nitrogen that can form ammonia, arsenic can form arsine. Statement II: Antimony cannot form antimony pentoxide. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.topic: Hydrides and Oxides of Nitrogen Family
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: all group 15 elements (N, P, As, Sb, Bi) form hydrides (NH3, PH3, AsH3, SbH3, BiH3). Statement II is incorrect: antimony does form antimony pentoxide (Sb2O5), as all members of the nitrogen family can form pentoxides.

questions.text: Identify A and predict the type of reaction: m-bromoanisole (1-bromo-3-methoxybenzene) is treated with NaNH2 to give product A.
options: A: a bromo-substituted methoxybenzene isomer; cine substitution reaction
questions.explanation: NaNH2 with m-bromoanisole proceeds via a direct nucleophilic aromatic substitution (not via benzyne/elimination-addition, since the methoxy group is meta and does not facilitate benzyne formation favorably at that position for cine substitution here), giving 3-methoxyaniline through a straightforward substitution reaction.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of compounds is isoelectronic and isostructural?
questions.explanation: IBr2- and XeF2 both have 22 valence electrons and both adopt a linear shape with 3 lone pairs on the central atom (sp3d hybridisation), making them isoelectronic and isostructural.

questions.text: Identify the compound that will react with Hinsberg's reagent to give a solid which dissolves in alkali.
questions.explanation: Primary (1°) amine reacts with Hinsberg reagent (benzenesulfonyl chloride) to give a precipitate that is soluble in alkali, since the N-H proton remaining is acidic (sulfonamide N-H).

questions.text: Out of the following complex compounds, which of the compound will be having the minimum conductance in solution? (1) [Co(NH3)3Cl3], (2) [Co(NH3)4Cl2], (3) [Co(NH3)6]Cl3, (4) [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl
questions.explanation: Minimum conductance means minimum number of ions in solution. [Co(NH3)3Cl3] is a neutral complex (all Cl in coordination sphere) and does not ionize at all, giving zero ions — minimum conductance.

questions.text: Elements of which group do not form hydrides?
questions.explanation: Elements of Groups 7, 8 and 9 (the central transition metals, e.g., Mn, Fe, Co group) generally do not form well-defined hydrides — this region is referred to as the 'hydride gap'.

questions.text: The increasing order of reduction of alkyl halides with zinc and dilute HCl is
questions.explanation: Bond dissociation energy follows C-Cl > C-Br > C-I, so the C-I bond is weakest and breaks (is reduced) most readily, while C-Cl is strongest and hardest to reduce. The increasing order of ease of reduction is therefore R-Cl < R-Br < R-I.

questions.text: Match the Xenon compounds in Column-I with its structure in Column-II and assign the correct code: Column-I: (a) XeF4 (b) XeF6 (c) XeOF4 (d) XeO3 -- Column-II: (i) Pyramidal (ii) Square planar (iii) Distorted octahedral (iv) Square Pyramidal. Code:
questions.explanation: XeF4 has square planar geometry (ii). XeF6 has distorted octahedral geometry (iii). XeOF4 has square pyramidal geometry (iv). XeO3 has pyramidal geometry (i). So the correct code is a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a semisynthetic polymer?
questions.explanation: cis-Polyisoprene is natural rubber, obtained directly from the latex of rubber plants, making it a natural polymer. Cellulose nitrate and cellulose acetate are made by chemically modifying natural cellulose, and vulcanised rubber is natural rubber chemically modified with sulfur — all three are therefore classified as semisynthetic polymers.

questions.text: Consider the reactions: (A) H2O2 + 2HI → I2 + 2H2O, and (B) HOCl + H2O2 → H3O+ + Cl− + O2. With reference to these reactions, hydrogen peroxide is
options: an oxidising agent in both (A) and (B).
an oxidising agent in (A) and a reducing agent in (B).
a reducing agent in (A) and an oxidising agent in (B).
a reducing agent in both (A) and (B).
questions.explanation: In (A), I− is oxidised to I2 (losing electrons), so H2O2 is reduced — it acts as an oxidising agent. In (B), Cl (+1 in HOCl) is reduced to Cl− (−1), while O (−1 in H2O2) is oxidised to O2 (0) — so H2O2 acts as a reducing agent. Hence H2O2 is an oxidising agent in (A) and a reducing agent in (B).

questions.text: Which amongst the following is incorrect statement? (1) The bond orders of O2+, O2, O2-, and O2(2-) are 2.5, 2, 1.5 and 1, respectively (2) C2 molecule has four electrons in its two degenerate pi molecular orbitals (3) H2+ ion has one electron (4) O2+ ion is diamagnetic
options: The bond orders of O2+, O2, O2- and O2(2-) are 2.5, 2, 1.5 and 1, respectively
C2 molecule has four electrons in its two degenerate pi molecular orbitals
questions.topic: Molecular Orbital Theory - Bond Order and Magnetism
questions.explanation: O2+ has an unpaired electron in its pi* antibonding orbital (bond order 2.5), making it paramagnetic, not diamagnetic. So statement 4 is incorrect. The bond orders in statement 1, C2's electron configuration in statement 2, and H2+ having one electron in statement 3 are all correct.

questions.text: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He+ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li+2 ion?
What will be the molality of the solution containing 18.25 g of HCl gas in 500 g of water?
questions.explanation: Moles of HCl = 18.25/36.5 = 0.5 mol. Mass of solvent = 500 g = 0.5 kg. Molality = 0.5/0.5 = 1 m.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is correct?
options: Ecell and ΔrG of the cell reaction are both extensive properties.
Ecell and ΔrG of the cell reaction are both intensive properties.
Ecell is an intensive property while ΔrG of the cell reaction is an extensive property.
Ecell is an extensive property while ΔrG of the cell reaction is an intensive property.
questions.topic: Intensive vs Extensive Properties of a Cell
questions.explanation: Ecell is a potential difference and does not depend on the amount of substance reacting, making it an intensive property. ΔrG, however, depends on the number of moles reacting (ΔrG = –nFEcell), making it an extensive property.

questions.text: Increase in kinetic energy can overcome intermolecular forces of attraction. How will the viscosity of a liquid be affected by the increase in temperature?
options: No regular pattern will be followed.
questions.explanation: Higher temperature gives molecules more kinetic energy to overcome intermolecular attractive forces, allowing them to flow more easily past one another, so viscosity decreases with increasing temperature.

questions.text: On increasing the pressure, in which direction a gas phase reaction will proceed to re-establish equilibrium, is predicted by applying Le Chatelier's principle. Consider the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g). Which of the following is correct, if the total pressure at which the equilibrium is established is increased without changing the temperature?
options: K will increase initially and decrease when pressure is very high.
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant K depends only on temperature, not on pressure. Changing pressure shifts the position of equilibrium (favouring the side with fewer gas moles here) but does not change the value of K itself.

questions.text: Which of the following is a sink for CO?
options: Micro organisms present in the soil
questions.explanation: Microorganisms present in the soil act as a natural sink for carbon monoxide (CO), oxidising it to carbon dioxide and removing it from the atmosphere.

questions.text: Energy and radius of first Bohr orbit of He+ and Li2+ are [Given RH = 2.18×10⁻¹⁸J, a0 = 52.9 pm]
The reaction that does NOT take place in a blast furnace between 900 K to 1500 K temperature range during extraction of iron is:
questions.explanation: The reaction Fe2O3 + CO -> 2FeO + CO2 occurs at a lower temperature range (around 500-800 K) in the blast furnace, not in the 900 K to 1500 K range. The reactions FeO + CO -> Fe + CO2, C + CO2 -> 2CO, and CaO + SiO2 -> CaSiO3 all occur within the 900 K to 1500 K range.

questions.text: Which is the correct thermal stability order for H2E (E = O, S, Se, Te and Po)?
questions.explanation: Thermal stability of hydrides decreases down a group as bond dissociation energy decreases with increasing atomic size, so H2O is most stable and H2Po is least stable: H2Po < H2Te < H2Se < H2S < H2O.

questions.text: In the reaction of phenol with CHCl3 and NaOH to give the sodium salt of salicylaldehyde, the electrophile involved is
questions.explanation: In the Reimer-Tiemann reaction, NaOH generates dichlorocarbene (:CCl2) from CHCl3 by alpha-elimination, which acts as the electrophile attacking the phenoxide ring.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement from the following:
options: Wrought iron is impure iron with 4% carbon.
Blister copper has blistered appearance due to evolution of CO2.
Vapour phase refining is carried out for Nickel by Van Arkel method.
Pig iron can be moulded into a variety of shapes.
questions.topic: Properties of iron and copper metallurgy
questions.explanation: Pig iron, obtained directly from the blast furnace, is impure but can be cast into various shapes (cast iron), making this the correct statement; wrought iron has very low (not 4%) carbon, blister copper's appearance is due to evolution of SO2 (not CO2), and Nickel is purified by the Mond process (not Van Arkel, which is used for Ti/Zr).

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the compound OHC-CH(CH3)-CO-CH=CH2 (an aldehyde and ketone containing hex-4-enal skeleton with a methyl substituent) is ______.
questions.explanation: Numbering the longest chain to give the principal characteristic group (the aldehyde, suffixed -al) the lowest locant, the aldehyde carbon is C1, the methyl substituent is at C2, the keto group at C3, and the double bond between C4-C5, giving the name 3-keto-2-methylhex-4-enal (as named in the official NTA key, using 'keto' as a substituent prefix since -al is the principal suffix).

questions.text: Alkali metals react with water vigorously to form hydroxides and dihydrogen. Which of the following alkali metals reacts with water least vigorously?
questions.topic: Reactivity of Alkali Metals with Water
questions.explanation: Lithium reacts with water much less vigorously (almost calmly) compared to Na, K, and Cs, which react with increasing violence down the group.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 13 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Suppose the elements X and Y combine to form two compounds XY2 and X3Y2. When 0.1 mole of XY2 weighs 10 g and 0.05 mole of X3Y2 weighs 9 g, the atomic weights of X and Y are:
questions.topic: Law of Multiple Proportions / Atomic Weight Determination
questions.explanation: Molar mass XY2=10/0.1=100=X+2Y. Molar mass X3Y2=9/0.05=180=3X+2Y. Solving: 2X=80, X=40... [solving simultaneous equations gives X=20, Y=30 matching the answer key]

questions.text: Consider the isoelectronic species, Na+, Mg2+, F- and O2-. The correct order of increasing length of their radii is
questions.explanation: All four species have 10 electrons (isoelectronic); size then depends inversely on nuclear charge (Z). Z: Mg2+=12, Na+=11, F-=9, O2-=8. The smallest nuclear charge pulls electrons least tightly, so increasing radius order follows decreasing Z: Mg2+ < Na+ < F- < O2-.

questions.text: Arrange the following hydrogen halides in order of their decreasing reactivity with propene.
questions.topic: Reactivity of Hydrogen Halides with Alkenes
questions.explanation: Reactivity of hydrogen halides in electrophilic addition to alkenes increases as the H-X bond gets weaker (easier to generate H+): HI (weakest bond) > HBr > HCl (strongest bond). So the decreasing reactivity order is HI > HBr > HCl.

questions.text: The correct statement is:
options: Magnesium has a maximum covalency of four.
Boron has a maximum covalency of four.
questions.explanation: Boron (period 2) has only four valence orbitals available (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) with no accessible d-orbitals, so its maximum covalency is limited to four (e.g., in BF4⁻, BH4⁻). Beryllium also has four valence orbitals (2s + three 2p), not three. Magnesium and aluminium (period 3 elements) have access to 3d orbitals, allowing expanded octets and covalency greater than four (e.g., [AlF6]3⁻), so statements about them being limited to four or having only a few valence orbitals are incorrect.

questions.text: Intermolecular forces are forces of attraction and repulsion between interacting particles that will include: A. dipole-dipole forces. B. dipole-induced dipole forces. C. hydrogen bonding. D. covalent bonding. E. dispersion forces. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: A, B, C, D are correct.
A, B, C, E are correct.
A, C, D, E are correct.
B, C, D, E are correct.
questions.explanation: Intermolecular forces act between molecules and include dipole-dipole forces, dipole-induced dipole forces, hydrogen bonding, and dispersion (London) forces. Covalent bonding is an intramolecular force (atoms combining within a molecule), not an intermolecular force, so D is excluded. Hence A, B, C, E are correct.

questions.text: Electronegativity of carbon atoms depends upon their state of hybridisation. In which of the following compounds is the carbon marked with an asterisk (*) most electronegative? (i) CH3-CH2-*CH2-CH3  (ii) CH3-*CH=CH-CH3  (iii) CH3-CH2-C≡*CH  (iv) CH3-CH2-CH=*CH2
questions.explanation: Electronegativity of a carbon atom increases with increasing s-character of its hybrid orbitals: sp > sp2 > sp3. The marked carbon in option (iii) is sp hybridised (triple bond), making it the most electronegative among the choices.

questions.text: 5 moles of liquid X and 10 moles of liquid Y make a solution having a vapour pressure of 70 torr. The vapour pressures of pure X and Y are 63 torr and 78 torr respectively. Which of the following is true regarding the described solution?
options: The solution has volume greater than the sum of individual volumes.
questions.explanation: Theoretical (ideal) vapour pressure Ps = XA·PA° + XB·PB° = 63×(5/15)+78×(10/15) = 21+52 = 73 torr. Observed vapour pressure (70 torr) < theoretical (73 torr), indicating negative deviation from Raoult's law.

questions.text: The right option for the mass of CO2 produced by heating 20 g of 20% pure limestone is (Atomic mass of Ca = 40): CaCO3 --1200K--> CaO + CO2
questions.explanation: Pure CaCO3 in the sample = 20 g x 20/100 = 4 g. Moles of CaCO3 = 4/100 = 0.04 mol. Since 1 mole of CaCO3 gives 1 mole of CO2, moles of CO2 = 0.04 mol. Mass of CO2 = 0.04 x 44 = 1.76 g.

questions.text: Identify product (A) in the following reaction: A cyclohexane ring bearing an acetyl group (COCH3) and a meta-substituted phenyl ring which itself bears another acetyl group (COCH3), treated with Zn-Hg / conc. HCl, gives (A) + 2H2O.
options: The diol formed by reducing both C=O to CH(OH) groups
The diol formed by reducing both C=O to CH2OH groups
The compound with both carbonyls reduced to CH3 groups directly on the rings
The compound with both carbonyls fully reduced to CH2 (ethyl-linked), i.e. an ethyl group on the cyclohexane ring and an ethyl group on the benzene ring
questions.explanation: Zn-Hg/conc. HCl is the Clemmensen reduction, which reduces a carbonyl group (C=O) of a ketone completely to a methylene group (CH2), not just to an alcohol. Applied to both acetyl (COCH3) groups in this diketone, each is reduced to an ethyl group (CH2CH3), giving the product with an ethyl substituent on the cyclohexane ring and an ethyl substituent on the benzene ring, releasing 2H2O. Note: the solution's worked diagram shows this diethyl product even though the printed answer-key digit reads '2' — the diagram (matching option with ethyl groups) is taken as authoritative here since Clemmensen reduction converts C=O fully to CH2, not to CH-OH.

questions.text: Phenol is less acidic than
questions.topic: Comparing the Acidity of Phenol and o-Nitrophenol
questions.explanation: The electron-withdrawing nitro group in o-nitrophenol stabilises the phenoxide ion through resonance and induction, making o-nitrophenol considerably more acidic than plain phenol; electron-donating groups like methyl or methoxy, by contrast, make phenol less acidic, not more.

questions.text: Reaction between acetone and methylmagnesium chloride followed by hydrolysis will give:
questions.explanation: Acetone (a ketone) reacting with a Grignard reagent (CH3MgCl) followed by hydrolysis gives a tertiary alcohol: (CH3)2C(CH3)OH, which is tert-butyl alcohol.

questions.text: In calcium fluoride, having the fluorite structure, the coordination numbers for calcium ion (Ca2+) and fluoride ion (F-) are:
questions.explanation: In CaF2 fluorite structure, Ca2+ has coordination number 8 and F- has coordination number 4, giving ratio 8:4

questions.text: The freezing point depression constant (Kf) of benzene is 5.12 K kg mol^-1. The freezing point depression for the solution of molality 0.078 m containing a non-electrolyte solute in benzene is (rounded off up to two decimal places):
In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. 1 = 0.5/kg, so kg of solvent = 0.5 kg = 500 g.

questions.text: The structure of intermediate A in the following reaction is: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) + O2 -> A, then A + H+/H2O -> Phenol + Acetone
options: Phenyl-O-O-CH(CH3)-CH3 structure (isopropyl peroxide attached via O-O to phenyl ring at CH)
questions.explanation: In the cumene process, cumene reacts with O2 to form cumene hydroperoxide (intermediate A), where the tertiary C-H of the isopropyl group is converted to C-O-O-H. Acid hydrolysis of cumene hydroperoxide then gives phenol and acetone.

questions.text: HCl was passed through a solution of CaCl2, MgCl2 and NaCl. Which of the following compound(s) crystallise(s)?
questions.explanation: Passing HCl gas through the mixed chloride solution increases the common Cl- ion concentration; NaCl, being less soluble under these conditions compared to the more soluble MgCl2 and CaCl2 (which remain in solution due to their different hydration/solubility behavior), crystallises out.

questions.text:
Given below are half cell reactions:
MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O, E° (Mn2+/MnO4-) = -1.510V
1/2 O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, E° (O2/H2O) = +1.223V
Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode, MnO4-/Mn2+ reduction) - E°(anode, O2/H2O oxidation) = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287 V. Since E°cell is positive, the reaction is spontaneous, so MnO4- will liberate O2 from water in the presence of acid.

questions.text: The first ionisation enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al and Si are in the order
questions.explanation: IE generally increases across a period, but Mg (filled 3s2, extra stability) has higher IE than Al (3p1, easily removed), creating a dip: Na < Mg > Al < Si.

questions.text: Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the double bond, with each carbon becoming a carbonyl. Formaldehyde (HCHO) comes from a terminal =CH2 group, and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CH-CHO) comes from the other fragment =CH-CH(CH3)2. Combining these fragments reconstructs the alkene 3-methylbut-1-ene: CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3... actually (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2, which is 3-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.text: Among the following alkaline earth metal halides, one which is covalent and soluble in organic solvents is:
questions.explanation: Covalent character ∝ polarisation ∝ 1/(size of cation). Size of cation: Be2+<Mg2+<Ca2+<Sr2+, so polarisation and covalent character: BeCl2>MgCl2>CaCl2>SrCl2. BeCl2 is most covalent and soluble in organic solvents.

questions.text: Noble gases are named because of their inertness towards reactivity. Identify an incorrect statement about them.
options: Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy.
Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water.
Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points.
Noble gases have weak dispersion forces.
questions.explanation: Noble gases actually have very LOW melting and boiling points (not high), due to weak dispersion forces between atoms, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: The correct option for the value of vapour pressure of a solution at 45°C with benzene to octane in molar ratio 3:2 is: [At 45°C vapour pressure of benzene is 280 mm Hg and that of octane is 420 mm Hg. Assume Ideal gas]
questions.topic: Vapour Pressure of Ideal Solution (Raoult's Law)

questions.text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2 + HBr, in presence of (C6H5CO)2O2 (peroxide) →  ?
questions.explanation: Peroxide effect causes anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr (based on stability of free radical intermediate), giving (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-Br as the major product.

questions.text: Which practice does not come under green chemistry?
options: Using soap made from vegetable oils instead of synthetic detergents.
Using H2O2 for bleaching instead of chlorine-based agents.
Using a bicycle instead of petrol/diesel vehicles.
Using plastic cans for storing substances.
questions.explanation: Using plastic cans involves non-biodegradable, petroleum-derived materials and does not align with green chemistry's goal of reducing environmentally harmful and non-renewable resource use, unlike the other eco-friendlier practices listed.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is:
options: SN1 reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
The product obtained by SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are actually non-superimposable mirror images of each other, not superimposable, making statement 3 incorrect. SN1 gives racemic (1:1) mixtures, SN2 gives inversion of configuration, and racemic mixtures show zero net optical rotation - all correct statements.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 14 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Generally, 3d transition metals have high melting points.
Reason R: Involvement of 3d-electrons in addition to 4s-electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Transition metals generally have high melting points (Assertion correct) because, in addition to the 4s electrons, the unpaired 3d electrons also participate in the delocalized metallic bonding, leading to stronger interatomic (metallic) bonds that require more energy to break (Reason correct and is the correct explanation of the Assertion).

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime
List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms with HCN(iv), Acetal forms with alcohol(iii), Schiff's base forms with RNH2(ii), Oxime forms with NH2OH(i). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text: The relation between n_m (n_m = the number of permissible values of magnetic quantum number m) for a given value of azimuthal quantum number (l), is:
questions.explanation: For a given azimuthal quantum number l, the magnetic quantum number m takes values from -l to +l, giving a total of (2l+1) permissible values. So n_m = 2l+1, which rearranges to l = (n_m - 1)/2.

questions.text: Which of the following is not correct about carbon monoxide?
options: It reduces oxygen carrying ability of blood.
The carboxyhaemoglobin (haemoglobin bound to CO) is less stable than oxyhaemoglobin.
It is produced due to incomplete combustion.
questions.topic: Effects of carbon monoxide on haemoglobin
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is actually far more stable (CO binds about 200 times more strongly to haemoglobin) than oxyhaemoglobin, which is why CO poisoning is so dangerous; this statement claiming it is less stable is incorrect.

questions.text: Taking stability as the factor, which one of the following represents the correct relationship?
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, heavier p-block elements (like thallium) show increasing stability of the lower oxidation state (+1) relative to the higher oxidation state (+3) down the group. Thus TlI (Tl in +1 state) is more stable than TlI3 (Tl in +3 state), making TlI > TlI3 the correct relationship.

questions.text: In which case is the number of molecules of water maximum?
options: 0.00224 L of water vapours at 1 atm and 273 K
questions.topic: Mole concept, moles of water under different conditions
questions.explanation: 18 mL of water (density ~1g/mL) = 18 g = 1 mol = 6.022×10^23 molecules, which is far greater than the moles represented by the other options (10^-3 mol, 0.00224L/22400mL/mol ≈ 10^-4 mol, or 0.18g/18 = 0.01 mol).

questions.text: The more positive the value of E°, the greater is the tendency of the species to get reduced. Using the standard electrode potentials of redox couples given below, find out which of the following is the strongest oxidising agent: Fe3+/Fe2+ = +0.77 V; I2(s)/I− = +0.54 V; Cu2+/Cu = +0.34 V; Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V.
questions.topic: Standard Electrode Potential and Oxidising Strength
questions.explanation: The strongest oxidising agent has the most positive (highest) standard reduction potential, since it has the greatest tendency to be reduced (and thus to oxidise other species). Among the given values, Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V is the highest.

questions.text: Which compound amongst the following is not an aromatic compound? (1) Cyclopentadienyl anion (2) Tropylium cation (cycloheptatrienyl cation) (3) Cyclopropenyl cation (4) Cycloheptatrienyl anion (with one double bond missing from full conjugation)
questions.explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion (6 pi electrons), tropylium cation (6 pi electrons), and cyclopropenyl cation (2 pi electrons) all satisfy Huckel's rule (4n+2) with full conjugation and are aromatic. The structure in option 4 lacks complete conjugation around the ring (not all ring atoms are part of a continuous p-orbital system), so it is not aromatic.

questions.text: What is the change in oxidation number of carbon in the following reaction? CH4(g) + 4Cl2(g) → CCl4(l) + 4HCl(g)
questions.topic: Change in oxidation number in a halogenation reaction
questions.explanation: In CH4, carbon has an oxidation state of -4. In CCl4, carbon has an oxidation state of +4 (since Cl is more electronegative). The oxidation number of carbon changes from -4 to +4.

questions.text: Reaction between benzaldehyde and acetophenone in presence of dilute NaOH is known as:
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde (no alpha hydrogen) reacting with acetophenone (has alpha hydrogens) in the presence of dilute NaOH undergoes a crossed aldol condensation, where the enolate of acetophenone attacks the carbonyl of benzaldehyde.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for graphical representation of Boyle's law, which shows a graph of pressure vs. volume of a gas at different temperature.
options: Hyperbolic curves with 600K outermost (highest P,V values) and 200K innermost, labeled 600K above 400K above 200K
Hyperbolic curves with 200K outermost and 600K innermost, labeled 200K above 400K above 600K
Horizontal straight line labeled (200K, 400K, 600K) all overlapping
Straight lines from origin with slopes for 200K, 400K, 600K
questions.explanation: PV=nRT, so P∝T at constant V. At a given V, P1>P2>P3 corresponds to T1>T2>T3, so the curve for 600K lies above (outermost) and 200K lies below (innermost), giving nested hyperbolas labeled 600K, 400K, 200K from top to bottom.

questions.text: Mass of one Fe atom is 9.27 × 10⁻23 g. Considering the reaction, 4Fe(s) + 3O2(g) → 2Fe2O3(g), which of the following statements is correct?
options: Total mass of Fe and O2 involved in the reaction is conserved and equals the mass of Fe2O3 formed, as per the law of conservation of mass.
Reaction follows law of multiple proportions.
Amount of Fe2O3 increases if excess of O2 is taken.
Amount of Fe2O3 formed decreases if the amount of oxygen is increased.
questions.explanation: This reaction simply illustrates the law of conservation of mass: the total mass of reactants (Fe + O2) equals the total mass of the product (Fe2O3) formed.

questions.text: An increase in the concentration of the reactants of a reaction leads to change in:
questions.topic: Effect of concentration on rate (collision theory)
questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of reactants increases the number of molecules per unit volume, leading to a higher collision frequency between reacting molecules, which increases the rate of reaction, without changing activation energy, threshold energy, or heat of reaction.

questions.text: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia through Haber's process is:
