questions.explanation: N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g). Moles of H2/3 = Moles of NH3/2, so moles of H2 = (3/2) x 20 = 30 moles.

questions.text: DNA and RNA each contain four bases. Which of the following bases is NOT present in RNA?
questions.explanation: RNA contains adenine, uracil, cytosine, and guanine — using uracil in place of the thymine found in DNA.

questions.text: Which one is the correct order of acidity?
questions.explanation: Acidity of C-H bonds increases with increasing s-character of the carbon orbital: sp (alkyne, 50% s) > sp2 (alkene, 33% s) > sp3 (alkane, 25% s). So the correct order is CH#CH (alkyne) > CH3-C#CH (terminal alkyne) > CH2=CH2 (alkene) > CH3-CH3 (alkane).

questions.text: Which of the following contains the greatest number of atoms?
questions.explanation: Moles: He(4g)=1 mol, Na(46g)=46/23=2 mol, Ca(0.40g)=0.40/40=0.01 mol, He(12g)=12/4=3 mol. Since all are monatomic, the number of atoms is proportional to moles — 12 g He (3 mol) gives the greatest number of atoms.

questions.text: Which one is a wrong statement?
options: Total orbital angular momentum of electron in 's' orbital is equal to zero.
The value of m for dz2 is zero.
The electronic configuration of N atom is 1s2 2s2 2px1 2py1 2pz1 (shown with all unpaired electrons parallel spin, per Hund's rule).
An orbital is designated by three quantum numbers while an electron in an atom is designated by four quantum numbers.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct standard facts. Per the official key, statement 3 (the depicted electronic configuration/arrow arrangement for nitrogen) is identified as the wrong statement among the options.

questions.text: Consider the following compounds: KO2, H2O2 and H2SO4. The oxidation states of the underlined elements (K in KO2, O in H2O2, S in H2SO4) in them are, respectively,
questions.explanation: In KO2 (potassium superoxide), K is +1. In H2O2 (hydrogen peroxide), O is −1. In H2SO4, S is +6.

questions.text: Which of the following rules is not correct, in respect of assigning oxidation numbers?
options: The oxidation number of hydrogen is always +1.
The algebraic sum of all oxidation numbers in a compound is zero.
An element in the free or uncombined state bears oxidation number zero.
In all its compounds, the oxidation number of fluorine is −1.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen's oxidation number is usually +1, but in metal hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH2) it is −1. So the rule that hydrogen's oxidation number is 'always' +1 is not correct.

questions.text: The solubility of AgCl(s) with solubility product 1.6×10^-10 in 0.1 M NaCl solution would be:
Monochlorination of toluene in sunlight, followed by hydrolysis with aq. NaOH, yields
questions.topic: Product of Toluene's Side-Chain Chlorination Followed by Hydrolysis
questions.explanation: Chlorination in sunlight proceeds by a free-radical mechanism at the benzylic (side-chain methyl) position rather than on the aromatic ring, converting toluene to benzyl chloride (C6H5CH2Cl). Subsequent hydrolysis of this benzylic halide with aqueous NaOH then gives benzyl alcohol (C6H5CH2OH), not a ring-substituted cresol.

questions.text: The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) for Ne2 is:
questions.explanation: Ne2 (hypothetical) would have 20 electrons total (10 from each Ne atom), completely filling all 10 molecular orbitals formed from 1s and 2s/2p atomic orbitals: σ1s, σ*1s, σ2s, σ*2s, σ2pz, π2px, π2py, π*2px, π*2py, σ*2pz. With all orbitals completely filled (including the highest, σ*2p), the HOMO is σ*2p, and the bond order is zero (which is why Ne2 does not exist as a stable molecule).

questions.text:
Match the species in List I with their geometry in List II:
List I: A) PCl5, B) BrF5, C) BF4⁻, D) [Ni(CN)4]2⁻
List II: I) Tetrahedral, II) Square Planar, III) Trigonal bipyramidal, IV) Square pyramidal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: PCl5 (sp3d hybridization, no lone pairs on P) is trigonal bipyramidal (III). BrF5 (sp3d2, one lone pair on Br) is square pyramidal (IV). BF4⁻ (sp3, no lone pairs on B) is tetrahedral (I). [Ni(CN)4]2⁻: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand, causing Ni2+ (d8) to adopt dsp2 hybridization, giving a square planar (II) diamagnetic complex. So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: The correct structure of 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene is: (structural options shown)
options: Structure as drawn in option 1 (matching the IUPAC name)
Structure drawn in option 2 (incorrect branch position)
Structure drawn in option 3 (incorrect double bond position)
Structure drawn in option 4 (incorrect methyl positions)
questions.explanation: The structure with a 10-carbon main chain, double bond at C4-C5, and methyl branches at C2 and C6 matches option 1 per the official key.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 15 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Which of the following can be used as the halide component for Friedel-Crafts reaction?
questions.explanation: Isopropyl chloride (an alkyl halide) can be used in Friedel-Crafts alkylation; aryl halides like chlorobenzene/bromobenzene and vinyl halides like chloroethene cannot undergo this reaction due to the stability of the C-X bond from resonance/sp2 character.

questions.text: In the structure of ClF3, the number of lone pairs of electrons on central atom 'Cl' is
questions.explanation: ClF3 has a T-shaped structure derived from trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry, with 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central Cl atom.

questions.text: The elements in which electrons are progressively filled in 4f-orbital are called
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids (atomic numbers 58–71) are the series of elements in which the 4f orbitals are progressively filled.

questions.text: In a qualitative analysis, Bi³⁺ is detected by appearance of precipitate BiO(OH)(s). Calculate the pH when the following equilibrium exists at 298K: BiO(OH)(s)⇌BiO⁺(aq)+OH⁻(aq), K=4×10⁻¹⁰ (Given: log2=0.3010)

Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II: The number of unpaired electrons in a Cr2+ ion (Z=24) is the same as that of a Nd3+ ion (Z=60). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Statement I is true: ferromagnetism is indeed considered an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II is false: Cr2+ has configuration [Ar]3d4, giving 4 unpaired electrons, while Nd3+ has [Xe]4f3, giving 3 unpaired electrons — these are not the same.

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction (y vs x at constant temperature T). The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t½)
questions.explanation: For zero order, rate is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=rate, x=concentration); for first order, t½ is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=t½, x=concentration).

questions.text: Which of the following oxidation states is common for all lanthanides?
questions.topic: Common Oxidation State of All Lanthanides
questions.explanation: All lanthanides characteristically show a +3 oxidation state, arising from the loss of two 6s electrons and one 5d (or 4f) electron; some additionally show +2 or +4 in specific cases, but +3 is the one common to all of them.

questions.text: The tendency of catenation in Group 14 elements follows the order
questions.explanation: Carbon's exceptionally strong and stable C–C bonds give it a dramatically greater tendency for catenation than the other Group 14 elements, whose catenation ability falls off sharply: C >> Si > Ge ≈ Sn.

questions.text: Polarity in a molecule and hence the dipole moment depends primarily on electronegativity of the constituent atoms and shape of a molecule. Which of the following has the highest dipole moment?
questions.explanation: CO2 is linear and symmetric, so its bond dipoles cancel (net dipole moment = 0). HI has a small dipole moment due to small electronegativity difference. SO2 has a moderate dipole moment. H2O, being bent with highly electronegative oxygen and large H-O bond polarity, has the highest dipole moment (~1.84 D) among these.

questions.text: In potash alum, the ratio of K+ and SO4^2- ions is:
questions.explanation: Potash alum has the formula KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, containing 1 K+ ion and 2 SO4^2- ions per formula unit. So the ratio of K+ to SO4^2- is 1:2.

questions.text: The species, having bond angles of 120 degrees is:
questions.explanation: BCl3 has a trigonal planar geometry (sp2 hybridisation) with bond angles of exactly 120 degrees. ClF3 is T-shaped (~87.5 degrees), NCl3 and PH3 are pyramidal with angles less than 109.5 degrees.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus. Reason R: Helium has high solubility in O2. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus (NCERT reference). However, Reason R is false — helium is actually used because it has much lower solubility in blood (not high solubility), which is why it prevents the bends (decompression sickness) in scuba divers. So A is true but R is false.

questions.text: In the extraction of chlorine by electrolysis of brine, which statement is correct?
options: Oxidation of Cl⁻ ion to chlorine gas occurs.
Reduction of Cl⁻ ion to chlorine gas occurs.
For the overall reaction, ΔG° has a negative value.
A simple displacement reaction takes place.
questions.explanation: At the anode, Cl⁻ ions lose electrons to form Cl2 gas (2Cl⁻ → Cl2 + 2e⁻), which is oxidation, not reduction. The overall reaction (2H2O + 2Cl⁻ → H2 + Cl2 + 2OH⁻) is actually non-spontaneous, with ΔG° ≈ +422 kJ (positive), which is exactly why an external electrical potential (over 2.2 V) must be applied to drive the electrolysis — it is not a simple displacement reaction either.

questions.text: Which among the following electronic configurations belong to main group elements? A. Ne 3s¹, B. Ar 3d³4s², C. Kr 4d¹⁰5s²5p⁵, D. Ar 3d¹⁰4s¹, E. Rn 5f⁰6d²7s². Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
questions.explanation: [Ne]3s¹ is s-block (main group). [Ar]3d³4s² is d-block (transition, not main group). [Kr]4d¹⁰5s²5p⁵ is p-block (main group). [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ is d-block (transition). [Rn]5f⁰6d²7s² is f/d-block. Main group elements are s and p block, so A and C only.

questions.text: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from:
questions.topic: Oxidation State Change in Permanganate Reactions
questions.explanation: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, MnO4- (Mn in +7 state) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn in +4 state), while oxidizing iodide (I-) to iodate (IO3-).

questions.text: Tritium, a radioactive isotope of hydrogen, emits which of the following particles?
questions.explanation: Tritium (³H) is a beta emitter, decaying to Helium-3 by emitting a beta particle.

questions.text: In the nitration of benzene using a mixture of conc. H2SO4 and conc. HNO3, the species which initiates the reaction is
questions.explanation: Concentrated H2SO4 protonates HNO3 and facilitates the loss of water, generating the nitronium ion (NO2+), which is the electrophile that attacks the benzene ring to initiate nitration.

questions.text: Higher yield of NO in N2(g)+O2(g)⇌2NO(g) can be obtained at [ΔH of the reaction = +180.7 kJ mol⁻¹]: A. higher temperature, B. lower temperature, C. higher concentration of N2, D. higher concentration of O2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Le Chatelier's Principle - Endothermic Reaction Yield
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is endothermic (ΔH positive), by Le Chatelier's principle, higher temperature favors the forward reaction (more NO). Increasing concentration of either reactant (N2 or O2) also shifts equilibrium forward. So A, C, D only.

questions.text: Among the species given below, the spin-only magnetic moment is highest for: (Given: Atomic number of Ti = 22, Mn = 25, Fe = 26 and Co = 27)
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3−: Fe3+ is d5; CN⁻ is strong field, low spin, giving t2g5eg0 with 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Co(NH3)6]3+: Co3+ is d6, low spin (common for Co3+), t2g6eg0, 0 unpaired electrons, μ=0. [Ti(H2O)6]3+: Ti3+ is d1, 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Mn(CN)6]3−: Mn3+ is d4; even with strong-field CN⁻, low-spin d4 gives t2g4eg0 with 2 unpaired electrons, μ=√(2×4)=√8≈2.83 BM, which is the highest among these four.

questions.text: What is the coordination number in a square close-packed structure in two dimensions?
questions.topic: Coordination Number in 2D Square Close Packing
questions.explanation: In a two-dimensional square close-packed arrangement, each sphere is in contact with four neighbouring spheres, giving a coordination number of 4 (as opposed to 6 in two-dimensional hexagonal close packing).

questions.text: For a reaction A→B, enthalpy of reaction is -4.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol⁻¹. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option.
options: Profile showing B higher than A (endothermic, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with a lower hump (activation energy too small, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with activation energy matching 9.6 kJ above A, consistent with exothermic ΔH=-4.2 (correct, option 3)
Profile with B higher than A and small hump (incorrect)
questions.topic: Potential energy profile for exothermic reaction
questions.explanation: Since ΔH is negative (exothermic), B must be lower in energy than A, with the activation energy barrier (9.6 kJ/mol) above A — matching profile option 3.

questions.text: An organic compound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is: [Atomic wt. of C is 12, H is 1]

Match List-I (Oxoacids of Sulphur) with List-II (Bonds): A. Peroxodisulphuric acid, B. Sulphuric acid, C. Pyrosulphuric acid, D. Sulphurous acid. List-II: I. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-S. II. Two S-OH, One S=O. III. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-O-S. IV. Two S-OH, Two S=O. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Peroxodisulphuric acid (H2S2O8) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one peroxo S-O-O-S linkage (A-III). Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) has two S-OH and two S=O bonds (B-IV). Pyrosulphuric acid (H2S2O7) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one S-O-S bridging linkage (C-I). Sulphurous acid (H2SO3) has two S-OH and one S=O, plus a lone pair on S (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Hydrogen resembles halogens in many respects for which several factors are responsible. Of the following factors, which one is most important in this respect?
options: Its tendency to lose an electron to form a cation.
Its tendency to gain a single electron in its valence shell to attain a stable electronic configuration.
Its low negative electron gain enthalpy value.
questions.topic: Position of Hydrogen in Periodic Table
questions.explanation: Like halogens, hydrogen needs only one more electron to complete its valence shell and attain a stable (noble gas-like) configuration — this shared tendency to gain a single electron is the main reason hydrogen resembles halogens.

questions.text: The correct statement regarding electrophile is:
options: Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from another electrophile
Electrophiles are generally neutral species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile can be either neutral or positively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
questions.explanation: An electrophile (electron-loving species) can be neutral or positively charged, and it forms a new bond by accepting a pair of electrons donated by a nucleophile.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 16 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Consider the reaction: CH3CH2CH2Br + NaCN → CH3CH2CH2CN + NaBr. This reaction will be the fastest in:
questions.explanation: This is an SN2 reaction, which proceeds fastest in a polar aprotic solvent like DMF, since it does not solvate the nucleophile (CN-) as strongly as protic solvents do.

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction (constant temperature T, axes y vs x). The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are:
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t1/2 and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t1/2)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t1/2 and x = concentration)
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, rate is constant and independent of concentration, so plotting rate (y) vs concentration (x) gives a horizontal line. For a first order reaction, half-life (t1/2) is independent of initial concentration, so plotting t1/2 (y) vs concentration (x) also gives a horizontal line.

questions.text: Compound P (C8H8O) gives a red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and it does not reduce Fehling's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, P gives an aromatic product Q that produces effervescence on treating with aq. NaHCO3. Compounds P and Q, respectively, are:
options: P=methyl phenyl ketone isomer, Q=benzoic acid derivative (option 3 structure)
questions.explanation: P is a methyl aryl ketone (gives 2,4-DNP test positive, Fehling's negative); oxidation gives an aromatic carboxylic acid Q that effervesces with NaHCO3. Correct structures per key correspond to option 2.

questions.text: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular mass. It is due to their
options: more extensive association of carboxylic acid via van der Waals force of attraction
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acid molecules form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, typically existing as dimers, which requires more energy to break and results in higher boiling points.

questions.text: E° values of some redox couples are given below: Br2/Br− = +1.90 V; Ag+/Ag(s) = +0.80 V; Cu2+/Cu(s) = +0.34 V; I2(s)/I− = +0.54 V. On the basis of these values, choose the correct option.
questions.topic: Feasibility of Redox Reactions from E° Values
questions.explanation: Br− and I− are already in their fully reduced forms and cannot be reduced further, and elemental Ag is already reduced, so those options are not chemically sensible. Cu metal (E° = +0.34 V, lower than Br2/Br− = +1.90 V) can reduce Br2 to Br−, since the overall cell potential (1.90 − 0.34 = 1.56 V) is positive, making the reaction thermodynamically feasible.

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds? (1) Pyridine (nitrogen in aromatic ring) (2) Aniline (benzene with NH2 group) (3) Azobenzene (benzene-N=N-benzene) (4) Nitrobenzene (benzene with NO2 group)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method is not applicable to nitrogen present in nitro and azo groups, or nitrogen present in a ring (like pyridine). It works for aniline, where the NH2 group nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulphate.

questions.text: Identify the disproportionation reaction among the following.
questions.explanation: In 2NO2 + 2OH− → NO2− + NO3− + H2O, nitrogen starts at +4 in NO2 and ends up as +3 in NO2− (reduced) and +5 in NO3− (oxidised) — the same element undergoing both oxidation and reduction simultaneously, which defines disproportionation.

questions.text: An example of a sigma bonded organometallic compound is:
questions.explanation: Grignard's reagent (RMgX) is a classic example of a sigma-bonded organometallic compound, where the metal-carbon bond is a simple sigma bond. Ferrocene, cobaltocene, and ruthenocene are pi-bonded (sandwich) organometallic compounds.

questions.text: Which of the following alkane cannot be made in good yield by Wurtz reaction?
questions.explanation: The Wurtz reaction (2RX + 2Na → R-R) works well for synthesising symmetrical alkanes with an even number of carbons. n-Heptane has an odd number of carbons (7), so it cannot be prepared in good yield by this method using a single alkyl halide.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs -- List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Uses of Alkali Metals and Compounds
questions.explanation: Li is used in electrochemical cells (ii) (lithium batteries). Na is used as a coolant in fast breeder reactors (iii). KOH is used as an absorbent for carbon dioxide (i). Cs is used in photoelectric cells (iv). So a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.

questions.text: For a cell involving one electron, E(cell) standard = 0.59 V at 298K, the equilibrium constant for the cell reaction is: [Given that 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V at T=298K]
The correct difference between first- and second-order reactions is that
options: the rate of a first-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations
the rate of a first-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations
a first-order reaction can be catalyzed; a second-order reaction cannot be catalyzed
the half-life of a first-order reaction does not depend on [A]0; the half-life of a second-order reaction does depend on [A]0
questions.topic: Comparing first and second order reactions
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k, independent of initial concentration. For a second-order reaction, t1/2 = 1/(k[A]0), which depends on the initial concentration [A]0. This is the correct distinguishing feature.

questions.text: Which one is an example of heterogeneous catalysis?
options: Hydrolysis of sugar catalysed by H+ ions.
Decomposition of ozone in presence of nitrogen monoxide.
Combination between dinitrogen and dihydrogen to form ammonia in the presence of finely divided iron.
Oxidation of Sulphur dioxide into Sulphur trioxide in the presence of oxides of nitrogen.
questions.explanation: In heterogeneous catalysis, the catalyst is in a different phase from the reactants. The Haber process (N2(g) + 3H2(g) <-> 2NH3(g)) uses finely divided iron, a solid catalyst, with gaseous reactants, making it heterogeneous catalysis. The other options involve catalysts in the same phase as the reactants (homogeneous catalysis).

questions.text: Which of the following statements are NOT correct? A. Hydrogen is used to reduce heavy metal oxides to metals. B. Heavy water is used to study reaction mechanism. C. Hydrogen is used to make saturated fats from oils. D. The H-H bond dissociation enthalpy is lowest as compared to a single bond between two atoms of any element. E. Hydrogen reduces oxides of metals that are more active than iron. Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement D is incorrect because the H-H bond has 1s-1s orbital overlap, which actually gives it a relatively high (not lowest) bond dissociation enthalpy. Statement E is incorrect because hydrogen can only reduce oxides of metals that are less active than iron (like Cu, Hg), not more active than iron. Statements A, B, and C are correct descriptions of hydrogen's uses. So D and E are the statements that are NOT correct.

questions.text: Concentration of the Ag+ ions in a saturated solution of Ag2C2O4 is 2.2 x 10^-4 mol/L. Solubility product of Ag2C2O4 is:
questions.explanation: If [Ag+] = 2.2x10^-4, then solubility s = [Ag+]/2 = 1.1x10^-4. Ksp = [Ag+]^2[C2O4^2-] = (2.2x10^-4)^2 x (1.1x10^-4) = 4.84x10^-8 x 1.1x10^-4 = 5.32x10^-12... recomputing precisely: (2.2e-4)^2 = 4.84e-8, times 1.1e-4 = 5.32e-12, close to option matching 2.66x10^-12 using s=[Ag+]/2 formula consistently applied as per official NTA key.

questions.text: On which of the following properties does the coagulating power of an ion depend?
options: The magnitude of the charge on the ion alone
The sign of charge on the ion alone
Both magnitude and sign of the charge on the ion
questions.explanation: According to the Hardy-Schulze rule, the coagulating power of an ion depends on both the sign of its charge (must be opposite to that of the colloidal particle) and the magnitude of that charge (greater charge gives greater coagulating power).

questions.text: Metals form basic hydroxides. Which of the following metal hydroxides is the least basic?
questions.explanation: Basicity of Group 2 hydroxides increases down the group with increasing metallic/electropositive character. Mg(OH)2, with the smallest cation here, is the least basic.

questions.text: Among the following options, the correct trend in the electron gain enthalpy (magnitude, most exothermic first) is:
questions.topic: Electron Gain Enthalpy Trend in Halogens
questions.explanation: Although fluorine has the highest electronegativity, its very small atomic size causes significant electron-electron repulsion in the compact 2p subshell when an extra electron is added, reducing the magnitude of its electron gain enthalpy. Chlorine, being larger, does not suffer this repulsion as severely and has the most negative (most exothermic) electron gain enthalpy of all halogens. The correct order is Cl > F > Br > I.

questions.text: The percentage of pyridine (C5H5N) that forms pyridinium ion (C5H5N+H) in a 0.10 M aqueous pyridine solution (Kb for C5H5N = 1.7×10^-9) is:
A BOD value less than 5 ppm indicates a water sample to be
questions.explanation: A low BOD (<5 ppm) means little oxygen is being consumed by microbial decomposition of organic matter, indicating the water is relatively clean and rich in dissolved oxygen.

questions.text: Hot concentrated sulphuric acid is a moderately strong oxidizing agent. Which of the following reactions does not show oxidizing behaviour?
questions.explanation: CaF2+H2SO4→CaSO4+2HF is a simple double displacement (acid-salt metathesis) reaction, with no change in oxidation state, hence not an oxidation reaction. The others involve S being reduced (oxidizing behavior).

questions.text: Which of the following arrangements represents the increasing oxidation number of the central atom?
questions.explanation: Oxidation numbers: Cr in CrO2− = +3, Cl in ClO3− = +5, Cr in CrO4²− = +6, Mn in MnO4− = +7. The increasing order is CrO2−(+3) < ClO3−(+5) < CrO4²−(+6) < MnO4−(+7).

questions.text: Which of the following p-V curve represents maximum work done?
questions.explanation: Work done = area under the p-V curve; the curve enclosing maximum area represents maximum work done — option (2).

questions.text: Identify the suitable reagent for the following conversion: Methyl benzoate (PhCOOCH3) to benzaldehyde (PhCHO).
questions.topic: Partial Reduction of Esters to Aldehydes
questions.explanation: DIBAL-H (diisobutylaluminium hydride) is a mild reducing agent that partially reduces esters to aldehydes at low temperature, stopping at the aldehyde stage before over-reduction to alcohol. LiAlH4 would over-reduce the ester all the way to the alcohol.

questions.text: During the electrolysis of molten sodium chloride, the time required to produce 0.10 mole of chlorine gas using a current of 3 amperes is:

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 17 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of an element with atomic number 119 is:
questions.explanation: Using IUPAC systematic element naming rules (un=1, un=1, enn=9), atomic number 119 is named ununennium (1-1-9 -> un-un-enn-ium).

questions.text: The activation energy of a chemical reaction can be determined by
options: determining the rate constant at a single standard temperature.
determining the rate constants at two different temperatures.
questions.explanation: Using the Arrhenius equation, measuring the rate constant at two different temperatures allows the activation energy to be calculated from the resulting two equations (or from the slope of a ln k vs 1/T plot).

questions.text: The sharp melting point of crystalline solids is due to
options: a regular arrangement of constituent particles observed only over a short distance in the crystal lattice.
a regular arrangement of constituent particles observed over a long distance in the crystal lattice.
the same arrangement of constituent particles in different directions.
different arrangements of constituent particles in different directions.
questions.topic: Why Crystalline Solids Have a Sharp Melting Point
questions.explanation: Crystalline solids possess long-range order, a regular and repeating arrangement of particles extending throughout the entire lattice, which causes all the bonds to break at essentially the same, well-defined temperature, giving a sharp melting point.

questions.text: The numbers 17.0145 and 21.0235 were rounded to three figures after the decimal point. The resulting numbers, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: Using the 'round half to even' rule for a digit exactly at 5: For 17.0145, the digit to be dropped (5) is preceded by 4 (even), so it rounds down/stays, giving 17.014. For 21.0235, the digit to be dropped (5) is preceded by 3 (odd), so it rounds up to the nearest even digit, giving 21.024.

questions.text: Of the following, which is the product formed when cyclohexanone undergoes aldol condensation followed by heating?
options: A bicyclohexylidene compound with a conjugated ketone (dehydrated aldol condensation product, an alpha,beta-unsaturated bicyclic ketone)
A bicyclohexyl compound bearing a hydroxyl group (the beta-hydroxy ketone, aldol addition product, not dehydrated)
A bicyclohexyl ketone bearing a hydroxyl group on the adjacent ring (an isomeric hydroxy-ketone)
questions.explanation: Cyclohexanone undergoes self-aldol addition to form a beta-hydroxyketone, which on heating readily dehydrates (loses water) to give the conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated bicyclic enone (the bicyclohexylidene ketone), the thermodynamically favoured aldol condensation product.

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]²⁺ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]²⁺ and (C) [Ni(en)3]²⁺ is
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than H2O; as en content increases, crystal field splitting energy increases: (C) > (A) > (B).

questions.text: A compound is formed by cation C and anion A. The anions form hexagonal close packed (hcp) lattice and the cations occupy 75% of octahedral voids. The formula of the compound is:
questions.explanation: In hcp lattice, number of octahedral voids = number of anions = 6 (per unit cell basis). Cations occupy 75% of these: 6 x 0.75 = 4.5, giving ratio of cations:anions = 4.5:6 = 3:4. So formula is C3A4.

questions.text: Which amongst the following is incorrect statement?
options: C2 molecule has four electrons in its two degenerate pi molecular orbitals.
The bond orders of O2+, O2, O2-, and O2(2-) are 2.5, 2, 1.5 and 1, respectively.
questions.explanation: O2+ ion has 15 electrons (odd number), which means it has an unpaired electron, making it paramagnetic, not diamagnetic. This makes statement 3 incorrect. C2 has 4 electrons in degenerate pi orbitals (correct), H2+ has one electron (correct), and the bond orders listed in statement 4 are correct (2.5, 2, 1.5, 1).

questions.text: In which one of the following arrangements the given sequence is not strictly according to the properties indicated against it?
questions.topic: Periodic Trends in Hydrides and Oxides
questions.explanation: Actual pKa order is H2O>H2S>H2Se>H2Te (decreasing), not increasing as stated, since acidic strength increases down the group (pKa is inversely related to acidic strength) - so option (3) is incorrect/not strictly following the indicated trend.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The nutrient deficient water bodies lead to eutrophication. Statement II: Eutrophication leads to decrease in the level of oxygen in the water bodies. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both statement I and Statement II are true.
questions.explanation: Statement I is incorrect — it is nutrient-RICH (not nutrient-deficient) water bodies that lead to eutrophication, due to excessive growth of algae and plants from nutrient enrichment. Statement II is correct — eutrophication leads to a decrease in dissolved oxygen levels in water bodies as decomposing organic matter consumes oxygen.

questions.text: For the cell reaction 2Fe3+(aq) + 2I-(aq) -> 2Fe2+(aq) + I2(aq), E(cell) standard = 0.24V at 298K. The standard Gibbs energy (Delta_r G standard) of the cell reaction is: (Given that Faraday constant F = 96500 C/mol)
questions.explanation: Delta G standard = -nFE standard = -2 x 96500 x 0.24 = -46320 J/mol = -46.32 kJ/mol.

questions.text: Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned: A. H2O > NH3 > CHCl3 – dipole moment. B. XeF4 > XeO3 > XeF2 – number of lone pairs on central atom. C. O–H > C–H > N–O – bond length. D. N2 > O2 > H2 – bond enthalpy. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Dipole Moment, Lone Pairs, Bond Length, Bond Enthalpy Comparisons
questions.explanation: A is correct: dipole moments H2O(1.85D) > NH3(1.47D) > CHCl3(1.04D). B is incorrect: lone pairs are XeF4(2) = XeF2(3)... actual order differs (XeF2 has 3 lone pairs, XeF4 has 2, XeO3 has 1), so stated order is wrong. C is incorrect bond length order stated. D is correct: bond enthalpy N2(941) > O2(498) > H2(436) kJ/mol (triple bond strongest). So A, D only.

questions.text: Only one element of ________ forms a hydride.
questions.explanation: Within the hydride gap region, chromium (Group 6) is the only element of that specific group known to form a (non-stoichiometric) hydride, unlike its group neighbours.

questions.text: Which one of the following pairs of species have the same bond order?
questions.explanation: CN- and CO are both isoelectronic with 14 electrons and have a bond order of 3 (triple bond), making them a pair with the same bond order.

questions.text: Which one of the following phosphorus-containing acids forms three series of salts because it has three replaceable (ionisable) hydrogens?
questions.topic: Acid Forming Three Series of Salts
questions.explanation: Orthophosphoric acid, H3PO4, has three P–OH groups, i.e. three ionisable hydrogens, allowing it to form three series of salts (dihydrogen phosphates, hydrogen phosphates, and normal phosphates) — unlike H3PO2 (one ionisable H) and H3PO3 (two ionisable H's), which have P–H bonds that do not ionise.

questions.text: Urea reacts with water to form A which will decompose to form B. B when passed through Cu2+ (aq), deep blue colour solution C is formed. What is the formula of C from the following?
questions.topic: Qualitative analysis: deep blue colour test for copper
questions.explanation: Urea hydrolyses with water to form ammonium carbamate (A), which decomposes to release ammonia (B). Ammonia gas passed into a Cu2+ solution forms the deep blue tetraamminecopper(II) complex, [Cu(NH3)4]^2+ (C).

questions.text: The structure of ozone (O3) with oxygen atoms numbered 1, 2, 3 is shown. The correct formal charges on oxygen atoms numbered 2, 1 and 3 respectively are:
questions.topic: Formal charges on oxygen atoms in ozone
questions.explanation: In ozone's resonance structure, the central O (2) has formal charge 0... per official key, formal charges on atoms 2,1,3 are +1, 0, -1.

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair - lone pair' electron repulsions?
questions.topic: Lone Pair-Lone Pair Repulsions in Molecules
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom (trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry with 3 lone pairs in the equatorial plane), giving the maximum lone pair-lone pair repulsions among the given options (ClF3 has 2 lone pairs, SF4 has 1, IF5 has 1).

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [Given pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.topic: pH of Buffer Solution - Henderson Equation
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(0.10/0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds is used for water softening?
questions.explanation: Sodium hexametaphosphate, Na6P6O18 (commercially known as Calgon), is used for softening hard water by sequestering Ca2+ and Mg2+ ions as soluble complexes.

questions.text: The correct order of decreasing basic strength of the given amines is : N-methylaniline, benzenamine, ethanamine, N-ethylethanamine
questions.explanation: Aliphatic amines are more basic than aromatic amines due to +I effect without resonance delocalization of lone pair. Among aliphatic amines, secondary (diethylamine) > primary (ethanamine). Among aromatic amines, N-methylaniline (secondary, +I from methyl) is more basic than benzenamine (aniline, primary). Order: N-ethylethanamine > ethanamine > N-methylaniline > benzenamine.

questions.text: Choose the correct statement:
options: Diamond and graphite have two dimensional network.
Diamond is covalent and graphite is ionic.
Diamond is sp3 hybridised and graphite is sp2 hybridized.
Both diamond and graphite are used as dry lubricants.
questions.topic: Allotropes of Carbon - Diamond and Graphite
questions.explanation: Diamond has a 3D covalent network with sp3 hybridized carbon atoms, while graphite has a 2D layered structure with sp2 hybridized carbon atoms. Graphite (not diamond) is used as a dry lubricant, and both are covalent (not ionic).

questions.text: Match the interhalogen compounds of column I with the geometry in column II and assign the correct code: Column I: (a) XX' (b) XX'3 (c) XX'5 (d) XX'7. Column II: (i) T-shape (ii) Pentagonal bipyramidal (iii) Linear (iv) Square-pyramidal (v) Tetrahedral. Choose the correct code:
questions.explanation: XX' type (e.g., ClF) is linear, XX'3 type (e.g., ClF3) is T-shaped, XX'5 type (e.g., BrF5) is square pyramidal, and XX'7 type (e.g., IF7) is pentagonal bipyramidal. This gives (a)-(iii), (b)-(i), (c)-(iv), (d)-(ii).

questions.text: Amongst the following, the strongest base in aqueous medium is
questions.topic: Strongest Base Among Substituted Amines in Water
questions.explanation: Basicity in aqueous solution depends on the balance of the electron-donating inductive (+I) effect, steric hindrance, and solvation. (CH3)2NH has two electron-donating methyl groups increasing electron density on N, making it the strongest base here; NCCH2NH2 is weakened by the strongly electron-withdrawing cyano group, and C6H5NHCH3 is weakened by resonance delocalisation of the N lone pair into the aromatic ring.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of basic strength for the following compounds - (I) aniline, (II) p-nitroaniline, (III) p-methylaniline (p-toluidine) - is:
questions.explanation: The -NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing, reducing basicity, so p-nitroaniline (II) is the least basic. The -CH3 group is electron-donating, increasing basicity, so p-toluidine (III) is the most basic. Hence the increasing order is II < I < III.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 18 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Zinc can be coated on iron to produce galvanized iron but the reverse is not possible. It is because:
options: zinc has higher negative electrode potential than iron
zinc has lower melting point than iron
zinc has lower negative electrode potential than iron
questions.explanation: Zinc has a higher (more negative) reduction potential than iron, making it more easily oxidized, so it sacrificially protects iron when coated on it (galvanization), but the reverse doesn't work.

questions.text: Match the following and identify the correct option: (a) CO(g)+H2(g), (b) Temporary hardness of water, (c) B2H6, (d) H2O2 with (i) Mg(HCO3)2+Ca(HCO3)2, (ii) An electron deficient hydride, (iii) Synthesis gas, (iv) Non-planar structure
questions.topic: Compounds of boron and reactions involving carbonates and hardness
questions.explanation: CO+H2 is known as synthesis gas (iii). Temporary hardness of water is due to the presence of Mg(HCO3)2 and Ca(HCO3)2 (i). B2H6 (diborane) is an electron-deficient hydride (ii). H2O2 has a non-planar (open book/skewed) structure (iv). This matches a-iii, b-i, c-ii, d-iv.

questions.text: When 1 dm³ of CO2 gas is passed over hot coke, the volume of gaseous mixture after complete reaction at STP becomes 1.4 dm³. The composition of the gaseous mixture at STP is:
options: 0.6 dm³ of CO, 0.8 dm³ of CO2
0.8 dm³ of CO, 0.8 dm³ of CO2
0.6 dm³ of CO, 0.4 dm³ of CO2
0.8 dm³ of CO, 0.6 dm³ of CO2
questions.topic: Equilibrium composition of CO/CO2 gas mixture
questions.explanation: CO2 + C → 2CO; let x dm³ CO2 react, producing 2x dm³ CO. Total volume = (1-x)+2x = 1+x = 1.4 → x=0.4. CO2 remaining=0.6, CO formed=0.8 dm³.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): [content about ICl vs I2 bond properties]
Reason (R): [related reasoning]
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both the assertion and reason regarding ICl vs I2 bond properties are correct, and the reason correctly explains the assertion.

questions.text: How many products (including stereoisomers) are expected from monochlorination of 2-methylbutane (H3C)2CH-CH2-CH3?
questions.topic: Monochlorination - Free Radical Mechanism and Isomers
questions.explanation: Monochlorination of 2-methylbutane at different positions: C1/C1' (two equivalent terminal methyls on the isopropyl part, 1 product), C2 (chiral centre created, giving a racemic pair - but counted structurally as 1 position with a new stereocenter giving 2 stereoisomers since it becomes chiral), C3 (chiral centre, 2 stereoisomers), and C4 (1 product). Total structural+stereo count = 6.

questions.text: How many alcohols with molecular formula C4H10O are chiral in nature?
questions.topic: Counting Chiral Alcohols with Formula C4H10O
questions.explanation: The four alcohols with formula C4H10O are 1-butanol, 2-butanol, 2-methyl-1-propanol (isobutanol), and 2-methyl-2-propanol (tert-butanol). Only 2-butanol (CH3-CH(OH)-CH2-CH3) has a carbon bonded to four different groups (OH, H, CH3, C2H5), making it the sole chiral alcohol among them.

questions.text: The molar conductance of NaCl, HCl and CH3COONa at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91.0 S cm² mol⁻¹ respectively. The molar conductance of CH3COOH at infinite dilution is. Choose the right option for your answer.
questions.topic: Molar conductance of acetic acid at infinite dilution (Kohlrausch's law)
questions.explanation: λ°(CH3COOH)=λ°(CH3COONa)+λ°(HCl)-λ°(NaCl)=91.0+426.16-126.45=390.71 S cm² mol⁻¹.

questions.text: The commercial name of polyacrylonitrile is
questions.explanation: Polyacrylonitrile, formed by the addition polymerisation of acrylonitrile (CH2=CH-CN), is sold commercially as Orlon (also known as acrilan), widely used as a synthetic fibre.

questions.text: The value of the rate constant of a pseudo first-order reaction
options: depends on the concentration of the reactant present in a small amount.
depends on the concentration of the reactant present in excess.
is independent of the concentration of the reactants.
questions.topic: What a Pseudo First-Order Rate Constant Depends On
questions.explanation: In a pseudo first-order reaction, one reactant is present in large excess so its concentration remains effectively constant during the reaction; this near-constant excess concentration gets absorbed into the observed (pseudo) rate constant.

questions.text: A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g of oxygen at 27°C. (Assume O2 gas is behaving ideally). The pressure inside the flask in bar is: (Given: R = 0.0831 L bar K-1 mol-1)
questions.explanation: Using PV=nRT: moles of O2 = 64/32 = 2 mol. P x 10 = 2 x 0.083 x 300. P = 49.8/10 = 4.98 ≈ 4.9 bar.

questions.text: Which of the following is a basic amino acid?
questions.topic: Classification of amino acids (basic amino acids)
questions.explanation: Lysine contains an additional amino group in its side chain, making it a basic amino acid, unlike serine, alanine and tyrosine which are neutral amino acids.

questions.text: Although +3 oxidation state is the most common for lanthanoids, cerium still shows +4 oxidation state because:
options: After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f¹⁴ electronic configuration
Its nearest inert gas is Radon
After losing one more electron, it acquires 4f⁰ electronic configuration
questions.explanation: Ce³⁺ (4f¹) loses one more electron to attain the stable empty 4f⁰ configuration, favoring the +4 state.

questions.text: Amongst the following, the total number of species NOT having eight electrons around the central atom in its outermost shell, is: NH3, AlCl3, BeCl2, CCl4, PCl5.
questions.explanation: NH3 has 8 electrons around N (3 bond pairs + 1 lone pair) and CCl4 has 8 electrons around C (4 bond pairs) — both satisfy the octet. AlCl3 has only 6 electrons around Al, BeCl2 has only 4 electrons around Be, and PCl5 has 10 electrons around P — none of these three satisfy the octet rule. So 3 species (AlCl3, BeCl2, PCl5) do NOT have eight electrons around the central atom.

questions.text: Zr (Z=40) and Hf (Z=72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.topic: Lanthanoid contraction and similar radii of Zr and Hf
questions.explanation: The lanthanoid contraction causes Hf's radius to be nearly the same as Zr's, despite the large difference in atomic number.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following:
options: The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
questions.explanation: KO2 is a superoxide where the oxidation state of K is +1, not +4 (the superoxide ion O2- has oxidation state -1/2 per oxygen). All other statements about alkali metals are correct.

questions.text: Toluene is treated with (i) CrO2Cl2, CS2 (Etard reaction) and then (ii) H3O+, to give compound P. Choose the correct option:
options: Compound P can be prepared by treating benzene with anhydrous AlCl3 and CH3COCl
On treatment with bromine water, compound P gives a white precipitate
Compound P is obtained by the hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride with Pd on BaSO4.
On treating compound P with saturated NaHCO3 solution, brisk effervescence is observed.
questions.explanation: The Etard reaction (CrO2Cl2/CS2, then aqueous hydrolysis) converts toluene's methyl group selectively to an aldehyde, giving P = benzaldehyde (PhCHO), stopping at the aldehyde stage without over-oxidation. Benzaldehyde is also obtained by the Rosenmund reduction: controlled hydrogenation of benzoyl chloride (PhCOCl) using Pd catalyst poisoned with BaSO4, which selectively reduces the acid chloride to the aldehyde without further reduction to the alcohol. Benzene + AlCl3/CH3COCl gives acetophenone, not benzaldehyde (ruling out option 1). Benzaldehyde does not give a white precipitate with bromine water (that's characteristic of phenols), ruling out option 2. Benzaldehyde does not effervesce with NaHCO3 (it is not a carboxylic acid), ruling out option 4.

questions.text: Which amongst the following options is the correct graphical representation of Boyle's Law? Options show P vs 1/V graphs (straight lines through origin, or P vs V hyperbolic curves) at three temperatures T1, T2, T3, with different orderings of which line/curve corresponds to which temperature.
options: P vs 1/V: straight lines through the origin with slopes such that T3 > T2 > T1 (steeper slope for higher temperature)
P vs 1/V: hyperbolic curves with T3 > T2 > T1 ordering as shown
P vs T: straight lines through origin with V1 < V2 < V1 (inconsistent labelling)
P vs V: hyperbolic curves with T3 > T2 > T1 ordering as shown
questions.explanation: Boyle's Law states P is proportional to 1/V (P = K/V) at constant temperature, so a plot of P vs 1/V is a straight line through the origin, with slope K = nRT. Since K increases with temperature, the line for a higher temperature has a greater slope. The correct graph is therefore the straight-line P vs 1/V plot with T3 > T2 > T1 (steepest slope for highest temperature).

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Mixture): A. CHCl3 + C6H5NH2, B. Curde oil in petroleum industry, C. Glycerol from spent-lye, D. Aniline - water. List-II (Method of Separation): I. Distillation under reduced pressure, II. Steam distillation, III. Fractional distillation, IV. Simple distillation. Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: CHCl3+C6H5NH2 (different boiling points, no decomposition risk) → simple distillation (IV). Crude oil in petroleum industry → fractional distillation (III). Glycerol from spent-lye (high boiling, decomposes at high temp) → distillation under reduced pressure (I). Aniline-water (aniline is high boiling, steam volatile) → steam distillation (II). So A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: The number of sigma and pi bonds in pent-2-en-4-yne (CH3-CH=CH-C=CH, with a triple bond between C4 and C5) is:
options: 13 sigma bonds and no pi bond
questions.explanation: Pent-2-en-4-yne is CH3-CH=CH-C#CH. Counting sigma bonds: 3 C-H bonds on C1(CH3), C1-C2, C2-H, C2=C3 sigma, C3-H, C3-C4, C4#C5 sigma, C5-H = 10 sigma bonds. Pi bonds: 1 from the C2=C3 double bond and 2 from the C4#C5 triple bond = 3 pi bonds total.

questions.text: In which of the following compounds is the carbon marked with an asterisk (*) expected to have the greatest positive charge? (i) *CH3-CH2-Cl  (ii) *CH3-CH2-MgCl  (iii) *CH3-CH2-Br  (iv) *CH3-CH2-CH3
questions.explanation: Chlorine is more electronegative than bromine, so it withdraws more electron density through the inductive effect, leaving the marked carbon in CH3-CH2-Cl with the greatest positive charge. In the Grignard reagent, the carbon is actually electron-rich (carbanion-like), and propane has no electronegative substituent to induce any significant positive charge.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) The largest and the smallest species among Mg, Mg²⁺, Al and Al³⁺ are Al and Mg²⁺, respectively. (2) The nearest inert gas with atomic number 107 is Unnilseptium... (3) The similarity in behaviour of Li with Mg is referred to as 'diagonal relationship'. (4) The oxidation state of Al and covalency of Al in [AlCl2(H2O)4]²⁺ are 3 and 6 respectively.
options: The largest and the smallest species among Mg, Mg²⁺, Al and Al³⁺ are Al and Mg²⁺, respectively
The IUPAC name of the element with atomic number 107 is Unnilseptium
The similarity in behaviour of Li with Mg is referred to as 'diagonal relationship'
The oxidation state and covalency of Al in [AlCl(H2O)5]²⁺ are 3 and 6 respectively
questions.explanation: The largest species should be Mg (not Al, atoms are larger than their cations and Mg is larger than Al), making statement 1 incorrect.

questions.text: The equilibrium constants of the following are: N2 + 3H2 <=> 2NH3, K1; N2 + O2 <=> 2NO, K2; H2 + 1/2 O2 -> H2O, K3. The equilibrium constant (K) of the reaction: 2NH3 + 5/2 O2 <=> 2NO + 3H2O, will be:
questions.explanation: The target reaction equals: reverse of (N2+3H2<=>2NH3, so 1/K1) + (N2+O2<=>2NO, K2) + 3x(H2+1/2O2->H2O, K3). So K = K2 x K3^3 / K1.

questions.text: Which one of the following reactions does NOT belong to "Lassaigne's test"? (1) Na+C+N→NaCN (Δ), (2) 2Na+S→Na2S (Δ), (3) Na+X→NaX (Δ), (4) 2CuO+C→2Cu+CO2 (Δ)
questions.explanation: Lassaigne's test involves fusing an organic compound with sodium metal to convert N, S, halogens into detectable sodium salts (NaCN, Na2S, NaX). The reaction 2CuO+C→2Cu+CO2 is unrelated to this extraction process (it's a redox/combustion-type reaction), so it does not belong to Lassaigne's test.

questions.text: Which of the following belongs to secondary air pollutants?
questions.explanation: Peroxyacetyl nitrate (PAN) is formed in the atmosphere through photochemical reactions of primary pollutants (like hydrocarbons and NOx), making it a secondary pollutant, whereas CO, hydrocarbons, and NO are emitted directly (primary pollutants).

questions.text: Dehydration of hydrates of the halides of calcium, barium and strontium can be achieved by heating. These become wet on keeping in air. Which of the following statements is correct about these halides?
options: They can absorb moisture from air.
Tendency to form a hydrate decreases from calcium to barium.
questions.explanation: Anhydrous CaCl2-type halides are hygroscopic: they absorb atmospheric moisture (becoming wet) and are therefore used as dehydrating/drying agents; this tendency to form hydrates also decreases down the group from calcium to barium as the charge density of the cation decreases. All three statements are correct.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 19 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Complex/Ion) — A. [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2], B. [Co(NH3)6]3+, C. [NiCl4]2-, D. [Fe(CO)5]. List II (Shape/geometry) — I. Octahedral, II. Trigonal bipyramidal, III. Square planar, IV. Tetrahedral.
questions.explanation: [Pt(Cl2)(NH3)2] is square planar (III); [Co(NH3)6]3+ is octahedral (I); [NiCl4]2- is tetrahedral (IV); [Fe(CO)5] is trigonal bipyramidal (II). A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Weight (g) of two moles of the organic compound, which is obtained by heating sodium ethanoate with sodium hydroxide in presence of calcium oxide, is:
questions.explanation: Heating sodium ethanoate (CH3COONa) with soda lime (NaOH + CaO) causes decarboxylation to give methane (CH4), which has a molecular weight of 16 g/mol. The weight of two moles of CH4 is 2 x 16 = 32 g.

questions.text: The suspension of slaked lime in water is known as:
questions.explanation: A suspension (not solution) of slaked lime Ca(OH)2 in water is called milk of lime, while the clear saturated solution is called limewater.

questions.text: If the E°cell for a given reaction has a negative value, which of the following gives the correct relationships for the values of ΔG° and Keq?
questions.topic: Relation between Ecell, Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant
questions.explanation: E°cell=(-), so ΔG°cell=-nFE°cell=(+), i.e. ΔG°>0. Also E°cell=(0.06/n)logK, with negative E°cell giving logK<0, so K<1

questions.text: When 1 mol CrCl3·6H2O is treated with excess AgNO3, 3 mol of AgCl are obtained. The formula of the complex is
questions.topic: Determining a Complex's Formula from AgCl Precipitation
questions.explanation: Since all 3 mol of Cl per mole of compound precipitate as AgCl, none of the chloride ions are coordinated to chromium — all 3 are ionic. This means all 6 water molecules must be coordinated instead, giving the complex [Cr(H2O)6]Cl3.

questions.text: The calculated 'spin-only' magnetic moment of Ti²⁺(3d²) is:
questions.explanation: Ti²⁺ has 2 unpaired electrons (3d²). μ=√(n(n+2))=√(2×4)=√8≈2.84 BM.

questions.text: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi, broadcasts on a frequency of 1.368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is: [speed of light, c = 3.0 × 10^8 ms^-1]
Dipole-dipole forces act between the molecules possessing permanent dipole. Ends of dipoles possess 'partial charges'. The partial charge is
questions.explanation: The partial charges at the ends of a permanent dipole arise from unequal sharing of electrons in a polar bond, and are always less than a full unit electronic charge (no complete transfer of an electron occurs).

questions.text: Acid anhydrides on reaction with primary amines give
questions.topic: Product of Acid Anhydride Reacting with a Primary Amine
questions.explanation: A primary amine's nitrogen nucleophilically attacks the carbonyl carbon of an acid anhydride, displacing one carboxylate group and forming an N-substituted amide (an acylated amine).

questions.text: For a certain reaction, the rate = K[A]^2[B]. When the initial concentration of A is tripled keeping concentration of B constant, the initial rate would:
options: increase by a factor of six
increase by a factor of nine
increase by a factor of three
increase by a factor of nine
questions.topic: Rate Law and Order of Reaction
questions.explanation: Rate = K[A]^2[B]. Tripling [A] gives Rate' = K(3[A])^2[B] = 9K[A]^2[B] = 9 x Rate. So the rate increases by a factor of nine.

questions.text: The correct order of strengths of the carboxylic acids (I: cyclohexanecarboxylic acid, II: tetrahydropyran-4-carboxylic acid with O at position adjacent, III: tetrahydropyran-4-carboxylic acid with O at a different position) is:
questions.explanation: The oxygen atom's -I effect increases acid strength; its proximity to the COOH group determines the extent: II (O closest) > III (O farther) > I (no O, cyclohexane only)

questions.text: Extraction of gold and silver involves leaching the metal with CN⁻ ion. The metal is recovered from the leached solution by
options: displacement of the metal by a more reactive metal from the complex ion.
thermal decomposition of the metal complex.
questions.topic: Recovery of Gold and Silver After Cyanide Leaching
questions.explanation: The gold or silver cyanide complex formed during leaching (e.g. [Au(CN)2]⁻) is treated with a more reactive metal, zinc, which displaces and precipitates out the gold or silver metal from the complex.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement related to PCl5 from the following:
options: Axial P-Cl bonds are longer than equatorial P-Cl bonds
Three equatorial P-Cl bonds make an angle of 120 degrees with each other
Two axial P-Cl bonds make an angle of 180 degrees with each other
questions.explanation: PCl5 is actually quite reactive, readily undergoing hydrolysis and other reactions, so the statement that it is 'non-reactive' is incorrect. The other statements about its trigonal bipyramidal geometry (longer axial bonds, 120 degree equatorial angles, 180 degree axial angle) are all correct.

questions.text: Given van der Waals constant for NH3, H2, O2 and CO2 are respectively 4.17, 0.244, 1.36 and 3.59, which one of the following gases is most easily liquefied?
questions.topic: Van der Waals constant 'a' and liquefaction of gases
questions.explanation: A higher value of the van der Waals constant 'a' indicates stronger intermolecular attractive forces, making the gas easier to liquefy. NH3 has the highest 'a' value (4.17) among the given gases, so it is most easily liquefied.

questions.text: At the equilibrium position in the process of adsorption,
questions.explanation: Adsorption is spontaneous (ΔG < 0) and accompanied by a decrease in entropy (ΔS < 0, since gas molecules become more ordered when adsorbed). Since ΔG = ΔH – TΔS, for ΔG to be negative with ΔS negative, ΔH must be even more negative than TΔS, i.e. ΔH < TΔS.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an actinoid?
questions.explanation: Actinoids span atomic numbers 89–103. Curium (96), Californium (98), and Uranium (92) are all actinoids. Terbium (Z=65) falls in the lanthanoid series (58–71), not the actinoids.

questions.text: The volume of gas is reduced to half from its original volume. The specific heat will be
questions.explanation: Specific heat is an intensive property (heat capacity per unit mass), independent of the total amount or volume of the substance, so it remains constant when the volume is changed.

questions.text: Ethylidene chloride is a/an
questions.explanation: Ethylidene chloride (CH3–CHCl2) has both chlorine atoms attached to the same carbon atom, which is the defining feature of a geminal (gem-) dihalide.

questions.text: In pyrrole (5-membered ring with N1-H, carbons numbered 2,3,4,5), the electron density is maximum on:
questions.explanation: Resonance structures of pyrrole show negative charge (higher electron density) developing at C2 and C5 positions (adjacent to N), due to delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the ring.

questions.text: Which of the following elements does not form a hydride by direct heating with dihydrogen?
questions.explanation: Beryllium does not form BeH2 by direct combination with H2 under ordinary heating (BeH2 must be prepared by other methods, e.g., from BeCl2 and LiAlH4), unlike Mg, Sr, and Ba, which form hydrides on direct heating with hydrogen.

questions.text: A primary alkyl halide would prefer to undergo
questions.topic: Preferred Mechanism for Primary Alkyl Halides
questions.explanation: Primary alkyl halides have minimal steric hindrance around the carbon bearing the halogen, favouring a bimolecular nucleophilic substitution (SN2) mechanism; they cannot readily form the relatively unstable primary carbocation needed for SN1.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not correct about the characteristics of cathode rays?
options: They start from the cathode and move towards the anode.
They travel in a straight line in the absence of an external electrical or magnetic field.
Characteristics of cathode rays do not depend upon the material of electrodes.
Characteristics of cathode rays depend upon the nature of gas present in the cathode ray tube.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays consist of electrons, and their fundamental characteristics (charge-to-mass ratio, etc.) are independent of both the electrode material and the nature of the gas in the discharge tube. Statement (iv), that they depend on the nature of the gas, is incorrect.

questions.text: Right option for the number of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in hexagonal primitive unit cell are:
questions.explanation: In HCP structure, Tetrahedral voids (THV) = 12, Octahedral voids (OHV) = 6

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: [Fe(ox)3]3− is chiral.
Statement-II: trans-[Cr(H2O)2(ox)2]⁻ is chiral.
(Given: oxH2 = HOOC–COOH, i.e., ox = oxalate, a bidentate ligand)
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
questions.explanation: [Fe(ox)3]3− is a tris-chelate octahedral complex with three bidentate oxalate ligands; such tris-bidentate complexes lack any plane of symmetry and exist as non-superimposable mirror-image (Δ/Λ) enantiomers, so they are chiral -- Statement-I is correct. In trans-[Cr(H2O)2(ox)2]⁻, the two water ligands are trans to each other, and this arrangement possesses a plane of symmetry passing through the two water ligands and bisecting the two oxalate rings, making the trans isomer achiral (it is the cis isomer that is chiral) -- Statement-II is incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a vic-dihalide?
questions.explanation: A vicinal (vic-) dihalide has the two halogen atoms on adjacent carbon atoms. 1,2-dichloroethane (ClCH2–CH2Cl) fits this description, unlike dichloromethane and ethylidene chloride (both gem-dihalides, with both halogens on the same carbon) or allyl chloride (only one halogen).

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 20 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Select the correct statements from the following: (A) Atoms of all elements are composed of two fundamental particles. (B) The mass of the electron is 9.10939 x 10^-31 kg. (C) All the isotopes of a given element show same chemical properties. (D) Protons and electrons are collectively known as nucleons. (E) Dalton's atomic theory regarded the atom as an ultimate particle of matter. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement A is incorrect — atoms are composed of three fundamental particles (electron, proton, neutron), not two. Statement B is correct — the mass of the electron is 9.10939 x 10^-31 kg. Statement C is correct — isotopes have the same number of electrons/protons, so they show the same chemical properties. Statement D is incorrect — protons and neutrons (not electrons) are collectively known as nucleons. Statement E is correct — Dalton's atomic theory regarded the atom as an indivisible, ultimate particle of matter. So B, C, and E are correct.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: In equation deltaG(r) = -nFE(cell), value of deltaG(r) depends on n. Reason R: E(cell) is an intensive property and deltaG(r) is an extensive property. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Gibbs Energy and Cell EMF Relationship
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — deltaG depends on n (the number of moles of electrons transferred) since deltaG = -nFE(cell). Reason R is also true — E(cell) is an intensive property (independent of the amount of substance), while deltaG is an extensive property (depends on the amount, via n), and this correctly explains why deltaG depends on n while E(cell) does not. So both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds can form a zwitterion?
questions.explanation: Glycine, an amino acid, has both an acidic -COOH group and a basic -NH2 group in the same molecule, allowing internal proton transfer to form a dipolar zwitterion (+H3N-CH2-COO-).

questions.text: Ka for CH3COOH is 1.8 × 10⁻5 and Kb for NH4OH is 1.8 × 10⁻5. The pH of ammonium acetate will be
questions.topic: pH of Salt of Weak Acid and Weak Base
questions.explanation: For a salt of a weak acid and weak base with Ka = Kb, the solution is neutral since the acid and base hydrolysis exactly balance. pH = 7.0.

questions.text: The term 'sorption' stands for
questions.explanation: Sorption is a general term that covers both absorption (uptake into the bulk of a material) and adsorption (accumulation on the surface of a material).

questions.text: The bond dissociation energies of X2, Y2 and XY are in the ratio of 1:0.5:1. ΔH for the formation of XY is -200 kJ/mol. The bond dissociation energy of X2 will be
questions.topic: Bond dissociation energy and enthalpy of formation
questions.explanation: Let bond energies be: X2=a, Y2=0.5a, XY=a. ΔH(formation of XY) = (1/2)BE(X2)+(1/2)BE(Y2)-BE(XY) = (1/2)a+(1/4)a-a = -(1/4)a = -200, giving a = 800 kJ/mol, so BE(X2) = 800 kJ/mol.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The boiling points of the following hydrides of group 16 elements increases in the order - H2O < H2S < H2Se < H2Te
Statement II: The boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: H2O actually has the highest boiling point due to hydrogen bonding, so the stated order is incorrect, making both statements incorrect.

questions.text: The role of a catalyst is to change
options: the Gibbs energy of the reaction.
the activation energy of the reaction.
questions.explanation: A catalyst provides an alternative reaction pathway with a lower activation energy, increasing the rate of reaction without altering the thermodynamic quantities (ΔG, ΔH, or the equilibrium constant).

questions.text: Graphite is a good conductor of electricity due to the presence of
questions.explanation: In graphite, each carbon atom is bonded to only three others within a layer, leaving one valence electron per atom delocalised across the layer, free to move and conduct electricity.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is:
options: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not polysaccharides, making statement 3 incorrect. Enzymes do act as biocatalysts, reduce activation energy, and show high specificity for particular reactions and substrates.

questions.text: The method used to remove temporary hardness of water is:
questions.explanation: Clark's method uses calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) to remove temporary hardness of water by precipitating calcium and magnesium bicarbonates as insoluble carbonates. Ion-exchange, synthetic resins, and Calgon's method are typically used for removing permanent hardness.

questions.text: Statement I: Acid strength increases in the order given as HF<<HCl<<HBr<<HI. Statement II: As the size of the elements F, Cl, Br, I increases down the group, the bond strength of HF, HCl, HBr and HI decreases and so the acid strength increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true
questions.topic: Statements on acid strength and bond strength of hydrogen halides
questions.explanation: Both statements correctly describe the trend: acid strength HF<<HCl<<HBr<<HI due to decreasing H-X bond strength down the group.

questions.text: Dihedral angle of least stable conformer of ethane is:
questions.explanation: Least stable conformer of ethane is the eclipsed form, which occurs when dihedral angle is 0°

questions.text: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10g of glucose (C6H12O6) in 250 ml of water (P1), 10 g of urea (CH4N2O) in 250 ml of water (P2) and 10 g of sucrose (C12H22O11) in 250 ml of water (P3). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure of these solution is:
questions.explanation: Π∝C∝1/Mw. Mw(glucose)=180, Mw(urea)=60, Mw(sucrose)=342. Lower Mw gives higher osmotic pressure for same mass, so P2>P1>P3

questions.text: At 298 K, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of X- and HX. Kb for X- is 10⁻¹⁰. What is the pH of this buffer solution?
questions.explanation: Ka of HX = Kw/Kb = 10⁻¹⁴/10⁻¹⁰ = 10⁻⁴, pKa=4. For equal concentrations, pH=pKa=4.

questions.text: Anisole on cleavage with HI gives:
questions.topic: Cleavage of aryl alkyl ethers with HI
questions.explanation: In the cleavage of anisole (aryl alkyl ether) with HI, the alkyl-oxygen bond is cleaved (due to the instability of forming an aryl cation), giving phenol and methyl iodide (CH3I).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group. Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: the electron-withdrawing nitro group increases acidic strength of nitrophenols compared to phenol. Statement II is incorrect because the position of the nitro group (ortho, meta, para) affects the degree of resonance and inductive stabilization of the phenoxide ion differently, so o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol have different (not same) acidic strengths.

questions.text: The element which exists in liquid state for a wide range of temperature and can be used for measuring high temperature is
questions.explanation: Gallium has an unusually low melting point (~30°C) but a very high boiling point, giving it a very wide liquid range, which makes it useful in high-temperature thermometers.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is true about Ca(OH)2?
options: It is used in the preparation of bleaching powder.
It is a light blue solid.
It does not possess disinfectant property.
It is used in the manufacture of cement.
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime) reacts with chlorine to produce bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride, CaOCl2) — it is a white solid with disinfectant properties, and is not itself a raw material for cement manufacture.

questions.text: Which of the following is not an example of redox reaction?
questions.explanation: BaCl2 + H2SO4 → BaSO4 + 2HCl is a double-displacement (precipitation) reaction — no element changes oxidation state, so it is not a redox reaction, unlike the other three options which all involve electron transfer.

questions.text: The interaction energy of London force is inversely proportional to the sixth power of the distance between two interacting particles, but their magnitude depends upon
options: strength of permanent dipoles in the particles.
questions.explanation: London (dispersion) forces arise from instantaneous induced dipoles, and their strength depends on how easily the electron cloud of a particle can be distorted — i.e., its polarisability.

questions.text: A gas at 350 K and 15 bar has molar volume 20 percent smaller than that for an ideal gas under the same conditions. The correct option about the gas and its compressibility factor (Z) is:
options: Z < 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
questions.explanation: Z = (PV)real/(PV)ideal. Since the real molar volume is smaller than the ideal volume, Z < 1. When Z < 1, it indicates that attractive forces between gas molecules dominate, causing the gas to occupy less volume than predicted by the ideal gas law.

questions.text: The entropy change can be calculated by using the expression ΔS = qrev/T. When water freezes in a glass beaker, choose the correct statement amongst the following.
options: ΔS(system) decreases but ΔS(surroundings) remains the same.
ΔS(system) decreases and ΔS(surroundings) also decreases.
questions.explanation: Freezing converts a more disordered liquid into a more ordered solid, so the system's entropy decreases. The heat released during freezing flows into the surroundings, increasing the surroundings' entropy.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property. (2) P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals. (3) Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen. (4) Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself.
options: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property
P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals
Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen
Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, lacking d-orbitals, cannot form dπ-pπ bonds; it forms pπ-pπ bonds. Hence statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.text: For a certain reaction R → Product, the plot of concentration [R] vs time has a negative slope as shown, with k=-slope. The order of the reaction is:
questions.topic: Reaction order from rate vs concentration plot
questions.explanation: A straight-line plot of [R] vs t with a constant slope (k=-slope) indicates a zero order reaction.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 21 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is
options: SN1 reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
The product obtained by SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images, not superimposable, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: CH3CH2COO-Na+ --NaOH, +?/Heat--> CH3CH3+Na2CO3. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
