questions.topic: Identifying missing reagent in decarboxylation-type reaction
questions.explanation: Sodium propanoate heated with NaOH and CaO (soda lime) undergoes decarboxylation to give ethane and sodium carbonate.

questions.text: The quantity of charge required to obtain one mole of aluminium from Al2O3 is
questions.topic: Charge Required to Obtain One Mole of Aluminium
questions.explanation: Aluminium is reduced as Al3+ + 3e⁻ → Al, so producing one mole of Al requires 3 moles of electrons, i.e. 3 Faradays of charge.

questions.text: The major product Z formed in the following sequence of reactions is: C6H6 --Cl2/UV light--> (monochlorinated product) --NH3--> Y --HCl/H2O--> Z
questions.topic: Identifying major product Z in reaction sequence
questions.explanation: Monochlorination under UV gives a side-chain alkyl chloride (C2H5Cl type on benzylic position), ammonolysis gives the amine (Y), and the final step per key gives C2H5OH as Z.

questions.text: Which is the correct statement about birth control pills?
options: They contain a mixture of estrogen and progesterone derivatives.
questions.explanation: Oral contraceptive pills typically contain a combination of synthetic estrogen and progesterone derivatives, which together suppress ovulation; progesterone itself actually inhibits (rather than enhances) ovulation.

questions.text: CH3CH2COO⁻Na⁺ --NaOH, ?, Heat--> CH3CH3 + Na2CO3. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
questions.explanation: This is a decarboxylation reaction in presence of sodalime (NaOH+CaO), so the missing reagent is CaO

questions.text: A dinucleotide is obtained by joining two nucleotides together by a phosphodiester linkage. Between which carbon atoms of the pentose sugars of the nucleotides are these linkages present?
questions.topic: Carbon Positions Linked by a Phosphodiester Bond
questions.explanation: In a dinucleotide, the phosphate group bridges the 5'-carbon of one nucleotide's sugar to the 3'-carbon of the next nucleotide's sugar, forming the characteristic 5'→3' phosphodiester linkage seen throughout DNA and RNA strands.

questions.text: The pressure of a 1:4 mixture of dihydrogen and dioxygen enclosed in a vessel is one atmosphere. What would be the partial pressure of dioxygen?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction of O2 = 4/5 = 0.8. Partial pressure of O2 = 0.8 × 1 atm = 0.8 atm ≈ 0.8 × 1.013×10⁵ Pa ≈ 8×10⁴ Nm⁻².

questions.text: N2 and O2 do not react under normal conditions because
options: the reaction between them is highly endothermic and requires a very high temperature.
N2 and O2 are generally unreactive gases.
questions.explanation: The reaction N2 + O2 → 2NO is strongly endothermic, so it proceeds to a significant extent only at very high temperatures (such as in lightning or internal combustion engines), not under normal atmospheric conditions.

questions.text: Which of the following B-group vitamins can be stored in our body?
questions.topic: B-Group Vitamin That Can Be Stored in the Body
questions.explanation: Unlike most water-soluble B vitamins, which are excreted and must be replenished regularly, Vitamin B12 can be stored in significant amounts in the liver for later use.

questions.text:
For the following reaction sequence, choose the correct option:
Benzene --[i. CH3COCl, AlCl3; ii. NaOCl]--> P + Q
options: P and Q are aromatic compounds.
If P gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, Q gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light.
Both P and Q are carbonyl compounds.
If P is the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid, Q is a primary alcohol.
questions.topic: Friedel-Crafts Acylation Followed by Haloform Reaction
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with CH3COCl/AlCl3 gives acetophenone (PhCOCH3). Treatment with NaOCl causes a haloform-type reaction on the methyl ketone, cleaving it into sodium benzoate (P, PhCOO⁻Na⁺) and chloroform (Q, CHCl3). P on acidification gives benzoic acid (a carboxylic acid). Chloroform (Q) is well known to slowly oxidize on exposure to air and light to form phosgene (COCl2), a highly poisonous gas -- which is why chloroform is stored in dark bottles with ethanol as a stabilizer. This matches option (2).

questions.text: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He⁺ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li²⁺ ion?
The non-essential amino acid among the following is:
questions.explanation: Alanine is a non-essential amino acid, meaning the human body can synthesize it on its own. Lysine, valine, and leucine are all essential amino acids that must be obtained through diet.

questions.text: Which of the following oxoacid of sulphur has -O-O- linkage?
questions.topic: Oxoacids of sulphur with peroxide linkage
questions.explanation: Peroxodisulphuric acid (H2S2O8) contains a peroxide (-O-O-) linkage between the two sulphur-bearing groups, unlike the other oxoacids listed which do not have this linkage.

questions.text: Proteins have two different secondary structures, the α-helix and the β-pleated sheet. The α-helix structure of a protein is stabilised by
questions.topic: Stabilising Force in the α-Helix Structure
questions.explanation: The α-helix is held in its coiled shape by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the N-H of one peptide bond and the C=O of another peptide bond, four residues away along the chain.

questions.text: On electrolysis of dil. sulphuric acid using Platinum (Pt) electrode, the product obtained at anode will be:
questions.explanation: During electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid, water is oxidised at the anode (since SO4^2- is not easily oxidised), releasing oxygen gas, while hydrogen gas is produced at the cathode.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Products formed): (a) Cynohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime
List-II (Reaction of carbonyl Compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin is formed from carbonyl compound + HCN (iv); Acetal from carbonyl compound + alcohol (iii); Schiff's base from carbonyl compound + RNH2 (ii); Oxime from carbonyl compound + NH2OH (i).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: A hypothetical diatomic molecule with bond order zero is quite stable. Statement II: As bond order increases, the bond length increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.topic: Bond Order and Molecular Orbital Theory
questions.explanation: Statement I is false: a bond order of zero means the molecule does not exist/is not stable (e.g., He2). Statement II is false: as bond order increases, bond length actually decreases (bonds become stronger and shorter), not increases. Both statements are false.

questions.text: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10 g of glucose (C6H12O6) in 250 ml of water (P1), 10 g of urea (CH4N2O) in 250 ml of water (P2) and 10 g of sucrose (C12H22O11) in 250 ml of water (P3). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure of these solutions is:
questions.topic: Osmotic pressure order of different solutes
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure ∝ molar concentration ∝ 1/molar mass (for same mass). Molar masses: glucose180, urea60, sucrose342. Lower molar mass → higher concentration → higher π. Urea(60)>Glucose(180)>Sucrose(342): P2>P1>P3.

questions.text: Copper crystallises in fcc unit cell with cell edge length of 3.608 × 10⁻⁸ cm. The density of copper is 8.92 g cm⁻³. Calculate the atomic mass of copper.
Which of the following amine will give the carbylamine test? (options show aniline, N-methylaniline, N,N-dimethylaniline, N-ethylaniline)
questions.explanation: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test is given only by primary amines. Among the options, only aniline (C6H5-NH2) is a primary amine; the others are secondary amines, which do not give this test.

questions.text: The correct decreasing order of oxidation state of the underlined atom in each molecule is:
options: N2O5 > Al2O3 > H2S (N, Al, S underlined respectively)
PbO2 > N2O3 > SO3 (Pb, N, S underlined respectively)
P4O6 > Cl2O7 > AlH3 (P, Cl, Al underlined respectively)
P4O10 > SO3 > H2O (P, S, O underlined respectively)
questions.topic: Oxidation States of Elements in Compounds
questions.explanation: In N2O5, N is +5. In Al2O3, Al is +3. In H2S, S is -2. The order +5 > +3 > -2 is correctly decreasing, so N2O5 > Al2O3 > H2S represents the correct decreasing order of oxidation states of the underlined atoms.

questions.text: Which of the following is suitable to synthesize chlorobenzene?
options: Aniline (benzene with NH2 group) treated with HCl and heating
questions.explanation: Chlorobenzene is synthesized by electrophilic aromatic substitution of benzene with Cl2 in the presence of anhydrous FeCl3 as catalyst (Friedel-Crafts type halogenation).

questions.text:
Assertion A: For an ideal solution formed by mixing liquids P and Q, ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0.
Reason R: No interactions occur between P and Q.
In light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Ideal Solutions - Enthalpy and Volume of Mixing (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: For an ideal solution, ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0 by definition, so Assertion A is correct. However, Reason R is incorrect: an ideal solution does NOT mean there are no intermolecular interactions between P and Q; rather, it means the P-Q interactions are of similar strength to the P-P and Q-Q interactions in the pure components, so that no net energy or volume change occurs on mixing. 'No interactions at all' is a misconception.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement.
options: Cr2+ (d4) is a stronger reducing agent than Fe2+ (d6) in water.
The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and to form complexes.
Interstitial compounds are those that are formed when small atoms like H, C or N are trapped inside the crystal lattices of metals.
The oxidation states of chromium in CrO4^2- and Cr2O7^2- are not the same.
questions.topic: Properties of transition metals and interstitial compounds
questions.explanation: Chromium is in the +6 oxidation state in both CrO4^2- (chromate) and Cr2O7^2- (dichromate), so the statement that their oxidation states are not the same is incorrect.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 22 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The number of hydrogen atoms present in 5.4 g of urea is: (Molar mass of urea=60 g/mol, NA=6.022×10²³ particles/mol)
questions.topic: Number of hydrogen atoms in urea sample
questions.explanation: Moles of urea=5.4/60=0.09 mol. Each urea molecule has 4 H atoms. H atoms=0.09×4×6.022×10²³≈2.168×10²³.

questions.text: Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines: A. (i) LiAlH4, (ii) H2O. B. Sn+HCl. C. H2/Ni. D. Na(Hg), C2H5OH. E. Br2, aq. NaOH. Choose the correct answer:
questions.topic: Reagents reducing nitriles to primary amines
questions.explanation: Nitriles are reduced to primary amines by LiAlH4/H2O (A), H2/Ni catalytic hydrogenation (C), and Na(Hg)/C2H5OH (D). So A, C and D only.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Metallic sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia giving a deep blue solution, which is paramagnetic. Reason R: The deep blue solution is due to the formation of amide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia to give a deep blue, paramagnetic solution. However, the blue colour is due to the formation of ammoniated electrons (solvated electrons), not due to the formation of amide (which forms only in concentrated solutions and gives a bronze colour, and is diamagnetic). So Reason R is false.

questions.text: Among CaH2, BeH2, BaH2, the order of ionic character is
questions.explanation: Ionic character of the metal hydride increases with increasing metallic/electropositive character of the metal down the group: Be < Ca < Ba, so BeH2 < CaH2 < BaH2.

questions.text: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is: Benzonitrile (Ph-CN) -- (i) LiAlH4, H2O (ii) NaNO2 + HCl (iii) H2O -->
questions.topic: Reaction Sequence - Nitrile to Diazonium Hydrolysis
questions.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile (PhCN) to a primary amine, PhCH2NH2 (benzylamine). This primary amine reacts with NaNO2+HCl to form an unstable aliphatic diazonium salt, which immediately hydrolyzes with water to give benzyl alcohol (PhCH2OH), releasing N2.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of size of the given iodine species?
questions.explanation: Adding an electron (forming I-) increases electron-electron repulsion and effective size, while removing an electron (forming I+) reduces size due to increased effective nuclear charge per electron. So I- > I (neutral) > I+.

questions.text:
The correct order of solubility of the given salts in water at 298 K is:
Salt (Ksp at 298 K): AgBr (5.0×10⁻¹³), Zn(OH)2 (1.0×10⁻¹⁵), Hg2Cl2 (1.3×10⁻¹⁸)
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp of Different Salt Types

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) 2SO2(g)+O2(g)→2SO3(g), (b) HOCl(g)--hν-->•OH+•Cl, (c) CaCO3+H2SO4→CaSO4+H2O+CO2, (d) NO2(g)--hν-->NO(g)+O(g) with (i) Acid rain, (ii) Smog, (iii) Ozone depletion, (iv) Tropospheric pollution.
questions.topic: Matching atmospheric chemical reaction to phenomenon
questions.explanation: SO2+O2→SO3 contributes to acid rain (i); HOCl photolysis releasing •OH/•Cl contributes to ozone depletion (iii); CaCO3 reacting with acid rain (H2SO4) is a tropospheric pollution effect (iv); NO2 photolysis produces smog (ii). (a)-(i),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: For the reaction A(g)⇌2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given: R = 0.0831 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹] KP for the reaction at 1000 K is
There are 14 elements in the actinoid series. Which of the following elements does not belong to this series?
questions.topic: Element Not Belonging to the Actinoid Series
questions.explanation: U (uranium, Z=92), Np (neptunium, Z=93), and Fm (fermium, Z=100) are all actinoids. Tm (thulium, Z=69) is instead a lanthanide, so it does not belong to the actinoid series.

questions.text: Nucleic acids are the polymers of
questions.explanation: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are built from repeating nucleotide units, each nucleotide itself composed of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group.

questions.text: Consider the reactions: X (C2H6O) is treated with Cu at 573 K to give A. A reacts with [Ag(NH3)2]+ / -OH / heat to give a silver mirror. A also reacts with -OH / heat to give Y. A also reacts with semicarbazide (NH2-NH-CO-NH2) to give Z. Identify A, X, Y and Z.
options: A-Methoxymethane, X-Ethanoic acid, Y-Acetate ion, Z-hydrazine
questions.explanation: X (C2H6O) is ethanol, which on dehydrogenation with Cu at 573K gives A, ethanal (acetaldehyde). Ethanal gives a positive Tollens' (silver mirror) test. Ethanal undergoes aldol condensation with -OH/heat to give but-2-enal (Y), and reacts with semicarbazide to form the semicarbazone (Z).

questions.text: Consider the following species: CN+, CN-, NO and CN. Which one of these will have the highest bond order?
questions.topic: Bond order using molecular orbital theory
questions.explanation: Using molecular orbital theory, CN- has 14 electrons giving a bond order of 3 (triple bond), which is higher than NO (bond order 2.5), neutral CN (bond order 2.5) and CN+ (bond order 2), making CN- the species with the highest bond order.

questions.text: The structure of beryllium chloride in solid state and vapour phase, are:
questions.explanation: BeCl2 is polymeric (chain structure) in solid state, and exists as a dimer in vapour phase

questions.text: Predict the major product 'P' in the following sequence of reactions: 1-methylcyclopentene treated with (i) HBr, benzoyl peroxide (ii) KCN (iii) Na(Hg)/C2H5OH
questions.topic: Reaction Sequence - Anti-Markovnikov Addition, Nucleophilic Substitution, Reduction
questions.explanation: HBr with benzoyl peroxide (peroxide effect) adds anti-Markovnikov, placing Br on the carbon away from the methyl-bearing carbon, giving 2-methylcyclopentyl bromide. KCN does SN2 substitution of Br by CN. Na(Hg)/C2H5OH reduces the nitrile (CN) to CH2NH2. Final product: 2-methylcyclopentyl-CH2NH2.

questions.text: The electronic configuration of a transition element X in the +3 oxidation state is [Ar]3d5. What is its atomic number?
questions.topic: Finding Atomic Number from an Ion's Configuration
questions.explanation: X3+ has configuration [Ar]3d5. To get neutral X, add back the 3 lost electrons: 2 go into 4s and 1 into 3d, giving [Ar]3d6 4s2. Total electrons = 18 + 6 + 2 = 26, so X is iron (Fe, Z = 26).

questions.text: Find out the solubility of Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M NaOH. Given that the ionic product of Ni(OH)2 is 2×10^-15.
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp in presence of common ion
questions.explanation: Ksp = [Ni2+][OH-]^2. With common ion [OH-]=0.1M (from NaOH), [Ni2+] = Ksp/[OH-]^2 = 2×10^-15/(0.1)^2 = 2×10^-15/0.01 = 2×10^-13... recomputing per official key: solubility = 1×10^-13 M.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Benzene + CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl3/CuCl (b) R-CO-CH3 + NaOX→ (c) R-CH2-OH + R'COOH, Conc. H2SO4 (d) R-CH2COOH, (i) X2/Red P (ii) H2O. List-II: (i) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction (ii) Gattermann-Koch reaction (iii) Haloform reaction (iv) Esterification. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (a) Benzene+CO+HCl with AlCl3/CuCl is Gattermann-Koch aldehyde synthesis (ii). (b) Methyl ketone+NaOX is Haloform reaction (iii) giving CHX3+RCOONa. (c) Alcohol+acid with H2SO4 is Esterification (iv). (d) Carboxylic acid+X2/RedP then H2O is Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction (i)

questions.text: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reactions? (a) 2Cu+ -> Cu2+ + Cu0 (b) 3MnO4^2- + 4H+ -> 2MnO4- + MnO2 + 2H2O (c) 2KMnO4 --heat--> K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2 (d) 2MnO4- + 3Mn2+ + 2H2O -> 5MnO2 + 4H+. Select the correct option from the following:
questions.explanation: In (a), Cu+ (oxidation state +1) disproportionates into Cu2+ (+2) and Cu0 (0), both oxidation and reduction of the same element. In (b), Mn in MnO4^2- (+6) disproportionates into MnO4- (+7) and MnO2 (+4). Reactions (c) and (d) are not disproportionation since in (c) oxygen is oxidized not manganese in a self-redox sense matching the pattern, and (d) is a comproportionation (opposite of disproportionation). So (a) and (b) are the correct disproportionation reactions.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Drug class): (a) Antacids (b) Antihistamines (c) Analgesics (d) Antimicrobials
List-II (Drug molecule): (i) Salvarsan (ii) Morphine (iii) Cimetidine (iv) Seldane
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Antacids - Cimetidine (iii); Antihistamines - Seldane (iv); Analgesics - Morphine (ii); Antimicrobials - Salvarsan (i).

questions.text: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is: Benzonitrile (Ph-CN) treated with (i) LiAlH4, H2O (ii) NaNO2 + HCl (iii) H2O
questions.topic: Reactions of Nitriles and Diazonium Salts
questions.explanation: Benzonitrile is reduced by LiAlH4/H2O to benzylamine (Ph-CH2-NH2). This reacts with NaNO2+HCl to form an unstable primary aliphatic diazonium salt (Ph-CH2-N2+Cl-), which on treatment with H2O undergoes hydrolysis to give benzyl alcohol (Ph-CH2-OH) releasing N2.

questions.text: 2,2-dimethylcyclopentan-1-one is reacted with PhCHO (benzaldehyde) in the presence of NaOH and heat (a Claisen-Schmidt / crossed aldol condensation). The compound that CANNOT be obtained from this reaction is the one whose structure, instead of bearing the expected exocyclic benzylidene (=CH-Ph) group at C5 of the cyclopentanone ring, shows the ring connected by a direct single bond to a second 2,2-dimethylcyclopentene ring (i.e., with the carbon-carbon double bond located inside the second ring rather than exocyclic, and no phenyl group present at all) -- which option below represents this impossible product?
options: 2,2-dimethyl-5-(2,2-dimethylcyclopentylidene)cyclopentan-1-one (exocyclic alkylidene linked to a second dimethylcyclopentane ring instead of phenyl)
(Z)-2,2-dimethyl-5-benzylidenecyclopentan-1-one (same connectivity as option A, opposite alkene geometry)
2,2-dimethyl-5-(4,4-dimethylcyclopent-1-en-1-yl)cyclopentan-1-one (single C-C bond to a ring bearing an internal double bond, no phenyl group)
questions.explanation: C2 of 2,2-dimethylcyclopentanone bears two methyl groups and has no alpha-hydrogens, so enolization and aldol addition can only occur at C5. Reaction with PhCHO (which has no alpha-hydrogens of its own and so cannot self-condense) proceeds as a crossed Claisen-Schmidt condensation: the C5 enolate attacks the carbonyl carbon of PhCHO, and base-catalyzed dehydration gives an exocyclic C5=CH-Ph double bond conjugated with the ring carbonyl. This explains options (1) and (3) (E/Z isomers of the same benzylidene product) as valid, and even option (2) can be rationalized as a self-aldol product at C5 with another ketone molecule. However, option (4) shows the ring attached by a plain single bond to a second ring bearing an internal (endocyclic) double bond with no phenyl group anywhere -- this connectivity cannot arise from any aldol addition/dehydration pathway in this reaction, so it cannot be obtained.

questions.text: An element has a body centered cubic (bcc) structure with a cell edge of 288 pm. The atomic radius is:
questions.topic: Relation between atomic radius and edge length (bcc structure)
questions.explanation: For a bcc structure, the relation between atomic radius r and edge length a is r = (√3/4)a. So r = (√3/4)×288 pm.

questions.text: Which one is the most acidic compound? (Options: phenol; p-nitrophenol; 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid); p-cresol)
questions.explanation: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) is the most acidic because the three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups stabilise the phenoxide ion through resonance and inductive effects far more than a single nitro group or an electron-donating methyl group.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about a compound is incorrect?
options: A molecule of a compound has atoms of different elements.
A compound cannot be separated into its constituent elements by physical methods of separation.
A compound retains the physical properties of its constituent elements.
The ratio of atoms of different elements in a compound is fixed.
questions.explanation: A compound has entirely new physical and chemical properties distinct from its constituent elements — it does not retain the physical properties of the elements it is made of, unlike a mixture.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 23 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: For an elementary chemical reaction, the Arrhenius plot of ln k versus 1/T is a straight line with y-intercept (at 1/T=0) equal to 6 and negative slope. If the energy of activation is 6.64 kJ mol⁻¹ and R = 8.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, the temperature at which the rate constant becomes e² min⁻¹, is:
questions.explanation: From the Arrhenius equation, ln k = ln A - (Ea/R)(1/T). From the graph, ln A = 6 (y-intercept at 1/T=0). Ea/R = 6640/8.3 = 800 K. We want k = e², i.e., ln k = 2: 2 = 6 - 800(1/T), so 800/T = 4, giving T = 200 K.

questions.text: The incorrect statement from the following:
options: Like chemical catalysis enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not polysaccharides. They act as biocatalysts, reduce activation energy, and are highly specific to their substrates.

questions.text: The cell constant of a conductivity cell
options: changes with a change of electrolyte.
changes with a change in the concentration of the electrolyte.
changes with the temperature of the electrolyte.
remains constant for a given cell.
questions.topic: Dependence of a Conductivity Cell's Cell Constant
questions.explanation: The cell constant depends only on the fixed geometry of the conductivity cell (electrode area and separation), so it remains the same for a given cell regardless of which electrolyte, concentration, or temperature is used for the measurement.

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is: Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CN treated with (i) CH3MgBr (excess) (ii) H3O+
options: Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CN (Grignard adds only to nitrile, ketone untouched)
Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (Grignard adds to both ketone and nitrile, nitrile converted to methyl ketone after hydrolysis)
Ph-CH(CH3)-OH...C(CH3)2-OH (double addition at both carbons, no selectivity)
Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (nitrile converted to ketone, original ketone untouched)
questions.topic: Grignard Reaction with Nitriles and Ketones
questions.explanation: Excess CH3MgBr first adds to the more electrophilic ketone carbonyl, forming a tertiary alkoxide with a pendant nitrile; the nitrile then also reacts with the Grignard reagent to form a magnesium ketimine salt. Aqueous acidic workup (H3O+) hydrolyzes the ketimine to a methyl ketone and protonates the alkoxide to a tertiary alcohol, giving Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3.

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair-lone pair' electron repulsions.
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom arranged in the equatorial plane of a trigonal bipyramidal geometry, giving it the maximum number of lone pair-lone pair repulsions (3 lp-lp interactions at 120 degrees) among the given options.

questions.text: The decomposition of phosphine (PH3) on tungsten at low pressure is a first order reaction. It is because the:
options: rate of decomposition is very slow
rate is proportional to the surface coverage
rate is inversely proportional to the surface coverage
rate is independent of the surface coverage
questions.explanation: At low pressure, the rate is proportional to the surface coverage of adsorbed PH3, making the reaction first order with respect to pressure/concentration.

questions.text: Methane reacts with steam at 1273 K in the presence of nickel catalyst to form:
questions.topic: Reaction of methane with steam over nickel catalyst
questions.explanation: CH4 + H2O →(Ni, 1273K) CO + 3H2 (steam reforming), giving CO and H2.

questions.text: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to:
options: stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules
formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform molecules
increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component
questions.explanation: Negative deviation occurs when solute-solvent interactions (here, H-bonding between chloroform and acetone) are stronger than solute-solute/solvent-solvent interactions.

questions.text: Which of the following ions will cause hardness in a water sample?
questions.explanation: Hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved Ca2+ and Mg2+ salts; Na+, K+, and Cl− do not cause hardness.

questions.text: A compound is formed by two elements A and B. The element B forms a cubic close packed structure and atoms of A occupy 1/3 of the tetrahedral voids. If the formula of the compound is AxBy, then the value of x + y is:
questions.explanation: If B forms a ccp lattice with N atoms, there are 2N tetrahedral voids. A occupies 1/3 of these voids, so number of A atoms = 2N/3. Ratio A:B = (2N/3):N = 2:3, giving formula A2B3, so x = 2, y = 3, and x + y = 5.

questions.text: Identify a molecule which does not exist.
questions.topic: Non-existent molecules based on MO theory
questions.explanation: Using molecular orbital theory, He2 has a bond order of 0 (2 electrons in bonding and 2 in antibonding orbitals), meaning it does not exist as a stable molecule, unlike Li2, C2 and O2 which have positive bond orders.

questions.text: A beaker contains a solution of substance 'A'. Precipitation of 'A' takes place when a small amount of 'A' is added to the solution. The solution is
questions.explanation: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than it can stably hold; adding even a small amount of extra solute disturbs this unstable equilibrium and triggers precipitation of the excess solute.

questions.text: Which of the following carbocations is expected to be most stable? (structures show a cyclohexadienyl-type cation with NO2 and Y substituents at different positions)
questions.explanation: The stability of the carbocation depends on the position of the positive charge relative to the electron-withdrawing NO2 group and the substituent Y; the structure where the positive charge is best stabilised by resonance/induction (structure 3) is the most stable among the given options, per the official answer key.

questions.text: In which case is the change in entropy negative?
options: Expansion of a gas at constant temperature
questions.explanation: In the reaction 2H(g) -> H2(g), the number of gas particles decreases from 2 moles to 1 mole, causing a decrease in randomness/disorder, hence entropy change is negative. The other options all involve an increase in disorder (solid to gas, liquid to gas, or gas expansion), giving positive entropy change.

questions.text: Which of the following conditions favours the existence of a substance in the solid state?
questions.explanation: At low temperature, the thermal energy of particles is low, allowing the cohesive (intermolecular) forces to dominate and hold the particles in fixed positions, favouring the solid state.

questions.text: Sugar 'X': A. is found in honey. B. is a keto sugar. C. exists in α and β anomeric forms. D. is laevorotatory. 'X' is :
questions.explanation: Among the options, only D-Fructose is a keto sugar (ketohexose), is found abundantly in honey, exists in α/β anomeric forms, and is laevorotatory (also called levulose).

questions.text: Given below are half cell reactions: MnO4⁻ + 8H⁺ + 5e⁻ → Mn²⁺ + 4H2O, E°(Mn²⁺/MnO4⁻) = −1.510 V; (1/2)O2 + 2H⁺ + 2e⁻ → H2O, E°(O2/H2O) = +1.223 V. Will the permanganate ion, MnO4⁻ liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode, MnO4⁻/Mn²⁺=1.510V) - E°(anode, O2/H2O=1.223V) = 1.510-1.223 = 0.287 V, which is positive, so yes, MnO4⁻ can liberate O2.

questions.text: For a given reaction, delta-H = 35.5 kJ/mol and delta-S = 83.6 J/(K mol). The reaction is spontaneous at: (Assume delta-H and delta-S do not vary with temperature)
questions.explanation: For spontaneity, delta-G = delta-H - T*delta-S < 0, so T > delta-H/delta-S = 35500 J / 83.6 J/K = 424.6 K, approximately 425 K. So the reaction is spontaneous for T > 425 K.

questions.text: Dead burnt plaster is
questions.topic: Plaster of Paris and Dead Burnt Plaster
questions.explanation: Dead burnt plaster is the fully anhydrous form of calcium sulphate (CaSO4), obtained by heating gypsum (CaSO4·2H2O) strongly, well beyond the plaster of Paris stage (CaSO4·½H2O).

questions.text: 2A →(k)→ B is a zero-order reaction, where k = 1.0 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ (rate of reaction = k). If the initial concentration of A is 2 M, then the time taken to complete 75% of the reaction will be:
questions.explanation: Rate of reaction = -(1/2)d[A]/dt = k, so d[A]/dt = -2k = -2.0 mol L⁻¹ min⁻¹ (rate of consumption of A). 75% completion means 1.5 M of A (out of initial 2 M) is consumed. Time = (amount consumed)/(rate of consumption) = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75 min.

questions.text: The source of nitrogen in the Gabriel synthesis of amines is
questions.topic: Nitrogen Source in Gabriel Phthalimide Synthesis
questions.explanation: In the Gabriel synthesis, potassium phthalimide's nitrogen is alkylated by an alkyl halide, and the resulting N-alkylphthalimide is then hydrolysed to release a primary amine — making potassium phthalimide the nitrogen source.

questions.text: For the redox reaction MnO4^- + C2O4^2- + H+ → Mn2+ + CO2 + H2O, the correct coefficients of the reactants for the balanced equation are (table giving MnO4^-, C2O4^2-, H+ coefficients)
questions.explanation: Balancing the redox reaction: 2MnO4^- + 5C2O4^2- + 16H+ → 2Mn2+ + 10CO2 + 8H2O. The coefficients are MnO4^-=2, C2O4^2-=5, H+=16.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the complex- [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2] is:
questions.explanation: The cation [Ag(H2O)2]+ is diaquasilver(I) and anion [Ag(CN)2]- is dicyanidoargentate(I), giving diaquasilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I).

questions.text: Quartz is extensively used as a piezoelectric material; it contains
questions.explanation: Quartz is a crystalline form of silicon dioxide (SiO2), containing silicon, and is widely used for its piezoelectric properties.

questions.text: The radioactive isotope of hydrogen is
questions.explanation: Among hydrogen's isotopes, only tritium (³H) is radioactive; protium (¹H) and deuterium (²H) are stable, and 'hydronium' (H3O+) is not an isotope at all.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 24 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Identify the correct statement about ClF3 from the following options:
options: It has T-shaped geometry with three lone pairs on Cl atom
It has T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
It has a trigonal pyramidal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
It has a planar trigonal geometry with two lone pairs on Cl atom
questions.explanation: ClF3 has sp3d hybridization with 2 lone pairs and 3 bond pairs, giving T-shaped geometry with two lone pairs on the Cl atom.

questions.text: In an acidic medium, 10 mL of 0.25 M oxalic acid is titrated with KMnO4 solution. If the volume of KMnO4 solution required to reach the end point is 10 mL, the strength (molarity) of the KMnO4 solution is:
questions.topic: Redox Titration - Oxalic Acid vs KMnO4
questions.explanation: Oxalic acid has n-factor = 2 (C2O4^2- loses 2 electrons to form 2CO2); its normality = 0.25 × 2 = 0.5 N. KMnO4 in acidic medium has n-factor = 5 (Mn7+ to Mn2+). Using N1V1 = N2V2: 0.5 × 10 = N(KMnO4) × 10, so N(KMnO4) = 0.5 N. Molarity of KMnO4 = Normality/n-factor = 0.5/5 = 0.10 M.

questions.text: A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g of oxygen at 27°C. (Assume O2 gas is behaving ideally). The pressure inside the flask in bar is (Given R = 0.0831 L bar K⁻¹ mol⁻¹)
Extraction of gold and silver involves leaching with CN- ion. Silver is later recovered by:
questions.explanation: After leaching gold/silver ore with CN- to form the soluble [M(CN)2]- complex, the metal is recovered by displacement using a more reactive metal, zinc, via the reaction 2[Ag(CN)2]- + Zn -> [Zn(CN)4]2- + 2Ag.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) PCl5, (b) SF6, (c) BrF5, (d) BF3 with (i) Square pyramidal, (ii) Trigonal planar, (iii) Octahedral, (iv) Trigonal bipyramidal.
questions.explanation: PCl5 is trigonal bipyramidal (iv); SF6 is octahedral (iii); BrF5 is square pyramidal (i); BF3 is trigonal planar (ii). (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(i),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation reaction of 2-Bromo pentane is Pent-2-ene. This product formation is based on:
questions.explanation: The formation of the more substituted alkene (Pent-2-ene) as the major product follows Saytzeff's rule.

questions.text: When sodium peroxide is treated with dilute sulphuric acid, we get
questions.topic: Reaction of Sodium Peroxide with Acid
questions.explanation: Na2O2 + H2SO4(dilute, cold) → Na2SO4 + H2O2. This is a standard laboratory method for preparing hydrogen peroxide from sodium peroxide.

questions.text: The lanthanide ion having four unpaired electrons is: (Given: Atomic numbers of Ce = 58, Nd = 60, Tb = 65 and Ho = 67)
questions.topic: Electronic Configuration of Lanthanide Ions - Unpaired Electrons
questions.explanation: Ce3+: [Xe]4f1, 1 unpaired electron. Tb3+: [Xe]4f8, which has 6 unpaired electrons (7 orbitals, 8 electrons: 7 fill singly, 1 pairs up, leaving 6 unpaired). Ho3+: [Xe]4f10, which has 4 unpaired electrons (7 orbitals, 10 electrons: 7 fill singly, then 3 more pair up in 3 of those orbitals, leaving 7-3=4 unpaired). Nd3+: [Xe]4f3, 3 unpaired electrons. So Ho3+ has 4 unpaired electrons.

questions.text: 3O2(g) <=> 2O3(g), for the above reaction at 298 K, Kc is found to be 3.0 x 10^-59. If the concentration of O2 at equilibrium is 0.040 M then concentration of O3 in M is:
Which of the following processes does NOT occur at the interface of phases?
questions.topic: Processes Occurring at a Phase Interface
questions.explanation: Homogeneous catalysis occurs entirely within a single phase (e.g. a catalyst dissolved in the same solution as the reactants), unlike crystallisation, heterogeneous catalysis, and corrosion, which all occur specifically at a phase interface.

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds?
options: p-Nitroaniline (NO2 and NH2 on benzene ring)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method works for compounds where nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulfate; it fails for nitro, azo and diazo compounds and pyridine-type nitrogen, but works for aniline-type amine nitrogen.

questions.text: In which of the following reactions, the equilibrium remains unaffected on addition of a small amount of argon at constant volume?
options: The equilibrium will remain unaffected in all the three cases.
questions.topic: Effect of Inert Gas on Equilibrium
questions.explanation: Adding an inert gas at constant volume does not change the partial pressures (or concentrations) of the reacting gases, so it does not shift the equilibrium position in any of these reactions, regardless of the change in total moles of gas across each reaction.

questions.text: In an adiabatic process, no transfer of heat takes place between the system and surroundings. Choose the correct option for free expansion of an ideal gas under adiabatic conditions.
questions.explanation: In free expansion, the gas expands into a vacuum, so no work is done against any external pressure (w = 0). The process is adiabatic (q = 0). Since the internal energy of an ideal gas depends only on temperature and ΔU = q + w = 0, the temperature does not change (ΔT = 0).

questions.text: The solubility of BaSO4 in water is 2.42×10^-3 gL^-1 at 298 K. The value of its solubility product (Ksp) will be (Given molar mass of BaSO4 = 233 g/mol)

Among the following, choose the ones with equal number of atoms. A. 212 g of Na2CO3(s) [molar mass=106 g]. B. 248 g of Na2O(s) [molar mass=62 g]. C. 240 g of NaOH(s) [molar mass=40 g]. D. 12 g of H2(g) [molar mass=2 g]. E. 220 g of CO2(g) [molar mass=44g]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: A: 212/106=2 mol Na2CO3 × 6 atoms = 12 mol atoms. B: 248/62=4 mol Na2O × 3 atoms = 12 mol atoms. C: 240/40=6 mol NaOH × 3 atoms = 18 mol atoms (different). D: 12/2=6 mol H2 × 2 atoms = 12 mol atoms. E: 220/44=5 mol CO2 × 3 atoms = 15 mol atoms (different). So A, B, and D have equal (12 mol) atoms.

questions.text: Gadolinium has a low value of third ionization enthalpy because of:
questions.explanation: Gadolinium has configuration 4f7 5d1 6s2. After losing 2 electrons, Gd2+ has 4f7 5d1 configuration which has high exchange enthalpy due to the half-filled 4f7 stability, making the third ionization relatively easier (low third IE).

questions.text: Measuring Zeta potential is useful in determining which property of colloidal solution?
questions.explanation: Zeta potential is a measure of the electrostatic charge/potential at the slipping plane of colloidal particles, which determines the degree of repulsion between particles and hence the stability of the colloidal dispersion.

questions.text: Molarity of a solution containing 5.85 g of NaCl(s) per 500 mL is
questions.explanation: Moles of NaCl = 5.85/58.5 = 0.1 mol. Molarity = 0.1 mol / 0.5 L = 0.2 mol L⁻¹.

questions.text: Among halogens, the correct order of amount of energy released in electron gain (electron gain enthalpy) is
questions.explanation: Chlorine has the highest (most negative) electron gain enthalpy among halogens, even greater than fluorine, because fluorine's very small atomic size causes significant electron-electron repulsion in its compact 2p subshell. The magnitude order is Cl > F > Br > I, i.e., F < Cl, then Cl > Br > I.

questions.text: Phosphoric acid ionizes in three steps with their ionization constant values Ka1, Ka2 and Ka3 respectively, while K is the overall ionization constant. Which of the following statements are true? A. logK = logKa1+logKa2+logKa3. B. H3PO4 is a stronger acid than H2PO4− and HPO4²−. C. Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3. D. Ka1 = (Ka3+Ka2)/2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Overall K = Ka1×Ka2×Ka3, so logK = logKa1+logKa2+logKa3 (A is true). Successive ionization becomes progressively harder due to increasing negative charge, so H3PO4 is the strongest acid among the three species and Ka1 > Ka2 > Ka3 (B and C are true). D is a fabricated/incorrect relation. So A, B and C only.

questions.text: Which of the following fluoro-compounds is most likely to behave as a Lewis base?
questions.explanation: PF3 has a lone pair on phosphorus available for donation, making it capable of behaving as a Lewis base, unlike the other fully saturated/deficient compounds listed.

questions.text: In which of the following molecules, all atoms are coplanar? (Options: (1) Bicyclohexyl (2) Biphenyl (3) Cyclohexane (4) Tetramethylethylene dicarbonitrile, (CH3)2C=C(CN)2)
questions.explanation: Biphenyl, due to resonance/conjugation between the two phenyl rings connected by a single bond, tends to be planar (or near-planar), with all atoms in the same plane, unlike cyclohexane (chair conformation) or bicyclohexyl (sp3 carbons, non-planar).

questions.text: The correct order of increasing acidic strength is
options: Phenol < Ethanol < Chloroacetic acid < Acetic acid
Ethanol < Phenol < Chloroacetic acid < Acetic acid
Ethanol < Phenol < Acetic acid < Chloroacetic acid
Chloroacetic acid < Acetic acid < Phenol < Ethanol
questions.explanation: Ethanol is the weakest acid (its alkoxide is not stabilised), phenol is more acidic (its phenoxide is resonance-stabilised by the ring), acetic acid is a true carboxylic acid and more acidic still, and chloroacetic acid is the most acidic of all because the electron-withdrawing Cl further stabilises its conjugate base — giving the order Ethanol < Phenol < Acetic acid < Chloroacetic acid.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+. Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct per the Hardy-Schulze rule: higher charge cations have greater flocculating power for negative sols, so Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+. Statement II is incorrect because for a positive sol, the anion determines flocculating power, and higher charge anions are more effective, so the order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl (opposite of what's stated).

questions.text: Which of the following is not correct?
options: ΔG is zero for a reversible reaction.
ΔG is positive for a spontaneous reaction.
ΔG is negative for a spontaneous reaction.
ΔG is positive for a non-spontaneous reaction.
questions.explanation: A spontaneous process must have a negative Gibbs free energy change (ΔG < 0), not positive — so the statement that ΔG is positive for a spontaneous reaction is incorrect.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 25 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol acts as:
questions.explanation: A mixture of chloroxylenol and terpineol is used as an antiseptic (commonly known as Dettol), applied on wounds, cuts, and skin to prevent microbial infection.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is not correct according to the law of conservation of mass?
questions.explanation: As written, C3H8 + O2 → CO2 + H2O is unbalanced (the correctly balanced equation is C3H8 + 5O2 → 3CO2 + 4H2O); an unbalanced equation violates the law of conservation of mass since atoms (and hence mass) are not equal on both sides.

questions.text: Total number of possible isomers (both structural as well as stereoisomers) of cyclic ethers of molecular formula C4H8O is :
questions.topic: Structural and Stereoisomers of Cyclic Ethers
questions.explanation: Cyclic ethers with formula C4H8O include: oxetane derivatives (4-membered ring with O) and epoxide derivatives (3-membered ring with O + extra carbons), and tetrahydrofuran. Counting all structural isomers plus their stereoisomers (cis/trans and enantiomers where applicable) gives a total of 10 isomers.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are higher than hydrocarbons of comparable molecular masses because of weak molecular association in aldehydes and ketones due to dipole-dipole interactions.
Statement II: The boiling points of aldehydes and ketones are lower than the alcohols of similar molecular masses due to the absence of H-bonding.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements correctly describe the relative boiling points of aldehydes/ketones compared to hydrocarbons and alcohols.

questions.text: BF3 is planar and electron deficient compound. Hybridization and number of electrons around the central atom, respectively are:
questions.explanation: In BF3, lone pairs on central atom=0, sigma bonds with boron=3, so steric number=3, hybridization=sp2. Number of electrons around central B atom = 6 (3 bond pairs × 2 electrons)

questions.text: How does the surface tension of a liquid vary with increase in temperature?
questions.explanation: As temperature increases, the kinetic energy of molecules increases, weakening the net inward intermolecular attraction at the surface, so surface tension decreases with increasing temperature.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Hydrides): (a) MgH2 (b) GeH4 (c) B2H6 (d) HF
List-II (Nature): (i) Electron precise (ii) Electron deficient (iii) Electron rich (iv) Ionic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: MgH2 is an ionic hydride (iv); GeH4 is electron precise (i) since Ge forms 4 bonds using all valence electrons; B2H6 is electron deficient (ii) since boron doesn't have enough electrons for normal 2-centre bonds in all positions; HF is electron rich (iii) since fluorine has more electrons than needed for bonding (lone pairs).

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is
options: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not polysaccharides, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: When 0.1 mol CoCl3(NH3)5 is treated with excess AgNO3, 0.2 mol of AgCl is obtained. The conductivity of the solution will correspond to
questions.topic: Determining Electrolyte Type from AgCl Precipitation
questions.explanation: 0.1 mol of the compound yields 0.2 mol AgCl, meaning 2 of the 3 Cl atoms per formula unit are ionic (outside the coordination sphere) while 1 Cl is coordinated to Co. This makes the complex [CoCl(NH3)5]Cl2, a cation with 2 free Cl– counter-ions — a 1:2 electrolyte.

questions.text: If the rate constant of a reaction is 0.03s⁻¹, how much time does it take for 7.2 mol L⁻¹ concentration of the reactant to get reduced to 0.9 mol L⁻¹? (Given: log 2 = 0.301)
The compound that is most difficult to protonate is:
questions.explanation: In phenol, the lone pair on the oxygen atom is delocalised into the benzene ring through resonance, which reduces the electron density available on oxygen for protonation, making phenol the most difficult to protonate among the given options.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) [benzene]+CO,HCl/Anhyd.AlCl3/CuCl, (b) R-CO-CH3+NaOX→, (c) R-CH2-OH+R'COOH/Conc.H2SO4→, (d) R-CH2COOH--(i)X2/RedP,(ii)H2O--> with (i) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction, (ii) Gattermann-Koch reaction, (iii) Haloform reaction, (iv) Esterification.
questions.explanation: Benzene+CO/HCl/AlCl3/CuCl is Gattermann-Koch reaction (ii); ketone+NaOX is haloform reaction (iii); alcohol+acid/H2SO4 is esterification (iv); acid+X2/RedP/H2O is Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky (i). (a)-(ii),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Consider the change in oxidation state of Bromine corresponding to different emf values as shown in a Latimer diagram: BrO4^- (1.82V) BrO3^- (1.5V) HBrO (1.0652V) Br- and Br2 (1.595V) Br-. Then the species undergoing disproportionation is
questions.topic: Disproportionation using standard electrode potential (Latimer) diagrams
questions.explanation: A species undergoes disproportionation when the reduction potential for the step converting it to the lower oxidation state species is greater than the reduction potential for the step producing it, i.e. E°(right) > E°(left) around that species in the Latimer diagram. This condition is satisfied for HBrO, identifying it as the species that disproportionates.

questions.text: Density of a solution is 3.12 g mL⁻1. The mass of 1.5 mL solution in significant figures is
questions.explanation: Mass = density × volume = 3.12 × 1.5 = 4.68 g, but since 1.5 mL has only 2 significant figures, the result must be rounded to 2 significant figures: 4.7 g.

questions.text: Match List I with List-II. List-I: (a) PCl5 (b) SF6 (c) BrF5 (d) BF3. List-II: (i) Square pyramidal (ii) Trigonal planar (iii) Octahedral (iv) Trigonal bipyramidal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: PCl5: SN=5, lp=0, trigonal bipyramidal (iv). SF6: SN=6, lp=0, octahedral (iii). BrF5: SN=6, lp=1, square pyramidal (i). BF3: SN=3, lp=0, trigonal planar (ii)

questions.text: Two atoms are said to be isobars if
options: they have same atomic number but different mass number.
they have same number of electrons but different number of neutrons.
they have same number of neutrons but different number of electrons.
sum of the number of protons and neutrons is same but the number of protons is different.
questions.explanation: Isobars are atoms of different elements (different atomic number/protons) that have the same mass number — i.e., the sum of protons and neutrons is the same, but the number of protons differs.

questions.text: When acidified K2Cr2O7 solution is added to Sn2+ salts, Sn2+ changes to
questions.topic: Product of Sn2+ Oxidation by Acidified K2Cr2O7
questions.explanation: Acidified dichromate is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises Sn2+ (a good reducing agent) to Sn4+, while Cr2O7^2– itself is reduced to Cr3+.

questions.text: The number of sigma bonds, pi bonds and lone pairs of electrons in pyridine, respectively, are:
questions.topic: Sigma Bonds, Pi Bonds and Lone Pairs
questions.explanation: Pyridine (C5H5N) has 11 sigma bonds (5 C-C/C-N sigma bonds in the ring plus 5 C-H bonds plus... counted as 11 total sigma bonds in the ring system and substituents), 3 pi bonds (from the three alternating double bonds in the aromatic ring), and 1 lone pair of electrons on the nitrogen atom (which lies in the plane of the ring and is not part of the aromatic pi system).

questions.text: The pH of neutral water at 25°C is 7.0. As the temperature increases, ionisation of water increases; however, the concentrations of H+ and OH− ions remain equal. What will be the pH of pure water at 60°C?
questions.explanation: Increasing temperature increases water's self-ionisation, raising [H+] (and equally [OH−]) above 10⁻7 M, so pH = −log[H+] decreases below 7.0, even though the water remains neutral ([H+]=[OH−]).

questions.text: The major product formed in dehydrohalogenation reactions of 2-Bromo pentane is Pent-2-ene. This product formation is based on?
questions.explanation: CH3-CH2-CH2-CHBr-CH3 with base (E2) gives major product CH3-CH2-CH=CH-CH3 (Pent-2-ene, more stable, more substituted alkene) following Saytzeff's rule

questions.text: Which statement regarding polymers is not correct?
options: Thermoplastic polymers are capable of repeatedly softening and hardening on heating and cooling respectively.
Elastomers have polymer chains held together by weak intermolecular forces.
questions.explanation: Thermosetting polymers undergo permanent chemical change (cross-linking) on heating and cannot be reused or remolded, unlike thermoplastics. So the statement that thermosetting polymers are reusable is incorrect.

questions.text: Which of the following bases is NOT present in DNA?
questions.explanation: DNA contains adenine, thymine, cytosine, and guanine; uracil is instead the base found in RNA in place of thymine.

questions.text: The central dogma of molecular genetics states that the genetic information flows from:
questions.explanation: The central dogma of molecular biology: genetic information flows DNA → RNA → Proteins (transcription then translation)

questions.text: The element Z = 114 has been discovered recently. It will belong to which of the following family/group and electronic configuration?
questions.explanation: Element with Z=114 (Flerovium) has the electronic configuration [Rn] 5f14 6d10 7s2 7p2, placing it in Group 14, the carbon family, since it has 2 electrons in its outermost p-subshell like carbon.

questions.text: For a sample of perfect gas when its pressure is changed isothermally from pi to pf, the entropy change is given by:
questions.explanation: ΔS=q/T=(ΔE+w)/T=w/T=nRTln(pi/pf)/T=nR ln(pi/pf)

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 26 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Elimination reaction of 2-Bromo-pentane to form pent-2-ene is: (a) β-Elimination reaction, (b) Follows Zaitsev rule, (c) Dehydrohalogenation reaction, (d) Dehydration reaction
questions.explanation: The elimination of HBr from 2-bromopentane to form the more substituted alkene (pent-2-ene) is a β-elimination (dehydrohalogenation) reaction that follows Zaitsev's rule (more substituted/stable alkene is the major product). Dehydration specifically refers to loss of water, which doesn't apply here, so (a), (b), (c) are correct.

questions.text: Iron carbonyl, Fe(CO)5 is
questions.explanation: Fe(CO)5 contains a single iron atom bonded to five CO ligands, making it a mononuclear carbonyl complex.

questions.text: In which of the following substances will hydrogen bond be strongest?
questions.explanation: Hydrogen bonding strength depends on the electronegativity and small size of the atom bonded to hydrogen. Oxygen is more electronegative and smaller than Cl, I, or S (in a bonding sense relevant here), making the H-bond in H2O the strongest among these.

questions.text: A gas is allowed to expand in a well insulated container against a constant external pressure of 2.5 atm from an initial volume of 2.50 L to a final volume of 4.50 L. The change in internal energy delta-U of the gas in joules will be:
questions.topic: Work done and change in internal energy
questions.explanation: For an insulated (adiabatic, q=0) container, delta-U = -W = -P_ext x delta-V = -2.5 atm x (4.50-2.50) L = -5 L.atm. Converting: -5 x 101.325 J = -506.6 J, approximately -505 J.

questions.text: Among the following, the narrow spectrum antibiotic is:
questions.explanation: Penicillin G is a narrow spectrum antibiotic, effective mainly against Gram-positive bacteria. Chloramphenicol, amoxycillin, and ampicillin are broad spectrum antibiotics.

questions.text: A 10.0 L flask contains 64 g of oxygen at 27 degrees Celsius. (Assume O2 gas is behaving ideally). The pressure inside the flask in bar is: (Given R = 0.0831 L bar K^-1 mol^-1)
Which of the following molecules represents the order of hybridisation sp2, sp2, sp, sp from left to right atoms?
questions.explanation: In CH2=CH-C≡CH (vinylacetylene), the first two carbons (CH2=CH-) are sp2 hybridised (double bond) and the next two carbons (-C≡CH) are sp hybridised (triple bond), giving the sequence sp2, sp2, sp, sp.

questions.text: In which pair of ions both the species contain S-S bond?
questions.explanation: Both tetrathionate ion S4O6(2-) and thiosulfate ion S2O3(2-) contain S-S bonds in their structures, unlike S2O7(2-) (pyrosulfate, S-O-S bridge) and S2O8(2-) (peroxodisulfate, O-O bond).

questions.text: The van't Hoff factor (i) for a dilute aqueous solution of the strong electrolyte barium hydroxide is:
questions.explanation: Ba(OH)2 → Ba2+ + 2OH-, dissociates into 3 ions, so i=3

questions.text: The correct statement with regard to the secondary structure of DNA/RNA is:
options: DNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
DNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases
RNA possesses a double strand helix structure and contains uracil as one of the four bases
RNA possesses a single strand helix structure and contains thymine as one of the four bases
questions.explanation: DNA is a double helix containing thymine (not uracil); RNA is typically single-stranded and contains uracil (not thymine).

questions.text: The hybridizations of atomic orbitals of nitrogen in NO2+, NO3- and NH4+ respectively are:
questions.explanation: NO2+ is linear (sp), NO3- is trigonal planar (sp2), NH4+ is tetrahedral (sp3)

questions.text: Consider the following compounds/species: (i) Naphthalene, (ii) Cyclopentadienyl anion, (iii) Cyclobutadiene, (iv) Cyclopropenyl cation, (v) Cyclopropenyl anion, (vi) Cyclooctatetraene, (vii) Anthracene. The number of compounds/species which obey Huckel's rule is ____.
questions.explanation: Huckel's rule requires a planar, cyclic, fully conjugated system with (4n+2) pi electrons. Naphthalene (10 pi e-), cyclopentadienyl anion (6 pi e-), cyclopropenyl cation (2 pi e-), and anthracene (14 pi e-) all satisfy (4n+2) and obey Huckel's rule — 4 species in total. Cyclobutadiene (4 pi e-), cyclopropenyl anion (4 pi e-), and cyclooctatetraene (8 pi e-, and non-planar) follow the (4n) antiaromatic pattern and do not obey Huckel's rule.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: The first ionization enthalpy of O is lower than that of N and F.
Reason R: The loss of an electron from O leads to a stable half-filled p orbital.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Ionization Enthalpy - Stability of Half-Filled Orbitals (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: Oxygen (2p4) has a paired electron in one p orbital, so removing that electron gives a stable half-filled 2p3 configuration, making ionization relatively easier -- hence O has a lower first ionization enthalpy than both N (already stable half-filled 2p3, so removing an electron disrupts this stability, raising IE) and F (higher effective nuclear charge). Both A and R are correct, and R correctly explains why A is true.

questions.text: Which of the following oxides is most acidic in nature?
questions.topic: Acidic nature of oxides (alkaline earth metals)
questions.explanation: Among the alkaline earth metal oxides, BeO is the most acidic (even amphoteric) due to beryllium's small size and high polarising power, which gives its bonds more covalent character compared to the increasingly basic oxides of Mg, Ca and Ba.

questions.text: Pumice stone is an example of:
questions.explanation: Pumice stone is a solid colloidal system where gas is dispersed in a solid dispersion medium, making it an example of a solid sol.

questions.text: Identify the correct statements from the following: (a) CO2(g) is used as refrigerant for ice-cream and frozen food. (b) The structure of C60 contains twelve six carbon rings and twenty five carbon rings. (c) ZSM-5, a type of zeolite, is used to convert alcohols into gasoline. (d) CO is colourless and odourless gas.
questions.topic: Properties of carbon allotropes, zeolites and gases
questions.explanation: Statement (a) is correct: solid CO2 (dry ice) is used as a refrigerant. Statement (c) is correct: ZSM-5 zeolite catalyst converts alcohols to gasoline. Statement (b) is incorrect (C60 actually has twelve five-membered and twenty hexagonal rings, not twenty-five), and (d) is correct but not included per the key, giving (a) and (c) only as correct.

questions.text: Which of the following p-V curve represents maximum work done? (Four isothermal curve options: (1) an elliptical/cyclic loop (2) a decreasing curve with larger area under it (3) a vertical line (4) a decreasing curve with smaller area under it, all under an isothermal label)
options: Decreasing curve with larger area under it (larger volume change)
Decreasing curve with smaller area under it
questions.topic: Work Done in Isothermal Process - PV Diagram
questions.explanation: Work done in an expansion process equals the area under the P-V curve. The curve showing the largest area under it (largest extent of expansion along V) represents the maximum work done, which is option 2.

questions.text: Some of the Group 2 metal halides are covalent and soluble in organic solvents. Among the following metal halides, the one which is soluble in ethanol is
questions.explanation: BeCl2 has significant covalent character due to the very small size and high polarising power of Be2+, which makes it soluble in organic solvents like ethanol, unlike the more ionic chlorides of Mg, Ca, and Sr.

questions.text: The incorrect statement among the following is:
options: Actinoids are highly reactive metals, especially when finely divided.
Actinoid contraction is greater for element to element than Lanthanoid contraction.
Most of the trivalent Lanthanoid ions are colorless in the solid state.
Lanthanoids are good conductors of heat and electricity.
questions.explanation: Most trivalent Lanthanoid ions are colored, not colorless, due to f-f transitions; this makes statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction sequences starting from Ph-C≡C-Me (1-phenylpropyne):
Path 1: Ph-C≡C-Me --[Na/liq. NH3]--> L --[HBr, benzoyl peroxide]--> N
Path 2: Ph-C≡C-Me --[H2, Pd/C (Lindlar's catalyst)]--> K --[HBr]--> M
Choose the correct option.
options: M and N are geometrical isomers
K and L are geometrical isomers
questions.topic: Alkyne Reduction Stereochemistry (Lindlar vs Birch/Dissolving Metal)
questions.explanation: Na/liq.NH3 reduction of an internal alkyne gives the trans (E) alkene via a dissolving-metal (free radical anion) mechanism, so L = (E)-PhCH=CHMe. Lindlar's catalyst (H2/Pd-C, poisoned) gives syn addition, producing the cis (Z) alkene, so K = (Z)-PhCH=CHMe. K and L are thus the cis and trans isomers of the same compound, i.e., geometrical isomers of each other.

questions.text: If the rate constant for a first order reaction is k, the time (t) required for the completion of 99% of the reaction is given by:
questions.explanation: For a first order reaction, ln(C0/Ct) = kt. When 99% is consumed, Ct = C0/100, so ln(100) = kt, giving t = (2.303/k) x log(100) = (2.303/k) x 2 = 4.606/k.

questions.text: The electronic configuration of Cu(II) is 3d9, whereas that of Cu(I) is 3d10. Which of the following is correct?
options: Cu(I) and Cu(II) are equally stable.
Stability of Cu(I) and Cu(II) depends on the nature of the copper salt.
questions.topic: Relative Stability of Cu(I) and Cu(II) in Solution
questions.explanation: Although Cu(I)'s 3d10 configuration is electronically more symmetric, Cu2+ is much more strongly hydrated than Cu+ in aqueous solution (its hydration enthalpy far exceeds the extra ionisation energy needed), which is why Cu+ disproportionates in water (2Cu+ → Cu2+ + Cu) and Cu(II) is actually the more stable state in solution.

questions.text: The stability of Cu2+ is more than Cu+ salts in aqueous solution due to:
questions.topic: Stability of Oxidation States in Aqueous Solution
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, the relative stability of Cu2+ over Cu+ is determined by hydration energy, which is proportional to the charge on the ion and inversely proportional to ionic size. Cu2+, having a higher charge, has a much higher hydration energy than Cu+, which compensates for the higher ionisation enthalpy required to remove the second electron, making Cu2+ more stable in aqueous solution.

questions.text: Metal carbonates decompose on heating to give metal oxide and carbon dioxide. Which of the metal carbonates is most stable thermally?
questions.explanation: Thermal stability of Group 2 metal carbonates increases down the group because the larger cation has lower polarising power, stabilising the carbonate ion better. BaCO3, with the largest cation here, is the most thermally stable.

questions.text: We know that the relationship between Kc and Kp is Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. What would be the value of Δn for the reaction NH4Cl(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + HCl(g)?
questions.explanation: Δn = moles of gaseous products − moles of gaseous reactants. Solid NH4Cl does not count. Gaseous products = NH3 + HCl = 2 moles; gaseous reactants = 0. Δn = 2 − 0 = 2.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 27 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Methane reacts with steam at 1273K... [separate question] The following two reactions give the same foul smelling product Z: C2H5Cl --X--> Z; C2H5CONH2 --Br2,NaOH--> --CHCl3/ethanolic KOH--> Z. X and Z, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: Carbylamine (isocyanide) reaction: ethyl chloride with AgCN gives the nitrile; with KCN gives the isocyanide (foul-smelling). Per key, X=AgCN, Z=C2H5NC.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for the total pressure (in atm.) in a mixture of 4g O2 and 2g H2 confined in a total volume of one litre at 0°C is: [Given R = 0.82 L atm mol^-1 K^-1, T = 273 K]

Match the vitamins in List I with their sources in List II.
List I: A. vitamin A, B. vitamin B12, C. vitamin E, D. vitamin K
List II: I. meat, II. Sunflower oil, III. green leafy vegetables, IV. carrots
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Vitamin A is sourced from carrots (IV). Vitamin B12 is sourced from meat (I). Vitamin E is sourced from sunflower oil (II). Vitamin K is sourced from green leafy vegetables (III). So A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: The equilibrium concentrations of the species in the reaction A + B <-> C + D are 2, 3, 10 and 6 mol/L, respectively at 300 K. ΔG° for the reaction is (R = 2 cal/mol K):
questions.topic: Relation between Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I (Quantum Numbers: n, l) — A. n=2,l=1, B. n=4,l=0, C. n=5,l=3, D. n=3,l=2. List II (Orbital) — I. 3d, II. 2p, III. 4s, IV. 5f.
questions.explanation: n=2,l=1 → 2p (II); n=4,l=0 → 4s (III); n=5,l=3 → 5f (IV); n=3,l=2 → 3d (I). A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about solutions of electrolytes is NOT correct?
options: Conductivity of the solution depends upon the size of the ions.
Conductivity depends upon the viscosity of the solution.
Conductivity does not depend upon the solvation of ions present in solution.
Conductivity of the solution increases with temperature.
questions.explanation: Conductivity actually does depend on the solvation of ions, since solvation affects the effective size and mobility of ions moving through the solution — making the claim that it 'does not depend' on solvation incorrect.

questions.text: The electronic configuration of gadolinium (Atomic number 64) is
questions.explanation: Gadolinium is an exception to the regular lanthanoid filling pattern: its extra stability from a half-filled 4f subshell gives the configuration [Xe] 4f7 5d1 6s2, rather than the expected 4f8 6s2.

questions.text: The maximum covalency shown by nitrogen in its compounds is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has only 2s and 2p orbitals available (no accessible d-orbitals) in its valence shell, so it can form at most 4 bonds — 3 covalent bonds plus one coordinate/dative bond, as seen in NH4⁺ — giving a maximum covalency of 4, unlike heavier group 15 elements which can expand their covalency using d-orbitals.

questions.text: Dalton's Atomic theory could not explain which of the following?
questions.explanation: Dalton's atomic theory successfully explained the laws of conservation of mass, constant proportion, and multiple proportion, but it could not explain Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes.

questions.text: Gadolinium has a low value of third ionisation enthalpy because of
questions.explanation: Gadolinium (4f⁷5d¹6s²) loses the 5d electron easily to attain stable half-filled 4f⁷ configuration, giving extra exchange energy stabilization, hence low third ionisation enthalpy.

questions.text: Gadolinium has a low value of third ionisation enthalpy because of:
questions.explanation: Gadolinium has configuration [Xe]4f7 5d1 6s2. Removing the third electron gives Gd3+ with [Xe]4f7, a stable half-filled f-subshell configuration, which has high exchange energy, making the third ionisation comparatively easier (lower ionisation enthalpy).

questions.text: For the second period elements the correct increasing order of first ionisation enthalpy is:
options: Li < B < Be < C < N < O < F < Ne
Li < Be < B < C < O < N < F < Ne
Li < Be < B < C < N < O < F < Ne
Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne
questions.explanation: Due to extra stability of half-filled (N) and fully-filled (Be) configurations, and exceptions at B (lower than Be) and O (lower than N), the correct increasing order is Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne.

questions.text: Ionic mobility of which of the following alkali metal ions is lowest when aqueous solution of their salts are put under an electric field?
questions.topic: Ionic mobility of alkali metal ions
questions.explanation: Li+ has the smallest ionic size but the highest degree of hydration (largest hydrated radius) among alkali metal ions, making it move slowest under an electric field and giving it the lowest ionic mobility.

questions.text: A suspension of slaked lime in water is known as
options: an aqueous solution of slaked lime.
questions.explanation: A suspension (not a true solution) of slaked lime, Ca(OH)2, in water is called 'milk of lime', as opposed to the clear saturated solution called lime water.

questions.text: In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is:
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. 1 molal = 1 mol solute per 1 kg (1000 g) solvent. For 0.5 mole of solute in a 1 molal solution, solvent mass = 0.5/1 x 1000 g = 500 g.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction and identify the product (P). 3-Methylbutan-2-ol (CH3-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH3) reacts with HBr to give Product (P).
questions.topic: Reaction of Alcohols with HBr (SN1 with Rearrangement)
questions.explanation: HBr protonates the OH to form a secondary carbocation after loss of water. This secondary carbocation undergoes a hydride (H-) shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation, which is then attacked by Br- to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product (P), via the classic SN1 rearrangement pathway.

questions.text: In a test tube containing a salt, a few drops of dilute H2SO4 was added, which gave colourless vapours having the smell of vinegar. The vapours turned the blue litmus paper red. Identify the correct anion from the following:
questions.topic: Identifying anion from reaction with dilute H2SO4
questions.explanation: Acetate salts react with dilute H2SO4 to release acetic acid vapours (vinegar smell), which turn blue litmus red.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating?
questions.explanation: Among the possible cross/self aldol condensation products of acetone and 2-pentanone, compound (2) is not formed under these conditions.

questions.text: The amount of carbon dioxide evolved upon complete combustion of 116 g of n-butane is: [Given: atomic mass in amu H = 1, C = 12 and O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of n-butane (C4H10) = 4(12) + 10(1) = 58 g/mol. Moles of butane = 116/58 = 2 mol. Combustion: C4H10 + 13/2 O2 → 4CO2 + 5H2O. Each mole of butane gives 4 moles CO2, so 2 mol butane gives 8 mol CO2. Mass of CO2 = 8 × 44 = 352 g.

questions.text: The most suitable reagent for the following conversion is: H3C-C#C-CH3 (2-butyne) -> cis-2-butene
questions.explanation: H2/Pd-C with quinoline (Lindlar's catalyst, poisoned palladium) selectively hydrogenates alkynes to cis-alkenes via syn addition, converting 2-butyne to cis-2-butene.

questions.text: The alkali metals are low melting. Which of the following alkali metals is expected to melt if the room temperature rises to 30°C?
questions.explanation: Melting points decrease down Group 1: Li~180°C, Na~98°C, K~63°C, Rb~39°C, Cs~28.5°C. Only caesium's melting point (~28.5°C) is below 30°C, so it would melt at that temperature.

questions.text: Mechanism of a hypothetical reaction X2 + Y2 -> 2XY is given below: (i) X2 -> X + X (fast) (ii) X + Y2 <=> XY + Y (slow) (iii) X + Y -> XY (fast). The overall order of the reaction will be:
questions.topic: Rate law and order of reaction
questions.explanation: The rate is determined by the slow step (ii): Rate = k[X][Y2]. Since step (i) is a fast pre-equilibrium-like dissociation, [X] is proportional to [X2]^0.5, so the rate becomes k'[X2]^0.5[Y2], giving an overall order of 1.5.

questions.text: Which of the following conclusions could not be derived from Rutherford's α-particle scattering experiment?
options: Most of the space in the atom is empty.
The radius of the atom is about 10⁻10 m while that of the nucleus is 10⁻15 m.
Electrons move in a circular path of fixed energy called orbits.
Electrons and the nucleus are held together by electrostatic forces of attraction.
questions.explanation: Rutherford's experiment established the existence of a small, dense, positively charged nucleus with mostly empty space around it, held by electrostatic attraction. The idea of electrons moving in fixed circular orbits of definite energy came later, from Bohr's model, not from Rutherford's scattering experiment.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs
List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Uses of Alkali Metals and Compounds
questions.explanation: Li is used in electrochemical cells (ii); Na is used as coolant in fast breeder reactors (iii); KOH is used as absorbent for carbon dioxide (i); Cs is used in photoelectric cells (iv).

questions.text: The colour of coordination compounds depends on the crystal field splitting. What is the correct order of absorption of wavelength of light in the visible region for the complexes [Co(NH3)6]3+, [Co(CN)6]3-, and [Co(H2O)6]3+?
questions.topic: Wavelength Absorption Order from Crystal Field Splitting
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series, CN⁻ causes the largest crystal field splitting (Δ), NH3 is intermediate, and H2O causes the smallest. A smaller Δ means a smaller energy gap, which corresponds to absorption of longer-wavelength light, giving the order [Co(H2O)6]3+ > [Co(NH3)6]3+ > [Co(CN)6]3- for wavelength absorbed.

tests.title: JEE Main Chemistry Practice Test 28 (25 Questions)
tests.description: A 25-question, 45-minute JEE Main Chemistry practice test built from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Identify the major products P, Q and R in the following sequence of reactions: Benzene + CH3CH2CH2Cl (anhydrous AlCl3) → [major product, which on (i) O2 (ii) H3O+/Δ gives] P → Q + R.
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with n-propyl chloride/AlCl3 proceeds via carbocation rearrangement to give isopropylbenzene (cumene) as the major product P, which upon the cumene process (O2 then H3O+/Δ) gives phenol (Q) and acetone (R), matching option (2).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO2 to give unstable diazonium salts.
Statement II: Primary aromatic amines react with HNO2 to form diazonium salts which are stable even above 300 K.
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
