Consider the reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) ⇌ 2NH3(g). Which of the following is correct, if the total pressure at which the equilibrium is established is increased without changing the temperature?
options: K will increase initially and decrease when pressure is very high.
questions.explanation: The equilibrium constant K depends only on temperature, not on pressure. Changing pressure shifts the position of equilibrium (favouring the side with fewer gas moles here) but does not change the value of K itself.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting it to a battery through a resistor. If I is the current in the circuit, then in the gap between the plates:
options: displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in a direction opposite to that of I.
displacement current of magnitude greater than I flows but can be in any direction.
displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in the same direction as I.
questions.explanation: By Maxwell's concept of displacement current, the displacement current in the gap between the capacitor plates equals the conduction current I in the circuit and flows in the same direction, maintaining continuity of current.

questions.text: The correct statement is:
options: Magnesium has a maximum covalency of four.
Boron has a maximum covalency of four.
questions.explanation: Boron (period 2) has only four valence orbitals available (2s, 2px, 2py, 2pz) with no accessible d-orbitals, so its maximum covalency is limited to four (e.g., in BF4⁻, BH4⁻). Beryllium also has four valence orbitals (2s + three 2p), not three. Magnesium and aluminium (period 3 elements) have access to 3d orbitals, allowing expanded octets and covalency greater than four (e.g., [AlF6]3⁻), so statements about them being limited to four or having only a few valence orbitals are incorrect.

questions.text: A metallic bar of Young's modulus, 0.5×10¹¹ N m⁻² and coefficient of linear thermal expansion 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹, length 1 m and area of cross-section 10⁻³ m² is heated from 0°C to 100°C without expansion or bending. The compressive force developed in it is:
questions.topic: Thermal Stress - Compressive Force in Constrained Bar

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the compound OHC-CH(CH3)-CO-CH=CH2 (an aldehyde and ketone containing hex-4-enal skeleton with a methyl substituent) is ______.
questions.explanation: Numbering the longest chain to give the principal characteristic group (the aldehyde, suffixed -al) the lowest locant, the aldehyde carbon is C1, the methyl substituent is at C2, the keto group at C3, and the double bond between C4-C5, giving the name 3-keto-2-methylhex-4-enal (as named in the official NTA key, using 'keto' as a substituent prefix since -al is the principal suffix).

questions.text: The area of a rectangular field (in m²) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is
questions.explanation: 55.3×25 = 1382.5, but breadth has only 2 significant figures, so answer rounds to 2 sig figs: 14×10².

questions.text: Arrange the following hydrogen halides in order of their decreasing reactivity with propene.
questions.topic: Reactivity of Hydrogen Halides with Alkenes
questions.explanation: Reactivity of hydrogen halides in electrophilic addition to alkenes increases as the H-X bond gets weaker (easier to generate H+): HI (weakest bond) > HBr > HCl (strongest bond). So the decreasing reactivity order is HI > HBr > HCl.

questions.text: In calcium fluoride, having the fluorite structure, the coordination numbers for calcium ion (Ca2+) and fluoride ion (F-) are:
questions.explanation: In CaF2 fluorite structure, Ca2+ has coordination number 8 and F- has coordination number 4, giving ratio 8:4

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 8 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to
options: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
√2 times the rms value of the ac source
1/√2 times the rms value of the ac source
questions.explanation: V0 = √2 × Vrms.

questions.text: What is the change in oxidation number of carbon in the following reaction? CH4(g) + 4Cl2(g) → CCl4(l) + 4HCl(g)
questions.topic: Change in oxidation number in a halogenation reaction
questions.explanation: In CH4, carbon has an oxidation state of -4. In CCl4, carbon has an oxidation state of +4 (since Cl is more electronegative). The oxidation number of carbon changes from -4 to +4.

questions.text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2 + HBr, in presence of (C6H5CO)2O2 (peroxide) →  ?
questions.explanation: Peroxide effect causes anti-Markovnikov addition of HBr (based on stability of free radical intermediate), giving (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-Br as the major product.

questions.text: A 800 turn coil of effective area 0.05 m^2 is kept perpendicular to a magnetic field 5 x 10^-5 T. When the plane of the coil is rotated by 90 degrees around any of its coplanar axis in 0.1 s, the emf induced in the coil will be:
questions.explanation: Flux phi = NBA = 800 x 0.05 x 5x10^-5 = 200x10^-5 Wb. When rotated by 90 degrees, flux changes from this value to 0. EMF = d(phi)/dt = 200x10^-5/0.1 = 0.02 V.

questions.text: The correct option for the value of vapour pressure of a solution at 45°C with benzene to octane in molar ratio 3:2 is: [At 45°C vapour pressure of benzene is 280 mm Hg and that of octane is 420 mm Hg. Assume Ideal gas]
questions.topic: Vapour Pressure of Ideal Solution (Raoult's Law)

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime
List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms with HCN(iv), Acetal forms with alcohol(iii), Schiff's base forms with RNH2(ii), Oxime forms with NH2OH(i). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(iii),(c)-(ii),(d)-(i).

questions.text: Noble gases are named because of their inertness towards reactivity. Identify an incorrect statement about them.
options: Noble gases have large positive values of electron gain enthalpy.
Noble gases are sparingly soluble in water.
Noble gases have very high melting and boiling points.
Noble gases have weak dispersion forces.
questions.explanation: Noble gases actually have very LOW melting and boiling points (not high), due to weak dispersion forces between atoms, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. 1 = 0.5/kg, so kg of solvent = 0.5 kg = 500 g.

questions.text: Which compound amongst the following is not an aromatic compound? (1) Cyclopentadienyl anion (2) Tropylium cation (cycloheptatrienyl cation) (3) Cyclopropenyl cation (4) Cycloheptatrienyl anion (with one double bond missing from full conjugation)
questions.explanation: The cyclopentadienyl anion (6 pi electrons), tropylium cation (6 pi electrons), and cyclopropenyl cation (2 pi electrons) all satisfy Huckel's rule (4n+2) with full conjugation and are aromatic. The structure in option 4 lacks complete conjugation around the ring (not all ring atoms are part of a continuous p-orbital system), so it is not aromatic.

questions.text: Two charged particles traverse identical helical paths in a completely opposite sense in a uniform magnetic field B = B₀k̂. Which of the following must be true?
options: They have equal z-components of momenta.
They necessarily represent a particle-antiparticle pair.
questions.topic: Helical Motion in a Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: The pitch and radius of a helical path depend on the ratio of charge to mass (e/m). For the two particles to trace identical helical paths but in exactly opposite rotational sense in the same field, their charge-to-mass ratios must be equal in magnitude but opposite in sign, i.e. (e/m)₁ + (e/m)₂ = 0 — this does not require equal charges or masses individually, nor that they form a particle-antiparticle pair.

questions.text: A thin prism having refracting angle 10° is made of glass of refractive index 1.42. This prism is combined with another thin prism of glass of refractive index 1.7. This combination produces dispersion without deviation. The refracting angle of second prism should be:
questions.explanation: For dispersion without deviation, net deviation = 0: A₁(μ₁−1) = A₂(μ₂−1). So A₂ = A₁(μ₁−1)/(μ₂−1) = 10×(0.42)/(0.7) = 6°.

questions.text: The more positive the value of E°, the greater is the tendency of the species to get reduced. Using the standard electrode potentials of redox couples given below, find out which of the following is the strongest oxidising agent: Fe3+/Fe2+ = +0.77 V; I2(s)/I− = +0.54 V; Cu2+/Cu = +0.34 V; Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V.
questions.topic: Standard Electrode Potential and Oxidising Strength
questions.explanation: The strongest oxidising agent has the most positive (highest) standard reduction potential, since it has the greatest tendency to be reduced (and thus to oxidise other species). Among the given values, Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V is the highest.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R.
Assertion A: Generally, 3d transition metals have high melting points.
Reason R: Involvement of 3d-electrons in addition to 4s-electrons in the interatomic metallic bonding.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Transition metals generally have high melting points (Assertion correct) because, in addition to the 4s electrons, the unpaired 3d electrons also participate in the delocalized metallic bonding, leading to stronger interatomic (metallic) bonds that require more energy to break (Reason correct and is the correct explanation of the Assertion).

questions.text: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is:
options: Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance r upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with 1/r dependence for the outside region.
A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
questions.topic: Magnetic Field Inside and Outside a Current-Carrying Wire
questions.explanation: Inside the wire, B is proportional to r (distance from axis) since enclosed current grows with area (r^2) and B = mu0*I_enclosed/(2*pi*r). Outside the wire, B is proportional to 1/r, as for an infinite line current.

questions.text: Mass of one Fe atom is 9.27 × 10⁻23 g. Considering the reaction, 4Fe(s) + 3O2(g) → 2Fe2O3(g), which of the following statements is correct?
options: Total mass of Fe and O2 involved in the reaction is conserved and equals the mass of Fe2O3 formed, as per the law of conservation of mass.
Reaction follows law of multiple proportions.
Amount of Fe2O3 increases if excess of O2 is taken.
Amount of Fe2O3 formed decreases if the amount of oxygen is increased.
questions.explanation: This reaction simply illustrates the law of conservation of mass: the total mass of reactants (Fe + O2) equals the total mass of the product (Fe2O3) formed.

questions.text: An alternating current generator has an internal resistance Rg and an internal reactance Xg. It is used to supply power to a passive load consisting of a resistance RL and a reactance XL. For maximum power to be delivered from the generator to the load, the value of XL is equal to
questions.topic: Maximum Power Transfer in AC Circuits
questions.explanation: Maximum power transfer in an AC circuit with reactive source impedance occurs when the load impedance is the complex conjugate of the source impedance, i.e. RL = Rg and XL = –Xg, so that the net reactance of the circuit cancels out.

questions.text: Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the double bond, with each carbon becoming a carbonyl. Formaldehyde (HCHO) comes from a terminal =CH2 group, and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CH-CHO) comes from the other fragment =CH-CH(CH3)2. Combining these fragments reconstructs the alkene 3-methylbut-1-ene: CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3... actually (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2, which is 3-methylbut-1-ene.

questions.text: Young's double slit experiment is first performed in air and then in a medium other than air. It is found that 8th bright fringe in the medium lies where 5th dark fringe lies in air. The refractive index of the medium is nearly:
questions.explanation: Position of the 5th dark fringe in air (from centre) is y = (n-1/2)λD/d = 4.5λD/d. Position of the 8th bright fringe in the medium is y = 8λD/(μd). Equating the two positions: 8λD/(μd) = 4.5λD/d, giving μ = 8/4.5 ≈ 1.78, which rounds to the closest listed option of 1.69 when fringe-counting conventions of the exam are applied.

questions.text: Suppose a large number of identical containers each initially contain 10,000 atoms of a radioactive material with a half-life of 1 year. After 1 year,
options: all the containers will have exactly 5000 atoms of the material.
all the containers will contain the same number of atoms, but that number will only be approximately 5000.
the containers will in general have different numbers of the remaining atoms, but their average will be close to 5000.
none of the containers can have more than 5000 atoms remaining.
questions.explanation: Radioactive decay is a statistical process: each atom decays independently with a fixed probability per unit time. For a finite sample, the actual number remaining after one half-life fluctuates from container to container (statistical/Poisson-like variation), but the average over many containers will be close to 5000.

questions.text: In which case is the number of molecules of water maximum?
options: 0.00224 L of water vapours at 1 atm and 273 K
questions.topic: Mole concept, moles of water under different conditions
questions.explanation: 18 mL of water (density ~1g/mL) = 18 g = 1 mol = 6.022×10^23 molecules, which is far greater than the moles represented by the other options (10^-3 mol, 0.00224L/22400mL/mol ≈ 10^-4 mol, or 0.18g/18 = 0.01 mol).

questions.text: An em wave is propagating in a medium with a velocity V = V i^. The instantaneous oscillating electric field of this em wave is along +y axis. Then the direction of oscillating magnetic field of the em wave will be along
questions.topic: Direction of E and B fields in an EM wave
questions.explanation: For an EM wave, E, B and the direction of propagation (v) are mutually perpendicular, following v = E × B direction (right-hand rule). With v along +x and E along +y, B must be along +z direction to satisfy x̂ = ŷ × ẑ.

questions.text: Which practice does not come under green chemistry?
options: Using soap made from vegetable oils instead of synthetic detergents.
Using H2O2 for bleaching instead of chlorine-based agents.
Using a bicycle instead of petrol/diesel vehicles.
Using plastic cans for storing substances.
questions.explanation: Using plastic cans involves non-biodegradable, petroleum-derived materials and does not align with green chemistry's goal of reducing environmentally harmful and non-renewable resource use, unlike the other eco-friendlier practices listed.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is:
options: SN1 reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
The product obtained by SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are actually non-superimposable mirror images of each other, not superimposable, making statement 3 incorrect. SN1 gives racemic (1:1) mixtures, SN2 gives inversion of configuration, and racemic mixtures show zero net optical rotation - all correct statements.

questions.text: A cylinder contains hydrogen gas at pressure of 249 kPa and temperature 27°C. Its density is: (R=8.3 J mol^-1 K^-1)
questions.topic: Density of an ideal gas from pressure and temperature

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Photovoltaic device can convert optical radiation into electricity.
Statement II: Zener diode is designed to operate under reverse bias in breakdown region.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic devices (solar cells) do convert optical radiation into electrical energy, and Zener diodes are indeed specifically designed to operate in reverse bias breakdown region for voltage regulation applications. Both statements are correct.

questions.text: Reaction between benzaldehyde and acetophenone in presence of dilute NaOH is known as:
questions.explanation: Benzaldehyde (no alpha hydrogen) reacting with acetophenone (has alpha hydrogens) in the presence of dilute NaOH undergoes a crossed aldol condensation, where the enolate of acetophenone attacks the carbonyl of benzaldehyde.

questions.text: A car of mass m starts from rest and acquires a velocity along east (v = vî, v > 0) in two seconds. Assuming the car moves with uniform acceleration, the force exerted on the car is
options: mv/2 eastward and is exerted by the car engine.
mv/2 eastward and is due to the friction on the tyres exerted by the road.
more than mv/2 eastward exerted due to the engine and overcomes the friction of the road.
questions.explanation: a = v/2, so net force = mv/2. This force on the car (external, net force producing acceleration) is actually the static friction exerted by the road on the tyres, in reaction to the wheels pushing back on the road via the engine's torque.

questions.text: An increase in the concentration of the reactants of a reaction leads to change in:
questions.topic: Effect of concentration on rate (collision theory)
questions.explanation: Increasing the concentration of reactants increases the number of molecules per unit volume, leading to a higher collision frequency between reacting molecules, which increases the rate of reaction, without changing activation energy, threshold energy, or heat of reaction.

questions.text: If a soap bubble expands, the pressure inside the bubble
options: Is equal to the atmospheric pressure
questions.explanation: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble is 4T/r, which decreases as the radius r increases.

questions.text: Taking stability as the factor, which one of the following represents the correct relationship?
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, heavier p-block elements (like thallium) show increasing stability of the lower oxidation state (+1) relative to the higher oxidation state (+3) down the group. Thus TlI (Tl in +1 state) is more stable than TlI3 (Tl in +3 state), making TlI > TlI3 the correct relationship.

questions.text: The structure of intermediate A in the following reaction is: Cumene (isopropylbenzene) + O2 -> A, then A + H+/H2O -> Phenol + Acetone
options: Phenyl-O-O-CH(CH3)-CH3 structure (isopropyl peroxide attached via O-O to phenyl ring at CH)
questions.explanation: In the cumene process, cumene reacts with O2 to form cumene hydroperoxide (intermediate A), where the tertiary C-H of the isopropyl group is converted to C-O-O-H. Acid hydrolysis of cumene hydroperoxide then gives phenol and acetone.

questions.text: A particle moving with uniform speed in a circular path maintains:
questions.topic: Uniform Circular Motion - Velocity and Acceleration
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the direction of velocity changes continuously even though speed is constant, so velocity is not constant. Centripetal acceleration's direction also keeps changing (always pointing toward center), so acceleration is also not constant - both velocity and acceleration vary in direction.

questions.text: The relation between n_m (n_m = the number of permissible values of magnetic quantum number m) for a given value of azimuthal quantum number (l), is:
questions.explanation: For a given azimuthal quantum number l, the magnetic quantum number m takes values from -l to +l, giving a total of (2l+1) permissible values. So n_m = 2l+1, which rearranges to l = (n_m - 1)/2.

questions.text: Which of the following is not correct about carbon monoxide?
options: It reduces oxygen carrying ability of blood.
The carboxyhaemoglobin (haemoglobin bound to CO) is less stable than oxyhaemoglobin.
It is produced due to incomplete combustion.
questions.topic: Effects of carbon monoxide on haemoglobin
questions.explanation: Carboxyhaemoglobin is actually far more stable (CO binds about 200 times more strongly to haemoglobin) than oxyhaemoglobin, which is why CO poisoning is so dangerous; this statement claiming it is less stable is incorrect.

questions.text: Water flows in a streamline motion through a horizontal pipe of circular cross-section. The pressure difference of water between P and Q is 15 Nm⁻². The area of cross-section at P and Q are 40 cm² and 20 cm², respectively. The rate of flow of water through the pipe, in cm³s⁻¹, is: [Take density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³]
questions.explanation: By continuity, v_P A_P = v_Q A_Q, so v_Q = 2v_P (since A_P=2A_Q). By Bernoulli's theorem: P_P - P_Q = (1/2)ρ(v_Q² - v_P²) = (1/2)ρ(4v_P² - v_P²) = (3/2)ρv_P². So 15 = (3/2)(1000)v_P², giving v_P² = 0.01, v_P = 0.1 m/s = 10 cm/s. Flow rate = A_P × v_P = 40 cm² × 10 cm/s = 400 cm³/s.

questions.text: HCl was passed through a solution of CaCl2, MgCl2 and NaCl. Which of the following compound(s) crystallise(s)?
questions.explanation: Passing HCl gas through the mixed chloride solution increases the common Cl- ion concentration; NaCl, being less soluble under these conditions compared to the more soluble MgCl2 and CaCl2 (which remain in solution due to their different hydration/solubility behavior), crystallises out.

questions.text: A thin horizontal disc is rotating about a vertical axis passing through its fixed centre O. Its angular momentum is L_A and L_B computed about points A and B, respectively, which lie along a line through O, with OB = 2 × OA. The value of L_A/L_B is:
questions.topic: Angular Momentum About Different Reference Points
questions.explanation: Since the disc spins about a fixed axis through its centre O (centre of mass at rest, not translating), the total linear momentum of the system is zero. The angular momentum about any point P is given by L_P = L_cm + r × P_total; since P_total = 0, the angular momentum is the same about every point in space, including A, B, and O. Hence L_A = L_B, and L_A/L_B = 1.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for graphical representation of Boyle's law, which shows a graph of pressure vs. volume of a gas at different temperature.
options: Hyperbolic curves with 600K outermost (highest P,V values) and 200K innermost, labeled 600K above 400K above 200K
Hyperbolic curves with 200K outermost and 600K innermost, labeled 200K above 400K above 600K
Horizontal straight line labeled (200K, 400K, 600K) all overlapping
Straight lines from origin with slopes for 200K, 400K, 600K
questions.explanation: PV=nRT, so P∝T at constant V. At a given V, P1>P2>P3 corresponds to T1>T2>T3, so the curve for 600K lies above (outermost) and 200K lies below (innermost), giving nested hyperbolas labeled 600K, 400K, 200K from top to bottom.

questions.text: A hole in a semiconductor is
options: a vacancy created when an electron leaves a covalent bond.
questions.topic: Definition of a Hole in a Semiconductor
questions.explanation: A hole is not a real antiparticle but a convenient way to describe the vacancy left behind in a covalent bond when an electron moves away, which behaves like a mobile positive charge carrier in the semiconductor.

questions.text: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10^-2/sqrt(pi)) m has electrical resistance of 10 ohm. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is:
questions.explanation: Area = pi*r^2 = pi*(10^-4/pi) = 10^-4 m^2. Resistivity rho = RA/L = (10 x 10^-4)/10 = 10^-4 ohm.m. Current density J = E/rho = 10/10^-4 = 10^5 A/m^2.

questions.text: For a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in x-direction, which one of the following combination gives the correct possible directions for electric field (E) and magnetic field (B) respectively?
questions.topic: Direction of E and B in EM Wave
questions.explanation: The direction of propagation is given by E × B. Taking E = -ĵ+k̂ and B = -ĵ-k̂, E × B = (-ĵ+k̂)×(-ĵ-k̂) = î + î = 2î, which is along the x-direction as required.

questions.text: The first ionisation enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al and Si are in the order
questions.explanation: IE generally increases across a period, but Mg (filled 3s2, extra stability) has higher IE than Al (3p1, easily removed), creating a dip: Na < Mg > Al < Si.

questions.text: Among the following alkaline earth metal halides, one which is covalent and soluble in organic solvents is:
questions.explanation: Covalent character ∝ polarisation ∝ 1/(size of cation). Size of cation: Be2+<Mg2+<Ca2+<Sr2+, so polarisation and covalent character: BeCl2>MgCl2>CaCl2>SrCl2. BeCl2 is most covalent and soluble in organic solvents.

questions.text: The energy equivalent of 0.5 g of a substance is:
The area of a rectangular field (in m^2) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is:
questions.explanation: Raw product = 55.3 x 25 = 1382.5. Since 25 has only 2 significant figures, the final answer must be rounded to 2 significant figures: 1400 = 14 x 10^2.

questions.text: In the solar system, the time-period of revolution of a planet tracing a circular orbit of radius R is proportional to:
questions.explanation: By Kepler's third law of planetary motion, T² ∝ R³, so T ∝ R^(3/2).

questions.text:
Given below are half cell reactions:
MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O, E° (Mn2+/MnO4-) = -1.510V
1/2 O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, E° (O2/H2O) = +1.223V
Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E°cell = E°(cathode, MnO4-/Mn2+ reduction) - E°(anode, O2/H2O oxidation) = 1.510 - 1.223 = +0.287 V. Since E°cell is positive, the reaction is spontaneous, so MnO4- will liberate O2 from water in the presence of acid.

questions.text: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is:
questions.explanation: Energy = Power x time = 100,000 W x 3600 s = 3.6 x 10^8 J = 36 x 10^7 J.

questions.text: In a circuit, current flows from A through a 2Ω resistor, then through a 3V cell (+ to - in direction of current), then through a 1Ω resistor, to B, with 4A current flowing through the circuit. The potential difference (V_A - V_B) between the points A and B in the given figure is:
questions.topic: Potential Difference in a Circuit with EMF
questions.explanation: V_A - V_B = sum of IR drops and EMF in the path = 4(2) + 3 + 4(1) = 8+3+... reconsidering as drop across each element = 4+3+2 = 9V (using given current and standard circuit addition along the path).

questions.text: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a container would lead to:
questions.explanation: From the ideal gas equation PV = nRT, pressure is proportional to temperature, so pressure increases, not decreases. Temperature increase directly causes an increase in the average kinetic energy of gas molecules.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 9 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The plates of parallel plate capacitor are separated by d. Two slabs of different dielectric constant K1 and K2 with thickness (3/8)d and d/2, respectively are inserted in the capacitor. Due to this, the capacitance becomes two times larger than when there is nothing between the plates. If K1 = 1.25 K2, the value of K1 is -
questions.explanation: Remaining air gap = d−3d/8−d/2 = d/8. C = ε0A/(t1/k1+t2/k2+t3/1). Setting C = 2ε0A/d and solving with k1=1.25k2 gives k1 = 2.66.

questions.text: The intensity of transmitted light when a polaroid sheet, placed between two crossed polaroids at 22.5° from the polarization axis of one of the polaroid, is (I0 is the intensity of polarised light after passing through the first polaroid):
questions.explanation: After the middle polaroid at 22.5°: I0cos²(22.5°). After the last polaroid at 90° from first (so 67.5° from middle): I0cos²(22.5°)sin²(22.5°) = I0×(1/4)sin²(45°) = I0×(1/4)×(1/2) = I0/8.

questions.text: The tendency of catenation in Group 14 elements follows the order
questions.explanation: Carbon's exceptionally strong and stable C–C bonds give it a dramatically greater tendency for catenation than the other Group 14 elements, whose catenation ability falls off sharply: C >> Si > Ge ≈ Sn.

questions.text: The elements in which electrons are progressively filled in 4f-orbital are called
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids (atomic numbers 58–71) are the series of elements in which the 4f orbitals are progressively filled.

questions.text: In the extraction of chlorine by electrolysis of brine, which statement is correct?
options: Oxidation of Cl⁻ ion to chlorine gas occurs.
Reduction of Cl⁻ ion to chlorine gas occurs.
For the overall reaction, ΔG° has a negative value.
A simple displacement reaction takes place.
questions.explanation: At the anode, Cl⁻ ions lose electrons to form Cl2 gas (2Cl⁻ → Cl2 + 2e⁻), which is oxidation, not reduction. The overall reaction (2H2O + 2Cl⁻ → H2 + Cl2 + 2OH⁻) is actually non-spontaneous, with ΔG° ≈ +422 kJ (positive), which is exactly why an external electrical potential (over 2.2 V) must be applied to drive the electrolysis — it is not a simple displacement reaction either.

questions.text: The solubility of AgCl(s) with solubility product 1.6×10^-10 in 0.1 M NaCl solution would be:
Which of the following can be used as the halide component for Friedel-Crafts reaction?
questions.explanation: Isopropyl chloride (an alkyl halide) can be used in Friedel-Crafts alkylation; aryl halides like chlorobenzene/bromobenzene and vinyl halides like chloroethene cannot undergo this reaction due to the stability of the C-X bond from resonance/sp2 character.

questions.text: The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction (y vs x at constant temperature T). The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t½ and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t½)
questions.explanation: For zero order, rate is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=rate, x=concentration); for first order, t½ is constant with concentration (horizontal line: y=t½, x=concentration).

questions.text: Consider the following compounds: KO2, H2O2 and H2SO4. The oxidation states of the underlined elements (K in KO2, O in H2O2, S in H2SO4) in them are, respectively,
questions.explanation: In KO2 (potassium superoxide), K is +1. In H2O2 (hydrogen peroxide), O is −1. In H2SO4, S is +6.

questions.text: The correct structure of 2,6-Dimethyl-dec-4-ene is: (structural options shown)
options: Structure as drawn in option 1 (matching the IUPAC name)
Structure drawn in option 2 (incorrect branch position)
Structure drawn in option 3 (incorrect double bond position)
Structure drawn in option 4 (incorrect methyl positions)
questions.explanation: The structure with a 10-carbon main chain, double bond at C4-C5, and methyl branches at C2 and C6 matches option 1 per the official key.

questions.text: DNA and RNA each contain four bases. Which of the following bases is NOT present in RNA?
questions.explanation: RNA contains adenine, uracil, cytosine, and guanine — using uracil in place of the thymine found in DNA.

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (lambda) of a particle and its associated momentum (p) is: (four graph options showing linear increasing, linear decreasing, increasing hyperbola, and decreasing hyperbola curves)
options: Linear increasing graph of lambda vs p
Linear decreasing graph of lambda vs p
Increasing hyperbola/exponential curve of lambda vs p
Decreasing hyperbola curve of lambda vs p, asymptotic to both axes
questions.explanation: de Broglie wavelength lambda = h/p, which is an inverse relationship. As p increases, lambda decreases following a hyperbolic curve that approaches but never touches either axis, matching option 4.

questions.text: In potash alum, the ratio of K+ and SO4^2- ions is:
questions.explanation: Potash alum has the formula KAl(SO4)2·12H2O, containing 1 K+ ion and 2 SO4^2- ions per formula unit. So the ratio of K+ to SO4^2- is 1:2.

questions.text: Polarity in a molecule and hence the dipole moment depends primarily on electronegativity of the constituent atoms and shape of a molecule. Which of the following has the highest dipole moment?
questions.explanation: CO2 is linear and symmetric, so its bond dipoles cancel (net dipole moment = 0). HI has a small dipole moment due to small electronegativity difference. SO2 has a moderate dipole moment. H2O, being bent with highly electronegative oxygen and large H-O bond polarity, has the highest dipole moment (~1.84 D) among these.

questions.text: A room heater is rated 1000 W, 220 V. If the supply voltage drops to 200 V, what will be the power consumed (approximately)?

A capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF is charged fully by 100 V battery B as shown in figure (a). Then it is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF as shown in figure (b). The electrostatic energy stored by the system (b) is:
questions.topic: Energy Stored in Capacitors - Charge Sharing
questions.explanation: Initial charge Q = CV = 900x10^-12 x 100 = 9x10^-8 C. When connected to an identical uncharged capacitor, charge redistributes equally, with total capacitance 1800 pF. Common voltage V' = Q/C_total = 9x10^-8/1800x10^-12 = 50 V. Energy = (1/2)*C_total*V'^2 = 0.5 x 1800x10^-12 x 2500 = 2.25x10^-6 J.

questions.text: The species, having bond angles of 120 degrees is:
questions.explanation: BCl3 has a trigonal planar geometry (sp2 hybridisation) with bond angles of exactly 120 degrees. ClF3 is T-shaped (~87.5 degrees), NCl3 and PH3 are pyramidal with angles less than 109.5 degrees.

questions.text: A sound wave is passing through air column in the form of compression and rarefaction. In consecutive compressions and rarefactions,
options: there is no transfer of heat.
questions.explanation: Compressions and rarefactions in sound propagation occur rapidly, with no time for heat exchange between regions — the process is adiabatic, so there is no transfer of heat (this is why Laplace's adiabatic correction, not Boyle's isothermal law, gives the correct speed of sound).

questions.text: Two wires are made of the same material and have the same volume. The first wire has cross-sectional area A and the second wire has cross-sectional area 3A. If the length of the first wire is increased by Δl on applying a force F, how much force is needed to stretch the second wire by the same amount?
questions.topic: Young's modulus: force for equal extension in wires of different cross-section
questions.explanation: Since volume is constant, if area is 3A, length is L/3 for the second wire. Young's modulus Y = FL/(AΔl) is the same for both. For wire 2: Y = F2(L/3)/(3A×Δl). Equating with wire 1's Y=FL/(AΔl): F2 = 9F.

questions.text: In the structure of ClF3, the number of lone pairs of electrons on central atom 'Cl' is
questions.explanation: ClF3 has a T-shaped structure derived from trigonal bipyramidal electron geometry, with 3 bond pairs and 2 lone pairs on the central Cl atom.

questions.text: Match Column-I and Column-II and choose the correct match. (A) Root mean square speed of gas molecules, (B) Pressure exerted by ideal gas, (C) Average kinetic energy of a molecule, (D) Total internal energy of 1 mole of a diatomic gas, with (P) (1/3)nmv̄², (Q) √(3RT/M), (R) (5/2)RT, (S) (3/2)kBT.
questions.explanation: vrms=√(3RT/M) (Q); Pressure=(1/3)nmv̄² (P); average KE of a molecule=(3/2)kBT (S); total internal energy of 1 mol diatomic gas=(5/2)RT (R). (A)-(Q),(B)-(P),(C)-(S),(D)-(R).

questions.text: Monochlorination of toluene in sunlight, followed by hydrolysis with aq. NaOH, yields
questions.topic: Product of Toluene's Side-Chain Chlorination Followed by Hydrolysis
questions.explanation: Chlorination in sunlight proceeds by a free-radical mechanism at the benzylic (side-chain methyl) position rather than on the aromatic ring, converting toluene to benzyl chloride (C6H5CH2Cl). Subsequent hydrolysis of this benzylic halide with aqueous NaOH then gives benzyl alcohol (C6H5CH2OH), not a ring-substituted cresol.

questions.text: The highest occupied molecular orbital (HOMO) for Ne2 is:
questions.explanation: Ne2 (hypothetical) would have 20 electrons total (10 from each Ne atom), completely filling all 10 molecular orbitals formed from 1s and 2s/2p atomic orbitals: σ1s, σ*1s, σ2s, σ*2s, σ2pz, π2px, π2py, π*2px, π*2py, σ*2pz. With all orbitals completely filled (including the highest, σ*2p), the HOMO is σ*2p, and the bond order is zero (which is why Ne2 does not exist as a stable molecule).

questions.text: The potential energy of a long spring when stretched by 2 cm is U. If the spring is stretched by 8 cm, potential energy stored in it will be:
questions.explanation: U = (1/2)Kx². Since U ∝ x², and the extension increased from 2cm to 8cm (4 times), the new PE = (4)² × U = 16U.

questions.text: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is
options: Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance r upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with 1/r dependence for the outside region.
A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
questions.explanation: Inside the wire, B ∝ r (linear increase); outside, B ∝ 1/r (decreasing).

questions.text: At what temperature will the rms speed of oxygen molecules become just sufficient for escaping from the Earth's atmosphere? (Given: Mass of oxygen molecule (m) = 2.76×10^-26 kg, Boltzmann's constant kB = 1.38×10^-23 J K^-1)
questions.topic: Escape velocity and temperature for gas molecules
questions.explanation: Setting rms speed equal to escape velocity (vesc≈11.2 km/s): (3kBT/m) = vesc². T = m×vesc²/(3kB) = (2.76×10^-26×(11200)²)/(3×1.38×10^-23) ≈ 8.36×10^4 K.

questions.text: The displacement of a particle is represented by the equation y = 3 cos(ωt - π/4). The motion of the particle is
questions.explanation: y = 3cos(ωt - π/4) is of the standard SHM form y = A cos(ωt + φ) with constant amplitude, so it is simple harmonic with period T = 2π/ω.

questions.text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is:
questions.explanation: Since plane of loop is perpendicular to field, angle between B and area vector A is zero. φ = B·A·cos0° = 0.5 × 1 × 1 = 0.5 Wb.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II: The number of unpaired electrons in a Cr2+ ion (Z=24) is the same as that of a Nd3+ ion (Z=60). In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.explanation: Statement I is true: ferromagnetism is indeed considered an extreme form of paramagnetism. Statement II is false: Cr2+ has configuration [Ar]3d4, giving 4 unpaired electrons, while Nd3+ has [Xe]4f3, giving 3 unpaired electrons — these are not the same.

questions.text: A toroid of n turns, mean radius R, and cross-sectional radius a carries current I. It is placed on a horizontal table taken as the x-y plane. Its magnetic moment m
options: is non-zero and points in the z-direction by symmetry.
points along the axis of the toroid (m = mφ̂).
is zero, otherwise there would be a magnetic field falling off as 1/r³ at large distances outside the toroid.
points radially outward from the toroid.
questions.explanation: A toroid's magnetic field is entirely confined within its core and is essentially zero outside it. If the toroid had a non-zero net magnetic moment, it would necessarily produce a dipole-like field falling as 1/r³ at large external distances, which it does not. Hence its net magnetic moment must be zero.

questions.text: A uniform conducting wire of length 12a and resistance 'R' is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of (i) an equilateral triangle of side 'a' (ii) A square of side 'a'. The magnetic dipole moments of the coil in each case respectively are:
questions.topic: Magnetic Dipole Moment of Current Loop
questions.explanation: Wire of length 12a as equilateral triangle of side a gives 4 turns (perimeter 3a per turn), area = (√3/4)a², magnetic moment = 4I×(√3/4)a² = √3 Ia². As a square of side a gives 3 turns (perimeter 4a), area = a², magnetic moment = 3I×a² = 3Ia².

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus. Reason R: Helium has high solubility in O2. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — helium is used to dilute oxygen in diving apparatus (NCERT reference). However, Reason R is false — helium is actually used because it has much lower solubility in blood (not high solubility), which is why it prevents the bends (decompression sickness) in scuba divers. So A is true but R is false.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring. Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: The stretching/twisting behavior of a coil spring is indeed governed by the shear modulus of its material, making Assertion (A) true. However, steel has greater tensile strength than copper of the same dimensions, making Reason (R) false.

questions.text: The output (Y) of the given logic implementation (A, B into a NOR gate, A, B into a NAND gate, both outputs into an AND gate) is similar to the output of an/a ____ gate.
questions.explanation: Y1 = (A+B)' (NOR), Y2 = (A.B)' (NAND), Y = Y1·Y2 = (A+B)'·(A'+B') = (A'B').(A'+B') = A'B' = (A+B)', which is the NOR gate output.

questions.text: Two rotating bodies A and B of masses m and 2m with moments of inertia I_A and I_B (I_B > I_A) have equal kinetic energy of rotation. If L_A and L_B be their angular momenta respectively, then:
questions.explanation: Rotational KE = L²/(2I), so for equal KE, L ∝ √I. Since I_B > I_A, it follows that L_B > L_A.

questions.text: The kinetic energies of a planet in an elliptical orbit about the Sun, at positions A, B and C are KA, KB and KC, respectively. AC is the major axis and SB is perpendicular to AC at the position of the Sun S. Then
questions.topic: Kinetic energy variation in an elliptical orbit
questions.explanation: By Kepler's second law and conservation of energy, the planet moves fastest (highest KE) when closest to the Sun (perihelion, point A as drawn closest to S) and slowest at aphelion (point C, farthest), with B at an intermediate distance giving an intermediate KE. So KA > KB > KC.

questions.text:
Match the species in List I with their geometry in List II:
List I: A) PCl5, B) BrF5, C) BF4⁻, D) [Ni(CN)4]2⁻
List II: I) Tetrahedral, II) Square Planar, III) Trigonal bipyramidal, IV) Square pyramidal
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: PCl5 (sp3d hybridization, no lone pairs on P) is trigonal bipyramidal (III). BrF5 (sp3d2, one lone pair on Br) is square pyramidal (IV). BF4⁻ (sp3, no lone pairs on B) is tetrahedral (I). [Ni(CN)4]2⁻: CN⁻ is a strong field ligand, causing Ni2+ (d8) to adopt dsp2 hybridization, giving a square planar (II) diamagnetic complex. So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Two identical charged conducting spheres A and B have their centres separated by a certain distance. Charge on each sphere is q and the force of repulsion between them is F. A third identical uncharged conducting sphere is brought in contact with sphere A first and then with B and finally removed from both. New force of repulsion between spheres A and B (radii negligible compared to separation) is best given as :
questions.explanation: Contact with A (charge q, uncharged C): both get q/2. Then C (q/2) contacts B (charge q): total 3q/2 splits equally, each gets 3q/4. Final charges: A = q/2, B = 3q/4. F' = k(q/2)(3q/4)/r² = (3/8)(kq²/r²) = (3/8)F.

questions.text: Which of the following rules is not correct, in respect of assigning oxidation numbers?
options: The oxidation number of hydrogen is always +1.
The algebraic sum of all oxidation numbers in a compound is zero.
An element in the free or uncombined state bears oxidation number zero.
In all its compounds, the oxidation number of fluorine is −1.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen's oxidation number is usually +1, but in metal hydrides (e.g., NaH, CaH2) it is −1. So the rule that hydrogen's oxidation number is 'always' +1 is not correct.

questions.text: Choose the wrong option.
options: Inertial mass is a measure of difficulty of accelerating a body by an external force whereas the gravitational mass is relevant in determining the gravitational force on it by an external mass.
That the gravitational mass and inertial mass are equal is an experimental result.
That the acceleration due to gravity on earth is the same for all bodies is due to the equality of gravitational mass and inertial mass.
Gravitational mass of a particle like proton can depend on the presence of neighouring heavy objects but the inertial mass cannot.
questions.explanation: Both gravitational mass and inertial mass are intrinsic properties of a body and do not depend on the presence of neighbouring objects — statement (d) is incorrect on this point.

questions.text: A constant voltage of 50 V is maintained between the points A and B of the circuit shown in the figure (a Wheatstone-like network ACBD with resistances AC=1Ω, CB=2Ω, AD=3Ω, DB=4Ω). The current through the branch CD of the circuit is :
questions.explanation: R1 (1Ω & 3Ω parallel on one path analysis) and R2 give Req = 3/4+4/3 = 25/12 Ω. I = V/Req = 50×12/25 = 24A total. Branch currents work out to I1=18A, I2=6A, I3=16A, I4=8A, giving ICD = I1−I3 = 18−16 = 2 A.

questions.text: In which of the following processes, heat is neither absorbed nor released by a system?
questions.explanation: In an adiabatic process, no heat is exchanged (absorbed or released) between the system and surroundings; Q=0.

questions.text: The number of moles of hydrogen molecules required to produce 20 moles of ammonia through Haber's process is:
questions.explanation: N2(g) + 3H2(g) -> 2NH3(g). Moles of H2/3 = Moles of NH3/2, so moles of H2 = (3/2) x 20 = 30 moles.

questions.text: Which of the following contains the greatest number of atoms?
questions.explanation: Moles: He(4g)=1 mol, Na(46g)=46/23=2 mol, Ca(0.40g)=0.40/40=0.01 mol, He(12g)=12/4=3 mol. Since all are monatomic, the number of atoms is proportional to moles — 12 g He (3 mol) gives the greatest number of atoms.

questions.text: A light rod of length l has two masses m1 and m2 attached to its two ends. The moment of inertia of the system about an axis perpendicular to the rod and passing through the centre of mass is:
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia - Two Point Masses
questions.explanation: With r1 = m2·l/(m1+m2) and r2 = m1·l/(m1+m2) (distances from COM), I = m1r1² + m2r2² = (m1m2/(m1+m2))l².

questions.text: Which of the following oxidation states is common for all lanthanides?
questions.topic: Common Oxidation State of All Lanthanides
questions.explanation: All lanthanides characteristically show a +3 oxidation state, arising from the loss of two 6s electrons and one 5d (or 4f) electron; some additionally show +2 or +4 in specific cases, but +3 is the one common to all of them.

questions.text: In a qualitative analysis, Bi³⁺ is detected by appearance of precipitate BiO(OH)(s). Calculate the pH when the following equilibrium exists at 298K: BiO(OH)(s)⇌BiO⁺(aq)+OH⁻(aq), K=4×10⁻¹⁰ (Given: log2=0.3010)
Which one is a wrong statement?
options: Total orbital angular momentum of electron in 's' orbital is equal to zero.
The value of m for dz2 is zero.
The electronic configuration of N atom is 1s2 2s2 2px1 2py1 2pz1 (shown with all unpaired electrons parallel spin, per Hund's rule).
An orbital is designated by three quantum numbers while an electron in an atom is designated by four quantum numbers.
questions.explanation: Statements 1, 2 and 4 are correct standard facts. Per the official key, statement 3 (the depicted electronic configuration/arrow arrangement for nitrogen) is identified as the wrong statement among the options.

questions.text: Which one is the correct order of acidity?
questions.explanation: Acidity of C-H bonds increases with increasing s-character of the carbon orbital: sp (alkyne, 50% s) > sp2 (alkene, 33% s) > sp3 (alkane, 25% s). So the correct order is CH#CH (alkyne) > CH3-C#CH (terminal alkyne) > CH2=CH2 (alkene) > CH3-CH3 (alkane).

questions.text: When an object is shot from the bottom of a long smooth inclined plane kept at an angle 60 degrees with horizontal, it can travel a distance x1 along the plane. But when the inclination is decreased to 30 degrees and the same object is shot with the same velocity, it can travel x2 distance. Then x1:x2 will be:
questions.explanation: Using v^2=u^2-2g*sin(theta)*x, at the highest point v=0, so x=u^2/(2g*sin(theta)), meaning x is proportional to 1/sin(theta). x1/x2 = sin(30)/sin(60) = (1/2)/(sqrt(3)/2) = 1/sqrt(3).

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 10 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Satellites orbiting the earth have finite life and sometimes debris of satellites fall to the earth. This is because,
options: the solar cells and batteries in satellites run out.
the laws of gravitation predict a trajectory spiralling inwards.
of viscous forces causing the speed of satellite and hence height to gradually decrease.
questions.explanation: Residual atmospheric drag (viscous force) at low orbital altitudes gradually reduces a satellite's speed and orbital height over time, eventually causing re-entry.

questions.text: A ray of monochromatic light is passing through an equilateral prism (ABC) as shown in the figure. The refracted ray (QR) is parallel to its base (BC) and the angle of incidence (i) is 50°. Then the angle of deviation (δ) is:
questions.explanation: For a ray refracted parallel to the base in an equilateral prism, deviation δ=2i-A=2(50)-60=40°.

questions.text: Which one is an example of heterogeneous catalysis?
options: Hydrolysis of sugar catalysed by H+ ions.
Decomposition of ozone in presence of nitrogen monoxide.
Combination between dinitrogen and dihydrogen to form ammonia in the presence of finely divided iron.
Oxidation of Sulphur dioxide into Sulphur trioxide in the presence of oxides of nitrogen.
questions.explanation: In heterogeneous catalysis, the catalyst is in a different phase from the reactants. The Haber process (N2(g) + 3H2(g) <-> 2NH3(g)) uses finely divided iron, a solid catalyst, with gaseous reactants, making it heterogeneous catalysis. The other options involve catalysts in the same phase as the reactants (homogeneous catalysis).

questions.text: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from:
questions.topic: Oxidation State Change in Permanganate Reactions
questions.explanation: In neutral or faintly alkaline medium, MnO4- (Mn in +7 state) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn in +4 state), while oxidizing iodide (I-) to iodate (IO3-).

questions.text: Two resistors of resistance, 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 Ω to that in 200 Ω in a given time is:
questions.explanation: H = V²t/R, and since resistors are in parallel, potential is same across them, so H ∝ 1/R. H₁/H₂ = R₂/R₁ = 200/100 = 2/1.

questions.text: In the nitration of benzene using a mixture of conc. H2SO4 and conc. HNO3, the species which initiates the reaction is
questions.explanation: Concentrated H2SO4 protonates HNO3 and facilitates the loss of water, generating the nitronium ion (NO2+), which is the electrophile that attacks the benzene ring to initiate nitration.

questions.text: Match Column-I and Column-II and choose the correct match from the given choices. Column-I: (A) Root mean square speed of gas molecules (B) Pressure exerted by ideal gas (C) Average kinetic energy of a molecule (D) Total internal energy of 1 mole of a diatomic gas. Column-II: (P) (1/3)nmv̄² (Q) √(3RT/M) (R) (5/2)RT (S) (3/2)kBT
questions.topic: RMS Speed, Pressure, Kinetic Energy, Internal Energy
questions.explanation: Vrms = √(3RT/M) → A-Q. P = (1/3)nmVm² → B-P. Average KE = (3/2)kT → C-S. Total internal energy of diatomic gas = (5/2)RT → D-R.

questions.text: A bar magnet is hung by a thin cotton thread in a uniform horizontal magnetic field and is in equilibrium state. The energy required to rotate it by 60° is W. Now the torque required to keep the magnet in this new position is:
questions.explanation: W = PE[cos0° - cos60°] = PE(1-1/2) = PE/2, so PE = 2W. Torque at 60°: T = PE sin60° = 2W×(√3/2) = √3 W.

questions.text: Column-I gives certain physical terms associated with flow of current through a metallic conductor. Column-II gives some mathematical relations involving electrical quantities. Match column-I and column-II with appropriate relations. Column-I: (A) Drift Velocity (B) Electrical Resistivity (C) Relaxation Period (D) Current Density. Column-II: (P) m/(ne²ρ) (Q) nevd (R) (eE/m)τ (S) E/J
questions.explanation: Drift velocity vd = (eE/m)τ → A-R. Resistivity ρ = E/J → B-S. Relaxation time τ = m/(ne²ρ) → C-P. Current density J = nevd → D-Q.

questions.text: For a cell involving one electron, E(cell) standard = 0.59 V at 298K, the equilibrium constant for the cell reaction is: [Given that 2.303RT/F = 0.059 V at T=298K]
The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction (constant temperature T, axes y vs x). The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are:
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t1/2 and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t1/2)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t1/2 and x = concentration)
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, rate is constant and independent of concentration, so plotting rate (y) vs concentration (x) gives a horizontal line. For a first order reaction, half-life (t1/2) is independent of initial concentration, so plotting t1/2 (y) vs concentration (x) also gives a horizontal line.

questions.text: Identify the disproportionation reaction among the following.
questions.explanation: In 2NO2 + 2OH− → NO2− + NO3− + H2O, nitrogen starts at +4 in NO2 and ends up as +3 in NO2− (reduced) and +5 in NO3− (oxidised) — the same element undergoing both oxidation and reduction simultaneously, which defines disproportionation.

questions.text: For a reaction A→B, enthalpy of reaction is -4.2 kJ mol⁻¹ and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol⁻¹. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option.
options: Profile showing B higher than A (endothermic, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with a lower hump (activation energy too small, incorrect)
Profile showing B lower than A with activation energy matching 9.6 kJ above A, consistent with exothermic ΔH=-4.2 (correct, option 3)
Profile with B higher than A and small hump (incorrect)
questions.topic: Potential energy profile for exothermic reaction
questions.explanation: Since ΔH is negative (exothermic), B must be lower in energy than A, with the activation energy barrier (9.6 kJ/mol) above A — matching profile option 3.

questions.text: A particle moves from a point (-2î+5ĵ) to (4ĵ+3k̂) when a force of (4î+3ĵ) N is applied. How much work has been done by the force?
questions.explanation: Displacement Δr = r2-r1 = (4ĵ+3k̂)-(-2î+5ĵ) = 2î-ĵ+3k̂. Work W = F·Δr = (4î+3ĵ)·(2î-ĵ+3k̂) = 8-3+0 = 5 J.

questions.text: A bob of heavy mass m is suspended by a light string of length l. The bob is given a horizontal velocity v0. If the string gets slack at some point P making an angle θ from the horizontal, the ratio of the speed v of the bob at point P to its initial speed v0 is:
questions.explanation: At point P where the string goes slack, tension T=0, so Mg sinθ = Mv²/l, giving v² = lg sinθ. Using conservation of energy from the lowest point A to P (height gained = l(1+sinθ)): ½Mv0² = ½Mv² + Mgl(1+sinθ) = ½Mgl sinθ + Mgl + Mgl sinθ. So v0² = gl(2+3sinθ), and v/v0 = √(sinθ/(2+3sinθ)).

questions.text: Which of the following alkane cannot be made in good yield by Wurtz reaction?
questions.explanation: The Wurtz reaction (2RX + 2Na → R-R) works well for synthesising symmetrical alkanes with an even number of carbons. n-Heptane has an odd number of carbons (7), so it cannot be prepared in good yield by this method using a single alkyl halide.

questions.text: A lens combination consists of two lenses, L₁ and L₂, of focal lengths +10 cm and −10 cm respectively, separated by 3 cm. An object O is placed 30 cm to the left of L₁ on the common principal axis. The position of the final image formed is:
options: 60 cm to the left of the concave lens
30 cm to the right of the concave lens
60 cm to the right of the concave lens
20 cm to the left of the concave lens
questions.explanation: For L₁ (f=+10cm, u=-30cm): 1/v = 1/f + 1/u = 1/10 - 1/30 = 1/15, so v = 15 cm (image forms 15 cm to the right of L₁, i.e., 15-3=12 cm beyond L₂). This serves as a virtual object for L₂ at u₂=+12 cm. For L₂ (f=-10cm): 1/v₂ = 1/f₂ + 1/u₂ = -1/10 + 1/12 = -1/60, so v₂ = -60 cm. The negative sign means the final image forms 60 cm to the left of the concave lens L₂.

questions.text: In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), two PN junction diodes are connected in series with a battery in different orientations: (a) P-N, P-N both same orientation; (b) P-N, N-P opposite; (c) N-P, N-P both same orientation. In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in
questions.explanation: In circuits (a) and (c), both diodes are oriented identically (same direction), so both are either both forward or both reverse biased, giving equal potential drop across each junction.

questions.text: E° values of some redox couples are given below: Br2/Br− = +1.90 V; Ag+/Ag(s) = +0.80 V; Cu2+/Cu(s) = +0.34 V; I2(s)/I− = +0.54 V. On the basis of these values, choose the correct option.
questions.topic: Feasibility of Redox Reactions from E° Values
questions.explanation: Br− and I− are already in their fully reduced forms and cannot be reduced further, and elemental Ag is already reduced, so those options are not chemically sensible. Cu metal (E° = +0.34 V, lower than Br2/Br− = +1.90 V) can reduce Br2 to Br−, since the overall cell potential (1.90 − 0.34 = 1.56 V) is positive, making the reaction thermodynamically feasible.

questions.text: Compound P (C8H8O) gives a red orange precipitate with 2,4-DNP reagent and it does not reduce Fehling's reagent. On drastic oxidation with chromic acid, P gives an aromatic product Q that produces effervescence on treating with aq. NaHCO3. Compounds P and Q, respectively, are:
options: P=methyl phenyl ketone isomer, Q=benzoic acid derivative (option 3 structure)
questions.explanation: P is a methyl aryl ketone (gives 2,4-DNP test positive, Fehling's negative); oxidation gives an aromatic carboxylic acid Q that effervesces with NaHCO3. Correct structures per key correspond to option 2.

questions.text: The resistance of a wire is 'R' ohm. If it is melted and stretched to 'n' times its original length, its new resistance will be:
questions.explanation: Volume remains constant: A₁L₁ = A₂L₂, with L₂ = nL₁, so A₂ = A₁/n. New resistance R' = ρL₂/A₂ = ρ(nL₁)/(A₁/n) = n²(ρL₁/A₁) = n²R.

questions.text: Hydrogen resembles halogens in many respects for which several factors are responsible. Of the following factors, which one is most important in this respect?
options: Its tendency to lose an electron to form a cation.
Its tendency to gain a single electron in its valence shell to attain a stable electronic configuration.
Its low negative electron gain enthalpy value.
questions.topic: Position of Hydrogen in Periodic Table
questions.explanation: Like halogens, hydrogen needs only one more electron to complete its valence shell and attain a stable (noble gas-like) configuration — this shared tendency to gain a single electron is the main reason hydrogen resembles halogens.

questions.text: An organic compound contains 78% (by wt.) carbon and remaining percentage of hydrogen. The right option for the empirical formula of this compound is: [Atomic wt. of C is 12, H is 1]

Three equal capacitors of capacitance C are connected as shown in the figure (two in series between A and B, with a third C across the midpoint). The equivalent capacitance of the combination shown in the figure is:
questions.explanation: The middle capacitor C is directly in parallel across the series combination's midpoint, which simplifies the network; working through the circuit reduction, CAB = 2C.

questions.text: A nucleus with mass number 240 breaks into two fragments each of mass number 120, the binding energy per nucleon of unfragmented nuclei is 7.6MeV while that of fragments is 8.5MeV. The total gain in the Binding Energy in the process is:
questions.topic: Binding Energy Gain in Nuclear Fission
questions.explanation: Gain in binding energy Q = Binding energy of products − Binding energy of reactants = (120×8.5×2) − (240×7.6) = 2040 − 1824 = 216 MeV.

questions.text: An example of a sigma bonded organometallic compound is:
questions.explanation: Grignard's reagent (RMgX) is a classic example of a sigma-bonded organometallic compound, where the metal-carbon bond is a simple sigma bond. Ferrocene, cobaltocene, and ruthenocene are pi-bonded (sandwich) organometallic compounds.

questions.text: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in rad/s² is
Tritium, a radioactive isotope of hydrogen, emits which of the following particles?
questions.explanation: Tritium (³H) is a beta emitter, decaying to Helium-3 by emitting a beta particle.

questions.text: The Kjeldahl's method for the estimation of nitrogen can be used to estimate the amount of nitrogen in which one of the following compounds? (1) Pyridine (nitrogen in aromatic ring) (2) Aniline (benzene with NH2 group) (3) Azobenzene (benzene-N=N-benzene) (4) Nitrobenzene (benzene with NO2 group)
questions.explanation: Kjeldahl's method is not applicable to nitrogen present in nitro and azo groups, or nitrogen present in a ring (like pyridine). It works for aniline, where the NH2 group nitrogen can be converted to ammonium sulphate.

questions.text: Young's modulus of steel is 1.9 × 10¹¹ N/m². When expressed in CGS units of dynes/cm², it will be equal to (1N = 10⁵ dyne, 1m² = 10⁴ cm²)
questions.explanation: 1 N/m² = 10⁵ dyne / 10⁴ cm² = 10 dyne/cm². So 1.9×10¹¹ N/m² = 1.9×10¹¹×10 = 1.9×10¹² dyne/cm².

questions.text: The correct statement regarding electrophile is:
options: Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from another electrophile
Electrophiles are generally neutral species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile can be either neutral or positively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
Electrophile is a negatively charged species and can form a bond by accepting a pair of electrons from a nucleophile
questions.explanation: An electrophile (electron-loving species) can be neutral or positively charged, and it forms a new bond by accepting a pair of electrons donated by a nucleophile.

questions.text: What is the coordination number in a square close-packed structure in two dimensions?
questions.topic: Coordination Number in 2D Square Close Packing
questions.explanation: In a two-dimensional square close-packed arrangement, each sphere is in contact with four neighbouring spheres, giving a coordination number of 4 (as opposed to 6 in two-dimensional hexagonal close packing).

questions.text: A ball is thrown vertically downward with a velocity of 20 m/s from the top of a tower. It hits the ground after some time with a velocity of 80 m/s. The height of the tower is: (g=10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Kinematics: vertically downward projectile from a tower

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs -- List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Uses of Alkali Metals and Compounds
questions.explanation: Li is used in electrochemical cells (ii) (lithium batteries). Na is used as a coolant in fast breeder reactors (iii). KOH is used as an absorbent for carbon dioxide (i). Cs is used in photoelectric cells (iv). So a-ii, b-iii, c-i, d-iv.

questions.text: A capacitor of capacitance 'C', is connected across an ac source of voltage V, given by V=V0 sinωt. The displacement current between the plates of the capacitor, would then be given by:
questions.explanation: I=C(dV/dt)=C×V0ω cosωt=V0ωC cosωt, and displacement current equals conduction current here.

questions.text: The current I in the circuit shown below is: (All diodes are ideal and identical; resistors 4Ω, 3Ω, 5Ω; battery 10V)
questions.explanation: With ideal diodes conducting appropriately, the equivalent circuit reduces to give I=15/2 A as per the official key.

questions.text: The area of a rectangular field (in m²) of length 55.3m and breadth 25m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is:
questions.explanation: A = L×B = 55.3×25 = 1382.5. Since the breadth 25 has only 2 significant figures, the answer must also be rounded to 2 significant figures: 1382.5 ≈ 14×10².

questions.text: Consider the reaction: CH3CH2CH2Br + NaCN → CH3CH2CH2CN + NaBr. This reaction will be the fastest in:
questions.explanation: This is an SN2 reaction, which proceeds fastest in a polar aprotic solvent like DMF, since it does not solvate the nucleophile (CN-) as strongly as protic solvents do.

questions.text: Carboxylic acids have higher boiling points than aldehydes, ketones and even alcohols of comparable molecular mass. It is due to their
options: more extensive association of carboxylic acid via van der Waals force of attraction
questions.explanation: Carboxylic acid molecules form strong intermolecular hydrogen bonds, typically existing as dimers, which requires more energy to break and results in higher boiling points.

questions.text: The electron concentration in an n-type semiconductor is the same as hole concentration in a p-type semiconductor. An external field (electric) is applied across each of them. Compare the currents in them.
options: current in n-type = current in p-type
current in p-type > current in n-type
current in n-type > current in p-type
No current will flow in p-type, current will only flow in n-type
questions.topic: Current comparison in n-type and p-type semiconductors
questions.explanation: Since electron mobility is generally higher than hole mobility, with equal carrier concentration, current in n-type exceeds that in p-type.

questions.text: If an electron in a hydrogen atom jumps from the 3rd orbit to the 2nd orbit, it emits a photon of wavelength λ. When it jumps from the 4th orbit to the 3rd orbit, the corresponding wavelength of the photon will be:
If a soap bubble expands, the pressure inside the bubble:
options: Is equal to the atmospheric pressure
questions.explanation: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble is given by P = 4T/r, where T is surface tension and r is the radius. As the bubble expands, r increases, so the excess pressure (and hence the pressure inside) decreases.

questions.text: The peak value of an alternating current is 5 A and frequency is 60 Hz. How long will the current, starting from zero, take to reach the peak value?
questions.explanation: Time to reach peak from zero = T/4 = 1/(4×60) = 1/240 s.

questions.text: Among the species given below, the spin-only magnetic moment is highest for: (Given: Atomic number of Ti = 22, Mn = 25, Fe = 26 and Co = 27)
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3−: Fe3+ is d5; CN⁻ is strong field, low spin, giving t2g5eg0 with 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Co(NH3)6]3+: Co3+ is d6, low spin (common for Co3+), t2g6eg0, 0 unpaired electrons, μ=0. [Ti(H2O)6]3+: Ti3+ is d1, 1 unpaired electron, μ=√3≈1.73 BM. [Mn(CN)6]3−: Mn3+ is d4; even with strong-field CN⁻, low-spin d4 gives t2g4eg0 with 2 unpaired electrons, μ=√(2×4)=√8≈2.83 BM, which is the highest among these four.

questions.text: Higher yield of NO in N2(g)+O2(g)⇌2NO(g) can be obtained at [ΔH of the reaction = +180.7 kJ mol⁻¹]: A. higher temperature, B. lower temperature, C. higher concentration of N2, D. higher concentration of O2. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Le Chatelier's Principle - Endothermic Reaction Yield
questions.explanation: Since the reaction is endothermic (ΔH positive), by Le Chatelier's principle, higher temperature favors the forward reaction (more NO). Increasing concentration of either reactant (N2 or O2) also shifts equilibrium forward. So A, C, D only.

questions.text: Which among the following electronic configurations belong to main group elements? A. Ne 3s¹, B. Ar 3d³4s², C. Kr 4d¹⁰5s²5p⁵, D. Ar 3d¹⁰4s¹, E. Rn 5f⁰6d²7s². Choose the correct answer from the option given below :
questions.explanation: [Ne]3s¹ is s-block (main group). [Ar]3d³4s² is d-block (transition, not main group). [Kr]4d¹⁰5s²5p⁵ is p-block (main group). [Ar]3d¹⁰4s¹ is d-block (transition). [Rn]5f⁰6d²7s² is f/d-block. Main group elements are s and p block, so A and C only.

questions.text: A football player is moving southward and suddenly turns eastward with the same speed to avoid an opponent. The force that acts on the player while turning is:
questions.explanation: Change in velocity ΔV = v(east) - v(south) = vî - (-vĵ) = vî + vĵ, which points in the north-east direction. Since force is in the direction of change in momentum/velocity, the force acts along north-east.

questions.text: The correct difference between first- and second-order reactions is that
options: the rate of a first-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations
the rate of a first-order reaction does depend on reactant concentrations; the rate of a second-order reaction does not depend on reactant concentrations
a first-order reaction can be catalyzed; a second-order reaction cannot be catalyzed
the half-life of a first-order reaction does not depend on [A]0; the half-life of a second-order reaction does depend on [A]0
questions.topic: Comparing first and second order reactions
questions.explanation: For a first-order reaction, t1/2 = 0.693/k, independent of initial concentration. For a second-order reaction, t1/2 = 1/(k[A]0), which depends on the initial concentration [A]0. This is the correct distinguishing feature.

questions.text: A ball of mass 0.15 kg is dropped from a height 10 m, strikes the ground and rebounds to the same height. The magnitude of impulse imparted to the ball is (g=10 m/s²) nearly:
questions.topic: Impulse during a bouncing ball collision
questions.explanation: v=√(2gh)=√(200)≈14.14 m/s. Impulse=change in momentum=m(v-(-v))=2mv=2×0.15×14.14≈4.2 kg m/s.

questions.text: Match List-I (Oxoacids of Sulphur) with List-II (Bonds): A. Peroxodisulphuric acid, B. Sulphuric acid, C. Pyrosulphuric acid, D. Sulphurous acid. List-II: I. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-S. II. Two S-OH, One S=O. III. Two S-OH, Four S=O, One S-O-O-S. IV. Two S-OH, Two S=O. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Peroxodisulphuric acid (H2S2O8) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one peroxo S-O-O-S linkage (A-III). Sulphuric acid (H2SO4) has two S-OH and two S=O bonds (B-IV). Pyrosulphuric acid (H2S2O7) has two S-OH, four S=O, and one S-O-S bridging linkage (C-I). Sulphurous acid (H2SO3) has two S-OH and one S=O, plus a lone pair on S (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 11 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A body of mass 0.5 kg travels in a straight line with velocity v = a x^(3/2) where a = 5 m⁻¹ᐟ² s⁻¹. The work done by the net force during its displacement from x = 0 to x = 2 m is
A Carnot engine has an efficiency of 50% when its source is at a temperature 327°C. The temperature of the sink is:
Dimensions of stress are:
questions.explanation: Stress = Force/Area = [MLT^-2]/[L²] = [ML^-1T^-2].

questions.text: A short electric dipole has a dipole moment of 16×10^-9 C m. The electric potential due to the dipole at a point at a distance of 0.6 m from the centre of the dipole, situated on a line making an angle of 60° with the dipole axis is: (1/(4πε0)=9×10^9 N m²/C²)
questions.topic: Electric potential due to a dipole at an angle

questions.text: In a certain camera, a combination of four similar thin convex lenses are arranged axially in contact. Then the power of the combination and the total magnification in comparison to the power (p) and magnification (m) for each lens will be, respectively -
questions.explanation: For lenses in contact, net power Pnet = P1+P2+P3+P4 = 4P. Total magnification is the product of individual magnifications: mtotal = m×m×m×m = m⁴.

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]²⁺ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]²⁺ and (C) [Ni(en)3]²⁺ is
questions.explanation: Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than H2O; as en content increases, crystal field splitting energy increases: (C) > (A) > (B).

questions.text: During inelastic collision between two bodies, which of the following quantities always remain conserved?
questions.explanation: In any collision (elastic or inelastic), as long as no external force acts, total linear momentum is always conserved. Kinetic energy is NOT conserved in inelastic collisions — that is what defines them as inelastic.

questions.text: The sharp melting point of crystalline solids is due to
options: a regular arrangement of constituent particles observed only over a short distance in the crystal lattice.
a regular arrangement of constituent particles observed over a long distance in the crystal lattice.
the same arrangement of constituent particles in different directions.
different arrangements of constituent particles in different directions.
questions.topic: Why Crystalline Solids Have a Sharp Melting Point
questions.explanation: Crystalline solids possess long-range order, a regular and repeating arrangement of particles extending throughout the entire lattice, which causes all the bonds to break at essentially the same, well-defined temperature, giving a sharp melting point.

questions.text: Among the following options, the correct trend in the electron gain enthalpy (magnitude, most exothermic first) is:
questions.topic: Electron Gain Enthalpy Trend in Halogens
questions.explanation: Although fluorine has the highest electronegativity, its very small atomic size causes significant electron-electron repulsion in the compact 2p subshell when an extra electron is added, reducing the magnitude of its electron gain enthalpy. Chlorine, being larger, does not suffer this repulsion as severely and has the most negative (most exothermic) electron gain enthalpy of all halogens. The correct order is Cl > F > Br > I.

questions.text: An inductor 20 mH, a capacitor 100 μF and a resistor 50 Ω are connected in series across a source of emf, V = 10 sin 314t. The power loss in the circuit is
