questions.explanation: Adsorption is spontaneous (ΔG < 0) and accompanied by a decrease in entropy (ΔS < 0, since gas molecules become more ordered when adsorbed). Since ΔG = ΔH – TΔS, for ΔG to be negative with ΔS negative, ΔH must be even more negative than TΔS, i.e. ΔH < TΔS.

questions.text: A soap bubble, having radius of 1 mm, is blown from a detergent solution having a surface tension of 2.5 x 10^-2 N/m. The pressure inside the soap bubble equals at a point Z0 below the surface of water in a container. Taking g = 10 m/s^2, density of water = 1000 kg/m^3, then the value of Z0 is:
questions.topic: Surface Tension - Excess Pressure in Bubble
questions.explanation: Excess pressure inside soap bubble = 4T/r = (4 x 2.5x10^-2)/(1x10^-3) = 100 N/m^2. This equals pressure due to water column: rho*g*Z0 = 100, so Z0 = 100/(1000x10) = 0.01 m = 1 cm.

questions.text: A body initially at rest and sliding along a frictionless track from a height h just completes a vertical circle of diameter AB = D. The height h is equal to
questions.topic: Vertical circular motion: minimum height condition
questions.explanation: To just complete a vertical circle of diameter D, the minimum speed at the top requires total height h = (5/4)D above the bottom of the circular track for a point-mass sliding on a track (as opposed to 5R/2=5D/4 which equals this value since D=2R, confirming h=5D/4).

questions.text:
²⁹⁰₈₂X →(α) Y →(e⁺) Z →(β⁻) P →(e⁻) Q
In the nuclear emission stated above, the mass number and atomic number of the product Q respectively, are:
questions.topic: Nuclear Decay Series - Mass Number and Atomic Number
questions.explanation: X(290,82) → α decay → Y(286,80) → e⁺ (positron) emission decreases Z by 1 → Z(286,79) → β⁻ decay increases Z by 1 → P(286,80) → e⁻ emission (β⁻-like) increases Z by 1 → Q(286,81). So Q has mass number 286 and atomic number 81.

questions.text: In pyrrole (5-membered ring with N1-H, carbons numbered 2,3,4,5), the electron density is maximum on:
questions.explanation: Resonance structures of pyrrole show negative charge (higher electron density) developing at C2 and C5 positions (adjacent to N), due to delocalization of the nitrogen lone pair into the ring.

questions.text: The method used to remove temporary hardness of water is:
questions.explanation: Clark's method uses calcium hydroxide (slaked lime) to remove temporary hardness of water by precipitating calcium and magnesium bicarbonates as insoluble carbonates. Ion-exchange, synthetic resins, and Calgon's method are typically used for removing permanent hardness.

questions.text: Ionized hydrogen atoms and alpha-particles with same momenta enters perpendicular to a constant magnetic field B. The ratio of their radii of their paths rH : r(alpha) will be:
questions.topic: Motion of Charged Particle in Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: r = mv/qB, so for same momentum (mv), r is proportional to 1/q. Hydrogen ion has charge e, alpha particle has charge 2e. rH = 1/e (in relative units), r_alpha = 1/2e. rH/r_alpha = 2e/e = 2:1.

questions.text: Which of the following statement is not correct about the characteristics of cathode rays?
options: They start from the cathode and move towards the anode.
They travel in a straight line in the absence of an external electrical or magnetic field.
Characteristics of cathode rays do not depend upon the material of electrodes.
Characteristics of cathode rays depend upon the nature of gas present in the cathode ray tube.
questions.explanation: Cathode rays consist of electrons, and their fundamental characteristics (charge-to-mass ratio, etc.) are independent of both the electrode material and the nature of the gas in the discharge tube. Statement (iv), that they depend on the nature of the gas, is incorrect.

questions.text: The bond dissociation energies of X2, Y2 and XY are in the ratio of 1:0.5:1. ΔH for the formation of XY is -200 kJ/mol. The bond dissociation energy of X2 will be
questions.topic: Bond dissociation energy and enthalpy of formation
questions.explanation: Let bond energies be: X2=a, Y2=0.5a, XY=a. ΔH(formation of XY) = (1/2)BE(X2)+(1/2)BE(Y2)-BE(XY) = (1/2)a+(1/4)a-a = -(1/4)a = -200, giving a = 800 kJ/mol, so BE(X2) = 800 kJ/mol.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Young's Modulus, B. Compressibility, C. Bulk Modulus, D. Poisson's Ratio. List II — I. (Δd/d)/(ΔL/L), II. FL/A(ΔL), III. -(1/ΔP)(ΔV/V), IV. -P(ΔV/V).
questions.explanation: Young's modulus=FL/A(ΔL) (II); compressibility=-(1/ΔP)(ΔV/V) (III); Bulk modulus=-P(ΔV/V) (IV); Poisson's ratio=(Δd/d)/(ΔL/L) (I). So A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I.

questions.text: Water falls from a height of 60 m at the rate of 15 kg/s to operate a turbine. The losses due to frictional force are 10% of the input energy. How much power is generated by the turbine? (g=10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: Input power = mgh/t rate = 15×10×60=9000 W. After 10% loss, output=0.9×9000=8100 W=8.1 kW.

questions.text: Which of the following measurements is most precise?
questions.explanation: Precision depends on the smallest unit of measurement used. 5.00 mm represents the finest/smallest absolute resolution among the options, making it the most precise measurement.

questions.text: Select the correct statements from the following: (A) Atoms of all elements are composed of two fundamental particles. (B) The mass of the electron is 9.10939 x 10^-31 kg. (C) All the isotopes of a given element show same chemical properties. (D) Protons and electrons are collectively known as nucleons. (E) Dalton's atomic theory regarded the atom as an ultimate particle of matter. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Statement A is incorrect — atoms are composed of three fundamental particles (electron, proton, neutron), not two. Statement B is correct — the mass of the electron is 9.10939 x 10^-31 kg. Statement C is correct — isotopes have the same number of electrons/protons, so they show the same chemical properties. Statement D is incorrect — protons and neutrons (not electrons) are collectively known as nucleons. Statement E is correct — Dalton's atomic theory regarded the atom as an indivisible, ultimate particle of matter. So B, C, and E are correct.

questions.text: Which of the following elements does not form a hydride by direct heating with dihydrogen?
questions.explanation: Beryllium does not form BeH2 by direct combination with H2 under ordinary heating (BeH2 must be prepared by other methods, e.g., from BeCl2 and LiAlH4), unlike Mg, Sr, and Ba, which form hydrides on direct heating with hydrogen.

questions.text: The energy required to break one bond in DNA is 10^-20 J. This value in eV is nearly:
In Geiger-Marsden experiment, the number of scattered alpha-particles N(theta) is plotted as a function of scattering angle theta. Which of the following options represents the correct plot?
options: N(theta) stays roughly flat and high from 0 to 90 degrees, then declines sharply towards 180 degrees
N(theta) starts very high near 0 degrees and decreases steeply and monotonically as theta increases towards 180 degrees
N(theta) is low near 0 degrees, rises to a plateau/peak around 90 degrees, then falls back down near 180 degrees
N(theta) increases roughly linearly from a low value at 0 degrees to a higher value at 180 degrees
questions.explanation: In the Geiger-Marsden (Rutherford gold foil) scattering experiment, the number of scattered alpha particles N(theta) is maximum at small angles (most particles pass through with little deflection) and decreases monotonically and steeply as the scattering angle increases, since large-angle scattering (close encounters with the nucleus) is increasingly rare. This gives a steeply decreasing curve starting high near theta=0.

questions.text: Given van der Waals constant for NH3, H2, O2 and CO2 are respectively 4.17, 0.244, 1.36 and 3.59, which one of the following gases is most easily liquefied?
questions.topic: Van der Waals constant 'a' and liquefaction of gases
questions.explanation: A higher value of the van der Waals constant 'a' indicates stronger intermolecular attractive forces, making the gas easier to liquefy. NH3 has the highest 'a' value (4.17) among the given gases, so it is most easily liquefied.

questions.text: The electrostatic force between the metal plates of an isolated parallel plate capacitor C having a charge Q and area A, is
options: independent of the distance between the plates.
inversely proportional to the distance between the plates.
proportional to the square root of the distance between the plates.
linearly proportional to the distance between the plates.
questions.topic: Electrostatic force between plates of an isolated capacitor
questions.explanation: The force between the plates of a parallel plate capacitor (with fixed charge Q) is F = Q²/(2ε0A), which does not depend on the separation distance between the plates, since the charge and area are fixed.

questions.text: In an oscillating spring mass system, a spring is connected to a box filled with sand. As the box oscillates, sand leaks slowly out of the box vertically so that the average frequency ω(t) and average amplitude A(t) of the system change with time t. Which one of the following options schematically depicts these changes correctly?
options: ω(t) rising then flat; A(t) flat
ω(t) rising then flat; A(t) decreasing
questions.explanation: ω = √(k/m). As mass decreases (sand leaking out), ω increases. Energy E = ½kA² also decreases as mass/energy is lost with the leaking sand, so amplitude A decreases. Option (2) shows ω increasing and A decreasing.

questions.text: Dihedral angle of least stable conformer of ethane is:
questions.explanation: Least stable conformer of ethane is the eclipsed form, which occurs when dihedral angle is 0°

questions.text: Which of the following is an example of a vic-dihalide?
questions.explanation: A vicinal (vic-) dihalide has the two halogen atoms on adjacent carbon atoms. 1,2-dichloroethane (ClCH2–CH2Cl) fits this description, unlike dichloromethane and ethylidene chloride (both gem-dihalides, with both halogens on the same carbon) or allyl chloride (only one halogen).

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding enzymes is:
options: Like chemical catalysts enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not polysaccharides, making statement 3 incorrect. Enzymes do act as biocatalysts, reduce activation energy, and show high specificity for particular reactions and substrates.

questions.text: Three identical p-n junction diodes D1, D2 and D3 are connected across a 5V battery with their respective 1kOhm resistors in a circuit as shown (D1 and its resistor in one branch, D2 and its resistor in a second parallel branch, D3 and its resistor in a third parallel branch, with D3 oriented in reverse relative to D1 and D2). If the width of the depletion regions of D1, D2 and D3 are W1, W2 and W3, respectively, then the correct option is:
questions.topic: p-n Junction Diode - Depletion Region Width
questions.explanation: D1 and D2 are forward biased in the circuit (current flows through them, reducing their depletion region width), while D3 is reverse biased (increasing its depletion region width). Due to the differing branch configurations and resistances, the forward bias across D2 is less than that of D1, leading to depletion width ordering W3 > W2 > W1, with D3 (reverse biased) having the widest depletion region.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 15 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The element which exists in liquid state for a wide range of temperature and can be used for measuring high temperature is
questions.explanation: Gallium has an unusually low melting point (~30°C) but a very high boiling point, giving it a very wide liquid range, which makes it useful in high-temperature thermometers.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property. (2) P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals. (3) Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen. (4) Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself.
options: Phosphorus, arsenic and antimony show catenation property
P(C2H5)3 and As(C6H5)3 form dπ-dπ bond with transition metals
Nitrogen can form dπ-pπ bond with oxygen
Nitrogen can form pπ-pπ multiple bonds with itself
questions.explanation: Nitrogen, lacking d-orbitals, cannot form dπ-pπ bonds; it forms pπ-pπ bonds. Hence statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.text: Find the value of the angle of emergence from the prism. Refractive index of the glass is √3 (prism angle 60°, ray incident normally on one face).
questions.topic: Angle of emergence from a prism
questions.explanation: With normal incidence on one face (angle of incidence 0°), refraction at the second face: using Snell's law with A=60°, μ=√3, the emergent angle works out to 60°.

questions.text:
For the following reaction sequence, choose the correct option:
Benzene --[i. CH3COCl, AlCl3; ii. NaOCl]--> P + Q
options: P and Q are aromatic compounds.
If P gives a carboxylic acid on acidification, Q gives a poisonous gas on exposure to air and light.
Both P and Q are carbonyl compounds.
If P is the sodium salt of a carboxylic acid, Q is a primary alcohol.
questions.topic: Friedel-Crafts Acylation Followed by Haloform Reaction
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts acylation of benzene with CH3COCl/AlCl3 gives acetophenone (PhCOCH3). Treatment with NaOCl causes a haloform-type reaction on the methyl ketone, cleaving it into sodium benzoate (P, PhCOO⁻Na⁺) and chloroform (Q, CHCl3). P on acidification gives benzoic acid (a carboxylic acid). Chloroform (Q) is well known to slowly oxidize on exposure to air and light to form phosgene (COCl2), a highly poisonous gas -- which is why chloroform is stored in dark bottles with ethanol as a stabilizer. This matches option (2).

questions.text: Which of the following is not an example of redox reaction?
questions.explanation: BaCl2 + H2SO4 → BaSO4 + 2HCl is a double-displacement (precipitation) reaction — no element changes oxidation state, so it is not a redox reaction, unlike the other three options which all involve electron transfer.

questions.text: A radioactive nucleus (A,Z)X undergoes spontaneous decay in the sequence X→(Z-1)B→(Z-3)C→(Z-2)D, where Z is the atomic number of element X. The possible decay particles in the sequence are:
questions.explanation: Step 1 (Z→Z-1): β⁺ decay (Z decreases by 1, A roughly same). Step 2 (Z-1→Z-3): α decay (Z decreases by 2). Step 3 (Z-3→Z-2): β⁻ decay (Z increases by 1). So sequence is β⁺, α, β⁻.

questions.text: For a certain reaction R → Product, the plot of concentration [R] vs time has a negative slope as shown, with k=-slope. The order of the reaction is:
questions.topic: Reaction order from rate vs concentration plot
questions.explanation: A straight-line plot of [R] vs t with a constant slope (k=-slope) indicates a zero order reaction.

questions.text: A capillary tube of radius r is immersed in water and water rises in it to a height h. The mass of the water in the capillary is 5 g. Another capillary tube of radius 2r is immersed in water. The mass of water that will rise in this tube is:
questions.topic: Capillary rise and mass of water
questions.explanation: Mass of water risen = ρ×πr²×h. Since h ∝ 1/r (capillary rise), mass ∝ r²×(1/r) = r. Doubling the radius doubles the mass: 5×2 = 10 g.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor of capacitance 20 microfarad is being charged by a voltage source whose potential is changing at the rate of 3 V/s. The conduction current through the connecting wires, and the displacement current through the plates of the capacitor, would be, respectively:
questions.explanation: q = CV, so dq/dt = C(dV/dt) = 20 microF x 3 V/s = 60 microA. This is the conduction current ic. By Maxwell's theory, the displacement current id always equals the conduction current in such a circuit, so id = ic = 60 microA.

questions.text: A nucleus of mass number 189 splits into two nuclei having mass number 125 and 64. The ratio of radius of two daughter nuclei respectively is
The maximum elongation of a steel wire of 1 m length if the elastic limit of steel and its Young's modulus, respectively, are 8×10⁸ N m⁻² and 2×10¹¹ N m⁻², is:
questions.explanation: ΔL = FL/AY, so (ΔL·Y)/L = F/A = 8×10⁸ (elastic limit stress). ΔL × 2×10¹¹ / 1 = 8×10⁸, so ΔL = 8×10⁸ / 2×10¹¹ = 4×10⁻³ m = 4 mm.

questions.text: The quantity of charge required to obtain one mole of aluminium from Al2O3 is
questions.topic: Charge Required to Obtain One Mole of Aluminium
questions.explanation: Aluminium is reduced as Al3+ + 3e⁻ → Al, so producing one mole of Al requires 3 moles of electrons, i.e. 3 Faradays of charge.

questions.text: A disc of radius 2m and mass 100 kg rolls on a horizontal floor. Its centre of mass has speed of 20 cm/s. How much work is needed to stop it?
questions.explanation: Total KE of rolling disc = (1/2)mv^2(1 + K^2/R^2). For a disc, K^2/R^2 = 1/2. KE = (1/2)(100)(0.2)^2(1+0.5) = (3/4)(100)(0.04) = 3 J. Work needed to stop = KE = 3 J.

questions.text: One main scale division of a Vernier calliper is equal to 1 mm and the number of divisions on the Vernier scale is 10. When both the jaws touch each other, the Vernier scale shifts to the left of zero of the main scale in such a way that the 4th Vernier division coincides with a division of the main scale. If this Vernier calliper measures the length of a wire to be 1 cm, the actual length of the wire is:
questions.explanation: Least count = 1 MSD - 1 VSD = 1mm - 0.9mm = 0.1mm = 0.01cm. Since the vernier zero is shifted to the left of the main scale zero with the 4th division coinciding, this is a negative zero error of magnitude 4 x 0.01cm = 0.04cm. Actual length = Observed reading - (Zero error) = 1cm - (-0.04cm) = 1.04cm. Note: this question was officially marked as Bonus (full credit given to all candidates) likely due to ambiguity in the zero-error sign convention used.

questions.text: The binding energy of a H-atom, considering an electron moving around a fixed nucleus (Bohr model), is given by (taking the electron's charge and mass as e and m respectively, with other symbols having their usual meaning): E_n = -(me⁴)/(8n²ε₀²h²). If one decides to work in a frame of reference where the electron is at rest, the corresponding expression obtained by transferring mass from the electron to the proton (to retain the same expression) would not be correct, because
options: n would no longer be integral.
Bohr-quantisation applies only to the electron.
the frame in which the electron is taken to be at rest is not an inertial frame.
the motion of the proton would not be in circular orbits, even approximately.
questions.topic: Reference Frame in the Bohr Model
questions.explanation: The Bohr model's quantisation rules are derived assuming motion relative to an inertial frame. A frame in which the orbiting electron is instantaneously at rest is a non-inertial (accelerating) frame, so the same quantisation condition and resulting energy expression cannot simply be transferred to it by swapping the electron and proton mass.

questions.text: A satellite of mass m is orbiting the earth (of radius R) at a height h from its surface. The total energy of the satellite in terms of g0, the value of acceleration due to gravity at the earth's surface, is:
questions.explanation: Total energy TE = KE + PE = (1/2)mv0² - GMm/(R+h). Since v0² = GM/(R+h), TE = (1/2)m[GM/(R+h)] - GMm/(R+h) = -GMm/(2(R+h)) = -mg0R²/(2(R+h)), using GM = g0R².

questions.text: The major product Z formed in the following sequence of reactions is: C6H6 --Cl2/UV light--> (monochlorinated product) --NH3--> Y --HCl/H2O--> Z
questions.topic: Identifying major product Z in reaction sequence
questions.explanation: Monochlorination under UV gives a side-chain alkyl chloride (C2H5Cl type on benzylic position), ammonolysis gives the amine (Y), and the final step per key gives C2H5OH as Z.

questions.text: An inductor of inductance L, a capacitor of capacitance C and a resistor of resistance 'R' are connected in series to an ac source of potential difference 'V' volts. Potential difference across L, C and R are 40 V, 10 V and 40 V, respectively. The amplitude of current flowing in the LCR series circuit is 10√2 A. The impedance of the circuit is:
questions.explanation: Net voltage=√((VL-VC)²+VR²)=√((40-10)²+40²)=√(900+1600)=50V. Impedance=Vrms/Irms... using amplitude values: Z=V(amplitude)/I(amplitude)=50/(10√2)=5/√2 Ω.

questions.text: Which of the following B-group vitamins can be stored in our body?
questions.topic: B-Group Vitamin That Can Be Stored in the Body
questions.explanation: Unlike most water-soluble B vitamins, which are excreted and must be replenished regularly, Vitamin B12 can be stored in significant amounts in the liver for later use.

questions.text: At 298 K, a certain buffer solution contains equal concentrations of X- and HX. Kb for X- is 10⁻¹⁰. What is the pH of this buffer solution?
questions.explanation: Ka of HX = Kw/Kb = 10⁻¹⁴/10⁻¹⁰ = 10⁻⁴, pKa=4. For equal concentrations, pH=pKa=4.

questions.text: The power of a crane, which lifts a mass of 1000 kg to a height of 20 m in 10 s is: (g=9.8 m/s²)
Which of the following statements is true about Ca(OH)2?
options: It is used in the preparation of bleaching powder.
It is a light blue solid.
It does not possess disinfectant property.
It is used in the manufacture of cement.
questions.explanation: Ca(OH)2 (slaked lime) reacts with chlorine to produce bleaching powder (calcium oxychloride, CaOCl2) — it is a white solid with disinfectant properties, and is not itself a raw material for cement manufacture.

questions.text: An infinitely long straight conductor carries a current of 5 A. An electron is moving with a speed of 10⁵ m/s parallel to the conductor. The perpendicular distance between the electron and the conductor is 20 cm at an instant. Calculate the magnitude of the force experienced by the electron at that instant.
questions.topic: Force on moving electron near current-carrying wire

questions.text: Three identical capacitors, P, Q and S, each of capacitance C, are connected to a battery of voltage V. P and Q are connected in series with each other, and this series combination is connected in parallel with S, with the whole combination connected across the battery V. If the energy stored in capacitor P and the total energy stored in the system are U_P and U_T, respectively, then the ratio U_P/U_T is:
questions.topic: Capacitors in Series and Parallel - Energy Stored
questions.explanation: The P-Q series combination and S are both connected directly across the battery, so each sees the full voltage V. Equivalent capacitance of P and Q in series is C/2, so charge on this branch is Q_series = (C/2)V, which is also the charge on each of P and Q individually (series components share charge). Energy in P: U_P = Q_series²/(2C) = (CV/2)²/(2C) = CV²/8. By symmetry U_Q = CV²/8 too. Energy in S: U_S = (1/2)CV² (full voltage V across capacitance C). Total: U_T = CV²/8 + CV²/8 + CV²/2 = 3CV²/4. Ratio U_P/U_T = (CV²/8)/(3CV²/4) = 1/6.

questions.text: Which is the correct statement about birth control pills?
options: They contain a mixture of estrogen and progesterone derivatives.
questions.explanation: Oral contraceptive pills typically contain a combination of synthetic estrogen and progesterone derivatives, which together suppress ovulation; progesterone itself actually inhibits (rather than enhances) ovulation.

questions.text: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He⁺ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li²⁺ ion?

In a uniform magnetic field of 0.049 T, a magnetic needle performs 20 complete oscillations in 5 seconds as shown. The moment of inertia of the needle is 9.8×10⁻⁶ kg m². If the magnitude of magnetic moment of the needle is x×10⁻⁵ A m²; then the value of 'x' is: [Figure: magnetic needle NS in uniform field B]
questions.topic: Oscillating Magnetic Needle - Magnetic Moment Calculation

questions.text: The non-essential amino acid among the following is:
questions.explanation: Alanine is a non-essential amino acid, meaning the human body can synthesize it on its own. Lysine, valine, and leucine are all essential amino acids that must be obtained through diet.

questions.text: A dinucleotide is obtained by joining two nucleotides together by a phosphodiester linkage. Between which carbon atoms of the pentose sugars of the nucleotides are these linkages present?
questions.topic: Carbon Positions Linked by a Phosphodiester Bond
questions.explanation: In a dinucleotide, the phosphate group bridges the 5'-carbon of one nucleotide's sugar to the 3'-carbon of the next nucleotide's sugar, forming the characteristic 5'→3' phosphodiester linkage seen throughout DNA and RNA strands.

questions.text: Anisole on cleavage with HI gives:
questions.topic: Cleavage of aryl alkyl ethers with HI
questions.explanation: In the cleavage of anisole (aryl alkyl ether) with HI, the alkyl-oxygen bond is cleaved (due to the instability of forming an aryl cation), giving phenol and methyl iodide (CH3I).

questions.text: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10g of glucose (C6H12O6) in 250 ml of water (P1), 10 g of urea (CH4N2O) in 250 ml of water (P2) and 10 g of sucrose (C12H22O11) in 250 ml of water (P3). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure of these solution is:
questions.explanation: Π∝C∝1/Mw. Mw(glucose)=180, Mw(urea)=60, Mw(sucrose)=342. Lower Mw gives higher osmotic pressure for same mass, so P2>P1>P3

questions.text: The interaction energy of London force is inversely proportional to the sixth power of the distance between two interacting particles, but their magnitude depends upon
options: strength of permanent dipoles in the particles.
questions.explanation: London (dispersion) forces arise from instantaneous induced dipoles, and their strength depends on how easily the electron cloud of a particle can be distorted — i.e., its polarisability.

questions.text: The quantities which have the same dimensions as those of solid angle are:
questions.explanation: Solid angle is dimensionless. Strain = change in configuration/original configuration = dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰]. Angle = arc/radius = L/L = dimensionless [M⁰L⁰T⁰]. So strain and angle both have the same (dimensionless) dimensions as solid angle.

questions.text: The displacement of a particle is given by x = (t – 2)² where x is in metres and t in seconds. The distance covered by the particle in first 4 seconds is
questions.explanation: x(0)=4, x(2)=0 (turning point where v=0), x(4)=4. From t=0 to 2, particle moves from x=4 to x=0 (distance 4m); from t=2 to 4, it moves from x=0 to x=4 (distance 4m). Total distance = 4+4 = 8 m.

questions.text: The entropy change can be calculated by using the expression ΔS = qrev/T. When water freezes in a glass beaker, choose the correct statement amongst the following.
options: ΔS(system) decreases but ΔS(surroundings) remains the same.
ΔS(system) decreases and ΔS(surroundings) also decreases.
questions.explanation: Freezing converts a more disordered liquid into a more ordered solid, so the system's entropy decreases. The heat released during freezing flows into the surroundings, increasing the surroundings' entropy.

questions.text: A U tube with both ends open to the atmosphere, is partially filled with water. Oil, which is immiscible with water, is poured into one side until it stands at a distance of 10 mm above the water level on the other side. Meanwhile the water rises by 65 mm from its original level. The density of the oil is:
questions.explanation: Water rises by 65mm on one side, so it falls by 65mm on the oil side, giving total oil column height = 65+65+10 = 140 mm. Pressure balance at the bottom: ρ_oil×g×140mm = ρ_water×g×130mm (difference in water levels = 2×65=130mm). ρ_oil = 1000×130/140 ≈ 928 kg/m³.

questions.text:
Match List I with List II.
List I (Spectral Lines of Hydrogen for transitions from): (A) n2=3 to n1=2 (B) n2=4 to n1=2 (C) n2=5 to n1=2 (D) n2=6 to n1=2
List II (Wavelengths (nm)): (I) 410.2 (II) 434.1 (III) 656.3 (IV) 486.1
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Hydrogen Spectral Lines - Balmer Series Wavelengths (Match List)
questions.explanation: Using 1/λ = RH(1/n1² - 1/n2²) with RH = 1.09×10⁷ m⁻¹ for the Balmer series (n1=2): n2=3→2 gives λ=656.3nm (III), n2=4→2 gives λ=486.1nm (IV), n2=5→2 gives λ=434.1nm (II), n2=6→2 gives λ=410.2nm (I). So A-III, B-IV, C-II, D-I.

questions.text: N2 and O2 do not react under normal conditions because
options: the reaction between them is highly endothermic and requires a very high temperature.
N2 and O2 are generally unreactive gases.
questions.explanation: The reaction N2 + O2 → 2NO is strongly endothermic, so it proceeds to a significant extent only at very high temperatures (such as in lightning or internal combustion engines), not under normal atmospheric conditions.

questions.text: A beam of light from a source L is incident normally on a plane mirror fixed at a certain distance x from the source. The beam is reflected back as a spot on a scale placed just above the source L. When the mirror is rotated through a small angle θ, the spot of light is found to move through a distance y on the scale. The angle θ is given by:
questions.topic: Reflection from a rotating plane mirror
questions.explanation: When a mirror rotates by θ, the reflected ray rotates by 2θ. For small angles, y = 2x·θ (small angle approximation over distance 2x path), giving θ = y/(2x).

questions.text: Two identical bodies are made of a material for which the heat capacity increases with temperature. One of these is at 100°C, while the other one is at 0°C. If the two bodies are brought into contact, then, assuming no heat loss, the final common temperature is:
questions.explanation: Since heat capacity increases with temperature, the hotter body (100°C) has a higher heat capacity, so it loses less temperature change for the same heat transferred compared to the colder body gaining; the equilibrium temperature shifts closer to the hotter body's value, making it more than 50°C.

questions.text: The incorrect statement regarding chirality is
options: SN1 reaction yields 1:1 mixture of both enantiomers
The product obtained by SN2 reaction of haloalkane having chirality at the reactive site shows inversion of configuration
Enantiomers are superimposable mirror images on each other
A racemic mixture shows zero optical rotation
questions.explanation: Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images, not superimposable, making statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group. Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: the electron-withdrawing nitro group increases acidic strength of nitrophenols compared to phenol. Statement II is incorrect because the position of the nitro group (ortho, meta, para) affects the degree of resonance and inductive stabilization of the phenoxide ion differently, so o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol have different (not same) acidic strengths.

questions.text: A gas at 350 K and 15 bar has molar volume 20 percent smaller than that for an ideal gas under the same conditions. The correct option about the gas and its compressibility factor (Z) is:
options: Z < 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z < 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and attractive forces are dominant
Z > 1 and repulsive forces are dominant
questions.explanation: Z = (PV)real/(PV)ideal. Since the real molar volume is smaller than the ideal volume, Z < 1. When Z < 1, it indicates that attractive forces between gas molecules dominate, causing the gas to occupy less volume than predicted by the ideal gas law.

questions.text: A full wave rectifier circuit consists of two p-n junction diodes, a center-tapped transformer, capacitor and a load resistance. Which of these components remove the ac ripple from the rectified output?
questions.explanation: The capacitor acts as a filter in the rectifier circuit, charging during peaks and discharging during troughs, which smooths out the pulsating DC output and removes the AC ripple.

questions.text: CH3CH2COO⁻Na⁺ --NaOH, ?, Heat--> CH3CH3 + Na2CO3. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
questions.explanation: This is a decarboxylation reaction in presence of sodalime (NaOH+CaO), so the missing reagent is CaO

questions.text: Four statements are given (A is mass number): A. Volume of a nucleus is proportional to A^(1/3). B. Volume of a nucleus is proportional to A. C. Difference in mass of an atom and its nucleus is called the mass defect. D. Difference in mass of a nucleus and its constituents is called the mass defect. Choose the correct answer:
options: A and D are true, but B and C are false
B and D are true, but A and C are false
B and C are true, but A and D are false
A and C are true, but B and D are false
questions.topic: Mass number and mass defect statements
questions.explanation: Nuclear volume ∝ A (B true, A false); mass defect = difference between mass of nucleus and sum of constituent masses (D true, C false). So B and D are true.

questions.text: The pressure of a 1:4 mixture of dihydrogen and dioxygen enclosed in a vessel is one atmosphere. What would be the partial pressure of dioxygen?
questions.explanation: Mole fraction of O2 = 4/5 = 0.8. Partial pressure of O2 = 0.8 × 1 atm = 0.8 atm ≈ 0.8 × 1.013×10⁵ Pa ≈ 8×10⁴ Nm⁻².

questions.text: Three objects, A: (a solid sphere), B: (a thin circular disk) and C: (a circular ring), each have the same mass M and radius R. They all spin with the same angular speed ω about their own symmetry axes. The amounts of work (W) required to bring them to rest, would satisfy the relation
questions.topic: Rotational kinetic energy and work to stop spinning bodies
questions.explanation: Work required to stop = rotational KE = (1/2)Iω². Moments of inertia: Ring C has I=MR² (largest), disk B has I=MR²/2, solid sphere A has I=2MR²/5 (smallest). So WC > WB > WA.

questions.text: When a voltage-measuring device is connected to AC mains, the meter shows a steady input voltage reading of 220V. This means
options: the input voltage cannot be an AC voltage, but must be a DC voltage.
the meter does not read v directly, but reads ⟨v²⟩ and is calibrated to display √⟨v²⟩.
the pointer of the meter is stuck due to a mechanical defect.
questions.topic: What an AC Voltmeter Actually Measures
questions.explanation: An AC voltmeter works on the heating effect of current, which depends on v². It actually measures the mean square value ⟨v²⟩ over a cycle and is calibrated to display its square root, √⟨v²⟩ — the rms voltage — which is why it shows a steady reading like 220V even for an alternating input.

questions.text: CH3CH2COO-Na+ --NaOH, +?/Heat--> CH3CH3+Na2CO3. Consider the above reaction and identify the missing reagent/chemical.
questions.topic: Identifying missing reagent in decarboxylation-type reaction
questions.explanation: Sodium propanoate heated with NaOH and CaO (soda lime) undergoes decarboxylation to give ethane and sodium carbonate.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 16 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Which of the following graph represents the variation of resistivity (ρ) with temperature (T) for copper?
options: Graph showing linear increase of ρ with T
Graph showing ρ decreasing exponentially with T
Graph showing ρ increasing exponentially with T
Graph showing ρ decreasing and flattening with T
questions.topic: Temperature dependence of resistivity of metals
questions.explanation: For metals like copper, resistivity increases almost linearly with increasing temperature over a normal range, matching the graph showing a linear (slightly curved) increase of ρ with T.

questions.text: The temperature inside a refrigerator is t2°C and the room temperature is t1°C. The amount of heat delivered to the room for each joule of electrical energy consumed ideally will be:
questions.explanation: For an ideal refrigerator, Q1/W = T1/(T1-T2) where T1=t1+273 (room, in Kelvin) and T2=t2+273 (inside fridge). So Q1/W = (t1+273)/(t1-t2).

questions.text: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 second. The angular acceleration in rad/s² is:

Given below are two statements: Statement I: A hypothetical diatomic molecule with bond order zero is quite stable. Statement II: As bond order increases, the bond length increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.topic: Bond Order and Molecular Orbital Theory
questions.explanation: Statement I is false: a bond order of zero means the molecule does not exist/is not stable (e.g., He2). Statement II is false: as bond order increases, bond length actually decreases (bonds become stronger and shorter), not increases. Both statements are false.

questions.text: Among CaH2, BeH2, BaH2, the order of ionic character is
questions.explanation: Ionic character of the metal hydride increases with increasing metallic/electropositive character of the metal down the group: Be < Ca < Ba, so BeH2 < CaH2 < BaH2.

questions.text: The correct decreasing order of oxidation state of the underlined atom in each molecule is:
options: N2O5 > Al2O3 > H2S (N, Al, S underlined respectively)
PbO2 > N2O3 > SO3 (Pb, N, S underlined respectively)
P4O6 > Cl2O7 > AlH3 (P, Cl, Al underlined respectively)
P4O10 > SO3 > H2O (P, S, O underlined respectively)
questions.topic: Oxidation States of Elements in Compounds
questions.explanation: In N2O5, N is +5. In Al2O3, Al is +3. In H2S, S is -2. The order +5 > +3 > -2 is correctly decreasing, so N2O5 > Al2O3 > H2S represents the correct decreasing order of oxidation states of the underlined atoms.

questions.text: In interference and diffraction, the light energy is redistributed. A. As there is no gain or loss of energy, these phenomena are consistent with the principle of conservation of energy. B. Diffraction and interference are characteristics exhibited only by light waves.
options: A is false, but B is true
A is true, but B is false
A is true and B is also true
Both A and B are false
questions.explanation: A is true (energy conserved, redistributed). B is false — diffraction/interference occur in all waves, not just light.

questions.text: An electron is moving in a circular path under the influence of a transverse magnetic field of 3.57×10⁻² T. If the value of e/m is 1.76×10¹¹ C/kg, the frequency of revolution of the electron is:
questions.topic: Electron in Circular Magnetic Field - Frequency

questions.text: There are 14 elements in the actinoid series. Which of the following elements does not belong to this series?
questions.topic: Element Not Belonging to the Actinoid Series
questions.explanation: U (uranium, Z=92), Np (neptunium, Z=93), and Fm (fermium, Z=100) are all actinoids. Tm (thulium, Z=69) is instead a lanthanide, so it does not belong to the actinoid series.

questions.text: A body cools from a temperature 3T to 2T in 10 minutes. The room temperature is T. Assume that Newton's law of cooling is applicable. The temperature of the body at the end of next 10 minutes will be:
questions.explanation: Using Newton's law of cooling with average temperature approximation over each interval, solving dT/dt = K(T_avg - T) for both 10-minute intervals gives the body's temperature after the second interval as (3/2)T.

questions.text:
A logic circuit provides the output Y as per the following truth table:
A B Y
0 0 1
0 1 0
1 0 1
1 1 0
The expression for the output Y is:
questions.topic: Logic Gate Truth Table - Boolean Expression
questions.explanation: From the truth table, Y=1 only when B=0 (regardless of A's value: A=0,B=0→Y=1; A=1,B=0→Y=1), and Y=0 when B=1. So Y = B̄ (NOT B), independent of A.

questions.text: Polar molecules are the molecules:
options: acquire a dipole moment only in the presence of electric field due to displacement of charges
acquire a dipole moment only when magnetic field is absent
having a permanent electric dipole moment
questions.explanation: Polar molecules possess a permanent electric dipole moment even in the absence of an external field.

questions.text: The half-life of a radioactive substance is 30 minutes. The time (in minutes) taken between 40% decay and 85% decay of the same radioactive substance is:
questions.explanation: At 40% decay, 60% remains: 0.6 = 2^(-t1/30). At 85% decay, 15% remains: 0.15 = 2^(-t2/30). Using logs, t1/t2 = log(0.6)/log(0.15) ratio works out so that t2 - t1 = 60 minutes (t1≈19.2 min from start to 40% decay, t2≈79.2 min from start to 85% decay, difference = 60 min).

questions.text: On electrolysis of dil. sulphuric acid using Platinum (Pt) electrode, the product obtained at anode will be:
questions.explanation: During electrolysis of dilute sulphuric acid, water is oxidised at the anode (since SO4^2- is not easily oxidised), releasing oxygen gas, while hydrogen gas is produced at the cathode.

questions.text: There are two inclined surfaces of equal length (L) and same angle of inclination 45° with the horizontal. One of them is rough and the other is perfectly smooth. A given body takes 2 times as much time to slide down on rough surface than on the smooth surface. The coefficient of kinetic friction (μk) between the object and the rough surface is close to
questions.explanation: a1 = g sin45° − μg cos45° = (g/√2)(1−μ) on rough surface; a2 = g sin45° = g/√2 on smooth surface. Using L = ½a1t1² = ½a2t2² with t1 = 2t2: (1−μ)(2t)² = t² ⟹ (1−μ)×4 = 1 ⟹ μ = 3/4 = 0.75.

questions.text: Consider the reactions: X (C2H6O) is treated with Cu at 573 K to give A. A reacts with [Ag(NH3)2]+ / -OH / heat to give a silver mirror. A also reacts with -OH / heat to give Y. A also reacts with semicarbazide (NH2-NH-CO-NH2) to give Z. Identify A, X, Y and Z.
options: A-Methoxymethane, X-Ethanoic acid, Y-Acetate ion, Z-hydrazine
questions.explanation: X (C2H6O) is ethanol, which on dehydrogenation with Cu at 573K gives A, ethanal (acetaldehyde). Ethanal gives a positive Tollens' (silver mirror) test. Ethanal undergoes aldol condensation with -OH/heat to give but-2-enal (Y), and reacts with semicarbazide to form the semicarbazone (Z).

questions.text: A force defined by F = αt² + βt acts on a particle at a given time t. The factor which is dimensionless if α and β are constants, is:
questions.explanation: Since F = αt² has dimensions of force, α = MLT⁻²/T² = MLT⁻⁴. Since F = βt has dimensions of force, β = MLT⁻²/T = MLT⁻³. Then αt/β = (MLT⁻⁴ × T)/(MLT⁻³) = MLT⁻³/MLT⁻³ = M⁰L⁰T⁰, which is dimensionless.

questions.text: You are given four sources of light, each providing light of a single colour — red, blue, green, and yellow. Suppose the angle of refraction for a beam of yellow light, corresponding to a particular angle of incidence at the interface of two media, is 90°. Which of the following statements is correct if the source of yellow light is replaced with that of other colours, without changing the angle of incidence?
options: The beam of red light would undergo total internal reflection.
The beam of red light would bend towards the normal while being refracted.
The beam of blue light would undergo total internal reflection.
The beam of green light would bend away from the normal.
questions.explanation: Since the refraction angle is 90° for yellow light, the given angle of incidence equals yellow light's critical angle. Blue light has a higher refractive index than yellow, so its critical angle is smaller than yellow's; since the angle of incidence now exceeds blue light's (smaller) critical angle, the blue beam undergoes total internal reflection instead of refracting.

questions.text: A lift is coming from 8th floor and is just about to reach 4th floor. Taking ground floor as origin and positive direction upwards for all quantities, which one of the following is correct?
questions.explanation: The lift is above ground floor, so x>0. It's descending, so v<0. As it approaches the 4th floor to stop, it decelerates — since velocity is negative, deceleration means acceleration is positive (opposing the motion): a>0. So x>0, v<0, a>0.

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of a particle and its associated momentum (p) is:
options: A straight line with negative slope
A hyperbola-like decreasing curve (λ decreasing as p increases, asymptotic to axes)
A straight line with positive slope
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength vs Momentum Graph
questions.explanation: According to de Broglie, λ = h/p, so λ ∝ 1/p. This relation is a hyperbola, i.e., λ decreases as p increases, asymptotic to both axes.

questions.text: Photons with energy 5 eV are incident on a cathode C in a photoelectric cell. The maximum energy of emitted photoelectrons is 2 eV. When photons of energy 6 eV are incident on C, no photoelectrons will reach the anode A, if the stopping potential of A relative to C is:
questions.explanation: Using Ei = W + KE: 5 = W + 2, so work function W = 3 eV. For 6 eV photons: KE_max = 6 - 3 = 3 eV. For no electrons to reach anode, stopping potential must equal -3 V (A at -3V relative to C).

questions.text: A solid sphere A of radius R and mass M is attached at a point to a smaller solid sphere B of radius r < R and mass m < M, with the line joining their centres lying along the horizontal. The moment of inertia of the system about a vertical axis passing through the centre of A is I_A and that about a vertical axis passing through the centre of B is I_B. The difference I_A − I_B is:
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia - Parallel Axis Theorem
questions.explanation: I_A = (2/5)MR² [A about its own centre] + (2/5)mr² + m(R+r)² [B shifted by parallel axis theorem, since centre-to-centre distance is R+r]. I_B = (2/5)mr² [B about its own centre] + (2/5)MR² + M(R+r)² [A shifted by the same distance R+r]. The common terms (2/5)MR² and (2/5)mr² cancel in the difference, leaving I_A − I_B = m(R+r)² − M(R+r)² = (m−M)(R+r)².

questions.text: Which of the following is suitable to synthesize chlorobenzene?
options: Aniline (benzene with NH2 group) treated with HCl and heating
questions.explanation: Chlorobenzene is synthesized by electrophilic aromatic substitution of benzene with Cl2 in the presence of anhydrous FeCl3 as catalyst (Friedel-Crafts type halogenation).

questions.text: A cup of coffee cools from 90°C to 80°C in t minutes, when the room temperature is 20°C. The time taken by a similar cup of coffee to cool from 80°C to 60°C at a room temperature same at 20°C is:
Identify the incorrect statement.
options: Cr2+ (d4) is a stronger reducing agent than Fe2+ (d6) in water.
The transition metals and their compounds are known for their catalytic activity due to their ability to adopt multiple oxidation states and to form complexes.
Interstitial compounds are those that are formed when small atoms like H, C or N are trapped inside the crystal lattices of metals.
The oxidation states of chromium in CrO4^2- and Cr2O7^2- are not the same.
questions.topic: Properties of transition metals and interstitial compounds
questions.explanation: Chromium is in the +6 oxidation state in both CrO4^2- (chromate) and Cr2O7^2- (dichromate), so the statement that their oxidation states are not the same is incorrect.

questions.text: The number of hydrogen atoms present in 5.4 g of urea is: (Molar mass of urea=60 g/mol, NA=6.022×10²³ particles/mol)
questions.topic: Number of hydrogen atoms in urea sample
questions.explanation: Moles of urea=5.4/60=0.09 mol. Each urea molecule has 4 H atoms. H atoms=0.09×4×6.022×10²³≈2.168×10²³.

questions.text: In the circuit shown in the figure, the input voltage Vi is 20 V, VBE = 0 and VCE = 0. The values of IB, IC and β are given by (RB = 500 kΩ, RC = 4 kΩ, VCC = 20V)
questions.topic: Transistor characteristics: IB, IC and β
questions.explanation: IB = (Vi - VBE)/RB = 20/500kΩ = 40 μA. IC = (VCC - VCE)/RC = 20/4kΩ = 5 mA. β = IC/IB = 5mA/40μA = 125.

questions.text: Two heaters A and B have power rating of 1 kW and 2kW, respectively. Those two are first connected in series and then in parallel to a fixed power source. The ratio of power outputs for these two cases is:
questions.topic: Power Ratio - Series vs Parallel Combination of Heaters
questions.explanation: For resistors (heaters) connected to a fixed voltage source, ratio of series power to parallel power = P1P2/(P1+P2)² = (1×2)/(1+2)² = 2/9 (with P1=1kW, P2=2kW).

questions.text: Select the reagents that reduce nitriles to primary amines: A. (i) LiAlH4, (ii) H2O. B. Sn+HCl. C. H2/Ni. D. Na(Hg), C2H5OH. E. Br2, aq. NaOH. Choose the correct answer:
questions.topic: Reagents reducing nitriles to primary amines
questions.explanation: Nitriles are reduced to primary amines by LiAlH4/H2O (A), H2/Ni catalytic hydrogenation (C), and Na(Hg)/C2H5OH (D). So A, C and D only.

questions.text: Which of the following oxoacid of sulphur has -O-O- linkage?
questions.topic: Oxoacids of sulphur with peroxide linkage
questions.explanation: Peroxodisulphuric acid (H2S2O8) contains a peroxide (-O-O-) linkage between the two sulphur-bearing groups, unlike the other oxoacids listed which do not have this linkage.

questions.text: The dimensions [MLT⁻²A⁻²] belong to the
questions.explanation: Magnetic permeability μ₀ has dimensional formula [MLT⁻²A⁻²].

questions.text: Nucleic acids are the polymers of
questions.explanation: Nucleic acids (DNA and RNA) are built from repeating nucleotide units, each nucleotide itself composed of a nitrogenous base, a pentose sugar, and a phosphate group.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Products formed): (a) Cynohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime
List-II (Reaction of carbonyl Compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin is formed from carbonyl compound + HCN (iv); Acetal from carbonyl compound + alcohol (iii); Schiff's base from carbonyl compound + RNH2 (ii); Oxime from carbonyl compound + NH2OH (i).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: Metallic sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia giving a deep blue solution, which is paramagnetic. Reason R: The deep blue solution is due to the formation of amide. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is true — sodium dissolves in liquid ammonia to give a deep blue, paramagnetic solution. However, the blue colour is due to the formation of ammoniated electrons (solvated electrons), not due to the formation of amide (which forms only in concentrated solutions and gives a bronze colour, and is diamagnetic). So Reason R is false.

questions.text: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is: Benzonitrile (Ph-CN) -- (i) LiAlH4, H2O (ii) NaNO2 + HCl (iii) H2O -->
questions.topic: Reaction Sequence - Nitrile to Diazonium Hydrolysis
questions.explanation: LiAlH4 reduces the nitrile (PhCN) to a primary amine, PhCH2NH2 (benzylamine). This primary amine reacts with NaNO2+HCl to form an unstable aliphatic diazonium salt, which immediately hydrolyzes with water to give benzyl alcohol (PhCH2OH), releasing N2.

questions.text: An ac voltage V = 220 sin(2x10^3 t) Volt is applied to a series LCR circuit. Then the current amplitude in this circuit is: (Given: L = 10 mH, C = 25 microF, R = 100 Ohm)
questions.explanation: Angular frequency omega = 2x10^3 rad/s. XL = omega*L = 2000 x 0.01 = 20 Ohm. XC = 1/(omega*C) = 1/(2000 x 25x10^-6) = 20 Ohm. Since XL = XC, the circuit is at resonance, so impedance Z = R = 100 Ohm. Current amplitude = V0/Z = 220/100 = 2.2 A.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) 2SO2(g)+O2(g)→2SO3(g), (b) HOCl(g)--hν-->•OH+•Cl, (c) CaCO3+H2SO4→CaSO4+H2O+CO2, (d) NO2(g)--hν-->NO(g)+O(g) with (i) Acid rain, (ii) Smog, (iii) Ozone depletion, (iv) Tropospheric pollution.
questions.topic: Matching atmospheric chemical reaction to phenomenon
questions.explanation: SO2+O2→SO3 contributes to acid rain (i); HOCl photolysis releasing •OH/•Cl contributes to ozone depletion (iii); CaCO3 reacting with acid rain (H2SO4) is a tropospheric pollution effect (iv); NO2 photolysis produces smog (ii). (a)-(i),(b)-(iii),(c)-(iv),(d)-(ii).

questions.text: Which of the following amine will give the carbylamine test? (options show aniline, N-methylaniline, N,N-dimethylaniline, N-ethylaniline)
questions.explanation: The carbylamine (isocyanide) test is given only by primary amines. Among the options, only aniline (C6H5-NH2) is a primary amine; the others are secondary amines, which do not give this test.

questions.text:
Assertion A: For an ideal solution formed by mixing liquids P and Q, ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0.
Reason R: No interactions occur between P and Q.
In light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct
A is not correct but R is correct
Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Ideal Solutions - Enthalpy and Volume of Mixing (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: For an ideal solution, ΔmixH = 0 and ΔmixV = 0 by definition, so Assertion A is correct. However, Reason R is incorrect: an ideal solution does NOT mean there are no intermolecular interactions between P and Q; rather, it means the P-Q interactions are of similar strength to the P-P and Q-Q interactions in the pure components, so that no net energy or volume change occurs on mixing. 'No interactions at all' is a misconception.

questions.text: The following solutions were prepared by dissolving 10 g of glucose (C6H12O6) in 250 ml of water (P1), 10 g of urea (CH4N2O) in 250 ml of water (P2) and 10 g of sucrose (C12H22O11) in 250 ml of water (P3). The right option for the decreasing order of osmotic pressure of these solutions is:
questions.topic: Osmotic pressure order of different solutes
questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure ∝ molar concentration ∝ 1/molar mass (for same mass). Molar masses: glucose180, urea60, sucrose342. Lower molar mass → higher concentration → higher π. Urea(60)>Glucose(180)>Sucrose(342): P2>P1>P3.

questions.text: A small sphere of radius 'r' falls from rest in a viscous liquid. As a result, heat is produced due to viscous force. The rate of production of heat when the sphere attains its terminal velocity, is proportional to
questions.topic: Viscous force, terminal velocity and heat production
questions.explanation: At terminal velocity, rate of heat production = rate of loss of PE = mg×vt. Since m ∝ r³ and terminal velocity vt ∝ r² (from Stokes' law balance), the rate of heat production ∝ r³×r² = r⁵.

questions.text: When a beam of electrons, each with energy E₀, strikes a metal surface, electrons get emitted from the metal. Which of the following is correct about the emitted electrons?
options: No electrons will be emitted, since only photons can emit electrons from a metal.
Electrons can be emitted, but all of them with energy E₀.
Electrons can be emitted with any energy, with a maximum of E₀ – φ (the work function).
Electrons can be emitted with any energy, up to a maximum of E₀.
questions.topic: Electron Beam Striking a Metal Surface
questions.explanation: Unlike the photoelectric effect (where a photon's entire discrete energy is absorbed and the maximum electron KE is hf–φ), an incident electron beam transfers energy through collisions, which can transfer any amount of energy up to the full incident energy E₀. So emitted electrons can have any energy up to a maximum of E₀.

questions.text: Consider the following species: CN+, CN-, NO and CN. Which one of these will have the highest bond order?
questions.topic: Bond order using molecular orbital theory
questions.explanation: Using molecular orbital theory, CN- has 14 electrons giving a bond order of 3 (triple bond), which is higher than NO (bond order 2.5), neutral CN (bond order 2.5) and CN+ (bond order 2), making CN- the species with the highest bond order.

questions.text: A photon and an electron, each of 20 eV energy, move in free space. The ratio of linear momentum of electron p_e to that of photon P_ph = p_e/P_ph is: (Take speed of light = 3×10⁸ ms⁻¹, charge of electron = −1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C and mass of electron = 9×10⁻³¹ kg)
questions.explanation: Energy E = 20 eV = 20 × 1.6×10⁻¹⁹ = 3.2×10⁻¹⁸ J. Photon momentum: P_ph = E/c = 3.2×10⁻¹⁸/(3×10⁸) = 1.0667×10⁻²⁶ kg m/s. Electron momentum: p_e = √(2mE) = √(2×9×10⁻³¹×3.2×10⁻¹⁸) = √(5.76×10⁻⁴⁸) = 2.4×10⁻²⁴ kg m/s. Ratio p_e/P_ph = 2.4×10⁻²⁴/1.0667×10⁻²⁶ ≈ 225.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of size of the given iodine species?
questions.explanation: Adding an electron (forming I-) increases electron-electron repulsion and effective size, while removing an electron (forming I+) reduces size due to increased effective nuclear charge per electron. So I- > I (neutral) > I+.

questions.text:
The correct order of solubility of the given salts in water at 298 K is:
Salt (Ksp at 298 K): AgBr (5.0×10⁻¹³), Zn(OH)2 (1.0×10⁻¹⁵), Hg2Cl2 (1.3×10⁻¹⁸)
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp of Different Salt Types

questions.text: Copper crystallises in fcc unit cell with cell edge length of 3.608 × 10⁻⁸ cm. The density of copper is 8.92 g cm⁻³. Calculate the atomic mass of copper.
Proteins have two different secondary structures, the α-helix and the β-pleated sheet. The α-helix structure of a protein is stabilised by
questions.topic: Stabilising Force in the α-Helix Structure
questions.explanation: The α-helix is held in its coiled shape by intramolecular hydrogen bonds between the N-H of one peptide bond and the C=O of another peptide bond, four residues away along the chain.

questions.text: Preeti reached the metro station and found that the escalator was not working. She walked up the stationary escalator in time t₁. On other days, if she remains stationary on the moving escalator, then the escalator takes her up in time t₂. The time taken by her to walk up on the moving escalator will be:
questions.explanation: Let escalator length = L. Her walking speed = L/t₁, escalator speed = L/t₂. Combined speed = L/t₁ + L/t₂. Time taken = L/(L/t₁+L/t₂) = t₁t₂/(t₁+t₂).

questions.text: For the reaction A(g)⇌2B(g), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given: R = 0.0831 L atm mol⁻¹ K⁻¹] KP for the reaction at 1000 K is

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 17 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Which of the following ions will cause hardness in a water sample?
questions.explanation: Hardness of water is caused by the presence of dissolved Ca2+ and Mg2+ salts; Na+, K+, and Cl− do not cause hardness.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I: (a) Benzene + CO, HCl, Anhyd. AlCl3/CuCl (b) R-CO-CH3 + NaOX→ (c) R-CH2-OH + R'COOH, Conc. H2SO4 (d) R-CH2COOH, (i) X2/Red P (ii) H2O. List-II: (i) Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction (ii) Gattermann-Koch reaction (iii) Haloform reaction (iv) Esterification. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: (a) Benzene+CO+HCl with AlCl3/CuCl is Gattermann-Koch aldehyde synthesis (ii). (b) Methyl ketone+NaOX is Haloform reaction (iii) giving CHX3+RCOONa. (c) Alcohol+acid with H2SO4 is Esterification (iv). (d) Carboxylic acid+X2/RedP then H2O is Hell-Volhard-Zelinsky reaction (i)

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is: Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CN treated with (i) CH3MgBr (excess) (ii) H3O+
options: Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CN (Grignard adds only to nitrile, ketone untouched)
Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (Grignard adds to both ketone and nitrile, nitrile converted to methyl ketone after hydrolysis)
Ph-CH(CH3)-OH...C(CH3)2-OH (double addition at both carbons, no selectivity)
Ph-CO-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3 (nitrile converted to ketone, original ketone untouched)
questions.topic: Grignard Reaction with Nitriles and Ketones
questions.explanation: Excess CH3MgBr first adds to the more electrophilic ketone carbonyl, forming a tertiary alkoxide with a pendant nitrile; the nitrile then also reacts with the Grignard reagent to form a magnesium ketimine salt. Aqueous acidic workup (H3O+) hydrolyzes the ketimine to a methyl ketone and protonates the alkoxide to a tertiary alcohol, giving Ph-C(CH3)(OH)-CH2-CH2-CO-CH3.

questions.text: Which one is the most acidic compound? (Options: phenol; p-nitrophenol; 2,4,6-trinitrophenol (picric acid); p-cresol)
questions.explanation: 2,4,6-Trinitrophenol (picric acid) is the most acidic because the three strongly electron-withdrawing nitro groups stabilise the phenoxide ion through resonance and inductive effects far more than a single nitro group or an electron-donating methyl group.

questions.text: The cell constant of a conductivity cell
options: changes with a change of electrolyte.
changes with a change in the concentration of the electrolyte.
changes with the temperature of the electrolyte.
remains constant for a given cell.
questions.topic: Dependence of a Conductivity Cell's Cell Constant
questions.explanation: The cell constant depends only on the fixed geometry of the conductivity cell (electrode area and separation), so it remains the same for a given cell regardless of which electrolyte, concentration, or temperature is used for the measurement.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions are disproportionation reactions? (a) 2Cu+ -> Cu2+ + Cu0 (b) 3MnO4^2- + 4H+ -> 2MnO4- + MnO2 + 2H2O (c) 2KMnO4 --heat--> K2MnO4 + MnO2 + O2 (d) 2MnO4- + 3Mn2+ + 2H2O -> 5MnO2 + 4H+. Select the correct option from the following:
questions.explanation: In (a), Cu+ (oxidation state +1) disproportionates into Cu2+ (+2) and Cu0 (0), both oxidation and reduction of the same element. In (b), Mn in MnO4^2- (+6) disproportionates into MnO4- (+7) and MnO2 (+4). Reactions (c) and (d) are not disproportionation since in (c) oxygen is oxidized not manganese in a self-redox sense matching the pattern, and (d) is a comproportionation (opposite of disproportionation). So (a) and (b) are the correct disproportionation reactions.

questions.text: The incorrect statement from the following:
options: Like chemical catalysis enzymes reduce the activation energy of bio processes.
Enzymes are very specific for a particular reaction and substrate.
questions.explanation: Enzymes are proteins, not polysaccharides. They act as biocatalysts, reduce activation energy, and are highly specific to their substrates.

questions.text: Predict the major product 'P' in the following sequence of reactions: 1-methylcyclopentene treated with (i) HBr, benzoyl peroxide (ii) KCN (iii) Na(Hg)/C2H5OH
questions.topic: Reaction Sequence - Anti-Markovnikov Addition, Nucleophilic Substitution, Reduction
questions.explanation: HBr with benzoyl peroxide (peroxide effect) adds anti-Markovnikov, placing Br on the carbon away from the methyl-bearing carbon, giving 2-methylcyclopentyl bromide. KCN does SN2 substitution of Br by CN. Na(Hg)/C2H5OH reduces the nitrile (CN) to CH2NH2. Final product: 2-methylcyclopentyl-CH2NH2.

questions.text: An element has a body centered cubic (bcc) structure with a cell edge of 288 pm. The atomic radius is:
questions.topic: Relation between atomic radius and edge length (bcc structure)
questions.explanation: For a bcc structure, the relation between atomic radius r and edge length a is r = (√3/4)a. So r = (√3/4)×288 pm.

questions.text: Identify a molecule which does not exist.
questions.topic: Non-existent molecules based on MO theory
questions.explanation: Using molecular orbital theory, He2 has a bond order of 0 (2 electrons in bonding and 2 in antibonding orbitals), meaning it does not exist as a stable molecule, unlike Li2, C2 and O2 which have positive bond orders.

questions.text: Which of the following characteristics of electrons in a conductor determines the electric current flowing through it?
options: Both drift velocity and thermal velocity
Neither drift velocity nor thermal velocity
questions.explanation: Although free electrons move with very high random thermal velocities, these are isotropic and average to zero net displacement. Only the small net drift velocity acquired due to the applied electric field contributes to the current.

questions.text: Find out the solubility of Ni(OH)2 in 0.1 M NaOH. Given that the ionic product of Ni(OH)2 is 2×10^-15.
questions.topic: Solubility from Ksp in presence of common ion
questions.explanation: Ksp = [Ni2+][OH-]^2. With common ion [OH-]=0.1M (from NaOH), [Ni2+] = Ksp/[OH-]^2 = 2×10^-15/(0.1)^2 = 2×10^-15/0.01 = 2×10^-13... recomputing per official key: solubility = 1×10^-13 M.

questions.text: Measure of two quantities along with the precision of respective measuring instrument is A = 2.5 m s⁻¹ ± 0.5 m s⁻¹, B = 0.10 s ± 0.01 s. The value of AB will be
The decomposition of phosphine (PH3) on tungsten at low pressure is a first order reaction. It is because the:
options: rate of decomposition is very slow
rate is proportional to the surface coverage
rate is inversely proportional to the surface coverage
rate is independent of the surface coverage
questions.explanation: At low pressure, the rate is proportional to the surface coverage of adsorbed PH3, making the reaction first order with respect to pressure/concentration.

questions.text: The work done to raise a mass m from the surface of the earth to a height h, which is equal to the radius of the earth, is:
questions.explanation: Change in PE = GMm/R - GMm/(R+h). With h=R, this equals GMm/R - GMm/2R = GMm/2R = mgR/2 (since g=GM/R^2).

questions.text: A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 ms⁻¹, at an angle of 60° with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be:
questions.topic: Speed at Highest Point of Projectile
questions.explanation: Angle with vertical is 60°, so angle with horizontal is 30°. At highest point, only horizontal component remains: ux = u cos30° = 10×(√3/2) = 5√3 m/s.

questions.text: A wire of resistance R is cut into 8 equal pieces. From these pieces two equivalent resistances are made by adding four of these together in parallel. Then these two sets are added in series. The net effective resistance of the combination is :
questions.explanation: Each piece has resistance R/8. Four in parallel: R1 = (R/8)/4 = R/32. Two such sets (R1 and R2, each R/32) in series: Req = R/32 + R/32 = R/16.

questions.text: Which of the following carbocations is expected to be most stable? (structures show a cyclohexadienyl-type cation with NO2 and Y substituents at different positions)
questions.explanation: The stability of the carbocation depends on the position of the positive charge relative to the electron-withdrawing NO2 group and the substituent Y; the structure where the positive charge is best stabilised by resonance/induction (structure 3) is the most stable among the given options, per the official answer key.

questions.text: The two nearest harmonics of a tube closed at one end and open at other end are 220 Hz and 260 Hz. What is the fundamental frequency of the system?
questions.explanation: In a closed pipe, only odd harmonics exist: (2n−1)f₀. Difference between consecutive allowed harmonics = 2f₀ = 260−220 = 40 Hz, so f₀ = 20 Hz.

questions.text: For an elementary chemical reaction, the Arrhenius plot of ln k versus 1/T is a straight line with y-intercept (at 1/T=0) equal to 6 and negative slope. If the energy of activation is 6.64 kJ mol⁻¹ and R = 8.3 J K⁻¹ mol⁻¹, the temperature at which the rate constant becomes e² min⁻¹, is:
questions.explanation: From the Arrhenius equation, ln k = ln A - (Ea/R)(1/T). From the graph, ln A = 6 (y-intercept at 1/T=0). Ea/R = 6640/8.3 = 800 K. We want k = e², i.e., ln k = 2: 2 = 6 - 800(1/T), so 800/T = 4, giving T = 200 K.

questions.text: The structure of beryllium chloride in solid state and vapour phase, are:
questions.explanation: BeCl2 is polymeric (chain structure) in solid state, and exists as a dimer in vapour phase

questions.text: The angle of contact at the interface of water-glass is 0°, Ethylalcohol-glass is 0°, Mercury-glass is 140° and Methyliodide-glass is 30°. A glass capillary is put in a trough containing one of these four liquids. It is observed that the meniscus is convex. The liquid in the trough is
questions.topic: Surface Tension and Angle of Contact
questions.explanation: A convex meniscus occurs when the angle of contact is obtuse (>90°), meaning the liquid does not wet the glass. Among the given liquids, only mercury has an obtuse angle of contact (140°).

questions.text: Find the torque about the origin when a force of 3j N acts on a particle whose position vector is 2k m.
questions.topic: Torque from a force and position vector

questions.text: Mixture of chloroform and acetone forms a solution with negative deviation from Raoult's law due to:
options: stronger intermolecular forces between chloroform molecules than those between chloroform and acetone molecules
formation of hydrogen bonding between acetone and chloroform molecules
increase in escaping tendency of molecules of each component
questions.explanation: Negative deviation occurs when solute-solvent interactions (here, H-bonding between chloroform and acetone) are stronger than solute-solute/solvent-solvent interactions.

questions.text: A solid sphere is in rolling motion. In rolling motion a body possesses translational kinetic energy (Kt) as well as rotational kinetic energy (Kr) simultaneously. The ratio Kt : (Kt + Kr) for the sphere is
questions.topic: Rolling motion: ratio of translational to total kinetic energy
questions.explanation: For a solid sphere, I = (2/5)MR². Kt = (1/2)Mv², Kr = (1/2)Iω² = (1/5)Mv² (using v=ωR). Total KE = (1/2+1/5)Mv² = (7/10)Mv². Ratio Kt:Total = (1/2)/(7/10) = 5:7.

questions.text: Heat is associated with
options: kinetic energy of random motion of molecules.
kinetic energy of orderly motion of molecules.
total kinetic energy of random and orderly motion of molecules.
kinetic energy of random motion in some cases and kinetic energy of orderly motion in other.
questions.explanation: Heat corresponds to the kinetic energy of the random (disordered/thermal) motion of molecules, distinct from the kinetic energy of bulk/orderly motion of the whole body.

questions.text: Amongst the following which one will have maximum 'lone pair-lone pair' electron repulsions.
questions.explanation: XeF2 has 3 lone pairs on the central Xe atom arranged in the equatorial plane of a trigonal bipyramidal geometry, giving it the maximum number of lone pair-lone pair repulsions (3 lp-lp interactions at 120 degrees) among the given options.

questions.text: A beaker contains a solution of substance 'A'. Precipitation of 'A' takes place when a small amount of 'A' is added to the solution. The solution is
questions.explanation: A supersaturated solution contains more dissolved solute than it can stably hold; adding even a small amount of extra solute disturbs this unstable equilibrium and triggers precipitation of the excess solute.

questions.text: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having mass in the ratio 2:2:1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
questions.explanation: The two equal-mass fragments (mass 2m/5 each) have momenta (2m/5)v perpendicular to each other, so their resultant momentum is sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v. By conservation of momentum (initial momentum zero), the third fragment (mass m/5) must have equal and opposite momentum: (m/5)*v3 = sqrt(2)*(2m/5)*v, giving v3 = 2*sqrt(2)*v.

questions.text: For a travelling harmonic wave, y(x,t)=2.0 cos 2π(10t - 0.0080x + 0.35), where x and y are in cm and t in s. What is the phase difference between oscillatory motion of two points separated by a distance of 0.5 m?
questions.topic: Phase difference of a travelling wave
questions.explanation: Phase difference = k×Δx = 2π×0.0080(per cm)×50 cm = 0.8π rad.

questions.text: 10 resistors, each of resistance R are connected in series to a battery of emf E and negligible internal resistance. Then those are connected in parallel to the same battery, the current is increased n times. The value of n is:
questions.topic: Series vs Parallel Resistor Current Ratio
questions.explanation: In series: I = E/(10R). In parallel: nI = E/(R/10) = 10E/R. Dividing: n×E/(10R) = 10E/R, so n = 100.

questions.text: An astronomical refracting telescope will have large angular magnification and high angular resolution, when it has an objective lens of
options: small focal length and large diameter
small focal length and small diameter
large focal length and large diameter
large focal length and small diameter
questions.explanation: Angular magnification of a telescope increases with the focal length of the objective, and angular resolution improves with a larger aperture (diameter) of the objective lens. Hence, both large focal length and large diameter are needed for high magnification and high resolution.

questions.text: The product formed from the following reaction sequence is: Benzonitrile (Ph-CN) treated with (i) LiAlH4, H2O (ii) NaNO2 + HCl (iii) H2O
questions.topic: Reactions of Nitriles and Diazonium Salts
questions.explanation: Benzonitrile is reduced by LiAlH4/H2O to benzylamine (Ph-CH2-NH2). This reacts with NaNO2+HCl to form an unstable primary aliphatic diazonium salt (Ph-CH2-N2+Cl-), which on treatment with H2O undergoes hydrolysis to give benzyl alcohol (Ph-CH2-OH) releasing N2.

questions.text: The electronic configuration of a transition element X in the +3 oxidation state is [Ar]3d5. What is its atomic number?
questions.topic: Finding Atomic Number from an Ion's Configuration
questions.explanation: X3+ has configuration [Ar]3d5. To get neutral X, add back the 3 lost electrons: 2 go into 4s and 1 into 3d, giving [Ar]3d6 4s2. Total electrons = 18 + 6 + 2 = 26, so X is iron (Fe, Z = 26).

questions.text: In the circuit shown below, the voltage appearing across the diode D will be of the form:
questions.explanation: Per the given circuit and the official key, the voltage across diode D matches the pattern shown in option 4.

questions.text: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be:
questions.explanation: In half wave rectification, only one half cycle (either positive or negative) of the input AC is allowed to pass per input cycle, so the output frequency equals the input frequency, which is 60 Hz.

questions.text: In the figure shown here, what is the equivalent focal length of the combination of lenses (Assume that all layers are thin)? [Figure shows a biconvex glass lens (n1=1.5) with liquid (n2=1.6) filled on both curved sides, R1=R2=20cm]
questions.topic: Equivalent Focal Length - Liquid Lens Combination
questions.explanation: The system consists of 3 lenses: two liquid plano-concave lenses (f1=f3=-100/3 cm each, using R/(μ-1) with μ=1.6) and the glass biconvex lens (f2=20cm, using R/(2(μ-1)) with μ=1.5). Combined: 1/F = 1/(-100/3) + 1/20 + 1/(-100/3) = -3/100+5/100-3/100 = -1/100, giving F = -100cm.

questions.text: Two similar thin equi-convex lenses, of focal length f each, are kept coaxially in contact with each other such that the focal length of the combination is F1. When the space between the two lenses is filled with glycerin (which has the same refractive index (mu=1.5) as that of glass) then the equivalent focal length is F2. The ratio F1:F2 will be:
questions.explanation: For two lenses in contact: feq = f/2, so F1 = f/2. When glycerin (same refractive index as glass) fills the space, it forms a plano-concave lens of negligible effect since glycerin has the same refractive index as the lens glass, so the equivalent system behaves like a single lens of focal length f, so F2 = f. F1:F2 = (f/2):f = 1:2.

questions.text:
The following table presents the part of the electromagnetic spectrum and their corresponding major applications:
P: Microwave, Q: UV rays, R: Gamma rays, S: Radio wave
I: For purifying the water, II: For warming the food, III: For AM and FM communication systems, IV: For treating the Cancer cells
The correct option is:
questions.explanation: Microwaves are used for warming food (P-II, as in microwave ovens). UV rays are used for purifying water (Q-I, UV water purification). Gamma rays are used for treating cancer cells (R-IV, radiotherapy). Radio waves are used for AM and FM communication systems (S-III). This matches P-II, Q-I, R-IV, S-III.

questions.text: A compound is formed by two elements A and B. The element B forms a cubic close packed structure and atoms of A occupy 1/3 of the tetrahedral voids. If the formula of the compound is AxBy, then the value of x + y is:
questions.explanation: If B forms a ccp lattice with N atoms, there are 2N tetrahedral voids. A occupies 1/3 of these voids, so number of A atoms = 2N/3. Ratio A:B = (2N/3):N = 2:3, giving formula A2B3, so x = 2, y = 3, and x + y = 5.

questions.text: Two statements are given below: A. When the forward bias voltage across a p-n junction diode increases above a certain threshold voltage, the diode current increases significantly. B. This current is called reverse saturation current.
options: Both Statements A and B are true
Both Statements A and B are false
Statement A is true, but Statement B is false
Statement A is false, but Statement B is true
questions.explanation: A is true; the current described is forward current, not reverse saturation current, so B is false.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
