Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R
Assertion A: The potential (V) at any axial point, at 2 m distance (r) from the centre of the dipole of dipole moment vector P of magnitude, 4×10⁻⁶ C m, is ±9×10³ V. (Take 1/4πε₀ = 9×10⁹ SI units)
Reason R: V = ±2P/(4πε₀r²), where r is the distance of any axial point, situated at 2 m from the centre of the dipole.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
questions.topic: Axial Potential Due to Electric Dipole (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: V_axial = ±kp/r² = ±(9×10⁹ × 4×10⁻⁶)/2² = ±9×10³ V, so Assertion A is true. However, the correct formula for axial potential is V = ±p/(4πε₀r²) (without the factor of 2 in numerator for this form, as kp/r² already equals p/(4πε₀r²)), so Reason R (with the extra factor 2P) is false/incorrectly stated.

questions.text: A cricket ball of mass 150 g moving with a speed of 126 km/h hits at the middle of the bat, held firmly at its position by the batsman. The ball moves straight back to the bowler after hitting the bat. Assuming that collision between ball and bat is completely elastic and the two remain in contact for 0.001s, the force that the batsman had to apply to hold the bat firmly at its place would be
questions.explanation: Speed = 126 km/h = 35 m/s. Since the ball reverses direction, Δv = 35−(−35) = 70 m/s. Δp = 0.15×70 = 10.5 kg·m/s. Force = Δp/Δt = 10.5/0.001 = 1.05×10⁴ N.

questions.text: A particle executing SHM has maximum speed 30 cm/s and maximum acceleration 60 cm/s². The period of oscillation is
questions.explanation: Maximum speed vmax = Aω = 30 and maximum acceleration amax = Aω² = 60. Dividing, ω = amax/vmax = 60/30 = 2 rad/s. Period T = 2π/ω = 2π/2 = π s.

questions.text: Methane reacts with steam at 1273K... [separate question] The following two reactions give the same foul smelling product Z: C2H5Cl --X--> Z; C2H5CONH2 --Br2,NaOH--> --CHCl3/ethanolic KOH--> Z. X and Z, respectively, are:
questions.explanation: Carbylamine (isocyanide) reaction: ethyl chloride with AgCN gives the nitrile; with KCN gives the isocyanide (foul-smelling). Per key, X=AgCN, Z=C2H5NC.

questions.text: The equilibrium concentrations of the species in the reaction A + B <-> C + D are 2, 3, 10 and 6 mol/L, respectively at 300 K. ΔG° for the reaction is (R = 2 cal/mol K):
questions.topic: Relation between Gibbs Energy and Equilibrium Constant

questions.text: A balloon is made of a material of surface tension S and its inflation outlet (from where gas is filled in it) has small area A. It is filled with a gas of density ρ and takes a spherical shape of radius R. When the gas is allowed to flow freely out of it, its radius r changes from R to 0(zero) in time T. If the speed v(r) of gas coming out of the balloon depends on r as rᵃ and T ∝ Sᵅ Aᵝ ργ Rᵟ then
questions.explanation: Using dimensional analysis on T ∝ SᵅAᵝργRᵟ: [M⁰L⁰T] = [MT⁻²]ᵅ[L²]ᵝ[ML⁻³]γ[L]ᵟ. Equating powers of M, L, T and solving gives option (3): a=−1/2, α=−1/2, β=−1, γ=1/2, δ=7/2.

questions.text: The moment of inertia of a thin rod about an axis passing through its mid-point and perpendicular to the rod is 2400 g cm². The length of the 400 g rod is nearly:
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of a Rod - Finding Length

questions.text: The stability of Cu2+ is more than Cu+ salts in aqueous solution due to:
questions.topic: Stability of Oxidation States in Aqueous Solution
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, the relative stability of Cu2+ over Cu+ is determined by hydration energy, which is proportional to the charge on the ion and inversely proportional to ionic size. Cu2+, having a higher charge, has a much higher hydration energy than Cu+, which compensates for the higher ionisation enthalpy required to remove the second electron, making Cu2+ more stable in aqueous solution.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for the total pressure (in atm.) in a mixture of 4g O2 and 2g H2 confined in a total volume of one litre at 0°C is: [Given R = 0.82 L atm mol^-1 K^-1, T = 273 K]
The ratio of wavelengths of the last line of Balmer series and the last line of Lyman series is:
questions.explanation: Last line (series limit) wavelength ∝ n₁² (where n₁ is the lower level). For Balmer, n₁=2 gives λ∝4; for Lyman, n₁=1 gives λ∝1. Ratio = 4:1 = 4.

questions.text: For the second period elements the correct increasing order of first ionisation enthalpy is:
options: Li < B < Be < C < N < O < F < Ne
Li < Be < B < C < O < N < F < Ne
Li < Be < B < C < N < O < F < Ne
Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne
questions.explanation: Due to extra stability of half-filled (N) and fully-filled (Be) configurations, and exceptions at B (lower than Be) and O (lower than N), the correct increasing order is Li < B < Be < C < O < N < F < Ne.

questions.text: The electronic configuration of Cu(II) is 3d9, whereas that of Cu(I) is 3d10. Which of the following is correct?
options: Cu(I) and Cu(II) are equally stable.
Stability of Cu(I) and Cu(II) depends on the nature of the copper salt.
questions.topic: Relative Stability of Cu(I) and Cu(II) in Solution
questions.explanation: Although Cu(I)'s 3d10 configuration is electronically more symmetric, Cu2+ is much more strongly hydrated than Cu+ in aqueous solution (its hydration enthalpy far exceeds the extra ionisation energy needed), which is why Cu+ disproportionates in water (2Cu+ → Cu2+ + Cu) and Cu(II) is actually the more stable state in solution.

questions.text: The given electrical network (OR gate followed by NOR-shaped gate then NOT gate, inputs A, B, output Y) is equivalent to:
questions.explanation: Combining an OR gate followed by stages that invert the combined output of A and B is equivalent to a single NOR gate: Y = NOT(A OR B).

questions.text: The maximum covalency shown by nitrogen in its compounds is
questions.explanation: Nitrogen has only 2s and 2p orbitals available (no accessible d-orbitals) in its valence shell, so it can form at most 4 bonds — 3 covalent bonds plus one coordinate/dative bond, as seen in NH4⁺ — giving a maximum covalency of 4, unlike heavier group 15 elements which can expand their covalency using d-orbitals.

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is
questions.explanation: Fringe width ∝ wavelength. Number of fringes ∝ 1/wavelength. n2 = n1×(λ1/λ2) = 8×(600/400) = 12.

questions.text: In a nuclear reactor, moderators slow down the fast neutrons produced in fission. Moderators are chosen to have light nuclei; heavy nuclei will not serve the purpose because
options: heavy nuclei would break up on collision.
elastic collision of neutrons with heavy nuclei will not slow them down effectively.
the net weight of the reactor would become unbearably high.
substances with heavy nuclei do not occur in liquid or gaseous form at room temperature.
questions.explanation: In an elastic collision, maximum kinetic energy transfer occurs when the colliding masses are comparable (as with billiard balls). A neutron colliding elastically with a much heavier nucleus bounces back with almost its original speed, transferring very little energy, so heavy nuclei are ineffective as moderators; light nuclei (comparable in mass to the neutron) slow neutrons down much more efficiently.

questions.text: Metal carbonates decompose on heating to give metal oxide and carbon dioxide. Which of the metal carbonates is most stable thermally?
questions.explanation: Thermal stability of Group 2 metal carbonates increases down the group because the larger cation has lower polarising power, stabilising the carbonate ion better. BaCO3, with the largest cation here, is the most thermally stable.

questions.text: The conductivity of a semiconductor increases with an increase in temperature because
options: the number density of free current carriers increases.
both the number density of carriers and the relaxation time increase.
the number density of current carriers increases and the relaxation time decreases, but the effect of the decrease in relaxation time is much smaller than the increase in number density.
questions.topic: Conductivity of a Semiconductor vs. Temperature
questions.explanation: Raising the temperature of a semiconductor exponentially increases the number of charge carriers generated by thermal excitation across the band gap, while the relaxation time (between collisions) decreases only mildly. Since the increase in carrier density dominates, overall conductivity increases with temperature.

questions.text: A cylindrical cork of uniform density floats in a liquid of density ρ₁. If the cork is depressed slightly and released, it oscillates harmonically with time period T. If the same cork floats in another liquid of density ρ₂, then the similar oscillation has time period 2T. The value of ρ₂/ρ₁ is:
questions.topic: Oscillation of a Floating Cylindrical Cork
questions.explanation: For a floating cylindrical cork displaced by x, the restoring force is F = -ρ_liquid A g x, giving effective spring constant k = ρ_liquid A g. Time period T = 2π√(m/k) = 2π√(m/(ρ_liquid A g)), so T ∝ 1/√ρ_liquid (mass m of the cork is fixed). Given T₂ = 2T₁: T₂/T₁ = √(ρ₁/ρ₂) = 2, so ρ₁/ρ₂ = 4, giving ρ₂/ρ₁ = 1/4.

questions.text: Which of the following oxides is most acidic in nature?
questions.topic: Acidic nature of oxides (alkaline earth metals)
questions.explanation: Among the alkaline earth metal oxides, BeO is the most acidic (even amphoteric) due to beryllium's small size and high polarising power, which gives its bonds more covalent character compared to the increasingly basic oxides of Mg, Ca and Ba.

questions.text: The electronic configuration of gadolinium (Atomic number 64) is
questions.explanation: Gadolinium is an exception to the regular lanthanoid filling pattern: its extra stability from a half-filled 4f subshell gives the configuration [Xe] 4f7 5d1 6s2, rather than the expected 4f8 6s2.

questions.text: If the rms current in a 50 Hz AC circuit is 5 A, the value of the current 1/300 seconds after its value becomes zero is
questions.explanation: Peak current I₀ = I_rms×√2 = 5√2 A. Angular frequency ω = 2πf = 100π rad/s. Phase angle at t = 1/300 s is ωt = 100π/300 = π/3 (60°). Instantaneous current i = I₀ sin(60°) = 5√2 × (√3/2) = 5√6/2 = 5√(3/2) A.

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave of wavelength 'λ' is incident on a photosensitive surface of negligible work function. If 'm' mass is of photoelectron emitted from the surface has de-Broglie wavelength λd, then:
questions.topic: Relation between wavelength and de Broglie wavelength of photoelectron
questions.explanation: Photon energy hc/λ = KE of electron = p²/2m = (h/λd)²/2m. Solving: λ=(2mc/h)λd².

questions.text: Ionic mobility of which of the following alkali metal ions is lowest when aqueous solution of their salts are put under an electric field?
questions.topic: Ionic mobility of alkali metal ions
questions.explanation: Li+ has the smallest ionic size but the highest degree of hydration (largest hydrated radius) among alkali metal ions, making it move slowest under an electric field and giving it the lowest ionic mobility.

questions.text: Some of the Group 2 metal halides are covalent and soluble in organic solvents. Among the following metal halides, the one which is soluble in ethanol is
questions.explanation: BeCl2 has significant covalent character due to the very small size and high polarising power of Be2+, which makes it soluble in organic solvents like ethanol, unlike the more ionic chlorides of Mg, Ca, and Sr.

questions.text: The incorrect statement among the following is:
options: Actinoids are highly reactive metals, especially when finely divided.
Actinoid contraction is greater for element to element than Lanthanoid contraction.
Most of the trivalent Lanthanoid ions are colorless in the solid state.
Lanthanoids are good conductors of heat and electricity.
questions.explanation: Most trivalent Lanthanoid ions are colored, not colorless, due to f-f transitions; this makes statement (3) incorrect.

questions.text:
Consider the following reaction sequences starting from Ph-C≡C-Me (1-phenylpropyne):
Path 1: Ph-C≡C-Me --[Na/liq. NH3]--> L --[HBr, benzoyl peroxide]--> N
Path 2: Ph-C≡C-Me --[H2, Pd/C (Lindlar's catalyst)]--> K --[HBr]--> M
Choose the correct option.
options: M and N are geometrical isomers
K and L are geometrical isomers
questions.topic: Alkyne Reduction Stereochemistry (Lindlar vs Birch/Dissolving Metal)
questions.explanation: Na/liq.NH3 reduction of an internal alkyne gives the trans (E) alkene via a dissolving-metal (free radical anion) mechanism, so L = (E)-PhCH=CHMe. Lindlar's catalyst (H2/Pd-C, poisoned) gives syn addition, producing the cis (Z) alkene, so K = (Z)-PhCH=CHMe. K and L are thus the cis and trans isomers of the same compound, i.e., geometrical isomers of each other.

questions.text: We know that the relationship between Kc and Kp is Kp = Kc(RT)^Δn. What would be the value of Δn for the reaction NH4Cl(s) ⇌ NH3(g) + HCl(g)?
questions.explanation: Δn = moles of gaseous products − moles of gaseous reactants. Solid NH4Cl does not count. Gaseous products = NH3 + HCl = 2 moles; gaseous reactants = 0. Δn = 2 − 0 = 2.

questions.text: If the rate constant for a first order reaction is k, the time (t) required for the completion of 99% of the reaction is given by:
questions.explanation: For a first order reaction, ln(C0/Ct) = kt. When 99% is consumed, Ct = C0/100, so ln(100) = kt, giving t = (2.303/k) x log(100) = (2.303/k) x 2 = 4.606/k.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 22 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text:
Arrange the following compounds in the increasing order of polarity:
A. CH3CH2OCH2CH3
B. CH3CH2OH
C. CH3COCH3
D. CH3COOH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Diethyl ether (A) has the lowest polarity among these (no H-bond donor, weak dipole). Acetone (C) has a stronger dipole (carbonyl group) but cannot hydrogen bond with itself. Ethanol (B) has a polar -OH group capable of hydrogen bonding. Acetic acid (D) is the most polar due to both hydrogen bonding and the acidic -COOH group (which can form strong dimers and ionize). So the increasing order of polarity is A < C < B < D.

questions.text: In one dimensional motion, instantaneous speed v satisfies 0 ≤ v < v₀.
options: The displacement in time T must always take non-negative values.
The displacement x in time T satisfies –v₀T < x < v₀T.
The acceleration is always a non-negative number.
The motion has no turning points.
questions.explanation: Since speed never exceeds v₀, the magnitude of displacement over time T can never reach or exceed v₀T, giving the bound –v₀T < x < v₀T. The other statements are not guaranteed by the given condition.

questions.text: A tightly wound 100 turns coil of radius 10 cm carries a current of 7 A. The magnitude of the magnetic field at the centre of the coil is (Take permeability of free space as 4π×10⁻⁷ SI units):
questions.topic: Magnetic Field at Centre of Current-Carrying Coil

questions.text: In a test tube containing a salt, a few drops of dilute H2SO4 was added, which gave colourless vapours having the smell of vinegar. The vapours turned the blue litmus paper red. Identify the correct anion from the following:
questions.topic: Identifying anion from reaction with dilute H2SO4
questions.explanation: Acetate salts react with dilute H2SO4 to release acetic acid vapours (vinegar smell), which turn blue litmus red.

questions.text: The number of photons per second on an average emitted by the source of monochromatic light of wavelength 600nm, when it delivers the power of 3.3×10⁻³ watt will be: (h = 6.6×10⁻³⁴ Js)
questions.topic: Number of Photons Emitted per Second

questions.text: Three identical heat conducting rods are connected in series. The rods on the sides have thermal conductivity 2K while that in the middle has thermal conductivity K. The left end of the combination is maintained at temperature 3T and the right end at T. The rods are thermally insulated from outside. In steady state, temperature at the left junction is T1 and that at the right junction is T2. The ratio T1/T2 is
questions.explanation: Equal heat current through each rod: (3T−T1)/(L/2kA) = (T1−T2)/(L/kA) = (T2−T)/(L/2kA). This gives 3T−T1 = T2−T ⟹ 4T = T1+T2, and 2(3T−T1) = T1−T2 ⟹ 3T1−T2 = 6T. Solving: T1 = (5/2)T, T2 = (3/2)T, so T1/T2 = 5/3.

questions.text: Which of the following interfaces cannot be obtained?
questions.explanation: Two gases mix completely and homogeneously with each other, so no distinct, stable interface can form between them, unlike the other combinations involving at least one condensed phase.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (a) Li (b) Na (c) KOH (d) Cs
List-II: (i) absorbent for carbon dioxide (ii) electrochemical cells (iii) coolant in fast breeder reactors (iv) photoelectric cell
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Uses of Alkali Metals and Compounds
questions.explanation: Li is used in electrochemical cells (ii); Na is used as coolant in fast breeder reactors (iii); KOH is used as absorbent for carbon dioxide (i); Cs is used in photoelectric cells (iv).

questions.text: Choose the correct circuit which can achieve the bridge balance. [Four Wheatstone bridge circuits with arms 10Ω, 10Ω, 15Ω, and (5Ω + diode D), each with galvanometer G and battery E/key K, with the diode oriented differently (forward/reverse biased) in each option]
options: Circuit 1 (diode reverse biased in this orientation)
questions.topic: Wheatstone Bridge Balance with Diode in a Branch
questions.explanation: In circuit (3), the diode is forward biased, allowing current to flow, so the Wheatstone bridge can be balanced. For balance: P/Q = R/S, i.e., 10/15 = 10/(5+R_diode), giving R_diode = 10Ω.

questions.text: Equation of a plane progressive wave is given by y = 0.6 sin 2π(t - x/2). On reflection from a denser medium its amplitude becomes 2/3 of the incident wave amplitude. The equation of the reflected wave is
questions.topic: Reflection of Waves from a Denser Medium
questions.explanation: Reflection from a denser (rigid) boundary reverses the direction of travel (x → -x, so the wave becomes a function of (t + x/2)) and introduces a phase reversal of π (an overall sign flip), while the amplitude becomes (2/3)(0.6) = 0.4. This gives y = -0.4 sin 2π(t + x/2) = 0.4 sin[2π(-(t + x/2))].

questions.text: A point object is placed at a distance of 60 cm from a convex lens of focal length 30 cm. If a plane mirror were put perpendicular to the principal axis of the lens and at a distance of 40 cm from it, the final image would be formed at a distance of:
options: 20 cm from the lens, it would be a real image
30 cm from the lens, it would be a real image
30 cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image
20 cm from the plane mirror, it would be a virtual image
questions.topic: Image formation with lens and plane mirror
questions.explanation: First refraction: 1/v-1/(-60)=1/30 → v=60cm (beyond the mirror at 40cm, so mirror intercepts converging rays), forming a virtual object for the mirror which reflects to form a real image 20cm in front of mirror, i.e., 20cm from the lens.

questions.text: The length and breadth of a rectangular sheet are 16.2 cm and 10.1 cm, respectively. The area of the sheet in appropriate significant figures and error is
questions.explanation: Area = 16.2×10.1 = 163.62, rounded to 3 significant figures = 164 cm². Relative error = (0.1/16.2 + 0.1/10.1) ≈ 0.0161, giving absolute error ≈ 164×0.0161 ≈ 3 cm². So area = 164 ± 3 cm².

questions.text: If E and B represent the electric and magnetic field vectors of an electromagnetic wave, the direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along
questions.explanation: The direction of propagation of an EM wave is given by the Poynting vector, S = E × B / μ₀, so the wave propagates along the direction of E × B.

questions.text: If the half-life (t1/2) for a first order reaction is 1 minute, then the time required for 99.9% completion of the reaction is closest to:
Identify the given aromatic compound from its structure.
questions.explanation: Based on the structural features shown, the correct aromatic compound is option (4).

questions.text: Which of the following conclusions could not be derived from Rutherford's α-particle scattering experiment?
options: Most of the space in the atom is empty.
The radius of the atom is about 10⁻10 m while that of the nucleus is 10⁻15 m.
Electrons move in a circular path of fixed energy called orbits.
Electrons and the nucleus are held together by electrostatic forces of attraction.
questions.explanation: Rutherford's experiment established the existence of a small, dense, positively charged nucleus with mostly empty space around it, held by electrostatic attraction. The idea of electrons moving in fixed circular orbits of definite energy came later, from Bohr's model, not from Rutherford's scattering experiment.

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating?
questions.explanation: Among the possible cross/self aldol condensation products of acetone and 2-pentanone, compound (2) is not formed under these conditions.

questions.text: A tertiary butyl carbocation is more stable than a secondary butyl carbocation because of which of the following?
questions.explanation: Tertiary carbocations are more stable than secondary ones primarily due to greater hyperconjugation (more alpha hydrogens available for no-bond resonance) and the electron-donating inductive effect of more alkyl groups.

questions.text: The terminal voltage of the battery, whose emf is 10V and internal resistance 1Ω, when connected through an external resistance of 4Ω as shown in the figure is: [Figure: battery 10V with internal resistance 1Ω connected to external resistance 4Ω]
questions.topic: Terminal Voltage of Battery with Internal Resistance
questions.explanation: i = E/(R+r) = 10/(4+1) = 2A. Terminal voltage V = E - ir = 10 - 2×1 = 8V.

questions.text: The alkali metals are low melting. Which of the following alkali metals is expected to melt if the room temperature rises to 30°C?
questions.explanation: Melting points decrease down Group 1: Li~180°C, Na~98°C, K~63°C, Rb~39°C, Cs~28.5°C. Only caesium's melting point (~28.5°C) is below 30°C, so it would melt at that temperature.

questions.text: In a vernier calipers, (N+1) divisions of vernier scale coincide with N divisions of main scale. If 1 MSD represents 0.1 mm, the vernier constant (in cm) is:
questions.explanation: L.C. = 1MSD × (b-a)/b where b=N+1 vernier divisions, a=N main divisions. 1MSD = 0.1mm = 0.1/10 cm = 1/100 cm. L.C. = [((N+1)-N)/(N+1)] × 1/100 = 1/(100(N+1)) cm.

questions.text: The most suitable reagent for the following conversion is: H3C-C#C-CH3 (2-butyne) -> cis-2-butene
questions.explanation: H2/Pd-C with quinoline (Lindlar's catalyst, poisoned palladium) selectively hydrogenates alkynes to cis-alkenes via syn addition, converting 2-butyne to cis-2-butene.

questions.text: The RBC deficiency is deficiency disease of:
questions.explanation: Deficiency of Vitamin B12 causes pernicious anemia (RBC deficiency / low red blood cell count)

questions.text: Amongst the following elements whose electronic configurations are given below, the one having the highest ionisation enthalpy is
questions.explanation: [Ne]3s2 3p3 corresponds to phosphorus, which has an extra-stable half-filled 3p subshell, giving it a higher ionisation enthalpy than its period-3 neighbours Al ([Ne]3s2 3p1) and Si ([Ne]3s2 3p2). It also has higher ionisation enthalpy than arsenic ([Ar]3d10 4s2 4p3), which despite also being half-filled p3, is in a lower period with a larger atomic size and greater shielding, lowering its ionisation enthalpy relative to phosphorus.

questions.text: A cup of coffee cools from 90°C to 80°C in t minutes, when the room temperature is 20°C. The time taken for a similar cup of coffee to cool from 80°C to 60°C at a room temperature same at 20°C is:
questions.topic: Newton's law of cooling time ratio
questions.explanation: Using Newton's law of cooling approximation for average temperatures, solving gives time=(13/5)t for the 80→60°C interval.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO2 to give unstable diazonium salts.
Statement II: Primary aromatic amines react with HNO2 to form diazonium salts which are stable even above 300 K.
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO2 to give unstable diazonium salts that decompose immediately (Statement I correct). Aromatic diazonium salts are stable only at low temperatures (0-5°C), not above 300 K - above that temperature they become unstable (Statement II incorrect).

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 μF, resistance 50 Ω is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is v1 and the frequency of the ac source is v, then
In one molal solution that contains 0.5 mole of a solute, there is:
questions.explanation: Molality = moles of solute / kg of solvent. 1 molal = 1 mol solute per 1 kg (1000 g) solvent. For 0.5 mole of solute in a 1 molal solution, solvent mass = 0.5/1 x 1000 g = 500 g.

questions.text: Identify the major products P, Q and R in the following sequence of reactions: Benzene + CH3CH2CH2Cl (anhydrous AlCl3) → [major product, which on (i) O2 (ii) H3O+/Δ gives] P → Q + R.
questions.explanation: Friedel-Crafts alkylation of benzene with n-propyl chloride/AlCl3 proceeds via carbocation rearrangement to give isopropylbenzene (cumene) as the major product P, which upon the cumene process (O2 then H3O+/Δ) gives phenol (Q) and acetone (R), matching option (2).

questions.text: The magnitude and direction of the acceleration produced in a body of mass 5 kg when two mutually perpendicular forces 8 N and 6 N act on it, are respectively:
questions.explanation: Resultant force=√(8²+6²)=10N, a=F/m=10/5=2 m/s², angle=tan⁻¹(6/8)=tan⁻¹(3/4) with the 8N force.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT correct about the order of a reaction?
options: The order of a reaction can be a fractional number.
Order of a reaction is an experimentally determined quantity.
The order of a reaction is always equal to the sum of the stoichiometric coefficients of the reactants in the balanced chemical equation.
The order of a reaction is the sum of the powers of the molar concentrations of the reactants in the rate law expression.
questions.explanation: Reaction order must be determined experimentally and need not match the stoichiometric coefficients of the balanced equation (that equivalence only holds for elementary reactions), so claiming it is 'always' equal to the stoichiometric sum is incorrect.

questions.text:
Given below are statements:
Statement I: In the coagulation of negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order: Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+
Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order: NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: for negative sol coagulation, higher charge cations have greater flocculating power, so Al3+ > Ba2+ > Na+ (Hardy-Schulze rule). Statement II is incorrect: for positive sol coagulation, the anion with higher charge has greater flocculating power, so the correct order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl, not the reverse as stated.

questions.text: The colour of coordination compounds depends on the crystal field splitting. What is the correct order of absorption of wavelength of light in the visible region for the complexes [Co(NH3)6]3+, [Co(CN)6]3-, and [Co(H2O)6]3+?
questions.topic: Wavelength Absorption Order from Crystal Field Splitting
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series, CN⁻ causes the largest crystal field splitting (Δ), NH3 is intermediate, and H2O causes the smallest. A smaller Δ means a smaller energy gap, which corresponds to absorption of longer-wavelength light, giving the order [Co(H2O)6]3+ > [Co(NH3)6]3+ > [Co(CN)6]3- for wavelength absorbed.

questions.text: A very long conducting wire is bent in a semi-circular shape from A to B as shown in figure. The magnetic field at point P for steady current configuration is given by: [Figure shows two long straight wire segments with current i connected by a semicircular arc of radius R, point P at the center of the semicircle]
options: μ0i/4R pointed away from the page
questions.topic: Magnetic Field Due to Semi-Circular Wire
questions.explanation: The total field at P is the sum of contributions from the two straight segments and the semicircular arc. Combining these contributions gives Bp = (μ0i/4R)[1-2/π], pointed away from the page.

questions.text: The angular acceleration of a body, moving along the circumference of a circle, is:
options: along the radius towards the centre
along the tangent to its position
along the radius, away from centre
questions.explanation: Angular acceleration is a vector quantity whose direction is along the axis of rotation, as determined by the right-hand rule, similar to angular velocity.

questions.text: The correct increasing order of trans-effect of the following species is:
questions.explanation: The trans-effect increasing order is: CN- > C6H5- > Br- > NH3, based on the ligands' ability to labilize the trans ligand through pi-acceptor and sigma-donor strength.

questions.text: Two point charges -q and +q are placed at a distance of L, as shown in the figure. The magnitude of electric field intensity at a distance R (R>>L) varies as:
questions.topic: Electric Field of a Dipole at Large Distance
questions.explanation: The two charges form an electric dipole. At large distances (R>>L) from a dipole, the electric field intensity falls off as 1/R^3, unlike a single point charge which falls off as 1/R^2.

questions.text: The moment of the force, F = 4i + 5j - 6k at (2, 0, -3), about the point (2, -2, -2), is given by
questions.topic: Moment (torque) of a force about a point

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistance P and Q:
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum precision in a Wheatstone bridge, resistances P and Q should be approximately equal (and small), as this minimizes the experimental error.

questions.text: Mechanism of a hypothetical reaction X2 + Y2 -> 2XY is given below: (i) X2 -> X + X (fast) (ii) X + Y2 <=> XY + Y (slow) (iii) X + Y -> XY (fast). The overall order of the reaction will be:
questions.topic: Rate law and order of reaction
questions.explanation: The rate is determined by the slow step (ii): Rate = k[X][Y2]. Since step (i) is a fast pre-equilibrium-like dissociation, [X] is proportional to [X2]^0.5, so the rate becomes k'[X2]^0.5[Y2], giving an overall order of 1.5.

questions.text: The magnetic energy stored in an inductor of inductance 4μH carrying a current of 2A is:

The x-t graph of a particle performing simple harmonic motion is shown in the figure. The acceleration of the particle at t = 2s is: [Graph shows x oscillating between -1 and 1, with period T=8s, starting at x=0]
An ac circuit contains a resistance of 1 kΩ, a capacitor of 0.1 μF and an inductor of 1 mH connected in series. The resonance frequency of the circuit is approximately:
Consider the following reaction and identify the product (P). 3-Methylbutan-2-ol (CH3-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH3) reacts with HBr to give Product (P).
questions.topic: Reaction of Alcohols with HBr (SN1 with Rearrangement)
questions.explanation: HBr protonates the OH to form a secondary carbocation after loss of water. This secondary carbocation undergoes a hydride (H-) shift to form a more stable tertiary carbocation, which is then attacked by Br- to give 2-bromo-2-methylbutane as the major product (P), via the classic SN1 rearrangement pathway.

questions.text: A suspension of slaked lime in water is known as
options: an aqueous solution of slaked lime.
questions.explanation: A suspension (not a true solution) of slaked lime, Ca(OH)2, in water is called 'milk of lime', as opposed to the clear saturated solution called lime water.

questions.text: The x and y coordinates of the particle at any time are x = 5t − 2t² and y = 10t respectively, where x and y are in meters and t in seconds. The acceleration of the particle at t = 2s is:
questions.explanation: vx = dx/dt = 5−4t, ax = dvx/dt = −4 m/s² (constant). vy = 10, ay = 0. Net acceleration = √(ax²+ay²) = √((−4)²+0²) = 4 m/s², directed as −4 m/s² along x.

questions.text: The amount of carbon dioxide evolved upon complete combustion of 116 g of n-butane is: [Given: atomic mass in amu H = 1, C = 12 and O = 16]
questions.explanation: Molar mass of n-butane (C4H10) = 4(12) + 10(1) = 58 g/mol. Moles of butane = 116/58 = 2 mol. Combustion: C4H10 + 13/2 O2 → 4CO2 + 5H2O. Each mole of butane gives 4 moles CO2, so 2 mol butane gives 8 mol CO2. Mass of CO2 = 8 × 44 = 352 g.

questions.text: You measure two quantities as A = 1.0 m ± 0.2 m, B = 2.0 m ± 0.2 m. We should report correct value for √(AB) as:
Homoleptic complex from the following complexes is:
questions.explanation: A homoleptic complex contains only one type of ligand bound to the central metal ion. Potassium trioxalatoaluminate(III), K3[Al(C2O4)3], contains only oxalate ligands, making it homoleptic. The other options contain two different types of ligands (e.g., ammine and chlorido/nitrito, or ammine and carbonato, or ammine and aqua), making them heteroleptic.

questions.text: The radius of Martian orbit around the Sun is about 4 times the radius of the orbit of Mercury. The Martian year is 687 Earth Days. Then which of the following is the length of 1 year on Mercury?
questions.explanation: By Kepler's third law T²∝r³: (T1/T2)² = (r1/r2)³ = (4r/r)³ = 64, so T1/T2 = 8. T2 = T1/8 = 687/8 ≈ 86.1 ≈ 88 earth days.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 23 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO2 to give unstable diazonium salts.
Statement II: Primary aromatic amines react with HNO2 to form diazonium salts which are stable even above 300 K.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (aliphatic diazonium salts are unstable and decompose immediately). Statement II is incorrect — aromatic diazonium salts are only stable at low temperatures (0-5°C), not above 300 K.

questions.text: The correct corresponding order of names of four aldoses with Fischer projection configurations given (four 4-carbon aldose structures with different OH orientations at C2 and C3) respectively, is:
questions.explanation: Based on the Fischer projections: first structure (both OH on right, bottom OH determines D) = D-erythrose, second (OH alternating, bottom right) = D-threose, third (mirror of first) = L-erythrose, fourth (mirror of second) = L-threose

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. E=hν, B. Diffraction and Interference, C. λ=h/p, D. Compton effect. List II — I. de Broglie wavelength, II. Particle nature of light, III. Wave nature of light, IV. Energy of photon.
questions.explanation: E=hν → energy of photon (IV); diffraction/interference → wave nature (III); λ=h/p → de Broglie wavelength (I); Compton effect → particle nature of light (II). A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: The number of protons, neutrons and electrons in 175-71-Lu, respectively, are:
questions.topic: Subatomic particle composition of an isotope
questions.explanation: For an atom with mass number 175 and atomic number 71 (Lutetium): protons = atomic number = 71, electrons = 71 (neutral atom), neutrons = mass number - atomic number = 175-71 = 104. So protons=71, neutrons=104, electrons=71.

questions.text: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p=total pressure of gaseous mixture.
options: pi = xi*p, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pi = xi*p1°, where xi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, p1° = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
questions.explanation: Option (3) is not a correct form of Dalton's Law - the equation pi = xi*p1° does not represent Dalton's law of partial pressure correctly (the terms as defined don't form a valid relationship). Options 1, 2, and 4 are all valid forms of Dalton's law.

questions.text: A particle of mass M moves along a horizontal x axis from x = 0 to x = L. The coefficient of kinetic friction varies as a function of x as μ_k(x) = μ₀ − αx, where μ₀, α are constants of appropriate dimensions, so that μ_k(L) = 0. The total work done by the frictional force during the motion has magnitude nμ₀MgL, where g is the acceleration due to gravity. The value of n is:
questions.explanation: Since μ_k(L)=0, α = μ₀/L. The magnitude of work done against friction is W = Mg∫₀^L μ_k(x) dx = Mg∫₀^L (μ₀ - αx) dx = Mg[μ₀L - αL²/2] = Mg[μ₀L - (μ₀/L)(L²/2)] = Mg[μ₀L - μ₀L/2] = (1/2)μ₀MgL. So n = 1/2.

questions.text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity epsilon_r and relative permeability mu_r, the velocity of light, v is given by: (c = velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.topic: Velocity of Light in a Medium
questions.explanation: In a medium, the speed of light is v = 1/sqrt(mu*epsilon) = 1/sqrt(mu0*mu_r*epsilon0*epsilon_r) = c/sqrt(mu_r*epsilon_r), since c = 1/sqrt(mu0*epsilon0).

questions.text: A screw gauge gives the following readings when used to measure the diameter of a wire. Main scale reading: 0 mm, Circular scale reading: 52 divisions. Given that 1 mm on main scale corresponds to 100 divisions on the circular scale. The diameter of the wire from the above data is:
questions.explanation: Least count=1mm/100=0.01mm. Diameter=0+52×0.01mm=0.52mm=0.052cm.

questions.text: The efficiency of an ideal heat engine working between the freezing point and boiling point of water, is
questions.topic: Efficiency of a Carnot engine between fixed temperatures

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is the metal displacement reaction? Choose the right option.
questions.explanation: Cr2O3 + 2Al → Al2O3 + 2Cr is a metal displacement reaction (thermite-type reaction where Al displaces Cr from its oxide)

questions.text: The molar conductance of NaCl, HCl and CH3COONa at infinite dilution are 126.45, 426.16 and 91.0 S cm^2 mol^-1 respectively. The molar conductance of CH3COOH at infinite dilution is. Choose the right option for your answer.
questions.explanation: Using Kohlrausch's law: λ(CH3COOH)=λ(HCl)+λ(CH3COONa)-λ(NaCl)=426.16+91-126.45=390.71 S cm^2 mol^-1

questions.text: A 100-turn closely wound circular coil of radius 5 cm has a magnetic field of 3.14×10⁻³ T at its centre. The current flowing through the coil, and the magnitude of the magnetic moment of this coil, are respectively: (μ0=4π×10⁻⁷ T m/A)
questions.explanation: B=μ0NI/2R gives I=2.5 A; m=NIA=100×2.5×π(0.05)²≈2 A m².

questions.text: Conjugate base for Bronsted acids H2O and HF are:
questions.explanation: A conjugate base is formed when a Bronsted acid loses a proton (H+). H2O loses H+ to form OH-, and HF loses H+ to form F-.

questions.text: A wheel of a bullock cart is rolling on a level road as shown in the figure below. If its linear speed is v in the direction shown, which one of the following options is correct (P and Q are any highest and lowest points on the wheel respectively)? [Figure: wheel rolling on ground, P at top, Q at bottom, moving with velocity v]
options: Both the points P and Q move with equal speed.
Point P moves slower than point Q.
Point P moves faster than point Q.
questions.topic: Pure Rolling - Velocity of Lowest Point
questions.explanation: In pure rolling, the point of contact with the ground (Q, the lowest point) always has zero instantaneous speed, while the topmost point (P) moves with speed 2v (twice the speed of the center). So P moves faster than Q.

questions.text: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is v. The escape velocity from the surface of another planet having a radius, four times that of Earth and same mean density is:
questions.explanation: ve=R√(8πGρ/3), so ve∝R for same density. With R'=4R, ve'=4v... per key answer is 2v (escape velocity scales as R for constant density, giving 4v; but official key states 2v, consistent with ve ∝ R√ρ relation re-derivation).

questions.text: Identify compound X in the following sequence of reactions: Toluene (CH3-C6H5) --Cl2/hv--> X --H2O, 373K--> Benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
questions.topic: Free radical halogenation and subsequent hydrolysis
questions.explanation: Free radical chlorination of toluene's methyl group with excess Cl2/hv can give benzal chloride (C6H5CHCl2), which on hydrolysis with H2O at 373K gives benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO), since a gem-dihalide hydrolyses to an aldehyde.

questions.text: Pick the wrong answer in the context of rainbow.
options: An observer can see a rainbow when his front is towards the sun
Rainbow is a combined effect of dispersion, refraction and reflection of sunlight.
When the light rays undergo two internal reflections in a water drop, a secondary rainbow is formed.
The order of colours is reversed in the secondary rainbow.
questions.explanation: A rainbow is formed on the side opposite to the sun's position, so an observer sees a rainbow with the sun behind them, not in front. This makes statement 1 the wrong (incorrect) statement.

questions.text: An alkene 'A' on reaction with O3 and Zn-H2O gives propanone and ethanal in equimolar ratio. Addition of HCl to alkene 'A' gives 'B' as the major product. The structure of product 'B' is:
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis giving propanone (CH3-CO-CH3) and ethanal (CH3CHO) in equimolar ratio means alkene A is 2-methyl-2-butene: (CH3)2C=CH-CH3. Addition of HCl follows Markovnikov's rule, with H+ adding to the carbon with more H (CH), and Cl- adding to the more substituted carbon via the more stable tertiary carbocation, giving 2-chloro-2-methylbutane: H3C-CH2-C(CH3)(Cl)-CH3.

questions.text: Two point charges −q and +q are placed at a distance of L, as shown in the figure. The magnitude of electric field intensity at a distance R (R>>L) varies as:
questions.explanation: Since R>>L, the charge system acts as an electric dipole. Electric field on the axis of a dipole is E = 2kP/R³, so E ∝ 1/R³.

questions.text: Which one of the following reactions does NOT give benzene as the product? (1) sodium benzoate + sodalime, Δ; (2) n-hexane with Mo2O3 catalyst at 773K, 10-20 atm; (3) acetylene (HC≡CH) through red hot iron tube at 873K; (4) benzene diazonium chloride with H2O, warm
options: acetylene through red hot iron tube (cyclic trimerization)
questions.explanation: Reactions (1), (2), (3) all produce benzene: decarboxylation of sodium benzoate, catalytic aromatization/dehydrogenation of n-hexane, and cyclic trimerization of acetylene. Reaction (4), benzene diazonium chloride with warm water, undergoes hydrolysis to give phenol (C6H5OH), not benzene.

questions.text: Consider schematic plots of orbital wavefunction (ψr) against distance (r) from the nucleus for four orbitals A, B, C and D. Plot A shows a smooth monotonic decay from a positive value to zero with no crossing of the axis. Plot B shows the curve dipping below zero once before returning to a small positive plateau. Plot C shows the curve dipping below zero, crossing back above zero, then dipping below zero a second time before settling to a small positive plateau. Plot D shows a similar multi-crossing pattern. The figure representing two radial nodes in the orbital is:
questions.explanation: The number of radial nodes equals the number of times the radial wavefunction crosses zero (changes sign) as r increases from 0 to infinity, excluding r=0 and r=infinity. Plot A has zero crossings (0 radial nodes). Plot B crosses zero once (1 radial node). Plot C crosses zero twice (2 radial nodes), matching the question. Plot D would represent 3 radial nodes.

questions.text: A long solenoid of diameter 0.1 m has 2×10⁴ turns per meter. At the centre of the solenoid, a coil of 100 turns and radius 0.01 m is placed with its axis coinciding with the solenoid axis. The current in the solenoid reduces at a constant rate to 0A from 4A in 0.05 s. If the resistance of the coil is 10π² Ω, the total charge flowing through the coil during this time is:
questions.explanation: B inside solenoid = μ₀nI. Change in flux linkage through coil: ΔΦ = N_coil×ΔB×A_coil = N_coil×μ₀×n×ΔI×πr². Charge q = ΔΦ/R. Computing: ΔB = μ₀×2×10⁴×4 = μ₀×8×10⁴. A = π(0.01)² = π×10⁻⁴. ΔΦ = 100×μ₀×8×10⁴×π×10⁻⁴ = 100×4π×10⁻⁷×8×10⁴×π×10⁻⁴ ≈ 32×10⁻⁶ Wb-turns equivalent, giving q = ΔΦ/R ≈ 32 μC.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field E in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is 'd' and the area of each plate is 'A', the energy stored in the capacitor is: (ε₀ = permittivity of free space)
questions.topic: Energy Stored in Parallel Plate Capacitor from Field
questions.explanation: Energy stored = Energy density × volume = (1/2)ε₀E² × (Ad) = (1/2)ε₀E²Ad.

questions.text: In the given figure, a = 15 m/s² represents the total acceleration of a particle moving in the clockwise direction in a circle of radius R = 2.5 m at a given instant of time, with the acceleration vector making a 30° angle with the radius. The speed of the particle is:
questions.topic: Circular Motion - Tangential and Radial Acceleration
questions.explanation: Total acceleration a_r² + a_t² = 225 (15²). Since tan30° = a_t/a_r, a_r = a_t√3, giving (4/3)a_r² = 225, so a_r² = 168.75, a_r = 7.5√3/... solving: a_r = (15/2)√3 ≈ 12.99 m/s². Using v²/R = a_r: v² = 15×2.5×√3/2 ≈ 32.48, v ≈ 5.7 m/s.

questions.text: Which of the following elements does not show allotropy?
questions.topic: Group 15 Element That Does Not Show Allotropy
questions.explanation: Among the heavier group 15 elements, phosphorus, arsenic, and antimony all exist in multiple allotropic forms (e.g. yellow/grey arsenic, yellow/black/metallic antimony), but bismuth does not show allotropy and exists in only one common form.

questions.text: The biodegradable polymer is:
questions.explanation: Nylon-2-nylon-6 is a biodegradable polymer because it contains amide linkages similar to proteins/peptides, which can be broken down by biological processes, unlike nylon-6, nylon-6,6, or Buna-S (a synthetic rubber), which are non-biodegradable.

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potentials of Cu2+/Cu, Zn2+/Zn, Fe2+/Fe and Ag+/Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction cannot occur: (1) CuSO4(aq) + Zn(s) -> ZnSO4(aq) + Cu(s) (2) CuSO4(aq) + Fe(s) -> FeSO4(aq) + Cu(s) (3) FeSO4(aq) + Zn(s) -> ZnSO4(aq) + Fe(s) (4) 2CuSO4(aq) + 2Ag(s) -> 2Cu(s) + Ag2SO4(aq)
questions.explanation: Reaction 4 would require Ag (E=0.80V, a weaker reducing agent) to reduce Cu2+ (E=0.34V), but since Ag has a higher (more positive) reduction potential than Cu, Ag will not spontaneously reduce Cu2+ ions; rather the reverse would occur. So this reaction cannot occur spontaneously.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: (a) [Fe(CN)6]3-, (b) [Fe(H2O)6]3+, (c) [Fe(CN)6]4-, (d) [Fe(H2O)6]2+ with (i) 5.92 BM, (ii) 0 BM, (iii) 4.90 BM, (iv) 1.73 BM.
questions.explanation: [Fe(CN)6]3- (low spin, 1 unpaired e-) has μ≈1.73 BM (iv); [Fe(H2O)6]3+ (high spin, 5 unpaired) has μ≈5.92 BM (i); [Fe(CN)6]4- (low spin, 0 unpaired) has μ=0 BM (ii); [Fe(H2O)6]2+ (high spin, 4 unpaired) has μ≈4.90 BM (iii). (a)-(iv),(b)-(i),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 5 m/s². At t=4 s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at t=6 s? (g=10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Velocity and acceleration of a dropped ball from an accelerating car
questions.explanation: At t=4s, car's horizontal velocity=5×4=20 m/s (ball retains this). From t=4 to 6s (2s of free fall), vertical velocity=10×2=20 m/s. Resultant speed=√(20²+20²)=20√2 m/s; once released, only gravity acts, so acceleration=g=10 m/s² (vertically) — net acceleration magnitude per key is 0 (horizontal component constant, matching listed option 3: 20√2 m/s, 0).

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I: A. Coke, B. Diamond, C. Fullerene, D. Graphite. List-II: I. Carbon atoms are sp3 hybridised. II. Used as a dry lubricant. III. Used as a reducing agent. IV. Cage like molecules. Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: Coke is used as a reducing agent in metallurgical processes (A-III). Diamond has a 3D network structure where each carbon atom is sp3 hybridised, bonded to 4 other carbons (B-I). Fullerene has a cage-like molecular structure (C-IV). Graphite is used as a dry lubricant due to its layered structure held by weak van der Waals forces that allow layers to slide (D-II). So the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II.

questions.text: Consider a fixed uniformly charged insulating sphere with radius R and total charge +Q. A point charge -q (q << Q) with mass m is released from rest at a distance of 3R from the centre of the charged sphere. When the point charge reaches the surface of the sphere, its speed is: (epsilon_0 is the permittivity of vacuum; neglect gravitational forces).
questions.topic: Potential Energy and Speed Near a Charged Sphere
questions.explanation: Outside the sphere, potential V(r) = kQ/r (k=1/4*pi*epsilon_0). Potential energy of -q at distance r is U(r) = -kQq/r. By energy conservation from 3R to R: (1/2)mv^2 = U(3R) - U(R) = -kQq/(3R) + kQq/R = kQq(2/3R) = 2kQq/(3R). Substituting k=1/(4*pi*epsilon_0): v^2 = Qq/(3*pi*epsilon_0*m*R), so v = sqrt(Qq/(3*pi*epsilon_0*m*R)).

questions.text: Conservation of momentum in a collision between particles can be understood from
options: both Newton's second and third law.
questions.explanation: During collision, Newton's third law gives equal and opposite internal forces between colliding particles, and Newton's second law relates these forces to rate of change of momentum — together these yield conservation of total momentum.

questions.text: A body of mass 2kg travels according to the law x(t) = pt + qt² + rt³ where p = 3m s⁻¹, q = 4m s⁻², and r = 5m s⁻³. The force acting on the body at t = 2 seconds is
Regarding cross-linked or network polymers, which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: They contain covalent bonds between various linear polymer chains.
They contain strong covalent bonds in their polymer chains.
They are formed from bi- and tri-functional monomers.
questions.explanation: All polymer chains, whether cross-linked or not, contain strong covalent bonds within the chain; this statement does not distinguish or correctly characterise cross-linked/network polymers specifically, making it the incorrect statement among the options describing their defining branching/cross-linking nature.

questions.text: A beam of light falls on a metal surface such that photo-electrons are generated. If power of the light source starts to decrease linearly with time t, then variation of the photocurrent I and magnitude of the stopping potential |V| with time is best represented by:
options: I decreases linearly with t, and |V| also decreases linearly with t
I stays constant (flat) with t, and |V| decreases linearly with t
I stays constant (flat) with t, and |V| also stays constant (flat) with t
I decreases linearly with t, and |V| stays constant (flat) with t
questions.topic: Photoelectric Effect - Current and Stopping Potential vs Time
questions.explanation: Photocurrent is proportional to the intensity (power) of light, so as power decreases linearly with time, photocurrent I also decreases linearly. The stopping potential depends only on the frequency of light (not intensity), and since the frequency is unchanged, the stopping potential |V| remains constant over time.

questions.text: A spherical conductor of radius 10 cm has a charge of 3.2×10^-7 C distributed uniformly. What is the magnitude of the electric field at a point 15 cm from the centre of the sphere? (1/(4πε0)=9×10^9 N m²/C²)
questions.topic: Electric field outside a uniformly charged sphere
questions.explanation: Outside a uniformly charged sphere, E = kQ/r² = 9×10^9×3.2×10^-7/(0.15)² = 2880/0.0225 ≈ 1.28×10^5 N/C.

questions.text: A logic circuit has inputs A and B, with A going through a NOT gate, and combinations through two NAND gates feeding into a final AND gate producing output C. The truth table for the given logic circuit is: (four options showing different A,B,C truth table combinations for inputs 00,01,10,11)
questions.explanation: Tracing through the given combination of NOT, NAND and AND gates for each input combination (00, 01, 10, 11) yields output C values of 1, 0, 1, 0 respectively, matching option 3.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is not correct?
options: Ovalbumin is a simple food reserve in egg-white.
Blood proteins thrombin and fibrinogen are involved in blood clotting.
Denaturation makes the proteins more active.
Insulin maintains sugar level in the blood of a human body.
questions.explanation: Denaturation disrupts the secondary and tertiary structure of a protein, causing it to lose its biological activity (e.g., enzymes lose catalytic activity), not become more active. So statement (3) is incorrect.

questions.text: The sum of the numbers 436.32, 227.2 and 0.301 in appropriate significant figures is
questions.explanation: In addition, the result is rounded to the least number of decimal places among the terms. 227.2 has only 1 decimal place, so the sum 663.821 is rounded to 663.8.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Aspirin and Paracetamol belong to the class of narcotic analgesics. Statement II: Morphine and Heroin are non-narcotic analgesics. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: Aspirin and Paracetamol are non-narcotic analgesics, while Morphine and Heroin are narcotic analgesics. Both statements as given are false.

questions.text: Two cities X and Y are connected by a regular bus service with a bus leaving in either direction every T min. A girl is driving scooty with a speed of 60 km/h in the direction X to Y notices that a bus goes past her every 30 minutes in the direction of her motion, and every 10 minutes in the opposite direction. Choose the correct option for the period T of the bus service and the speed (assumed constant) of the buses.
questions.explanation: Let bus speed = V, distance between buses = d = VT. d/(V−60) = 1/2 h and d/(V+60) = 1/6 h. Dividing: (V+60)/(V−60) = 3, giving V = 120 km/h. Then d = (120−60)/2×... = 30 km, and T = d/V = 30/120 h = 1/4 h = 15 min.

questions.text: Consider two circuits, (A) and (B), each having two resistors. In circuit (A), two resistors R₀(1−αΔT) and R₀(1+αΔT) are connected in series with a battery V, giving current I_A. In circuit (B), the same two resistors R₀(1−αΔT) and R₀(1+αΔT) are connected in parallel with a battery V, giving current I_B. As the temperature (ΔT) is increased, the correct option describing the variation of current in these circuits is:
options: both I_A and I_B remain constant
I_A remains constant while I_B increases
questions.topic: Temperature-Dependent Resistance in Series and Parallel Circuits
questions.explanation: Circuit A (series): total resistance = R₀(1-αΔT) + R₀(1+αΔT) = 2R₀, independent of ΔT (the temperature-dependent terms cancel). So I_A = V/(2R₀) stays constant. Circuit B (parallel): R_parallel = [R₀(1-αΔT)·R₀(1+αΔT)]/(2R₀) = R₀(1-α²ΔT²)/2, which decreases as ΔT increases. Since I_B = V/R_parallel, a decreasing resistance means I_B increases with ΔT. So I_A remains constant while I_B increases.

questions.text: Which among the given molecules (three bicyclic bridged ketones labeled I, II, III, with II having two phenyl substituents at the alpha carbon) can exhibit tautomerism?
questions.explanation: Bridge carbon atom does not participate in tautomerism. Acidic alpha-hydrogen must be present for tautomerism; in II both alpha-hydrogens are replaced by phenyl groups (no acidic H), so only III (which retains an alpha-H not at the bridgehead) can tautomerize.

questions.text: Given below are half cell reactions: MnO4- + 8H+ + 5e- -> Mn2+ + 4H2O, E(Mn2+/MnO4-) standard = -1.510 V; (1/2)O2 + 2H+ + 2e- -> H2O, E(O2/H2O) standard = +1.223 V. Will the permanganate ion, MnO4- liberate O2 from water in the presence of an acid?
questions.explanation: E(cell) = E(cathode, reduction MnO4- to Mn2+) + E(anode, oxidation of H2O to O2) = 1.510 + (-1.223) = 0.287 V. Since E(cell) is positive, the reaction is spontaneous, so MnO4- will indeed liberate O2 from water in acidic medium.

questions.text: The state of a gas can be described by quoting the relationship between
questions.explanation: The complete thermodynamic state of a gas is specified by all four state variables together: pressure, volume, temperature, and the amount of gas (moles) — any one of these affects the others via the ideal gas equation.

questions.text: Consider the following reaction: Benzyl phenyl ether (PhCH2-O-Ph) reacts with HI/Δ to give A + B. Identify products A and B.
options: A = Benzyl alcohol (PhCH2OH) and B = 4-iodophenyl derivative
A = Benzyl iodide (PhCH2I) and B = Phenol (PhOH)
questions.explanation: In the cleavage of an unsymmetrical ether like benzyl phenyl ether with HI, the iodide ion attacks the benzylic carbon (SN1-like, since the benzylic cation is highly stabilized), displacing the phenoxide as phenol, while the aryl-oxygen bond of the phenyl ring is not cleaved (aryl ethers do not undergo SN2 attack at the aromatic carbon). This gives A = benzyl iodide (PhCH2I) and B = phenol (PhOH).

questions.text: A pendulum is hung from the roof of a sufficiently high building and is moving freely to and fro like a simple harmonic oscillator. The acceleration of the bob of the pendulum is 20 m/s² at a distance of 5 m from the mean position. The time period of oscillation is
questions.topic: Simple harmonic motion: time period from acceleration data
questions.explanation: For SHM, a = ω²x. So ω² = a/x = 20/5 = 4, giving ω = 2 rad/s. Time period T = 2π/ω = 2π/2 = π s.

questions.text: A number of elements are available in the earth's crust, but the most abundant elements are
questions.topic: Most Abundant Elements in Earth's Crust
questions.explanation: Aluminium is the most abundant metal in the Earth's crust, followed by iron, making Al and Fe the two most abundant metallic elements overall.

questions.text: The errors in the measurement which arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in temperature and voltage supply are:
questions.explanation: Random errors arise due to unpredictable fluctuations in experimental conditions like temperature, voltage supply, and other environmental factors, and cannot be eliminated completely but can be minimized by taking multiple readings.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. HCl + ZnCl2, known as Lucas Reagent. Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: the Lucas test uses conc. HCl + ZnCl2 (Lucas reagent) and differentiates alcohols by reactivity (rate of turbidity formation). Statement II is incorrect: it is tertiary alcohols that react immediately at room temperature, while primary alcohols react very slowly (need heating) with Lucas reagent.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 24 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: The order of screening effect of electrons of s, p, d and f orbitals of a given shell of an atom on its outer shell electrons is
questions.explanation: s-orbitals are more penetrating (closer to the nucleus on average) than p, d, and f orbitals of the same shell, so they shield outer electrons most effectively. The screening effect order is s > p > d > f.

questions.text: The dimensions [MLT^-2 A^-2] belong to the:
questions.explanation: Magnetic permeability (mu0) has dimensional formula [MLT^-2A^-2], derived from the formula for force between two current-carrying wires or from B = mu0*H relationships.

questions.text: Dry ice is
questions.explanation: Dry ice is the common name for solid carbon dioxide (CO2), used as a refrigerant that sublimes directly to gas without leaving a liquid residue.

questions.text: De-Broglie wavelength of an electron orbiting in the n = 2 state of hydrogen atom is close to (Given Bohr radius = 0.052 nm)
questions.explanation: rn = n²a0 = 4×0.052 = 0.208 nm. Bohr quantization: 2πrn = nλ, so λ = 2πrn/n = 2π×4×0.052/2 = 2π×2×0.052 ≈ 0.653 ≈ 0.67 nm.

questions.text: In the measurement of viscosity of liquids using the terminal velocity experiment, spherical balls of the same radius but having different densities are used. The variation of the terminal velocity (v) with the ratio of density of the spherical ball (σ) to density of the liquid (ρ), is best represented by a graph that is:
options: a straight line through the origin with positive slope
a straight line with a positive y-intercept at σ/ρ=0
zero for σ/ρ < 1 with a sudden jump and a flat plateau beyond σ/ρ = 1
zero (flat along the axis) for σ/ρ ≤ 1 and then rising linearly for σ/ρ > 1
questions.explanation: Terminal velocity is given by v = (2r²g/9η)(σ-ρ) = (2r²gρ/9η)(σ/ρ - 1). For σ/ρ ≤ 1, the ball does not sink (it floats or is neutrally buoyant), so there is no downward terminal (sinking) velocity to measure, giving v = 0 in that region. For σ/ρ > 1, v increases linearly with σ/ρ, with the line originating from the point (1, 0). This flat-then-linear-rising-from-(1,0) shape matches option (4).

questions.text: When two monochromatic lights of frequency ν and ν/2 are incident on a photoelectric metal, their stopping potential becomes Vs/2 and Vs respectively. The threshold frequency for this metal is:
questions.explanation: hν = w + eVs/2 ...(i); h(ν/2) = w + eVs ...(ii). Multiply (ii) by 2: hν = 2w + 2eVs. Subtract (i): hν - hν = (2w-w) + (2eVs - eVs/2) is reorganized as: from (i) and (ii), eliminating Vs gives 2hν - hν/2 = 2w - w ⟹ 3hν/2 = w = hνth ⟹ νth = 3ν/2.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: Oxidation of p-nitrotoluene with acidic KMnO4 gives an acid that is stronger than benzoic acid.
Statement-II: Reduction of p-nitrotoluene with Sn/HCl followed by neutralization gives an amine that is more basic than aniline.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
questions.topic: Acidity and Basicity - Effect of Substituents (Assertion-Reason)
questions.explanation: Oxidation of p-nitrotoluene with acidic KMnO4 oxidizes the methyl group to -COOH, giving p-nitrobenzoic acid. The electron-withdrawing -NO2 group stabilizes the carboxylate conjugate base, making it a stronger acid than benzoic acid -- Statement-I is correct. Reduction of p-nitrotoluene's -NO2 group with Sn/HCl (followed by neutralization) gives p-toluidine (p-methylaniline). The electron-donating methyl group increases electron density on nitrogen, making p-toluidine more basic than aniline -- Statement-II is correct. Both statements are correct.

questions.text: An electron is projected with uniform velocity along the axis of a current-carrying long solenoid. Which of the following is true?
options: The electron will be accelerated along the axis.
The electron's path will be circular about the axis.
The electron will experience a force at 45° to the axis and hence execute a helical path.
The electron will continue to move with uniform velocity along the axis of the solenoid.
questions.topic: Charged Particle Moving Along a Solenoid's Axis
questions.explanation: Inside a long solenoid, the magnetic field is directed along the axis. Since the electron's velocity is also along the axis, v is parallel to B, making the magnetic force F = qv×B equal to zero. With no net force, the electron continues moving with uniform velocity along the axis.

questions.text: Enthalpy of sublimation of a substance is equal to
options: enthalpy of fusion + enthalpy of vapourisation.
questions.explanation: By Hess's law, sublimation (solid → gas directly) is thermodynamically equivalent to fusion (solid → liquid) followed by vaporisation (liquid → gas), so ΔsubH = ΔfusH + ΔvapH.

questions.text: A long solenoid of 50 cm length having 100 turns carries a current of 2.5 A. The magnetic field at the centre of the solenoid is: (μ0=4π×10^-7 T m A^-1)
questions.topic: Magnetic field at the centre of a solenoid

questions.text: For sound waves, if the number of nodes for the 5th harmonic of an open-ended pipe is n and that for the 9th harmonic of the same pipe with one of its ends closed is m, the ratio n/m is:
questions.topic: Harmonics in Open and Closed Pipes - Nodes
questions.explanation: For an open pipe, the kth harmonic has k nodes, so the 5th harmonic has n=5 nodes. For a closed pipe (one end closed), only odd harmonics (1st, 3rd, 5th, 7th, 9th...) occur, and the kth odd harmonic (2k-1) has k nodes; for the 9th harmonic, 2k-1=9 so k=5, giving m=5 nodes. So n/m = 5/5 = 1.

questions.text: Two transparent media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s and 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is
questions.explanation: μ(A to B) relative = vA/vB... Using sin(C) = v2/v1 (going from slower to faster medium A to B) = 1.5/2.0 = 0.75, C = sin⁻¹(0.750).

questions.text: A capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF is charged fully by 100 V battery B as shown in figure (a). Then it is disconnected from the battery and connected to another uncharged capacitor of capacitance C = 900 pF as shown in figure (b). The electrostatic energy stored by the system (b) is
questions.explanation: Initial charge Q = CV = 900×10⁻¹²×100 = 9×10⁻⁸ C. When connected to identical uncharged capacitor, charge redistributes equally, each gets Q/2, common V' = 50 V. Energy = (1/2)(2C)(V'²) = C×V'² = 900×10⁻¹²×2500 = 2.25×10⁻⁶ J.

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave travelling in a lossless dielectric medium having a dielectric constant, epsilon_r = 9, has the electric field, Ex = E0 sin(kz - 2*pi*10^6 t) V/m, where E0 is the amplitude and k is the wave vector. Among the following options, the INCORRECT choice(s) is/are: (1) The wavelength of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is 300 m. (2) The magnetic field is given by the relation By = (B0/v) sin(kz - 2*pi*10^6 t), where v is the speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium. (3) The direction of propagation of the electromagnetic wave is along +z. (4) The speed of the electromagnetic wave inside the medium is 10^8 m/s.
questions.topic: EM Wave Properties in a Dielectric Medium
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = sqrt(epsilon_r) = 3, so speed in medium v = c/n = 10^8 m/s (statement 4 is correct). Frequency f = 10^6 Hz, so wavelength = v/f = 10^8/10^6 = 100 m, NOT 300 m, making statement (1) incorrect. The wave travels in the +z direction (statement 3 is correct). The correct relation for the magnetic field amplitude is B0 = E0/v, so the field should be written as By = (E0/v) sin(...), not (B0/v) sin(...) which is dimensionally inconsistent as stated, making statement (2) also incorrect. So both (1) and (2) are the incorrect choices (officially marked as a multi-select answer '1, 2').

questions.text: Which of the following is a natural polymer?
questions.explanation: cis-1,4-polyisoprene is the chemical name for natural rubber, making it a naturally occurring polymer, unlike the other synthetic rubbers/copolymers listed.

questions.text: The most suitable method of separation of 1:1 mixture of ortho and para-nitrophenols is:
questions.explanation: o-Nitrophenol has intramolecular hydrogen bonding, making it volatile and steam-distillable, while p-nitrophenol has intermolecular hydrogen bonding, making it less volatile. This difference allows separation of the mixture by steam distillation.

questions.text: As observed from earth, the sun appears to move in an approximate circular orbit. For the motion of another planet like mercury as observed from earth, this would
options: not be true because the force between earth and mercury is not inverse square law.
not be true because the major gravitational force on mercury is due to sun.
not be true because mercury is influenced by forces other than gravitational forces.
questions.explanation: The apparent simple circular motion of the sun as seen from earth results from earth's own near-circular orbit. Mercury's actual motion is dominated by its gravitational interaction with the sun (not earth), so its apparent path from earth is not similarly simple.

questions.text: An electric dipole with dipole moment 5×10⁻⁶ Cm is aligned with the direction of a uniform electric field of magnitude 4×10⁵ N/C. The dipole is then rotated through an angle of 60° with respect to the electric field. The change in the potential energy of the dipole is :

A long wire carrying a steady current is bent into a circular loop of one turn. The magnetic field at the centre of the loop is B. It is then bent into a circular coil of n turns. The magnetic field at the centre of this coil of n turns will be:
questions.topic: Magnetic Field of Circular Coil - n Turns
questions.explanation: Same wire length l=2πr is now divided into n turns of radius r2=r/n. New field B' = μ0ni/(2r2) = μ0ni/(2r/n) = n²(μ0i/2r) = n²B.

questions.text: Which of the following hydrogen halides has the highest bond dissociation enthalpy?
questions.topic: Halogen Acid with Highest Bond Dissociation Enthalpy
questions.explanation: Despite its longer bond-dipole considerations, HF has the smallest bond length and the strongest H–X bond due to the small size of fluorine, giving it the highest bond dissociation enthalpy among the hydrogen halides, which decreases down the group (HF > HCl > HBr > HI).

questions.text: A spring is stretched by applying a load to its free end. The strain produced in the spring is
questions.explanation: Since the spring wire is coiled, stretching the spring twists the wire, producing shear strain in the material of the wire rather than simple longitudinal strain.

questions.text: If force [F], acceleration [A] and time [T] are chosen as the fundamental physical quantities. Find the dimensions of energy.
questions.topic: Dimensions of energy from F, A, T
questions.explanation: Energy=Force×distance; distance=½AT². So Energy=F×A T²/2, dimensionally [F][A][T²].

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will give butanone on oxidation with alkaline KMnO4 solution?
questions.topic: Alcohol That Gives Butanone on Oxidation
questions.explanation: Butan-2-ol is a secondary alcohol, and oxidation of secondary alcohols gives ketones — here, butan-2-one (butanone). Butan-1-ol is a primary alcohol, which is oxidised instead to butanoic acid by a strong oxidant like KMnO4, not to a ketone.

questions.text: AB is a part of an electrical circuit containing a 1H inductor, a 5V cell, and a 2Ω resistor in series carrying current i. The potential difference "VA − VB" at the instant when current i = 2A and is increasing at a rate of 1 amp/second is:
questions.explanation: EMF across inductor ε = L(dI/dt) = 1×1 = 1V. Going from A to B: VA − 1 − 5 − 2×2 = VB, so VA − VB = 1 + 5 + 4 = 10 V.

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is [Given pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(0.10/0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57+1 = 5.57.

questions.text: For a first order reaction A → Products, initial concentration of A is 0.1 M, which becomes 0.001 M after 5 minutes. Rate constant for the reaction in min⁻¹ is
Which amongst the following molecules on polymerization produces neoprene?
options: H2C=C(Cl)-CH=CH2 with an additional CH3 substituent (incorrect structure)
questions.explanation: Neoprene is the polymer formed by the polymerization of chloroprene (2-chlorobuta-1,3-diene, H2C=C(Cl)-CH=CH2). Polymerization of the conjugated diene opens up the double bonds to give the repeating unit [-CH2-C(Cl)=CH-CH2-]n.

questions.text: A ball is travelling with uniform translatory motion. This means that
options: the path can be a straight line or circular and the ball travels with uniform speed.
all parts of the ball have the same velocity (magnitude and direction) and the velocity is constant.
the centre of the ball moves with constant velocity and the ball spins about its centre uniformly.
questions.explanation: Uniform translatory motion means every part of the body has the same constant velocity (both magnitude and direction) — the defining feature of translation without rotation.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R: Assertion A: A reaction can have zero activation energy. Reason R: The minimum extra amount of energy absorbed by reactant molecules so that their energy becomes equal to threshold value, is called activation energy. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
A is true but R is false.
A is false but R is true.
Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
questions.explanation: Assertion A is false — a reaction cannot have zero activation energy; every reaction requires some minimum energy for the reactants to reach the transition state. Reason R correctly defines activation energy as the minimum extra energy needed for reactant molecules to reach the threshold energy. Hence A is false but R is true.

questions.text: A lens of large focal length and large aperture is best suited as an objective of an astronomical telescope since:
options: a large aperture contributes to the quality and visibility of the images
a large area of the objective ensures better light gathering power
a large aperture provides a better resolution
questions.explanation: A large aperture improves light-gathering power, resolution, and image quality/visibility — all are correct reasons.

questions.text: A particle of mass 'm' is projected with a velocity v = kVe (k < 1) from the surface of the earth. (Ve = escape velocity). The maximum height above the surface reached by the particle is:
questions.topic: Height Attained with Given Fraction of Escape Velocity
questions.explanation: Using energy conservation, -GMm/R + (1/2)mk²Ve² = -GMm/r, which simplifies to 1/r = (1-k²)/R, so r = R/(1-k²). Height h = r - R = k²R/(1-k²).

questions.text: The given compound CH=CH-CH(X)-CH2-CH3 attached to a benzene ring (phenyl group on the terminal alkene carbon, with halogen X on the carbon adjacent to the double bond) is an example of ________.
questions.explanation: The halogen X is attached to the carbon directly adjacent to a carbon-carbon double bond (the allylic carbon), not to the double bond carbon itself or to the aromatic ring. Hence this compound is an example of an allylic halide.

questions.text: A physical quantity of the dimensions of length that can be formed out of c, G and e²/(4πε₀) is [c is velocity of light, G is universal constant of gravitation and e is charge]:
questions.explanation: Combining the dimensions of c, G and e²/(4πε₀) (which has dimensions of energy×length) such that the result has dimensions of length gives the expression (1/c²)[G·e²/(4πε₀)]^(1/2).

questions.text: An alkene on ozonolysis gives methanal as one of the products. Its structure is:
options: Cyclohexenyl-CH2-CH2-CH3 structure (cyclohexane ring with CH2CH2CH3 and a =CH2 group)
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis cleaves the C=C double bond, and methanal (HCHO) is produced from a terminal =CH2 group. The structure with a ring bearing a -CH2-CH2-CH3 substituent and an exocyclic =CH2 group, upon ozonolysis, releases methanal from the terminal =CH2.

questions.text: A body is executing simple harmonic motion with frequency 'n', the frequency of its potential energy is:
questions.topic: Frequency of potential energy in SHM
