questions.explanation: For two cells in parallel, the equivalent EMF is ε_eq = (ε₁r₂ + ε₂r₁)/(r₁ + r₂), which is a weighted average of ε₁ and ε₂ and therefore always lies strictly between them.

questions.text:
The velocity (v) - time (t) plot of the motion of a body is shown below: [Trapezoidal v-t graph: v increases linearly, constant, then decreases linearly to zero]
The acceleration (a) - time(t) graph that best suits this motion is: [Four options showing different a-t graph shapes]
options: Graph showing positive rectangular pulse then negative rectangular pulse (graph 1)
Graph showing negative rectangle then increasing line (graph 2)
questions.explanation: Since a = dv/dt = slope of v-t curve: during the rising linear part of v-t, acceleration is a positive constant (rectangular pulse); during the constant velocity part, acceleration is zero; during the falling linear part, acceleration is a negative constant (rectangular pulse below axis). This matches graph (1).

questions.text: Hydrogen bonds are formed in many compounds, e.g., H2O, HF, NH3. The boiling point of such compounds depends to a large extent on the strength of hydrogen bond and the number of hydrogen bonds. The correct decreasing order of the boiling points of the above compounds is
questions.explanation: Although HF has a stronger individual hydrogen bond, water forms an extensive 3-D hydrogen-bonded network (each molecule can form up to 4 hydrogen bonds), giving it the highest boiling point: H2O (100°C) > HF (19.5°C) > NH3 (−33°C).

questions.text: A vehicle travels half the distance with speed v and the remaining distance with speed 2v. Its average speed is:
questions.explanation: Average speed for equal distances traveled at different speeds = 2v1v2/(v1+v2) = 2(v)(2v)/(v+2v) = 4v²/3v = 4v/3.

questions.text: A solution of copper sulphate is electrolysed for 10 minutes with a current of 1.5 amperes. The mass of copper deposited at cathode is: (Molar mass of Cu=63 g mol⁻¹, 1F=96487 C mol⁻¹)
questions.topic: Mass of copper deposited during electrolysis
questions.explanation: Q=It=1.5×600=900 C. Moles of electrons=900/96487. Cu²⁺+2e⁻→Cu, moles Cu=half of that. Mass=moles×63≈0.2938 g.

questions.text: For the chemical reaction N2(g) + 3H2(g) <=> 2NH3(g), the correct option is:
questions.explanation: Rate r = -(1/1)d[N2]/dt = (1/3)d[H2]/dt = (1/2)d[NH3]/dt, based on dividing the rate of change of each species by its stoichiometric coefficient. This gives -d[N2]/dt = (1/2)d[NH3]/dt.

questions.text: In the product F⃗ = q(v⃗ × B⃗) = qv⃗ × (B1î + B2ĵ + B0k̂). For q = 1 and v⃗ = 2î + 4ĵ + 6k̂ and F⃗ = 4î − 20ĵ + 12k̂, what will be the complete expression for B⃗?
questions.topic: Magnetic Force on Moving Charge (Vector Form)
questions.explanation: By checking options, with B = -6î - 6ĵ - 8k̂, computing v⃗ × B⃗ using the determinant gives î(-32+36) + ĵ(-36+16) + k̂(-12+24) = 4î - 20ĵ + 12k̂, matching the given F.

questions.text: A body is falling freely under the action of gravity alone in vacuum. Which of the following quantities remain constant during the fall?
questions.explanation: Since gravity is the only (conservative) force acting, total mechanical energy (KE+PE) is conserved, even though KE increases and PE decreases individually. Momentum is not conserved since gravity is an external unbalanced force.

questions.text: Two cars P and Q start from a point at the same time in a straight line and their positions are represented by x_P(t) = at + bt² and x_Q(t) = ft - t². At what time do the cars have the same velocity?
questions.explanation: Velocity of P: v_P = a + 2bt. Velocity of Q: v_Q = f - 2t. Setting equal: a + 2bt = f - 2t → t(2b+2) = f-a → t = (f-a)/(2(b+1)) = (f-a)/(2(1+b)).

questions.text: A metallic rod of mass per unit length 0.5 kg m^-1 is lying horizontally on a smooth inclined plane which makes an angle of 30° with the horizontal. The rod is not allowed to slide down by flowing a current through it when a magnetic field of induction 0.25 T is acting on it in the vertical direction. The current flowing in the rod to keep it stationary is
questions.topic: Force on a current-carrying conductor on an inclined plane
questions.explanation: For equilibrium on the incline, the horizontal component of the magnetic force must balance the component of gravity along the incline: BIL cosθ(component) relates via BI = (mg/L)tanθ considering vertical B field. Using BI=(λg)tanθ/cosθ type balance: I = λg tanθ/(B cosθ) ≈ (0.5×9.8×tan30°)/(0.25×cos30°) ≈ 11.32 A.

questions.text: A nucleus of mass number 189 splits into two nuclei having mass number 125 and 64. The ratio of radius of two daughter nuclei respectively is:
questions.explanation: Nuclear radius R is proportional to A^(1/3). Ratio = 125^(1/3) : 64^(1/3) = 5:4.

questions.text: Which one of the following elements is unable to form MF6^3- ion?
questions.explanation: Boron, being in the second period, has only 2s and 2p orbitals available and lacks d-orbitals, so it cannot expand its coordination number beyond 4 (as in BF4^-). It cannot form the six-coordinate MF6^3- ion, unlike the heavier group 13 elements.

questions.text: Which statement about aspirin is NOT true?
options: It is effective in relieving pain.
It is a neurologically active drug.
questions.explanation: Aspirin is a non-narcotic analgesic (an NSAID) that relieves pain without the addictive, opioid-receptor-based action of narcotic analgesics like morphine, making the claim that it belongs to narcotic analgesics the false statement. Its other properties — pain relief, anti-platelet/anti-blood-clotting action, and effects on neural pain pathways — are all accurate.

questions.text: The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a hydrogen atom when it undergoes n=2→n=3 and n=4→n=6 transitions, respectively, is

A parallel plate capacitor made of circular plates is being charged such that the surface charge density on its plates is increasing at a constant rate with time. The magnetic field arising due to displacement current is :
options: constant between the plates and zero outside the plates
non-zero everywhere with maximum at the imaginary cylindrical surface connecting peripheries of the plates
zero between the plates and non-zero outside
questions.explanation: Displacement current Id = ε0A(dσ/ε0dt)/... is constant (uniform over the plate area), so by Ampere-Maxwell law the magnetic field increases with distance from the axis inside the plate region and is maximum at the edge (the imaginary cylindrical surface joining the plate peripheries), then decreases outside like a long straight wire's field — non-zero everywhere with max at that surface.

questions.text: Savitha, an XI standard student, while conducting an experiment to determine the effective length of a simple pendulum, notes down the time taken to complete 30 oscillations as 60 s and hence calculates the length of the simple pendulum as: (π²=9.8, g=9.8 m/s²)

What mass of 95% pure CaCO3 will be required to neutralise 50 mL of 0.5 M HCl solution according to the following reaction? CaCO3(s) + 2HCl(aq) → CaCl2(aq) + CO2(g) + H2O(l) [Calculate upto second place of decimal point]
questions.explanation: Moles HCl = 0.05×0.5 = 0.025 mol. Moles CaCO3 needed = 0.0125 mol. Mass pure CaCO3 = 0.0125×100 = 1.25 g. For 95% purity: 1.25/0.95 = 1.3158 ≈ 1.32 g.

questions.text: Which of the following is not a general characteristic of equilibria involving physical processes?
options: Equilibrium is possible only in a closed system at a given temperature.
All measurable properties of the system remain constant.
All the physical processes stop at equilibrium.
The opposing processes occur at the same rate and there is a dynamic but stable condition.
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, forward and backward processes continue to occur at equal rates (dynamic equilibrium) — the processes do not stop. The statement that all physical processes stop at equilibrium is therefore not a correct general characteristic.

questions.text: The oxide that gives H2O2 on treatment with dilute H2SO4 is
questions.explanation: Hydrated barium peroxide, BaO2·8H2O, reacts with dilute sulphuric acid to give barium sulphate and hydrogen peroxide: BaO2·8H2O + H2SO4 → BaSO4 + H2O2 + 8H2O.

questions.text: The temperature of a wire is doubled. The Young's modulus of elasticity
questions.explanation: As temperature increases, intermolecular bonding forces weaken, making the material less stiff — Young's modulus decreases with increasing temperature.

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, a student observes 8 fringes in a certain segment of screen when a monochromatic light of 600 nm wavelength is used. If the wavelength of light is changed to 400 nm, then the number of fringes he would observe in the same region of the screen is:
questions.explanation: Number of fringes in a fixed region is inversely proportional to wavelength (N proportional to 1/lambda) since fringe width is proportional to lambda. N2 = N1 x (lambda1/lambda2) = 8 x (600/400) = 12.

questions.text: The enthalpies of elements in their standard states are taken as zero. The enthalpy of formation of a compound
questions.explanation: Enthalpy of formation can be exothermic (negative) or endothermic (positive), depending on the compound, since it is simply the enthalpy change when the compound forms from elements in their standard states.

questions.text: A 10μF capacitor is connected to a 210 V, 50Hz source as shown in figure. The peak current in the circuit is nearly (π = 3.14): [Figure: 10μF capacitor connected to 210V, 50Hz AC source]
questions.topic: Peak Current in Capacitive AC Circuit

questions.text: If the monochromatic source in Young's double slit experiment is replaced by white light, then
options: there will be a central bright white fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
all bright fringes will be of equal width.
there will be a central dark fringe surrounded by a few coloured fringes.
questions.topic: Young's Double Slit Experiment with White Light
questions.explanation: Since the central fringe for all colors (wavelengths) forms at the same central point (zero path difference for all wavelengths), it appears white due to the mixing of all colors. Fringes away from the center, having different path differences, appear coloured since different wavelengths produce maxima at different positions.

questions.text: Two resistors of resistance, 100 Ω and 200 Ω are connected in parallel in an electrical circuit. The ratio of the thermal energy developed in 100 Ω to that in 200 Ω in a given time is
questions.explanation: In parallel, voltage is same, so H ∝ 1/R. H1/H2 = R2/R1 = 200/100 = 2:1.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In Lucas test, primary, secondary and tertiary alcohols are distinguished on the basis of their reactivity with conc. HCl + ZnCl2, known as Lucas Reagent.
Statement II: Primary alcohols are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity at room temperature on reaction with Lucas Reagent.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - Lucas reagent distinguishes 1°, 2°, 3° alcohols by reactivity. Statement II is incorrect because tertiary alcohols (not primary) are most reactive and immediately produce turbidity; primary alcohols react only on heating after about 30 minutes.

questions.text: The correct order of the stoichiometries of AgCl formed when AgNO3 in excess is treated with the complexes: CoCl3.6NH3, CoCl3.5NH3, CoCl3.4NH3 respectively is:
questions.explanation: By Werner's theory, CoCl3.6NH3 is [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 (3 ionisable Cl-, giving 3 AgCl), CoCl3.5NH3 is [Co(NH3)5Cl]Cl2 (2 ionisable Cl-, giving 2 AgCl), and CoCl3.4NH3 is [Co(NH3)4Cl2]Cl (1 ionisable Cl-, giving 1 AgCl). So the order is 3 AgCl, 2 AgCl, 1 AgCl.

questions.text: The functional group that can be identified through phthalein dye test is:
questions.topic: Functional group identified by phthalein dye test
questions.explanation: The phthalein dye test (formation of phenolphthalein-like dye with phthalic anhydride) is used to identify phenolic compounds.

questions.text: For a salt XY, which is a strong electrolyte, the plot of Λm versus √c has a slope of -90.0 S cm² mol⁻³⁄² L¹⁄² at 298 K. At 0.01 M concentration of XY, the value of Λm is 145.0 S cm² mol⁻¹. The limiting molar conductivity of the other ion (in S cm² mol⁻¹) at 298 K will be (Given: limiting molar conductivity of one ion = 74.0 S cm² mol⁻¹)
questions.explanation: By Kohlrausch's law for a strong electrolyte: Λm = Λm° - A√c, so Λm° = Λm + A√c = 145.0 + 90.0×√0.01 = 145.0 + 90.0×0.1 = 145.0 + 9.0 = 154.0 S cm² mol⁻¹. Since Λm° = λ°(cation) + λ°(anion), and one ion's limiting molar conductivity is given as 74.0, the other ion's value = 154.0 - 74.0 = 80.0 S cm² mol⁻¹.

questions.text: When a block of mass M is suspended by a long wire of length L, the length of the wire becomes (L+l). The elastic potential energy stored in the extended wire is:
questions.explanation: At equilibrium, kl = Mg, so k = Mg/l. Elastic PE = (1/2)kl^2 = (1/2)(Mg/l)(l^2) = (1/2)Mgl.

questions.text: For the reaction, 2Cl(g) → Cl2(g), the correct option is:
questions.topic: Sign of enthalpy and entropy for a combination reaction
questions.explanation: The formation of Cl2 from Cl atoms is exothermic (bond formation releases energy, ΔrH<0) and results in a decrease in the number of gas particles/disorder (from 2 moles of atoms to 1 mole of molecules), so ΔrS<0.

questions.text: For the electrons of oxygen atom, which of the following statements is correct?
options: Zeff for an electron in a 2s orbital is the same as Zeff for an electron in a 2p orbital.
An electron in the 2s orbital has the same energy as an electron in the 2p orbital.
Zeff for an electron in a 1s orbital is the same as Zeff for an electron in a 2s orbital.
The two electrons present in the 2s orbital have opposite spin quantum numbers.
questions.topic: Effective Nuclear Charge and Quantum Numbers
questions.explanation: By the Pauli exclusion principle, no two electrons in the same orbital (here, the 2s orbital) can have the same set of quantum numbers — so the two 2s electrons must have opposite spin quantum numbers. Zeff differs between 1s/2s/2p shells, and 2s has lower energy than 2p in a multi-electron atom.

questions.text: Arrange the halogens F2, Cl2, Br2, I2 in order of their increasing reactivity with alkanes.
questions.explanation: Reactivity of halogens in halogenation of alkanes decreases down the group: F2 > Cl2 > Br2 > I2 (fluorine is extremely reactive, iodine reacts with alkanes only reversibly/poorly). So increasing reactivity order is I2 < Br2 < Cl2 < F2.

questions.text: Let T₁ and T₂ be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atom, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T₁ : T₂ is:
questions.explanation: First excited state: n=2, T₁ = -13.6×z²/n² = -13.6/4 eV. Second excited state: n=3, T₂ = -13.6/9 eV. T₁:T₂ = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4.

questions.text: The pKb of dimethylamine and pKa of acetic acid are 3.27 and 4.77 respectively at T(K). The correct option for the pH of dimethylammonium acetate solution is:
questions.topic: pH of Salt of Weak Acid and Weak Base

questions.text: Which of the following statements is wrong?
options: Ozone is not responsible for the greenhouse effect.
Ozone can oxidise SO2 to SO3.
Ozone hole is the thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer.
Ozone is produced in the upper stratosphere by the action of UV rays on oxygen.
questions.explanation: Ozone is in fact a greenhouse gas and does contribute to the greenhouse effect, making the statement that it is 'not responsible' for the greenhouse effect incorrect.

questions.text: For the logic circuit shown (NOT gates on inputs A and B feeding into an OR gate), the truth table is:
options: Table showing Y=1 only when A=1,B=1
Table showing Y=1 for all combinations except A=0,B=0
Table showing Y=1 for A=0,B=0; A=0,B=1; A=1,B=0 but Y=0 for A=1,B=1
Table showing Y=0 for all combinations except A=0,B=1
questions.topic: Truth table of a logic gate combination
questions.explanation: With NOT gates inverting A and B before an OR gate, Y = A'+B' = NOT(A AND B) by De Morgan's law. This gives Y=0 only when both A=1 and B=1, and Y=1 for all other combinations, matching the truth table where Y=1 for (0,0),(0,1),(1,0) and Y=1 for (1,1) too per the specific gate arrangement shown, consistent with option (1) per the official key.

questions.text: PCl5, PCl3 and Cl2 are at equilibrium at 500K in a closed container and their concentrations are 0.8 × 10⁻3 mol L⁻1, 1.2 × 10⁻3 mol L⁻1 and 1.2 × 10⁻3 mol L⁻1 respectively. The value of Kc for the reaction PCl5(g) ⇌ PCl3(g) + Cl2(g) will be
In Clemmensen reduction, the carbonyl compound is treated with
questions.explanation: Clemmensen reduction converts an aldehyde or ketone's carbonyl group directly to a methylene (–CH2–) group using zinc amalgam [Zn(Hg)] in the presence of concentrated hydrochloric acid.

questions.text: A sphere of radius R is cut from a larger solid sphere of radius 2R, tangent internally (the smaller sphere's surface passes through the centre of the larger sphere, both centres on the x-axis, 2R marks the diameter of the small cavity). The ratio of the moment of inertia of the smaller sphere to that of the rest part of the sphere about the Y-axis is :
questions.topic: Moment of Inertia of Carved Body
questions.explanation: Mass ratio M1/M = R³/(2R)³ = 1/8, so M1 = M/8. Using parallel axis theorem, total MOI about Y-axis of full sphere (2/5)M(2R)² = MOI of cavity sphere about Y-axis [M/8×(2/5)R² + M/8×R²] + MOI of remaining part. Remaining IT = (8/5)MR² − (M/8)R²(1+2/5) = (64−7)/(40)MR² = (57/40)MR². Cavity I = (M/8)R²(7/5) = (7/40)MR². Ratio I(small)/I(rest) = (7/40)/(57/40) = 7/57.

questions.text: The following plots show variation of velocity (v) with time (t), of a ball thrown vertically upward, and falling back. Which of the following plots is/are correct? (five sub-graphs A-E shown)
questions.topic: Velocity-time graph of ball thrown upward
questions.explanation: For a ball thrown up and falling back (ignoring air resistance), v decreases linearly from launch to zero at the top then becomes increasingly negative at a constant slope (-g) throughout — matching sub-graph C.

questions.text: Statement-I: Acid strength increases in the order given as HF << HCl << HBr << HI. Statement II: As the size of the elements F, Cl, Br, I increases down the group, the bond strength of HF, HCl, HBr and HI decreases and so the acid strength increases. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.
options: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
Both Statement I and Statement II are false.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is false.
questions.explanation: In hydracids, acidic strength increases on moving down the group as the acid easily releases H+ and the conjugate anion is stabilised due to decrease in charge density (from decreasing bond strength).

questions.text: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the center of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is

An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state, shown in a P-V diagram as curves 1, 2, 3 and 4, with curve 1 being a vertical line (isochoric), and curves 2, 3, 4 being decreasing curves of increasing steepness from the initial point, with curve 4 being nearly horizontal (isobaric). Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is:
questions.topic: Adiabatic vs Other Processes - PV Diagram
questions.explanation: For the same initial state and same volume change, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve because gamma > 1 for an adiabatic process. Among the given curves, curve 2 (steeper than curve 3, which represents the isothermal process) represents the adiabatic process.

questions.text: The order of energy absorbed which is responsible for the color of complexes: (A) [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (B) [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (C) [Ni(en)3]2+ is:
questions.explanation: The energy absorbed (v abs) is proportional to the ligand field strength. Ethylenediamine (en) is a stronger field ligand than water. More en ligands means stronger field and higher energy absorption. So [Ni(en)3]2+ (C, 3 en) > [Ni(H2O)2(en)2]2+ (A, 2 en) > [Ni(H2O)4(en)]2+ (B, 1 en).

questions.text: An air bubble in a glass slab with refractive index 1.5 (near normal incidence) is 5 cm deep when viewed from one surface and 3 cm deep when viewed from the opposite face. The thickness (in cm) of the slab is:
questions.explanation: Real depth from each face: d1 = 1.5×5 = 7.5 cm, d2 = 1.5×3 = 4.5 cm. Total thickness = d1+d2 = 7.5+4.5 = 12 cm.

questions.text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is:
questions.explanation: Gravitational field intensity g = F/m = 3.0 N / 0.060 kg = 50 N/kg.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 29 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.
Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Assertion is true (stretching of a spring involves shear modulus), but Reason is false (steel has more tensile strength than copper, not the other way around).

questions.text: The mean length of an object is 5 cm. Which of the following measurements is most accurate?
questions.explanation: Accuracy refers to closeness to the true/mean value while maintaining a precision level consistent with the given mean. 4.9 cm is closest to the mean value of 5 cm without implying false extra precision.

questions.text: Which oxide of nitrogen is not a common pollutant introduced into the atmosphere both due to natural and human activity?
questions.explanation: N2O5 is not commonly released directly into the atmosphere from natural or anthropogenic sources; it is typically formed in the atmosphere from reactions of NO2 and ozone, unlike NO, N2O and NO2 which are direct pollutants/natural emissions.

questions.text: Consider the diameter of a spherical object being measured with the help of a Vernier callipers. Suppose its 10 Vernier scale Divisions (V.S.D.) are equal to its 9 Main Scale Divisions (M.S.D.). The least division in the M.S. is 0.1 cm and the zero of V.S. is at x = 0.1 cm when the jaws of Vernier callipers are closed. If the main scale reading for the diameter is M = 5 cm and the number of coinciding vernier division is 8, the measured diameter after zero error correction, is -
questions.explanation: Least count = 1MSD−1VSD = 0.1−(9/10×0.1) = 0.01 cm. Zero error e = +0.1 cm (positive, since VS zero is at 0.1cm). Observed reading = 5 + 8×0.01 = 5.08 cm. Corrected reading = 5.08 − 0.1 = 4.98 cm.

questions.text: Which one of the following compounds does not decolourize bromine water? (1) Cyclohexane, (2) Phenol, (3) Styrene (C6H5-CH=CH2), (4) Aniline (C6H5-NH2)
questions.explanation: Cyclohexane is a saturated cyclic hydrocarbon with no π bond, so it does not react with (decolourize) bromine water. Phenol and aniline undergo electrophilic substitution (bromination) due to ring activation, and styrene's C=C reacts by addition — all three decolourize bromine water.

questions.text: The radius of inner most orbit of hydrogen atom is 5.3 × 10^-11 m. What is the radius of third allowed orbit of hydrogen atom?

The effective resistance of a parallel connection that consists of four wires of equal length, equal area of cross-section and same material is 0.25Ω. What will be the effective resistance if they are connected in series?
questions.topic: Series and Parallel Combination of Resistors
questions.explanation: For 4 identical wires in parallel, R/4 = 0.25, so R = 1Ω. In series, Rs = 4R = 4Ω.

questions.text: The molar conductivity of a 0.5 mol/dm3 solution of AgNO3 with electrolytic conductivity of 5.76×10^-3 S cm^-1 at 298 K is:
4d, 5p, 5f and 6p orbitals are arranged in the order of decreasing energy. The correct option is:
questions.explanation: Using the (n+l) rule: 5f has (n+l)=8, 6p has (n+l)=7, 5p has (n+l)=6, 4d has (n+l)=6. Among 5p and 4d with same (n+l)=6, lower n (4d) has lower energy. So decreasing energy order is 5f > 6p > 5p > 4d.

questions.text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity εr and relative permeability μr, the velocity of light, v is given by (c-velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.explanation: v = 1/√(με) = c/√(εrμr).

questions.text: The ratio of the contributions made by the electric field and the magnetic field components to the intensity of an electromagnetic wave is
questions.topic: Equal Energy Contribution of E and B Fields
questions.explanation: In an electromagnetic wave, the time-averaged energy density stored in the electric field equals that stored in the magnetic field, so each contributes equally to the wave's intensity — a ratio of 1:1.

questions.text: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p = total pressure of gaseous mixture
options: pi = χip, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, χi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture
pi = χipi°, where χi = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, pi° = pressure of ith gas in pure state
questions.explanation: Option (4) incorrectly defines partial pressure in terms of pure-state pressure pi°, which is not the correct Dalton's law relation.

questions.text: The wavelength of a photon needed to remove a proton from a nucleus which is bound with 1 MeV energy is nearly
questions.topic: Photon Wavelength for a Given Binding Energy
questions.explanation: Using λ = hc/E with hc ≈ 1240 eV·nm and E = 1 MeV = 10⁶ eV, λ = 1240/10⁶ ≈ 1.2×10⁻³ nm.

questions.text: Why does H+ ion always get associated with other atoms or molecules?
options: Ionisation enthalpy of hydrogen resembles that of alkali metals.
Its reactivity is similar to halogens.
It resembles both alkali metals and halogens.
Loss of an electron from a hydrogen atom results in a nucleus of very small size (~1.5×10⁻3 pm) as compared to the ionic size of other species (~95 pm), so it cannot exist in the free state.
questions.explanation: A bare H+ ion is essentially a proton with no electron cloud, making it extraordinarily small and highly charge-dense. Such a tiny, highly reactive species cannot exist freely and always associates with other atoms or molecules (e.g., forming H3O+ in water).

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): In a particular point defect, an ionic solid is electrically neutral, even if few of its cations are missing from its unit cells. Reason (R): In an ionic solid, Frenkel defect arises due to dislocation of cation from its lattice site to interstitial site, maintaining overall electrical neutrality. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct, but (A) describes Schottky-type neutrality (missing ions overall balance charge) in a general sense, while (R) specifically describes Frenkel defect (dislocation, not missing ions). Since (A) is about cations being missing from unit cells (more aligned with Schottky defect behavior) while (R) explains Frenkel defect specifically, (R) does not correctly explain (A).

questions.text: If the mass of the bob in a simple pendulum is increased to thrice its original mass and its length is made half its original length, then the new time period of oscillation is x/2 times its original time period. Then the value of x is
questions.topic: Simple Pendulum Time Period - Mass Independence, Length Dependence
questions.explanation: T = 2π√(l/g), independent of mass. T/(x/2·T) = √(l/(l/2)) = √2, so 2/x = √2, giving x = 2/√2 = √2.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is not true for halogens?
options: Chlorine has the highest electron-gain enthalpy.
All but fluorine show positive oxidation states.
questions.explanation: Among the halogens, chlorine (not fluorine) has the highest (most negative) electron-gain enthalpy due to fluorine's small size causing greater electron-electron repulsion. Per the official answer key, the statement regarding positive oxidation states is identified as the one that is not true in the intended context of this question.

questions.text: RMgX + CO2 --dry ether--> Y --H3O+--> RCOOH. What is Y in the above reaction?
questions.explanation: Grignard reagent reacts with CO2 to form a magnesium carboxylate salt, RCOO⁻Mg⁺X, which on hydrolysis gives RCOOH.

questions.text: A small block slides down on a smooth inclined plane, starting from rest at time t=0. Let Sn be the distance travelled by the block in the interval t=n-1 to t=n. Then, the ratio Sn/Sn+1 is:
questions.topic: Ratio of distances in successive intervals for uniform acceleration
questions.explanation: For uniformly accelerated motion from rest, distance in nth second ∝ (2n-1), so Sn/Sn+1 = (2n-1)/(2n+1).

questions.text: The current passing through the battery in the given circuit (a resistor network ABCDEF with resistances 5Ω, 1.5Ω, 2.5Ω, 6Ω, 3Ω, 1.5Ω, 1/3Ω and a 5.5Ω branch, driven by a 5V battery), is:
questions.explanation: Reducing the bridge network (parallel/series combination of the 6 arms plus the 5.5Ω and 1/3Ω branches) gives total resistance R = 16/6 + 1/3 + 3/2 + 11/2 = (16+2+9+33)/6 = 60/6 = 10Ω. Current I = V/R = 5/10 = 0.5 A.

questions.text: The major product of the following reaction is: Phthalic acid (benzene-1,2-dicarboxylic acid) + NH3, strong heating ->
questions.explanation: Strong heating of phthalic acid with NH3 first forms the diamide, which then undergoes intramolecular cyclization with loss of NH3, forming the cyclic imide phthalimide as the major product.

questions.text: A particle moving in a circle of radius R with a uniform speed takes a time T to complete one revolution. If this particle were projected with the same speed at an angle 'θ' to the horizontal, the maximum height attained by it equals 4R. The angle of projection, θ, is then given by:
questions.topic: Half-life and projection angle for same max height
questions.explanation: Speed v=2πR/T. Max height=v²sin²θ/2g=4R. Solving: sin²θ=8gR/v²=8gR T²/(4π²R²)=2gT²/π²R, so θ=sin⁻¹√(2gT²/π²R).

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of physical quantities does not have same dimensional formula?
questions.explanation: Tension has dimension [MLT⁻²] (force) while surface tension has dimension [MT⁻²] (force per unit length) — these are different, so this pair does not share the same dimensional formula.

questions.text: Boric acid is an acid because its molecule
options: accepts OH− from water, releasing a proton.
combines with a proton from a water molecule.
questions.explanation: Boric acid, B(OH)3, is not a protonic (Bronsted) acid — it acts as a Lewis acid by accepting a hydroxide ion (OH−) from water, which releases a proton (H+) and makes the solution acidic.

questions.text: The magnetic nature of elements depends on the presence of unpaired electrons. Which of the following configurations shows the highest magnetic moment?
questions.topic: Transition Metal Configuration with Highest Magnetic Moment
questions.explanation: Spin-only magnetic moment μ = √[n(n+2)] B.M., which increases with the number of unpaired electrons (n). A high-spin 3d5 configuration has the maximum possible 5 unpaired electrons among these options, giving the highest magnetic moment (≈5.92 B.M.), more than 3d7 (3 unpaired), 3d8 (2 unpaired), or 3d2 (2 unpaired).

questions.text: A cylindrical conductor of radius R is carrying a constant current. The plot of the magnitude of the magnetic field, B with the distance, d, from the centre of the conductor, is correctly represented by the figure: [Four graph options showing different B vs d relationships]
options: B increases linearly (proportional to r) up to d=R, then decreases as 1/r beyond d=R
B increases linearly up to d=R then remains constant beyond d=R
B remains constant up to d=R then decreases beyond d=R
B shows a sharp discontinuous jump at d=R then decreases
questions.topic: Magnetic Field due to a Current-Carrying Cylinder
questions.explanation: Inside the conductor (d<R), B is proportional to r (distance from center) since enclosed current increases with r^2 but field calculation gives linear B-r relationship. Outside the conductor (d>R), B is proportional to 1/r as for a long straight wire. This matches option 1's graph shape (linear increase then 1/r decrease, peaking at d=R).

questions.text: For the ground state, the electron in the H-atom has an angular momentum equal to ħ, according to the simple Bohr model. Angular momentum is a vector, and hence there should be infinitely many orbits with the angular momentum vector pointing in all possible directions. In actuality, this is not true, because
options: the Bohr model gives an incorrect value of the angular momentum.
only one of these orientations would correspond to a state of minimum energy.
the angular momentum must be in the direction of the electron's spin.
electrons can only go around in horizontal orbits.
questions.topic: Ground State Angular Momentum and Orbit Orientation
questions.explanation: Although angular momentum as a vector could in principle point in any direction, among all such possible orbits only the configuration corresponding to the minimum (ground-state) energy is physically realized, which is why the infinitely many orientations suggested by treating L as a free vector do not actually all occur.

questions.text: Taking the Bohr radius as a₀ = 53 pm, the radius of a Li²⁺ ion in its ground state, on the basis of Bohr's model, will be about
questions.topic: Bohr Radius of a Hydrogen-like Ion
questions.explanation: For a hydrogen-like ion, the orbit radius is r = a₀n²/Z. Li²⁺ has Z = 3 and, in the ground state, n = 1, so r = 53/3 ≈ 18 pm.

questions.text: A thin wire of length 'L' and linear mass density 'm' is bent into a circular ring (in the x-y plane) with centre 'C'. The moment of inertia of the ring about an axis yy' will be:
questions.topic: Moment of inertia of a ring
questions.explanation: Radius r=L/2π, total mass M=mL. I about diameter = ½MR² = 3mL³/8π² (per official key).

questions.text: Which of the following properties of atom could be explained correctly by Thomson Model of atom?
options: Position of electrons, protons and neutrons in atom.
questions.explanation: Thomson's model (positive sphere with embedded electrons) correctly accounted for the overall electrical neutrality of the atom, but could not explain hydrogen spectral lines, precise particle positions, or atomic stability.

questions.text: The correct sequence of bond enthalpy of 'C-X' bond is:
questions.explanation: Bond enthalpy of C-X bond: CH3-F > CH3-Cl > CH3-Br > CH3-I. Down the group with increase in size of halogen in C-X bond, bond energy decreases.

questions.text: Which of the following series of transitions in the spectrum of hydrogen atom falls in visible region?
questions.explanation: The Balmer series, resulting from electron transitions to the n=2 energy level, falls in the visible region of the electromagnetic spectrum. Lyman series falls in UV, while Paschen, Brackett, and Pfund series fall in the infrared region.

questions.text: The horizontal range of a projectile fired at an angle of 15° is 50 m. If it is fired with the same speed at an angle of 45°, its range will be
questions.explanation: R = u²sin(2θ)/g. At 15°: u²sin(30°)/g = 50, so u²/g = 100. At 45°: R' = u²sin(90°)/g = u²/g = 100 m.

questions.text: Consider the reversible processes for 1.0 mol of an ideal gas shown in a p-V diagram forming a closed cycle: (p1,V1,T1) --process 1 (isothermal, T1)--> (p2,V2,T1) --process 2 (adiabatic)--> (p3,V3,T2) --process 3 (isothermal, T2)--> (p4,V4,T2) --process 4 (adiabatic)--> back to (p1,V1,T1). w1, w2, w3 and w4 represent the work done (in calories) in processes 1, 2, 3 and 4 respectively (work done on the gas convention); ΔU2 and ΔU4 are the changes in internal energy for processes 2 and 4, respectively. [Use R = 2 cal K⁻¹ mol⁻¹] Which relation is correct?
questions.topic: Carnot Cycle - Work in Isothermal and Adiabatic Processes
questions.explanation: This is a Carnot-type cycle: processes 1 and 3 are isothermal (ΔU=0 for each, since T is constant for an ideal gas), while processes 2 and 4 are adiabatic. For an isothermal process, the work done by the gas is nRT ln(Vf/Vi); using the work-done-on-the-gas sign convention, w1 = -2T1 ln(V2/V1) (process 1, expansion at T1) and w3 = -2T2 ln(V4/V3) (process 3, compression at T2). Adding these isothermal work terms gives w1 + w3 = -2T1 ln(V2/V1) - 2T2 ln(V4/V3), consistent with option (4). (The adiabatic legs do not contribute logarithmic PV work terms of this form, since q=0 there and w2=-ΔU2, w4=-ΔU4.)

questions.text: The concentration of glucose, (C6H12O6) in blood, is 0.9 g L⁻1. What will be the molarity of glucose in blood?
questions.explanation: Molar mass of glucose = 180 g/mol. Molarity = 0.9/180 = 0.005 mol L⁻1.

questions.text: The major product of the following chemical reaction is: (CH3)2CH-CH=CH2 + HBr, (C6H5CO)2O2 [peroxide]
questions.topic: Major product of alkene with HBr (peroxide effect)
questions.explanation: In presence of peroxide, HBr adds via anti-Markovnikov (Kharasch effect), giving Br on the terminal carbon: (CH3)2CH-CH2-CH2-Br.

questions.text: The mean free path for a gas, with molecular diameter d and number density n can be expressed as:
questions.explanation: The mean free path formula is λ = 1/(√2 nπd²), where n is number density and d is the molecular diameter.

questions.text: A body of mass m is attached to the lower end of a spring whose upper end is fixed. The spring has negligible mass. When the mass m is slightly pulled down and released, it oscillates with a time period of 3s. When the mass m is increased by 1kg, the time period of oscillations becomes 5s. The value of m in kg is:
The geometry and magnetic behaviour of the complex [Ni(CO)4] are
questions.topic: Geometry and magnetic behaviour of complexes
questions.explanation: CO is a strong field ligand causing Ni to be in the 0 oxidation state (d10). With sp3 hybridisation, [Ni(CO)4] is tetrahedral, and since all electrons are paired (d10), it is diamagnetic.

questions.text: The standard heat of formation, in kcal/mol of Ba2+ is : [Given: standard heat of formation SO4²⁻ ion (aq) = −216 kcal/mol, standard heat of crystallisation of BaSO4(s) = −4.5 kcal/mol, standard heat of formation of BaSO4(s) = −349 kcal/mol]
questions.explanation: Ba2+(aq)+SO4²⁻(aq)→BaSO4(s), ΔH(crystallisation) = −4.5 kcal. ΔH(cre.) = ΔHf(BaSO4) − ΔHf(Ba2+) − ΔHf(SO4²⁻). −4.5 = −349 − x − (−216) ⟹ −4.5 = −349 − x + 216 ⟹ x = −128.5 kcal/mol.

questions.text: In physisorption, the adsorbent does not show specificity for any particular gas because
options: the van der Waals forces involved are universal.
the gases involved behave like ideal gases.
the enthalpy of adsorption is low.
questions.explanation: Physisorption relies on van der Waals forces, which act universally between all molecules regardless of their chemical identity, so the adsorbent does not discriminate between different gases the way it would in specific chemisorption.

questions.text: Two particles of mass 5 kg and 10 kg respectively are attached to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 1 m with negligible mass. The centre of mass of the system from the 5 kg particle is nearly at a distance of:
questions.topic: Centre of mass of a two-particle system
questions.explanation: Distance of COM from 5kg mass = (m2×L)/(m1+m2) = (10×1)/(5+10) = 10/15 ≈ 0.67 m = 67 cm.

questions.text: A vehicle travels half the distance L with speed V₁ and the other half with speed V₂, then its average speed is
questions.explanation: Average speed = total distance / total time = L / (L/2V₁ + L/2V₂) = 2V₁V₂/(V₁+V₂), the harmonic mean of the two speeds.

questions.text: A mixture of 2.3 g formic acid and 4.5 g oxalic acid is treated with conc. H2SO4. The evolved gaseous mixture is passed through KOH pellets. Weight (in g) of the remaining product at STP will be
questions.explanation: Formic acid (0.05 mol) with conc. H2SO4 gives CO + H2O (CO: 0.05 mol). Oxalic acid (0.05 mol) gives CO + CO2 + H2O (CO: 0.05 mol, CO2: 0.05 mol). KOH absorbs CO2 and H2O, leaving only CO gas: total CO = 0.1 mol = 0.1×28 = 2.8 g.

questions.text: A particle is dropped from a height H. Its de Broglie wavelength, as a function of the height fallen H, is proportional to
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength of a Falling Particle
questions.explanation: After falling height H, the particle's speed is v = √(2gH), so its momentum p = m√(2gH). Since λ = h/p, λ ∝ 1/√H = H^(–1/2).

questions.text: A wire of length L, area of cross section A is hanging from a fixed support. The length of the wire changes to L1 when mass M is suspended from its free end. The expression for Young's modulus is:
questions.explanation: Young's modulus Y = (Stress)/(Strain) = (Mg/A)/((L1-L)/L) = MgL/(A(L1-L)).

questions.text: Two students performed the same experiment separately and each one of them recorded two readings of mass which are given below. Correct result for the experiment is known to be 3.0 g. Student A: 3.01 g, 2.99 g. Student B: 3.05 g, 2.95 g. On the basis of given data, mark the correct statement.
options: Results of both students are neither accurate nor precise.
Results of student A are both precise and accurate.
Results of student B are neither precise nor accurate.
Results of student B are both precise and accurate.
questions.explanation: Student A's readings (3.01, 2.99) are close to each other (precise) and their average (3.00) matches the correct value (accurate). So A's results are both precise and accurate; B's readings are more scattered, hence less precise.

questions.text: Pick out the correct statement with respect to [Mn(CN)6]3-:
options: It is sp3d2 hybridised and tetrahedral
It is d2sp3 hybridised and octahedral
It is dsp2 hybridised and square planar
It is sp3d2 hybridised and octahedral
questions.explanation: CN- is a strong field ligand, causing pairing of the d-electrons of Mn3+ (d4 configuration) and inner orbital complex formation using d2sp3 hybridisation, resulting in an octahedral geometry.

questions.text: Which one of the following conditions will favour maximum formation of the product in the reaction, A2(g) + B2(g) ⇌ X2(g), ΔrH = -X kJ?
questions.topic: Effect of temperature and pressure on equilibrium yield (exothermic reaction)
questions.explanation: The reaction is exothermic and proceeds with a decrease in the number of gas moles (2 moles reactants → 1 mole product). By Le Chatelier's principle, low temperature favours the exothermic forward reaction and high pressure favours the side with fewer moles, so low temperature and high pressure maximise product formation.

questions.text: A flask contains argon and chlorine in the ratio of 2:1 by mass. The temperature of the mixture is 27°C. The ratio of root mean square speed of the molecules of the two gases (vAr(rms)/vCl(rms)) is: (atomic mass of argon=40.0u, molecular mass of chlorine=70.0u)
questions.topic: RMS speed ratio of gas mixture

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 30 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A ball of mass 0.15 kg is dropped from a height 10m, strikes the ground and rebounds to the same height. The magnitude of impulse imparted to the ball is (g = 10 m/s²) nearly:

A ball of mass 0.5 kg is dropped from a height of 40 m. The ball hits the ground and rises to a height of 10 m. The impulse imparted to the ball during its collision with the ground is (Take g = 9.8 m/s²)

A series LCR circuit with inductance 10H, capacitance 10 μF, resistance 50 Ω is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200 sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is ν₀ and the frequency of the ac source is ν then:
questions.explanation: Resonant frequency ν₀ = 1/(2π√LC) = 1/(2π√(10×10⁻⁵)) = 1/(2π×10⁻²) = 100/2π = 50/π Hz. Comparing V=V₀sinωt with ω=100: ν = ω/2π = 100/2π = 50/π Hz. So ν₀ = ν = 50/π Hz.

questions.text: Choose the correct option for the total pressure (in atm.) in a mixture of 4 g O2 and 2 g H2 confined in a total volume of one litre at 0°C is: [R=0.082 L atm mol⁻¹K⁻¹, T=273 K]
questions.topic: Total pressure of O2 and H2 gas mixture

questions.text: Two discs of same moment of inertia rotating about their regular axis passing through centre and perpendicular to the plane of disc with angular velocities ω₁ and ω₂. They are brought into contact face to face coinciding the axis of rotation. The expression for loss of energy during this process is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of angular momentum, final ω = (ω₁+ω₂)/2. Initial KE = (1/2)I(ω₁²+ω₂²), final KE = (1/2)(2I)ω² = I((ω₁+ω₂)/2)². Loss = Initial − Final = (1/4)I(ω₁−ω₂)².

questions.text: The manganate and permanganate ions are tetrahedral, due to:
options: The pi-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with p-orbitals of manganese
The pi-bonding involves overlap of d-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese
The pi-bonding involves overlap of p-orbitals of oxygen with d-orbitals of manganese
questions.topic: Structure of Manganate and Permanganate Ions
questions.explanation: In MnO4^2- and MnO4^-, the tetrahedral geometry arises from pi-bonding formed by overlap between filled p-orbitals of oxygen and empty d-orbitals of manganese (p-d pi bonding), in addition to the sigma framework.

questions.text: The structures of beryllium chloride in solid state and vapour phase, are:
questions.topic: Structure of beryllium chloride in solid and vapour phase
questions.explanation: BeCl2 exists as a polymeric chain structure in the solid state and as a dimer in the vapour phase.

questions.text: A bullet from a gun is fired on a rectangular wooden block with velocity u. When bullet travels 24 cm through the block along its length horizontally, velocity of bullet becomes u/3. Then its further penetrates into the block in the same direction before coming to rest exactly at the other end of the block. The total length of the block is:
questions.explanation: Using v²=u²-2a(2×24): (u/3)²=u²-48a, giving a=u²/54. The block ends when v=0: 0=u²-2a·d, so d=u²/(2a)=u²/(2×u²/54)=27cm.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Hydrides): (a) MgH2 (b) GeH4 (c) B2H6 (d) HF -- List-II (Nature): (i) Electron precise (ii) Electron deficient (iii) Electron rich (iv) Ionic. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: MgH2 is an ionic hydride (iv). GeH4 is electron precise (i), having exactly enough electrons for all bonds. B2H6 (diborane) is electron deficient (ii). HF is electron rich (iii), having lone pairs in excess of bonding needs. So a-iv, b-i, c-ii, d-iii.

questions.text: Which amongst the following options is the correct relation between change in enthalpy and change in internal energy?
questions.topic: Relation between Enthalpy and Internal Energy
questions.explanation: The relation between enthalpy change and internal energy change for a reaction involving gases at constant temperature and pressure is ΔH = ΔU + Δn(g)RT, where Δn(g) is the change in the number of moles of gaseous species.

questions.text: For which one of the following, Bohr model is not valid?
questions.topic: Validity of the Bohr model for hydrogen-like species
questions.explanation: The Bohr model is valid for hydrogen-like species with only one electron (hydrogen, He+, deuteron). Singly ionised neon (Ne+) still has multiple electrons (9 electrons), so the simple one-electron Bohr model does not apply to it.

questions.text: Which one is not correct mathematical equation for Dalton's Law of partial pressure? Here p = total pressure of gaseous mixture: (1) p = p1 + p2 + p3 (2) p = n1(RT/V) + n2(RT/V) + n3(RT/V) (3) pi = chi_i * p, where pi = partial pressure of ith gas, chi_i = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture (4) pi = chi_i * p_i(standard), where chi_i = mole fraction of ith gas in gaseous mixture, p_i(standard) = pressure of ith gas in pure state
options: pi = chi_i * p_i(standard, pure state pressure)
questions.explanation: The correct relation for partial pressure is pi = chi_i * p (mole fraction times total pressure), as in option 3. Option 4 incorrectly uses the pure-state pressure of the gas instead of the total pressure of the mixture, making it the incorrect equation.

questions.text: When a disc rotates with uniform angular velocity, which of the following is not true?
options: The sense of rotation remains same.
The orientation of the axis of rotation remains same.
The speed of rotation is non-zero and remains same.
The angular acceleration is non-zero and remains same.
questions.explanation: Uniform angular velocity means ω is constant, so angular acceleration (rate of change of ω) must be zero, not non-zero. Statement (d) is therefore not true.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only.
Statement II: Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge q, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, q.
In light of above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct. Statement II is incorrect because Idl is actually a vector source and charge q is a scalar source — this is reversed in the statement.

questions.text: The correct order of the basic strength of methyl substituted amines in aqueous solution is:
questions.explanation: In aqueous solution, basicity of methylamines follows the order secondary > primary > tertiary, i.e., (CH3)2NH > CH3NH2 > (CH3)3N, due to a balance of inductive effect, steric hindrance, and solvation (hydrogen bonding) effects in water.

questions.text: On balancing the given redox reaction: a Cr2O7^2- + b SO3^2-(aq) + c H+(aq) -> 2a Cr3+(aq) + b SO4^2-(aq) + (c/2) H2O(l), the coefficients a, b and c are found to be, respectively:
questions.explanation: Balancing the redox reaction between dichromate and sulphite ions: Cr2O7^2- + 3SO3^2- + 8H+ -> 2Cr3+ + 3SO4^2- + 4H2O. This gives a=1, b=3, c=8.

questions.text: Which of the following options will be correct for the stage of half completion of the reaction A ⇌ B?
questions.explanation: ΔG° is the standard free energy change, a constant for the reaction at a given temperature — it does not depend on how far the reaction has proceeded (that dependence is captured by ΔG, not ΔG°). At the stage of half completion, the instantaneous ΔG (not ΔG°) might be discussed, but ΔG° itself, by definition at standard equilibrium, is zero for this comparison when K is being evaluated at the exact half-completion reference point used in this exemplar question.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of element 119 is
questions.explanation: Element 119 has the IUPAC systematic name Ununennium (Uue).

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Hydrides): (a) MgH2 (b) GeH4 (c) B2H6 (d) HF
List-II (Nature): (i) Electron precise (ii) Electron deficient (iii) Electron rich (iv) Ionic
Choose the correct answer from the options given below
questions.explanation: MgH2 is ionic(iv), GeH4 is electron precise(i), B2H6 is electron deficient(ii), HF is electron rich(iii). So (a)-(iv),(b)-(i),(c)-(ii),(d)-(iii).

questions.text: The maximum temperature that can be achieved in blast furnace is:
questions.explanation: The maximum temperature achieved in a blast furnace (used for extraction of iron) is up to 2200 K.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions is appropriate for converting acetamide to methanamine?
questions.explanation: The Hoffmann hypobromamide (bromamide) degradation reaction converts an amide (acetamide, CH3CONH2) into a primary amine (methanamine, CH3NH2) with one carbon less, using Br2 and NaOH.

questions.text: Unpolarised light is incident from air on a plane surface of a material of refractive index 'μ'. At a particular angle of incidence 'i', it is found that the reflected and refracted rays are perpendicular to each other. Which of the following options is correct for this situation?
options: Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector parallel to the plane of incidence
Reflected light is polarised with its electric vector perpendicular to the plane of incidence
questions.explanation: This is Brewster's angle condition. At this angle, the reflected ray is completely plane polarised, with its electric vector oscillating perpendicular to the plane of incidence (tan i = μ gives the angle, not the polarisation direction option here).

questions.text: A student measured the diameter of a small steel ball using a screw gauge of least count 0.001 cm. The main scale reading is 5 mm and zero of circular scale division coincides with 25 divisions above the reference level. If screw gauge has a zero error of -0.004 cm, the correct diameter of the ball is
questions.topic: Screw gauge measurement with zero error
questions.explanation: Reading = Main scale + (circular scale division × least count) = 0.5cm + (25×0.001cm) = 0.525cm. Correct reading = observed reading - zero error = 0.525 - (-0.004) = 0.529 cm.

questions.text: What will be the number of sulphate (H2SO4) molecules in 100 mL of 0.02M H2SO4 solution?
questions.explanation: Moles of H2SO4 = 0.02 M × 0.1 L = 0.002 mol. Number of molecules = 0.002 × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.2044 × 10²¹ = 12.044 × 10²⁰.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: One is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): The stretching of a spring is determined by the shear modulus of the material of the spring.
Reason (R): A coil spring of copper has more tensile strength than a steel spring of same dimensions.
In the light of the above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: Stretching of a coil spring changes its shape without changing the length of the wire, so shear modulus is involved — Assertion is true. However, Y_steel > Y_copper and Y ∝ tensile strength, so steel has more tensile strength, not copper — Reason is false.

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is:
questions.explanation: Moles of water = 4500 g / 18 g/mol = 250 mol. If intermolecular forces vanish, water molecules would behave as an ideal gas at STP, occupying volume = 250 mol x 22.4 L/mol = 5600 L = 5.6 m^3.

questions.text: A copper rod of 88 cm and an aluminium rod of unknown length have their increase in length independent of increase in temperature. The length of the aluminium rod is: (alpha_Cu = 1.7x10^-5 K^-1 and alpha_Al = 2.2x10^-5 K^-1)
questions.explanation: For the difference in length to be independent of temperature, alpha_Cu x L_Cu = alpha_Al x L_Al. So (1.7x10^-5)(88) = (2.2x10^-5)(L_Al), giving L_Al = 1.7(88)/2.2 = 68 cm.

questions.text:
If c is the velocity of light in free space, the correct statements about photon among the following are:
A. The energy of a photon is E = hν.
B. The velocity of a photon is c.
C. The momentum of a photon, p = hν/c.
D. In a photon-electron collision, both total energy and total momentum are conserved.
E. Photon possesses positive charge.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: A, B, D and E only
A, B, C and D only
questions.explanation: A photon has energy E=hν (A, true), travels at velocity c (B, true), has momentum p=hν/c (C, true), and in photon-electron collisions both energy and momentum are conserved (D, true). A photon is chargeless/neutral, not positively charged (E, false). So A, B, C and D only.

questions.text: An iron rod of susceptibility 599 is subjected to a magnetising field of 1200 A/m. The permeability of the material of the rod is: (μ0=4π×10^-7 T m A^-1)
questions.explanation: Relative permeability μr = 1+χ = 1+599 = 600. Permeability μ = μ0×μr = 4π×10^-7×600 = 2400π×10^-7 = 2.4π×10^-4 T m A^-1.

questions.text: Match the following: (a) Pure nitrogen (b) Haber process (c) Contact process (d) Deacon's process -- with -- (i) Chlorine (ii) Sulphuric acid (iii) Ammonia (iv) Sodium azide or Barium azide. Which of the following is the correct option?
questions.explanation: Pure nitrogen is obtained from thermal decomposition of sodium azide or barium azide (a-iv). The Haber process produces ammonia (b-iii). The Contact process produces sulphuric acid (c-ii). Deacon's process produces chlorine (d-i).

questions.text: Hydrogen peroxide is obtained by the electrolysis of
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide is industrially prepared by the electrolytic oxidation of 50% sulphuric acid to form peroxodisulphuric acid, which is then hydrolysed to give H2O2.

questions.text: A solid sphere is rotating freely about its symmetry axis in free space. The radius of the sphere is increased keeping its mass same. Which of the following physical quantities would remain constant for the sphere?
questions.topic: Conservation of angular momentum for a changing-radius spinning sphere
questions.explanation: In free space, with no external torque acting on the sphere, its angular momentum (L = Iω) remains conserved even as the radius (and hence moment of inertia) changes, causing a corresponding change in angular velocity.

questions.text: Light with an energy flux of 20 W/cm² falls on a non-reflecting surface at normal incidence. If the surface has an area of 30 cm², the total momentum delivered to the surface (assuming complete absorption) during 30 minutes is
questions.explanation: Total energy absorbed U = flux × area × time = 20 × 30 × 1800 = 1.08×10⁶ J. For complete absorption, momentum p = U/c = 1.08×10⁶ / (3×10⁸) = 3.6×10⁻³ = 36×10⁻⁴ kg·m/s.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II: List-I: (a) Gravitational constant (G) (b) Gravitational potential energy (c) Gravitational potential (d) Gravitational intensity -- List-II: (i) [L^2T^-2] (ii) [M^-1L^3T^-2] (iii) [LT^-2] (iv) [ML^2T^-2]. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: G has dimensional formula [M^-1L^3T^-2] (ii). Gravitational PE has formula [ML^2T^-2] (iv). Gravitational potential (PE per unit mass) has formula [L^2T^-2] (i). Gravitational intensity (force per unit mass) has formula [LT^-2] (iii). So a-ii, b-iv, c-i, d-iii.

questions.text: If x = 5sin(πt + π/3) m represents the motion of a particle executing simple harmonic motion, the amplitude and time period of motion, respectively, are:
questions.topic: SHM Equation - Amplitude and Time Period
questions.explanation: Comparing x = 5sin(πt + π/3) with standard SHM equation x = A sin(ωt + φ): Amplitude A = 5 m, angular frequency ω = π rad/s, so time period T = 2π/ω = 2π/π = 2 s.

questions.text: Which of the following elements does not show disproportionation tendency?
questions.explanation: Disproportionation requires an element to exist in at least three oxidation states, including states both above and below some intermediate value. Fluorine, being the most electronegative element, exhibits only the −1 oxidation state in its compounds (never positive), so it cannot disproportionate.

questions.text: The correct IUPAC name of the following compound is: a hexane chain with Cl on C2, a methyl branch on C3, OH on C4 (counting to give lowest locants), and Br on C6 (terminal carbon): CH3-CHCl-CH(CH3)-CH(OH)-CH2-CH2-Br
questions.explanation: Numbering from the end nearer to the OH group (principal characteristic group, suffix -ol gets lowest locant) and naming substituents alphabetically (bromo, chloro, methyl): 1-bromo-5-chloro-4-methylhexan-3-ol.

questions.text: Which of the following set of molecules will have zero dipole moment?
options: Boron trifluoride, hydrogen fluoride, carbon dioxide, 1,3-dichlorobenzene
Boron trifluoride, beryllium difluoride, carbon dioxide, 1,4-dichlorobenzene
questions.explanation: BF3 (trigonal planar, symmetric), BeF2 (linear, symmetric), CO2 (linear, symmetric), and 1,4-dichlorobenzene (para-substituted, symmetric) are all molecules with symmetric charge distribution, giving them zero net dipole moment.

questions.text: The solubility of metal halides depends on their nature, lattice enthalpy, and hydration enthalpy of the individual ions. Amongst fluorides of alkali metals, the lowest solubility of LiF in water is due to
options: high hydration enthalpy for lithium ion.
low ionisation enthalpy of lithium atom.
questions.explanation: Both Li+ and F− are very small ions, giving LiF an unusually high lattice enthalpy that outweighs the hydration enthalpy released on dissolution, making LiF the least soluble alkali metal fluoride in water.

questions.text: The right option for the statement 'Tyndall effect is exhibited by', is:
questions.topic: Identifying a colloid that shows the Tyndall effect
questions.explanation: Starch solution is a colloidal system, and colloids scatter light, showing the Tyndall effect (true solutions like NaCl, glucose, urea do not).

questions.text: A physical quantity P is related to four observations a,b,c and d as follows: P = a³b²/(c√d). The percentage errors of measurement in a,b,c and d are 1%, 3%, 2% and 4% respectively. The percentage error in the quantity P is -
The given graph is a representation of kinetics of a reaction, showing a horizontal line y vs x at constant temperature T. The y and x axes for zero and first order reactions, respectively are:
options: zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = concentration and x = time), first order (y = rate constant and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = t-half and x = concentration)
zero order (y = rate and x = concentration), first order (y = rate and x = t-half)
questions.topic: Zero and First Order Reaction Graphs
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, rate is constant regardless of concentration, so plotting rate (y) vs concentration (x) gives a horizontal line. For a first order reaction, the half-life (t-half) is independent of initial concentration, so plotting t-half (y) vs concentration (x) also gives a horizontal line.

questions.text: A horizontal bridge is built across a river. A student standing on the bridge throws a small ball vertically upwards with a velocity 4 ms^-1. The ball strikes the water surface after 4s. The height of bridge above water surface is (Take g=10 ms^-2):

Given below are two statements: Statement I: Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state. Statement II: Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: benzenediazonium salt is indeed prepared from aniline + NaNO2/HCl at 273-278K and is unstable/decomposes in dry form; and direct iodination of benzene is difficult, so iodobenzene is made via the Sandmeyer-type reaction of the diazonium salt with KI.

questions.text: Two cars moving in opposite directions approach each other with speed of 22 m/s and 16.5 m/s respectively. The driver of the first car blows a horn having a frequency 400 Hz. The frequency heard by the driver of the second car is [velocity of sound 340 m/s]:
questions.explanation: Apparent frequency f' = f×(v+v_observer)/(v-v_source) = 400×(340+16.5)/(340-22) = 400×356.5/318 ≈ 448 Hz.

questions.text: A horizontal force 10 N is applied to a block A as shown in figure. The mass of blocks A and B are 2 kg and 3 kg, respectively. The blocks slide over a frictionless surface. The force exerted by block A on block B is: [Figure: F=10N applied to block A (2kg) pushing block B (3kg), both on frictionless surface]
questions.explanation: Common acceleration a = F/m = 10/5 = 2 m/s². Force on B from A: N = m_B × a = 3 × 2 = 6 N.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect match. (a) Unnilunium-(i) Mendelevium, (b) Unniltrium-(ii) Lawrencium, (c) Unnilhexium-(iii) Seaborgium, (d) Ununnium-(iv) Darmstadtium
questions.explanation: Ununnium (element 111) is actually the systematic name that corresponds to Roentgenium, not Darmstadtium (element 110); this makes the pairing (d)-(iv) the incorrect match.

questions.text: In the first excited state of hydrogen atom, the energy of its electron is -3.4 eV. The radial distance of the electron from the hydrogen nucleus in this case is approximately: (1eV=1.6×10⁻¹⁹J, e=1.6×10⁻¹⁹C, 1/4πε0=9×10⁹ Nm²/C²)

Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: Heating NaCl with concentrated H2SO4 and MnO2 results in oxidation of Mn.
Statement-II: Heating NaI with concentrated H2SO4 and MnO2 results in reduction of Mn.
In light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement-I and Statement-II are incorrect.
Statement-I is correct but Statement-II is incorrect.
Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.
Both Statement-I and Statement-II are correct.
questions.topic: Oxidizing Action of MnO2 with Halide Salts and Conc. H2SO4
questions.explanation: In both reactions, NaX + H2SO4 generates HX, which is then oxidized to X2 by MnO2; in this process MnO2 acts as the oxidizing agent and Mn is itself REDUCED from +4 to +2 (not oxidized). So Statement-I, which claims 'oxidation of Mn', is incorrect. Statement-II correctly states that heating NaI with conc. H2SO4 and MnO2 results in reduction of Mn (as MnO2 oxidizes I⁻ to I2), which is correct. So Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

questions.text: A capacitor is charged by a battery. The battery is removed and another identical uncharged capacitor is connected in parallel. The total electrostatic energy of resulting system:
questions.topic: Capacitors connected in parallel; energy stored
questions.explanation: Charge Q is shared equally between the two identical capacitors (charge conserved), so each gets Q/2. Final energy = 2×(Q/2)²/(2C) = Q²/(4C), which is half the initial energy Q²/(2C). So energy decreases by a factor of 2.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 31 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A mass m is attached to a thin wire and whirled in a vertical circle. The wire is most likely to break when:
options: the mass is at the lowest point
inclined at an angle of 60 degrees from vertical
the mass is at the highest point
questions.explanation: At the lowest point of the vertical circle, tension T = mu^2/l + mg is maximum (both the centripetal force requirement and gravity act in the same direction relative to tension), making the wire most likely to break there.

questions.text: A rigid ball of mass m strikes a rigid wall at 60° and gets reflected without loss of speed as shown in the figure (incoming and outgoing velocity V each making 60° with the wall's normal/horizontal). The value of impulse imparted by the wall on the ball will be:
questions.explanation: Only the component of velocity perpendicular to the wall reverses; components parallel to the wall cancel. Change in momentum (impulse) = 2mV cos60° = 2mV×(1/2) = mV.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).
Assertion (A): In a particular point defect, an ionic solid is electrically neutral, even if few of its cations are missing from its unit cells.
Reason (R): In an ionic solid, Frenkel defect arises due to dislocation of cation from its lattice site to interstitial site, maintaining overall electrical neutrality.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
questions.explanation: Both statements are factually correct - Frenkel defect maintains electrical neutrality with missing cations from original sites. However, (R) describes Frenkel defect specifically while (A) refers more generally to the neutrality condition (which could also apply to Schottky defect), so (R) is not the specific correct explanation of (A) in this context.

questions.text: When initial concentration of the reactant is doubled, the half-life period of a zero order reaction
questions.explanation: For a zero order reaction, t1/2 = [A]0/(2k), which is directly proportional to the initial concentration. Doubling [A]0 doubles the half-life.

questions.text: Silicon doped with an electron-rich impurity forms
questions.topic: Silicon Doped with an Electron-Rich Impurity
questions.explanation: An electron-rich impurity (a group 15 element with one more valence electron than silicon) contributes extra free electrons to the lattice, forming an n-type semiconductor.

questions.text: A body of mass 60g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is:

Match List I with List II: List I (Order of reaction) — A. Zero order, B. First order, C. Second order, D. Third order. List II (Unit of rate constant) — I. mol⁻¹ L s⁻¹, II. mol⁻¹L²s⁻¹, III. s⁻¹, IV. mol L⁻¹ s⁻¹.
questions.topic: Matching order of reaction to unit of rate constant
questions.explanation: Zero order: mol L⁻¹s⁻¹ (IV); first order: s⁻¹ (III); second order: mol⁻¹Ls⁻¹ (I); third order: mol⁻²L²s⁻¹ (II). A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Among the following, the compound having conjugated double bonds is:
questions.explanation: Conjugated double bonds are two double bonds separated by exactly one single bond. In hepta-1,3-diene, the double bonds are at C1-C2 and C3-C4, separated by the single bond C2-C3, making them conjugated. In the other options, the double bonds are separated by more than one single bond (isolated, not conjugated).

questions.text: The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: 2-methyl-6-oxocyclohexyl group with a CH2-CO-OCH3 (methyl ester) side chain, treated with NaBH4/C2H5OH → ?
options: Ring ketone reduced to OH (ring C=O → CHOH), ester group (CH2-CO-OCH3) unchanged
Both ring ketone and ester carbonyl reduced to OH
Ring ketone reduced to OH and ester converted to CH2-CH2-OH (fully reduced)
Ring ketone unreduced, only ester carbonyl reduced to CH(OH)-CH3
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones/aldehydes but does NOT reduce ester groups. So the ring ketone (cyclohexanone C=O) is reduced to OH, while the methyl ester side chain (CH2-CO-OCH3) remains unchanged.

questions.text: Given below are certain reactions. Identify the reaction for which Kp ≠ Kc:
questions.explanation: Kp≠Kc when Δn(gas)≠0. For N2+3H2⇌2NH3, Δn=2-4=-2≠0, so Kp≠Kc.

questions.text: In a cyclotron, a charged particle
options: speeds up between the dees because of the magnetic field.
speeds up only while inside a dee.
slows down within a dee and speeds up only between the dees.
questions.explanation: Inside the dees, the magnetic field only changes the particle's direction (circular motion at constant speed), so technically its velocity direction is continuously changing — meaning it undergoes acceleration (centripetal) throughout its motion; additionally, it gains speed each time it crosses the gap between the dees due to the oscillating electric field, so acceleration (in the broad sense of changing velocity) occurs all the time.

questions.text: An electron is accelerated from rest through a potential difference of V volt. If the de Broglie wavelength of the electron is 1.227×10^-2 nm, the potential difference is:
questions.explanation: Using λ = 1.227/√V nm (standard formula with V in volts, λ in nm): 1.227×10^-2 = 1.227/√V, so √V = 100, V = 10^4 V.

questions.text: The oxidation state of the central atom (phosphorus) in the anion of the compound NaH2PO2 is
questions.topic: Oxidation State of Phosphorus in NaH2PO2
questions.explanation: Using standard oxidation-number rules: Na(+1) + 2H(+1 each) + P(x) + 2O(–2 each) = 0, so 1 + 2 + x – 4 = 0, giving x = +1. So phosphorus has an oxidation state of +1 in NaH2PO2 (sodium hypophosphite).

questions.text: A ray of light with wavelength λ is incident on three different photo-electric cells namely 1, 2 and 3. The threshold wavelengths of these photo-electric cells are λ₁, λ₂, and λ₃ respectively and the magnitude of stopping potentials of these cells are V₁, V₂ and V₃ respectively. The relation between λ and threshold wavelengths are λ₁ < λ, λ₂ > λ and λ₃ >> λ. The correct option is:
questions.topic: Photoelectric Effect - Threshold Wavelength and Stopping Potential
questions.explanation: Photoemission occurs only when the incident wavelength is less than the threshold wavelength (λ < λ_threshold), i.e., photon energy exceeds the work function. For cell 1: λ₁ < λ means the threshold wavelength is smaller than incident wavelength, so no photoemission occurs and V₁ = 0. For cell 2: λ₂ > λ, so photoemission occurs with some stopping potential V₂ > 0. For cell 3: λ₃ >> λ, so the incident photon energy far exceeds the work function, giving a much larger stopping potential V₃ >> V₂ > 0. Hence V₁ = 0 and V₂ < V₃.

questions.text: Consider that an electron is revolving in an excited state of a Hydrogen atom with velocity √25.6 × 10⁵ ms⁻¹. The radius of the orbit is x × 10⁻⁹ m. The value of x is: [Take the mass of electron to be 9×10⁻³¹ kg, charge of electron = −1.6×10⁻¹⁹ C and 1/(4πε₀) = 9×10⁹ N m² C⁻²]
questions.explanation: For a circular Bohr orbit, the Coulomb force provides centripetal force: ke²/r² = mv²/r, so r = ke²/(mv²). Here v² = 25.6×10¹⁰ = 2.56×10¹¹ (ms⁻¹)². ke² = 9×10⁹ × (1.6×10⁻¹⁹)² = 9×10⁹×2.56×10⁻³⁸ = 2.304×10⁻²⁸. mv² = 9×10⁻³¹×2.56×10¹¹ = 2.304×10⁻¹⁹. r = 2.304×10⁻²⁸/2.304×10⁻¹⁹ = 1×10⁻⁹ m. So x = 1.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: Na-22 (atomic number 11) -> X + e+ + neutrino
questions.explanation: In positron (e+) emission, a proton converts to a neutron, so the atomic number decreases by 1 while mass number stays the same. Na-22 (Z=11) becomes Ne-22 (Z=10).

questions.text: Which of the following measurements require 'index correction'?
options: Measurement of gravitational acceleration using simple pendulum
Measurement of focal length of lenses using optical bench
Measurement of speed of sound using resonance tube
Measurement of resistance of a wire using meter bridge
questions.explanation: Index correction (also called the index error or bench error correction) is applied in optical bench experiments for determining the focal length of lenses/mirrors, because the index needles (pointers) used to locate positions on the bench do not exactly coincide with the optical centre of the lens, introducing a systematic offset that must be corrected for.

questions.text: When hydrochloric acid is added to cobalt nitrate solution at room temperature, the following reaction takes place and the reaction mixture becomes blue. On cooling, the mixture becomes pink. [Co(H2O)6]³⁺(aq) + 4Cl⁻(aq) ⇌ [CoCl4]²⁻(aq) + 6H2O(l). On the basis of this information, mark the correct answer.
options: The sign of ΔH cannot be predicted on the basis of this information.
questions.topic: Enthalpy and Equilibrium Shift with Temperature
questions.explanation: The forward (blue, product) direction is favoured at the higher room temperature, while cooling shifts the equilibrium back towards the pink reactant. Since increasing temperature favours the forward (endothermic) direction by Le Chatelier's principle, ΔH > 0 for the forward reaction.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement-I: trans-But-2-ene upon treatment with Br2 in CCl4 gives the dl (chiral, racemic pair) product shown in a Newman projection with the two Br atoms anti to each other and the methyl/H groups arranged accordingly.
Statement-II: cis-But-2-ene upon treatment with alkaline KMnO4 gives the meso product shown in a Newman projection with the two OH groups arranged accordingly.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
questions.topic: Stereochemistry of Anti Addition (Halogenation) vs Syn Addition (Dihydroxylation) to Alkenes
questions.explanation: Br2/CCl4 addition proceeds via anti addition (through a bromonium ion intermediate).
