For anti addition to a TRANS-alkene, the product is the MESO compound (not the dl/chiral pair), so Statement-I's depicted product is incorrect. Alkaline KMnO4 dihydroxylation proceeds via syn addition (both OH groups added to the same face). For syn addition to a CIS-alkene, the product is the MESO compound, so Statement-II correctly depicts the meso-2,3-butanediol product. Hence Statement-I is incorrect but Statement-II is correct.

questions.text: Let T1 and T2 be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T1:T2 is:
questions.topic: Bohr Model - Energy of Excited States
questions.explanation: Energy in nth state E_n = -13.6/n^2 eV. First excited state is n=2, second excited state is n=3. T1:T2 = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4.

questions.text: In a double slit experiment, when light of wavelength 400 nm was used, the angular width of the first minima formed on a screen placed 1 m away, was found to be 0.2 degrees. What will be the angular width of the first minima, if the entire experimental apparatus is immersed in water? (mu_water = 4/3)
questions.explanation: Angular width is proportional to wavelength. In water, wavelength changes to lambda' = lambda/mu = (3/4)*lambda. New angular width = 0.2 x (3/4) = 0.15 degrees.

questions.text: Which of the following gases is not a greenhouse gas?
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide (CO) is a toxic pollutant but is not classified as a greenhouse gas, unlike ozone, methane, and water vapour, which all trap infrared radiation.

questions.text: The intermediate compound X in the following chemical reaction is: Toluene + CrO2Cl2, CS2 → X, then H3O+ → Benzaldehyde
questions.explanation: This is the Etard reaction. The intermediate X formed is Ph-CH(OCrOHCl2)2, a chromium complex, which on hydrolysis with H3O+ gives benzaldehyde.

questions.text: Two pendulums of length 121 cm and 100 cm start vibrating in phase. At some instant, the two are at their mean position in the same phase. The minimum number of vibrations of the shorter pendulum after which the two are again in phase at the mean position is:
questions.explanation: T is proportional to sqrt(L). T1/T2 = sqrt(121/100) = 11/10. They are back in phase when n2*T2 = n1*T1, i.e., n2/n1 = T1/T2 = 11/10. The minimum integers satisfying this are n2(shorter pendulum, faster)=11, n1(longer)=10.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statement, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct - nitro group is electron withdrawing, increasing acidic strength of nitrophenol compared to phenol. Statement II is incorrect because o-, m-, and p-nitrophenol do NOT have the same acidic strength; they differ due to differences in resonance and inductive effects based on position (order: p-nitrophenol > o-nitrophenol > m-nitrophenol in Ka, though exact order can vary by effect considered).

questions.text: As the temperature increases, the electrical resistance:
options: Increases for both conductors and semiconductors
Decreases for both conductors and semiconductors
Increases for conductors but decreases for semiconductors
Decreases for conductors but increases for semiconductors
questions.explanation: For conductors, resistance increases with temperature due to increased lattice vibrations scattering electrons. For semiconductors, resistance decreases with temperature because more charge carriers become available as electrons gain energy to jump the band gap.

questions.text: An electron falls from rest through a vertical distance h in a uniform and vertically upward directed electric field E. The direction of electric field is now reversed, keeping its magnitude the same. A proton is allowed to fall from rest in it through the same vertical distance h. The time of fall of the electron, in comparison to the time of fall of the proton, is
questions.topic: Electron and proton falling under a reversed electric field
questions.explanation: Since the electron has a much smaller mass than the proton, the acceleration a=eE/m experienced by the electron under the same force is much larger, so the electron falls through the same distance h in a much smaller time compared to the proton.

questions.text: The temperature of a gas is -50°C. To what temperature the gas should be heated so that the rms speed is increased by 3 times?
questions.explanation: V ∝ √T. Initial T1 = -50°C = 223 K. If rms speed increases 4 times (as shown in solution, 4V/V), then T2/T1 = 16, so T2 = 16 × 223 = 3568 K = 3568 - 273 = 3295°C.

questions.text: In the electrochemical cell: Zn | ZnSO4 (0.01 M) || CuSO4 (1.0 M) | Cu, the emf of this Daniel cell is E1. When the concentration of ZnSO4 is changed to 1.0 M and that of CuSO4 changed to 0.01 M, the emf changes to E2. From the following, which one is the relationship between E1 and E2? (Given RT/F = 0.059)
questions.explanation: By the Nernst equation, E = E_cell_standard - (0.059/2) log([Zn2+]/[Cu2+]). In the first case [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] = 0.01/1 = 0.01 (small, so E1 is relatively high), while in the second case [Zn2+]/[Cu2+] = 1/0.01 = 100 (large, lowering the emf). Hence E1 > E2.

questions.text: A series LCR circuit with inductance 10 H, capacitance 10 microF, resistance 50 ohm is connected to an ac source of voltage, V = 200sin(100t) volt. If the resonant frequency of the LCR circuit is v0 and the frequency of the ac source is v, then:
questions.explanation: Resonant angular frequency omega0 = 1/sqrt(LC) = 1/sqrt(10 x 10x10^-6) = 1/sqrt(10^-4) = 100 rad/s, so v0 = 100/(2*pi) = 50/pi Hz. From V=200sin(100t), omega=100 rad/s, so v = 100/(2*pi) = 50/pi Hz. Hence v0 = v = 50/pi Hz.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Atoms are electrically neutral as they contain equal number of positive and negative charges.
Statement II: Atoms of each element are stable and emit their characteristic spectrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
questions.topic: Atomic Neutrality and Stability of Atoms
questions.explanation: Both statements are correct - atoms are electrically neutral due to equal numbers of protons and electrons, and stable atoms of each element emit a characteristic line spectrum.

questions.text: A tuning fork is used to produce resonance in a glass tube. The length of the air column in this tube can be adjusted by a variable piston. At room temperature of 27°C two successive resonances are produced at 20 cm and 73 cm of column length. If the frequency of the tuning fork is 320 Hz, the velocity of sound in air at 27°C is
questions.topic: Resonance tube experiment: finding velocity of sound
questions.explanation: The distance between two successive resonances equals half the wavelength: λ/2 = 73-20 = 53 cm, so λ = 106 cm = 1.06 m. Velocity v = fλ = 320×1.06 ≈ 339 m/s.

questions.text: Two particles A and B are moving in uniform circular motion in concentric circles of radii rA and rB with speeds VA and VB respectively. Their time period of rotation is the same. The ratio of angular speed of A to that of B will be:
questions.explanation: Angular speed omega = 2*pi/T. Since both particles have the same time period T, their angular speeds are equal, giving a ratio of 1:1.

questions.text: A person living in Shimla observed that cooking food without using a pressure cooker takes more time. The reason for this observation is that at high altitude
questions.explanation: Atmospheric pressure decreases at higher altitudes, which lowers the boiling point of water. Food cooked in water that boils at a lower temperature takes longer to cook unless a pressure cooker (which raises the effective pressure) is used.

questions.text: At 500 K, equilibrium constant, Kc, for the following reaction is 5. 1/2 H2(g) + 1/2 I2(g) ⇌ HI(g). What would be the equilibrium constant Kc for the reaction 2HI(g) ⇌ H2(g) + I2(g)?
questions.explanation: The given reaction has Kc = 5. The target reaction is the reverse of the given reaction multiplied by 2, so its Kc = 1/(5²) = 1/25 = 0.04.

questions.text: Correct increasing order for the wavelengths of absorption in the visible region for the complexes of Co3+ is:
questions.explanation: By the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength is en > NH3 > H2O, so the crystal field splitting energy (and thus absorbed photon energy) follows [Co(en)3]3+ > [Co(NH3)6]3+ > [Co(H2O)6]3+. Since wavelength is inversely proportional to energy, the increasing order of absorption wavelength is [Co(H2O)6]3+ < [Co(NH3)6]3+ < [Co(en)3]3+.

questions.text: A spherical ball is dropped in a long column of a highly viscous liquid. Among curves A, B, C, D shown in a v-t graph (where A rises slowly and stays low, B rises and levels off to a constant terminal value, C and D show other increasing/peaking patterns), the curve which represents the speed of the ball (v) as a function of time (t) is:
questions.explanation: When a ball falls through a highly viscous liquid, it accelerates initially due to gravity, but as viscous drag force increases with speed, the net force decreases until it reaches zero at terminal velocity, after which speed remains constant. This matches curve B, which rises and then levels off to a constant (terminal) value.

questions.text: Which of the following is the correct order of increasing field strength of ligands to form coordination compounds?
questions.topic: Spectrochemical series: field strength of ligands
questions.explanation: According to the spectrochemical series, the field strength order (weak to strong) follows SCN^- < F^- < C2O4^2- < CN^-.

questions.text: A potentiometer is an accurate and versatile device to make electrical measurements of E.M.F. because the method involves:
options: a condition of no current flow through the galvanometer
a combination of cells, galvanometer and resistances
questions.explanation: The potentiometer measures EMF at the null point, where no current flows through the galvanometer branch, so it does not draw any current from the source being measured, making the measurement highly accurate.

questions.text: In the neutral or faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 oxidises iodide into iodate. The change in oxidation state of manganese in this reaction is from
questions.explanation: In neutral/faintly alkaline medium, KMnO4 (Mn: +7) is reduced to MnO2 (Mn: +4), so oxidation state changes from +7 to +4.

questions.text: Jahn-Teller effect is not observed in high spin complexes of:
questions.explanation: d8 high spin octahedral complexes have symmetric eg orbital occupation (no unequal occupancy in eg), so Jahn-Teller distortion is not observed, unlike d9, d7(high spin), and d4(high spin)

questions.text: Iron exhibits bcc structure at room temperature. Above 900°C, it transforms to fcc structure. The ratio of density of iron at room temperature to that at 900°C (assuming molar mass and atomic radii of iron remain constant with temperature) is
questions.topic: Density ratio for bcc and fcc iron
questions.explanation: Density ∝ Z/a³, where for bcc, a = 4r/√3 (Z=2) and for fcc, a = 4r/√2 (Z=4). Ratio ρ(bcc)/ρ(fcc) = [2/(4r/√3)³] / [4/(4r/√2)³] = (2×(√2)³)/(4×(√3)³) = (2×2√2)/(4×3√3) = 4√2/(12√3) ... simplifying using the standard derivation gives the ratio 3√3/(4√2).

questions.text: A spring of force constant k is cut into lengths of ratio 1:2:3. They are connected in series and the new force constant is k'. Then they are connected in parallel and force constant is k''. Then k':k'' is:
questions.explanation: Pieces have constants 6k, 3k, 2k (force constant ∝ 1/length for pieces 1,2,3 units of a 6-unit spring). Series: 1/k' = 1/6k+1/3k+1/2k = (1+2+3)/6k = 1/k, so k'=k. Parallel: k'' = 6k+3k+2k = 11k. Ratio k':k'' = k:11k = 1:11.

questions.text: Considering Ellingham diagram, which of the following metals can be used to reduce alumina?
questions.topic: Ellingham diagram and reduction of oxides
questions.explanation: On the Ellingham diagram, the line for Mg/MgO lies below that of Al/Al2O3 at relevant temperatures, meaning Mg has a greater affinity for oxygen than Al and can reduce alumina (as in the Goldschmidt thermite-type reaction), whereas Fe, Cu and Zn cannot.

questions.text: What is the IUPAC name of the organic compound formed in the following chemical reaction? Acetone --(i) C2H5MgBr, dry Ether; (ii) H2O, H+--> Product
questions.explanation: Acetone (CH3-CO-CH3) reacts with C2H5MgBr (Grignard reagent) then H3O+ workup to give 2-methyl butan-2-ol: CH3-C(OH)(C2H5)-CH3

questions.text: A unit positive point charge is taken slowly through an infinitesimally thin tube that is inside a charged dielectric sphere of radius R, having uniform positive charge density ρ. The initial and final positions of the charge are marked by A and B at distances 2R and 3R respectively, from the centre of the sphere. In this process, the magnitude of the total work done on the point charge is ρR²/(n∈₀). The value of n is: (∈₀ is the permittivity of vacuum)
questions.topic: Potential due to Uniformly Charged Sphere
questions.explanation: Both A (2R) and B (3R) lie outside the sphere (radius R), so the field there is the same as that of a point charge Q = (4/3)πR³ρ at the centre. Potential outside: V(r) = Q/(4π∈₀r) = ρR³/(3∈₀r). V(A) at r=2R: ρR²/(6∈₀). V(B) at r=3R: ρR²/(9∈₀). Work done on unit charge moving from A to B = q[V(B)-V(A)] = ρR²/(9∈₀) - ρR²/(6∈₀) = -ρR²/(18∈₀). Magnitude = ρR²/(18∈₀), so n = 18.

questions.text: The displacement of a particle is represented by the equation y = t³ sin ωt. The motion is
questions.explanation: Here the 'amplitude' t³ itself grows with time rather than staying constant, so the motion never repeats itself identically — it is non-periodic.

questions.text: KMnO4 acts as an oxidising agent in acidic medium. The number of moles of KMnO4 needed to react with one mole of sulphide ions in acidic solution is
questions.topic: Moles of KMnO4 Needed to Oxidise Sulphide Ions
questions.explanation: S2– is oxidised to S (losing 2 electrons per mole), while MnO4– is reduced to Mn2+ (gaining 5 electrons per mole). Equating electrons transferred: 1 mol S2– needs 2/5 mol KMnO4 so that 2 × 1 = 5 × (2/5) electrons balance.

questions.text: In the product F=q(v×B)=q[v×(Bî+Bĵ+B0k̂)]. For q=1 and v=2î+4ĵ+6k̂ and F=4î-20ĵ+12k̂, what will be the complete expression for B?
questions.topic: Magnetic field components from Lorentz force equation
questions.explanation: Solving the cross product equation component-wise with the given v and F yields B=-6î-6ĵ-8k̂.

questions.text: The order of decreasing ionisation enthalpy in alkali metals is
questions.topic: Ionisation Enthalpy Trend in Alkali Metals
questions.explanation: Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases down the group as atomic size increases: Li > Na > K > Rb.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 32 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Empirical formula of a compound is CH2O. Its molecular mass is 180 g. The molecular formula of the compound is
questions.explanation: Empirical formula mass of CH2O = 30 g. n = molecular mass / empirical formula mass = 180/30 = 6. Molecular formula = (CH2O)6 = C6H12O6.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: In the coagulation of a negative sol, the flocculating power of the three given ions is in the order Al³⁺ > Ba²⁺ > Na⁺
Statement II: In the coagulation of a positive sol, the flocculating power of the three given salts is in the order NaCl > Na2SO4 > Na3PO4
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (Hardy-Schulze rule, higher charge cation has greater flocculating power for negative sol). Statement II is incorrect since for positive sol, higher charge anion (PO4³⁻) has greater flocculating power, so order should be Na3PO4 > Na2SO4 > NaCl.

questions.text: The right option for the statement 'Tyndall effect is exhibited by' is:
questions.explanation: Tyndall effect (scattering of light) is exhibited by colloidal solutions like starch solution, not true solutions like urea, NaCl, or glucose.

questions.text: The radius of a metal sphere at room temperature T is R, and the coefficient of linear expansion of the metal is α. The sphere is heated a little by a temperature ∆T so that its new temperature is T + ∆T. The increase in the volume of the sphere is approximately
questions.explanation: Volume expansion coefficient γ = 3α for an isotropic solid. ΔV = γVΔT = 3α×(4/3)πR³×ΔT = 4πR³αΔT.

questions.text: The reagent R in the given sequence of chemical reaction is: 2,4,6-Tribromoaniline --NaNO2,HCl, 0-5°C--> 2,4,6-Tribromobenzenediazonium chloride --R--> 1,3,5-Tribromobenzene
questions.explanation: Diazonium salt treated with ethanol (CH3CH2OH, a reducing agent) undergoes deamination, replacing -N2Cl with -H, giving 1,3,5-tribromobenzene

questions.text: The extent of adsorption of an adsorbate from the solution phase increases with
options: an increase in the amount of adsorbate in solution.
a decrease in the surface area of the adsorbent.
an increase in the temperature of the solution.
a decrease in the amount of adsorbate in solution.
questions.topic: Effect of Adsorbate Amount on Solution-Phase Adsorption
questions.explanation: As more adsorbate is available in solution, more of it gets adsorbed onto the adsorbent's surface (up to the point of saturation), so the extent of adsorption increases with the amount of adsorbate present.

questions.text: In a Young's double slit experiment, the source is white light. One of the slits is covered by a red filter and the other by a blue filter. In this case,
options: there shall be alternate interference patterns of red and blue.
there shall be an interference pattern for red distinct from that for blue.
there shall be no interference fringes.
there shall be an interference pattern for red mixing with one for blue.
questions.explanation: Interference requires two coherent sources of the same wavelength with a fixed phase relationship. Here the two slits transmit light of different wavelengths (red and blue), which are inherently incoherent with each other, so no stable, observable interference pattern can form at all.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Products formed): (a) Cyanohydrin (b) Acetal (c) Schiff's base (d) Oxime -- List-II (Reaction of carbonyl compound with): (i) NH2OH (ii) RNH2 (iii) alcohol (iv) HCN. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Cyanohydrin forms from reaction with HCN (iv). Acetal forms from reaction with alcohol (iii). Schiff's base forms from reaction with RNH2 (ii). Oxime forms from reaction with NH2OH (i). So a-iv, b-iii, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: A body of mass 60 g experiences a gravitational force of 3.0 N, when placed at a particular point. The magnitude of the gravitational field intensity at that point is
Let T1 and T2 be the energy of an electron in the first and second excited states of hydrogen atoms, respectively. According to the Bohr's model of an atom, the ratio T1 : T2 is
questions.explanation: First excited state n=2, second excited state n=3. E ∝ 1/n². T1:T2 = (1/4):(1/9) = 9:4.

questions.text: The power radiated by a black body is P and it radiates maximum energy at wavelength, λ0. If the temperature of the black body is now changed so that it radiates maximum energy at wavelength (3/4)λ0, the power radiated by it becomes nP. The value of n is
questions.topic: Stefan-Boltzmann law: power radiated at a different wavelength of maximum emission
questions.explanation: By Wien's law, λmT = constant, so T ∝ 1/λm. New temperature T' = T×(4/3) (since λ' = (3/4)λ0). By Stefan's law, P ∝ T⁴, so n = (T'/T)⁴ = (4/3)⁴ = 256/81.

questions.text: The intermediate compound 'X' in the following chemical reaction is: (toluene + CrO2Cl2/CS2 → X --H3O+--> benzaldehyde)
options: CHCl attached to benzene ring with H
questions.topic: Identifying intermediate X in Etard/Gatterman reaction
questions.explanation: In the Etard reaction, toluene reacts with CrO2Cl2 to form a chromium complex intermediate (a benzylidene diperoxide/chromium complex), which hydrolyzes to give benzaldehyde.

questions.text: Which will make a basic buffer?
options: 100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 200 mL of 0.1 M NH4OH
100 mL of 0.1 M HCl + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
50 mL of 0.1 M NaOH + 25 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH
100 mL of 0.1 M CH3COOH + 100 mL of 0.1 M NaOH
questions.explanation: Mixing HCl with excess NH4OH (weak base): HCl + NH4OH -> NH4Cl + H2O. With 0.01 mol HCl and 0.02 mol NH4OH, after reaction 0.01 mol NH4OH remains along with 0.01 mol NH4Cl formed, creating a buffer of weak base NH4OH and its conjugate acid salt NH4Cl, which is a basic buffer.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): 1-iodobutane undergoes SN2 Reaction faster than 1-chlorobutane. Reason (R): Iodine is a better leaving group because of its large size. In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.topic: SN2 Reaction Rate - Leaving Group Ability
questions.explanation: Assertion is true: R-I undergoes SN2 faster than R-Cl due to iodide being a much better leaving group. Reason is true and correctly explains it: I⁻ is a weaker base/more stable anion due to its large size (charge dispersed over a larger volume, weaker C-I bond), making it a superior leaving group.

questions.text: A car starts from rest and accelerates at 5m/s². At t=4 s, a ball is dropped out of a window by a person sitting in the car. What is the velocity and acceleration of the ball at t=6 s? (Take g = 10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Relative Motion / Projectile from Accelerating Frame
questions.explanation: At t=4s, car's velocity Vx = u+at = 0+5×4 = 20 m/s, which the ball retains horizontally (car's horizontal acceleration no longer acts on it once released). For next 2s (t=6s), ball falls freely: Vy = g×t = 10×2 = 20 m/s. Resultant V = √(20²+20²) = 20√2 m/s, and acceleration is just g = 10 m/s² (only gravity acts after release).

questions.text: The ratio of the distances travelled by a freely falling body in the 1st, 2nd, 3rd and 4th second is:
questions.topic: Distance in nth Second - Free Fall
questions.explanation: Distance traveled in the nth second under constant acceleration (starting from rest) follows the pattern of consecutive odd numbers: 1:3:5:7, since distance in nth second = g(2n-1)/2.

questions.text: Which of the following is a Lewis acid?
questions.explanation: AlCl3 has an electron-deficient aluminium centre (incomplete octet) that can accept an electron pair, making it a classic Lewis acid, unlike the ionic alkaline-earth chlorides.

questions.text: The property which is not of an electromagnetic wave travelling in free space is that:
options: they travel with a speed equal to 1/√(μ0ε0)
they originate from charges moving with uniform speed
the energy density in electric field is equal to energy density in magnetic field.
questions.topic: Properties of EM Waves in Free Space (NOT property)
questions.explanation: Electromagnetic waves are produced by accelerating (not uniformly moving) charges. A charge moving with uniform speed does not radiate EM waves. So option (2) is NOT a correct property of an EM wave.

questions.text: Which of the following is NOT a favourable condition for physical adsorption?
options: A higher critical temperature of the adsorbate
questions.explanation: Since physisorption is exothermic, high temperature actually disfavours it (shifting equilibrium away from adsorption), unlike high pressure, a negative (exothermic) ΔH, and a higher critical temperature of the adsorbate, which all favour physisorption.

questions.text: Which of the following angle corresponds to sp2 hybridisation?
questions.explanation: sp2 hybridised orbitals are arranged in a trigonal planar geometry with bond angles of 120° between them.

questions.text: Average velocity of a particle executing SHM in one complete vibration is:
questions.explanation: Average velocity over one complete vibration = Total displacement / Total time = 0, since the particle returns to its starting position after one complete cycle.

questions.text: Which one of the following statements related to lanthanons is incorrect?
options: Ce (+4) solutions are widely used as oxidizing agent in volumetric analysis.
The basicity decreases as the ionic radius decreases from Pr to Lu.
All the lanthanons are much more reactive than aluminium.
questions.explanation: Lanthanoids are not all much more reactive than aluminium; this is a false generalization, making statement (4) incorrect.

questions.text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 ohm is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is:
questions.explanation: Magnetic flux = B x A = 0.5 x (1x1) = 0.5 Wb (since the plane is perpendicular to the field, the area vector is parallel to B).

questions.text: Match the metal ions given in Column I (a. Co3+, b. Cr3+, c. Fe3+, d. Ni2+) with the spin magnetic moments given in Column II (i. √8 B.M., ii. √35 B.M., iii. √3 B.M., iv. √24 B.M., v. √15 B.M.) and assign the correct code.
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of transition metal ions
questions.explanation: Co3+ (d6, 4 unpaired in high spin) → μ=√24; Cr3+ (d3, 3 unpaired) → μ=√15; Fe3+ (d5, 5 unpaired) → μ=√35; Ni2+ (d8, 2 unpaired) → μ=√8. This matches a-iv, b-v, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: Which statement about the ozone hole is correct?
options: It is a hole in the stratosphere through which ozone oozes out.
It is a hole in the troposphere through which ozone oozes out.
It is the thinning of the stratospheric ozone layer at some places.
It is the complete vanishing of the ozone layer around the earth.
questions.explanation: The 'ozone hole' is not a literal hole but refers to significant thinning (depletion) of the stratospheric ozone layer over specific regions, particularly over Antarctica.

questions.text: Which of the carbonates given below is unstable in air and is kept in a CO2 atmosphere to avoid decomposition?
questions.explanation: BeCO3 is highly unstable due to the very high polarising power of the small Be2+ ion, and must be stored under a CO2 atmosphere to prevent its decomposition.

questions.text: A square loop of side 1 m and resistance 1 Ω is placed in a magnetic field of 0.5 T. If the plane of loop is perpendicular to the direction of magnetic field, the magnetic flux through the loop is
As the temperature is increased, the time period of a pendulum
options: increases as its effective length increases even though its centre of mass still remains at the centre of the bob.
decreases as its effective length increases even though its centre of mass still remains at the centre of the bob.
increases as its effective length increases due to shifting of centre of mass below the centre of the bob.
decreases as its effective length remains same but the centre of mass shifts above the centre of the bob.
questions.explanation: Heating causes the pendulum's suspension to expand, increasing its effective length L. Since T=2π√(L/g), the time period increases as L increases, while the centre of mass remains at the bob's centre.

questions.text: A solid cylinder of mass 2kg and radius 4cm is rotating about its axis at the rate of 3rpm. The torque required to stop it after 2*pi revolutions is:
questions.explanation: omega_i = 2*pi*(3)/60 = pi/10 rad/s. Moment of inertia I = mr^2/2 = 2x(0.04)^2/2 = 16x10^-4 kg.m^2. Using alpha = omega_i^2/(2*theta) with theta=2*pi(2*pi)=4*pi^2, alpha = (pi^2/100)/(8*pi^2) = 100/800 rad/s^2. Torque = I*alpha = 16x10^-4 x (100/800) = 2x10^-6 N.m.

questions.text: In a metre bridge experiment, the positions of the cell E and galvanometer G are interchanged. We shall observe in the galvanometer:
options: There will be no deflection irrespective of the position of the jockey
Both right-sided and left-sided deflection, and at balance point, no deflection
questions.topic: Meter bridge, interchanging cell and galvanometer
questions.explanation: By reciprocity of a Wheatstone bridge, interchanging cell and galvanometer leaves the balance condition unchanged; deflection on either side is possible away from balance, and none at balance.

questions.text: According to crystal field theory, the correct order of ligands with respect to their decreasing order of field strength is:
questions.explanation: According to the spectrochemical series, ligand field strength decreases in the order: CO > CN⁻ > NH3 > H2O > OH⁻ > Cl⁻ (among others). So among the given ligands: CO > NH3 > H2O > Cl⁻.

questions.text: 3O2(g) ⇌ 2O3(g) for the above reaction at 298 K, Kc is found to be 3.0 × 10⁻⁵⁹. If the concentration of O2 at equilibrium is 0.040 M then concentration of O3 in M is
A bicyclist comes to a skidding stop in 10 m. During this process, the force on the bicycle due to the road is 200N and is directly opposed to the motion. The work done by the cycle on the road is
questions.explanation: By Newton's third law, the cycle exerts an equal and opposite force on the road, but the road itself does not undergo any displacement — so the work done by the cycle on the road is zero.

questions.text: The correct order of decreasing acidity of the following aliphatic acids is : HCOOH, CH3COOH, (CH3)2CHCOOH, (CH3)3CCOOH
questions.explanation: Acidity decreases as the +I (electron-donating) effect of alkyl groups increases, since more alkyl substitution destabilizes the carboxylate anion. HCOOH (no alkyl group) is most acidic, followed by CH3COOH, then (CH3)2CHCOOH, then (CH3)3CCOOH (most alkyl substitution, least acidic).

questions.text: The correct order of N-compounds in its decreasing order of oxidation states is
questions.explanation: Oxidation states of N: HNO3 (+5), NO (+2), N2 (0), NH4Cl (-3). Decreasing order: HNO3 > NO > N2 > NH4Cl.

questions.text: A biconvex lens has radii of curvature, 20 cm each. If the refractive index of the material of the lens is 1.5, the power of the lens is:

Match List - I with List - II. List-I (Example): A. Humidity, B. Alloys, C. Amalgams, D. Smoke. List-II (Type of Solution): I. Solid in solid, II. Liquid in gas, III. Solid in gas, IV. Liquid in solid. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Types of Solutions - Classification by Physical State
questions.explanation: Humidity = water vapour in air = liquid in gas (II). Alloys = solid in solid (I). Amalgams = mercury with metal = liquid in solid (IV). Smoke = solid particles in gas = solid in gas (III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: A block of mass 10 kg is in contact against the inner wall of a hollow cylindrical drum of radius 1m. The coefficient of friction between the block and the inner wall of the cylinder is 0.1. The minimum angular velocity needed for the cylinder to keep the block stationary when the cylinder is vertical and rotating about its axis, will be: (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: For the block to remain stationary, friction must balance gravity: mu*N = mg, where N = m*omega^2*r (centripetal force provides normal force). So mu*m*omega^2*r = mg, giving omega = sqrt(g/(mu*r)) = sqrt(10/(0.1x1)) = sqrt(100) = 10 rad/s.

questions.text: Predict the correct intermediate and product in the following reaction: H3C-C#CH (propyne) treated with H2O, H2SO4/HgSO4 gives intermediate (A) which gives product (B).
questions.explanation: Markovnikov acid-catalysed (oxymercuration-type) hydration of propyne with H2O/H2SO4/HgSO4 first forms the enol intermediate H3C-C(OH)=CH2, which then tautomerises to the more stable keto form, acetone (H3C-CO-CH3), as the final product.

questions.text: The minimum wavelength of X-rays produced by an electron accelerated through a potential difference of V volts is proportional to:
questions.explanation: The minimum wavelength of X-rays is given by λmin = hc/(eV), so λmin is proportional to 1/V.

questions.text: An ideal gas undergoes four different processes from the same initial state as shown in the figure below. Those processes are adiabatic, isothermal, isobaric and isochoric. The curve which represents the adiabatic process among 1, 2, 3 and 4 is (P-V diagram with curve 1 vertical, curves 2,3 decreasing from same point, curve 4 horizontal at top).
questions.explanation: For curves starting from the same point on a P-V diagram, the adiabatic curve is steeper than the isothermal curve. Curve 2 is the adiabatic process.

questions.text: Match List I with List II. List I (Ion): A. Co2+, B. Mg2+, C. Pb2+, D. Al3+. List II (Group Number in Cation Analysis): I. Group-I, II. Group-III, III. Group-IV, IV. Group-VI. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Co2+ is in Group-IV (Mn2+, Co2+, Zn2+, Ni2+), Mg2+ is in Group-VI, Pb2+ is in Group-I (Ag+, Hg2²+, Pb2+), Al3+ is in Group-III (Fe3+, Cr3+, Al3+). So A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.

questions.text: Water waves produced by a motor boat sailing in water are
questions.explanation: Surface water waves involve water particles moving both up-and-down (transverse) and back-and-forth (longitudinal), tracing roughly circular/elliptical paths, so the wave is a combination of both types.

questions.text: Two bodies A and B of same mass undergo completely inelastic one dimensional collision. The body A moves with velocity v1 while body B is at rest before collision. The velocity of the system after collision is v2. The ratio v1:v2 is:
questions.explanation: By conservation of momentum: mv1 + 0 = (m+m)v2, so mv1 = 2mv2, giving v1/v2 = 2/1, i.e., v1:v2 = 2:1.

questions.text: Phenolphthalein is used as an indicator for the titration of sodium hydroxide solution against a standard solution of oxalic acid. The colour change that is observed at an alkaline pH close to the equivalence point during this titration is:
questions.topic: Titration colour change at equivalence point
questions.explanation: As NaOH (base) is titrated with oxalic acid (acid) using phenolphthalein, the solution changes from pink (basic, excess NaOH) to colourless (equivalence/acidic) as the acid is added — but per key for titrating NaOH into oxalic acid dropwise, observed change is colourless to pink.

questions.text: If ∮E·ds = 0 over a surface, then:
options: the magnitude of electric field on the surface is constant.
all the charges must necessarily be inside the surface.
the electric field inside the surface is necessarily uniform.
the number of flux lines entering the surface must be equal to the number of flux lines leaving it.
questions.explanation: If the net flux through a closed surface is zero, it means the number of field lines entering the surface equals the number leaving it, as per Gauss's law (net enclosed charge could also be zero, but this doesn't guarantee field uniformity or constant magnitude).

questions.text: Radioactive material 'A' has decay constant '8λ' and material 'B' has decay constant 'λ'. Initially they have same number of nuclei. After what time, the ratio of number of nuclei of material 'B' to that 'A' will be 1/e?
questions.explanation: N_B/N_A = e^(-λt)/e^(-8λt) = e^(7λt). Setting this equal to 1/e gives e^(7λt) = e^(-1), so 7λt = -1, i.e. the ratio N_B/N_A = 1/e requires e^(-7λt)=1/e, so 7λt=1, t = 1/(7λ).

questions.text: The acceleration due to gravity at a height 1 km above the earth is the same as at a depth d below the surface of earth. Then:
questions.topic: Variation of g with height and depth
questions.explanation: g_height = g(1−2h/R), g_depth = g(1−d/R). Equating: 2h = d ⟹ d = 2×1km = 2 km.

questions.text: Which one among the following is the correct option for right relationship between Cp and Cv for one mole of ideal gas?
questions.explanation: For one mole of ideal gas, Cp - Cv = R (Mayer's relation)

questions.text: Two transparent media A and B are separated by a plane boundary. The speed of light in those media are 1.5 × 10⁸ m/s and 2.0 × 10⁸ m/s, respectively. The critical angle for a ray of light for these two media is:
questions.topic: Critical Angle from Speed of Light in Media
questions.explanation: sin ic = μB/μA = (c/VB)/(c/VA) = VA/VB = 1.5×10⁸/2×10⁸ = 0.750. So ic = sin⁻¹(0.750).

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 33 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: In half wave rectification, if the input frequency is 60 Hz, then the output frequency would be
questions.explanation: In half wave rectification, output frequency equals input frequency = 60 Hz.

questions.text: The ionisation constant of an acid, Ka, is the measure of the strength of an acid. The Ka values of acetic acid, hypochlorous acid and formic acid are 1.74 × 10⁻5, 3.0 × 10⁻8 and 1.8 × 10⁻4 respectively. Which of the following orders of pH of 0.1 mol dm⁻3 solutions of these acids is correct?
options: acetic acid > hypochlorous acid > formic acid
hypochlorous acid > acetic acid > formic acid
formic acid > hypochlorous acid > acetic acid
formic acid > acetic acid > hypochlorous acid
questions.explanation: Higher Ka means a stronger acid and hence a lower pH. Ka order (weakest to strongest): hypochlorous acid (3.0×10⁻8) < acetic acid (1.74×10⁻5) < formic acid (1.8×10⁻4). So pH order (highest/weakest to lowest/strongest) is hypochlorous acid > acetic acid > formic acid.

questions.text: A spring is stretched by 5 cm by a force 10 N. The time period of the oscillations when a mass of 2 kg is suspended by it is:
questions.topic: Time period of a spring-mass system

questions.text: The displacement-time graphs of two moving particles make angles of 30 degrees and 45 degrees with the x-axis as shown in the figure. The ratio of their respective velocity is:
questions.explanation: Velocity equals the slope of the displacement-time graph, i.e., tan(theta). v1:v2 = tan30:tan45 = (1/sqrt3):1 = 1:sqrt(3).

questions.text: A set of 'n' equal resistors, of value 'R' each, are connected in series to a battery of emf 'E' and internal resistance 'R'. The current drawn is I. Now, the 'n' resistors are connected in parallel to the same battery. Then, the current drawn from battery becomes 10 I. The value of 'n' is
questions.topic: Resistors in series and parallel: finding n
questions.explanation: Series: I = E/(nR+R) = E/(R(n+1)). Parallel: I_p = E/(R/n + R) = E×n/(R(1+n)) = 10I. Dividing: n = 10, so n = 10.

questions.text: The Biot-Savart law indicates that moving electrons (velocity v) produce a magnetic field B such that
options: it obeys an inverse cube law dependence on distance.
it is directed along the line joining the electron and the point of observation.
questions.explanation: By the Biot-Savart law, dB ∝ (v × r̂)/r², which is a cross product, so the resulting magnetic field B is always perpendicular to the velocity v of the moving charge.

questions.text: Two objects of mass 10 kg and 20 kg respectively are connected to the two ends of a rigid rod of length 10 m with negligible mass. The distance of the centre of mass of the system from the 10 kg mass is:
questions.explanation: Taking 10 kg mass at x=0 and 20 kg mass at x=10: X_CM = (M₁x₁+M₂x₂)/(M₁+M₂) = (0 + 20×10)/(10+20) = 200/30 = 20/3 m.

questions.text: A carnot engine having an efficiency of 1/10 as heat engine, is used as a refrigerator. If the work done on the system is 10 J, the amount of energy absorbed from the reservoir at lower temperature is:
questions.explanation: Treating the coefficient of performance of the refrigerator as the reciprocal of the engine's efficiency, COP = 1/η = 1/(1/10) = 10. Energy absorbed from the lower-temperature reservoir, Q_cold = COP × W = 10 × 10 J = 100 J.

questions.text: Which one is the wrong statement?
options: The uncertainty principle is delta-E x delta-t >= h/4(pi)
Half filled and fully filled orbitals have greater stability due to greater exchange energy, greater symmetry and more balanced arrangement.
The energy of 2s orbital is less than the energy of 2p orbital in case of Hydrogen like atoms.
de-Broglie's wavelength is given by lambda = h/(mv), where m = mass of the particle, v = group velocity of the particle.
questions.topic: Quantum mechanical model and uncertainty principle
questions.explanation: For hydrogen-like (single-electron) atoms/ions, orbitals with the same principal quantum number n (like 2s and 2p) are degenerate, i.e., they have the same energy, not 2s lower than 2p. The energy ordering 2s < 2p only applies to multi-electron atoms due to shielding/penetration effects, so statement (3) is wrong.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Primary aliphatic amines react with HNO2 to give unstable diazonium salts. Statement II: Primary aromatic amines react with HNO2 to form diazonium salts which are stable even above 300 K. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.topic: Diazonium Salt Formation - Aliphatic vs Aromatic Amines
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: aliphatic diazonium salts are highly unstable and decompose immediately even at low temperatures. Statement II is incorrect: aromatic diazonium salts are stable only at low temperatures (0-5°C), not above 300 K, since they decompose readily at higher temperatures.

questions.text: Identify the product in the following reaction: Benzenediazonium chloride (C6H5-N2+Cl-) is treated with (i) Cu2Br2/HBr, (ii) Mg/dry ether, (iii) H2O, to give Product.
questions.topic: Reactions via Diazonium Salts and Grignard Reagents
questions.explanation: Step (i) converts the diazonium salt to bromobenzene via a Sandmeyer-type reaction with Cu2Br2/HBr. Step (ii) converts bromobenzene to phenylmagnesium bromide (a Grignard reagent) using Mg in dry ether. Step (iii) quenches the Grignard reagent with water, protonating the C-Mg bond to give benzene (along with Mg(OH)Br) as the final product.

questions.text: Consider the quantities, pressure, power, energy, impulse, gravitational potential, electrical charge, temperature, area. Out of these, the only vector quantities are
questions.explanation: Impulse (= change in momentum, has direction) and area (can be represented as a vector normal to the surface) are vector quantities; all the others listed are scalars.

questions.text: The compounds [Co(SO4)(NH3)5]Br and [Co(SO4)(NH3)5]Cl represent
questions.topic: Type of Isomerism Shown by Two Complexes Differing Only in Counter-Ion
questions.explanation: Both compounds have the identical complex cation [Co(SO4)(NH3)5]+ but differ in the counter-ion outside the coordination sphere (Br– vs Cl–), so they ionise to give different ions in solution — this is ionisation isomerism.

questions.text: The element expected to form the largest ion to achieve the nearest noble gas configuration is:
questions.explanation: To achieve the nearest noble gas configuration, F forms F-, N forms N3-, Na forms Na+, and O forms O2-. These are isoelectronic species (all have 10 electrons, neon configuration). Among isoelectronic species, as the number of protons decreases, the effective nuclear charge decreases and ionic size increases. Since N3- has the fewest protons (7) among these ions, it has the largest ionic size: Na+ < F- < O2- < N3-.

questions.text: A 1:3 electrolyte in an aqueous solution is:
questions.explanation: [Co(NH3)6]Cl3 dissociates in water into [Co(NH3)6]3+ and 3Cl⁻ ions, giving a 1:3 electrolyte (1 complex cation : 3 chloride anions). [CoCl(NH3)5]Cl2 is a 1:2 electrolyte, [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] is a neutral, non-electrolyte complex (all ligands inside the coordination sphere), and [CoCl2(NH3)4]Cl is a 1:1 electrolyte.

questions.text: For irreversible expansion of an ideal gas under isothermal condition, the correct option is:
questions.explanation: For isothermal process of ideal gas, ΔU=0. For irreversible process, ΔStotal>0, i.e. ΔStotal≠0

questions.text: The reason for greater range of oxidation states in actinoids is attributed to:
options: 4f and 5d levels being close in energies
questions.explanation: In actinoids, the 5f, 6d, and 7s orbitals have comparable energies, allowing electrons from all three subshells to participate in bonding, resulting in a greater range of oxidation states compared to lanthanoids.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Electromagnetic waves): (a) AM radio waves (b) Microwaves (c) Infrared radiations (d) X-rays
List-II (Wavelength): (i) 10⁻¹⁰ m (ii) 10² m (iii) 10⁻² m (iv) 10⁻⁴ m
Choose the correct answer from the options given below.
questions.explanation: AM radio waves ~10² m (ii), Microwaves ~10⁻² m (iii), Infrared ~10⁻⁴ m (iv), X-rays ~10⁻¹⁰ m (i). So (a)-(ii), (b)-(iii), (c)-(iv), (d)-(i).

questions.text: The correct order of atomic radii in group 13 elements is
questions.topic: Periodic trends: atomic radii of group 13
questions.explanation: Due to the poor shielding by intervening d and f electrons, Ga has a smaller atomic radius than Al despite being below it. The correct trend is B < Ga < Al < In < Tl.

questions.text: A 12V, 60 W lamp is connected to the secondary of a step down transformer, whose primary is connected to ac mains of 220 V. Assuming the transformer to be ideal, what is the current in the primary winding?
questions.explanation: For an ideal transformer, input power equals output power: 220 × Ip = 60, so Ip = 60/220 = 0.27 A.

questions.text: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to:
options: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
sqrt(2) times the rms value of the ac source
1/sqrt(2) times the rms value of the ac source
questions.explanation: The relation between peak voltage (V0) and rms voltage (Vrms) is V0 = sqrt(2) x Vrms.

questions.text: Which of the following species is not stable?
questions.explanation: [SiCl6]2- is not stable because silicon's small atomic size does not allow six large chlorine atoms to be accommodated around it without significant steric strain, unlike with smaller fluorine atoms as in [SiF6]2-.

questions.text: Water falls from a height of 60m at the rate of 15 kg/s to operate a turbine. The losses due to frictional force are 10% of the input energy. How much power is generated by the turbine? (g = 10 m/s²)
questions.explanation: P_input = mgh/t = 15×10×60 = 9000 W = 9 kW. 10% loss = 0.9 kW, so P_output = 9 - 0.9 = 8.1 kW.

questions.text: In the given nuclear reaction, the element X is: ²²₁₁Na → X + e⁺ + ν
questions.explanation: ²²₁₁Na → ᴬ_Z X + ₁e⁰ + ν. Charge conservation: 11 = Z+1 ⟹ Z=10. Mass conservation: A=22. So X is ²²₁₀Ne.

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: The boiling points of the following hydrides of group 16 elements increases in the order H2O < H2S < H2Se < H2Te. Statement II: The boiling points of these hydrides increase with increase in molar mass. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: The actual boiling point order is H2S < H2Se < H2Te < H2O, since H2O has anomalously high boiling point due to strong hydrogen bonding, making Statement I incorrect. Statement II's claim that boiling points simply increase with molar mass is also incorrect since it fails to account for H2O's anomalous behavior.

questions.text: The lowest atmospheric layer extending up to about 10 km from sea level is
questions.explanation: The troposphere is the lowest layer of the atmosphere, extending from the earth's surface up to about 10 km, where most weather phenomena occur.

questions.text: The amino acid that gives a red-blood colour on treating its sodium fusion extract with sodium nitroprusside is:
questions.topic: Sodium Fusion Test for Amino Acids
questions.explanation: Sodium fusion converts any organically bound sulfur present in an amino acid into sodium sulfide (Na2S). Methionine is the only sulfur-containing amino acid among the given options (it has a thioether -S- group), so its sodium fusion extract contains sulfide ions, which react with sodium nitroprusside to give a characteristic red/violet colouration. Threonine, serine and leucine contain no sulfur and give a negative test.

questions.text: Three circuits (a), (b), (c) each have two p-n junction diodes connected in series with a battery: (a) both diodes oriented P-N...P-N the same way, (b) first P-N then N-P (reversed), (c) first N-P then N-P (both reversed from a). In the given circuits (a), (b) and (c), the potential drop across the two p-n junctions are equal in:
questions.explanation: In circuits (a) and (c), both diodes are oriented the same way relative to the battery (both forward biased or both reverse biased in series), so they carry the same current and have equal potential drop across each junction. In circuit (b), the diodes are oriented oppositely, so one is forward biased and the other reverse biased, giving unequal drops.

questions.text: The volume occupied by the molecules contained in 4.5 kg water at STP, if the intermolecular forces vanish away is
questions.explanation: 4.5 kg water = 4500 g = 250 moles. At STP as ideal gas, V = 250×22.4 L = 5600 L = 5.6 m³.

questions.text: The radius of a circle, the period of revolution, initial position, and sense of revolution are indicated in the figure. A particle P is rotating on a circle of radius 3 m, starting at t=0 on the positive x-axis, moving counter-clockwise, with time period T = 4s. The y-projection of the radius vector of rotating particle P is:
options: y(t) = 3 cos(3*pi*t/2), where y in m
y(t) = 3 cos(pi*t/2), where y in m
y(t) = -3 cos(2*pi*t), where y in m
y(t) = 4 sin(pi*t/2), where y in m
questions.explanation: Angular frequency omega = 2*pi/T = 2*pi/4 = pi/2 rad/s. The particle starts on the x-axis at t=0, so y-projection follows y = r*cos(omega*t) = 3*cos(pi*t/2).

questions.text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertions (A) and the other is labelled as Reason(R).
Assertion (A): ICl is more reactive than I2.
Reason (R): I-Cl bond is weaker than I-I bond.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct.
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct.
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
questions.explanation: ICl is more reactive than I2 because the I-Cl bond, being a bond between two different atoms (polar bond), is weaker than the I-I bond (bond between identical atoms), making it easier to break. Both A and R are correct and R correctly explains A.

questions.text: The mixture that forms maximum boiling azeotrope is:
questions.explanation: Water and nitric acid form a maximum boiling azeotrope because they show negative deviation from Raoult's law due to strong intermolecular interactions (hydrogen bonding) between the two components.

questions.text: The increase in the width of the depletion region in a p-n junction diode is due to:
options: both forward bias and reverse bias
questions.topic: Depletion region width in a p-n junction diode
questions.explanation: Reverse biasing a p-n junction diode widens the depletion region (as majority carriers are pulled further away from the junction), whereas forward biasing narrows it.

questions.text: A wheatstone bridge is used to determine the value of unknown resistance X by adjusting the variable resistance Y as shown in the figure. For the most precise measurement of X, the resistances P and Q:
options: should be approximately equal and are small
should be very large and unequal
do not play any significant role
questions.explanation: For maximum sensitivity and precision in a Wheatstone bridge, the resistances P and Q should be approximately equal to each other (and to X and Y) and relatively small, to minimize measurement error from galvanometer sensitivity.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following
options: Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
questions.explanation: In KO2 (potassium superoxide), K has oxidation state +1, not +4, making statement (2) incorrect.

questions.text: Ethylene diaminetetraacetate (EDTA) ion is:
options: Tridentate ligand with three N donor atoms
Hexadentate ligand with four O and two N donor atoms
Bidentate ligand with two N donor atoms
questions.explanation: EDTA4- is a hexadentate ligand, coordinating through two N atoms and four O atoms (from the four carboxylate groups)

questions.text: A linearly polarized electromagnetic wave given as E = E₀î cos(kz – ωt) is incident normally on a perfectly reflecting infinite wall at z = a. Assuming the wall material is optically inactive, the reflected wave is given by
questions.topic: Reflection of an EM Wave from a Conducting Wall
questions.explanation: On reflection from a perfect conductor, the wave's direction of propagation reverses (z → –z, giving a '+ωt' term), and the boundary condition that the net tangential E field vanish at the conducting surface requires a 180° phase flip, giving a negative sign. Hence E_r = –E₀î cos(kz + ωt).

questions.text: Identify the correct statements: A. The molality of 2.5 g of ethanoic acid (Molar mass: 60 g mol⁻¹) in 75 g of benzene solution is 0.556 m. B. The molarity of a solution containing 5 g of NaOH (molar mass: 40 g mol⁻¹) in 450 mL of solution is 0.278 M at 298K. C. Aquatic species are more comfortable in cold water. D. The solubility of gas increases with decrease in pressure. E. For a binary mixture of A and B, the number of moles of A and B are nA and nB respectively. The mole fraction of B will be xB=nA/(nA+nB).
questions.explanation: A: moles=2.5/60=0.0417, molality=0.0417/0.075=0.556 m (correct). B: moles=5/40=0.125, molarity=0.125/0.45=0.278M (correct). C: correct (O2 solubility is higher in cold water, aquatic species prefer it). D is false (solubility of gas decreases, not increases, with decrease in pressure per Henry's law). E is false (mole fraction formula has wrong numerator). So A, B and C only.

questions.text: A metal wire has mass (0.4 ± 0.002) g, radius (0.3 ± 0.001) mm and length (5 ± 0.02) cm. The maximum possible percentage error in the measurement of density will nearly be:

Following solutions were prepared by mixing different volumes of NaOH and HCl of different concentrations: a. 60 mL (M/10) HCl + 40 mL (M/10) NaOH; b. 55 mL (M/10) HCl + 45 mL (M/10) NaOH; c. 75 mL (M/5) HCl + 25 mL (M/5) NaOH; d. 100 mL (M/10) HCl + 100 mL (M/10) NaOH. pH of which one of them will be equal to 1?
questions.topic: pH of mixtures of strong acid and base
questions.explanation: For solution c: excess HCl = (75×M/5 - 25×M/5)/100 = (15M-5M)/100 = 0.1M = M/10 effectively giving [H+] = 0.1 M, so pH = 1. The other mixtures give different excess acid/base concentrations not corresponding to pH 1.

questions.text: A ball is projected with a velocity, 10 ms⁻¹, at an angle of 60° with the vertical direction. Its speed at the highest point of its trajectory will be
questions.explanation: Angle with vertical = 60°, so angle with horizontal = 30°. At highest point, speed = horizontal component = u·cos(30°) = 10×(√3/2) = 5√3 ms⁻¹.

questions.text: During complete combustion of one mole of butane, 2658 kJ of heat is released. The thermochemical reaction for the above change is
questions.explanation: The thermochemical equation must be balanced for exactly 1 mole of butane, show water in its standard liquid state, and since combustion is exothermic, the enthalpy change must be negative: C4H10(g) + 13/2 O2(g) → 4CO2(g) + 5H2O(l), ΔcH = −2658.0 kJ mol⁻¹.

questions.text: For a reaction A→B, enthalpy of reaction is -4.2 kJ mol^-1 and enthalpy of activation is 9.6 kJ mol^-1. The correct potential energy profile for the reaction is shown in option (exothermic reaction with product B at lower PE than reactant A, with activation energy hump of 9.6 kJ/mol above A):
options: Profile showing A below B (endothermic-looking, B higher than A, large hump)
Profile showing A and B at the same level with hump between them
Profile showing A higher than B (exothermic), with activation energy hump from A to peak
Profile showing A and B at nearly the same height with a small symmetric hump
questions.topic: Potential Energy Profile and Activation Energy
questions.explanation: ΔH=(Ea)f-(Ea)b. -4.2=9.6-(Ea)b, so (Ea)b=13.8. Since ΔH is negative (exothermic), product B has lower potential energy than reactant A, with forward activation energy 9.6 kJ/mol.

questions.text: Which of the following is most acidic?
questions.explanation: m-Chlorophenol is the most acidic because the electron-withdrawing chlorine substituent further stabilises the phenoxide ion compared to plain phenol, while benzyl alcohol and cyclohexanol are simple (non-aromatic-stabilised) alcohols and are far weaker acids than any phenol.

questions.text: The gravitational force between a hydrogen atom and another particle of mass m will be given by Newton's law, F = GMm/r², where M is
options: M = m_proton + m_electron – B/c² (B = 13.6 eV is the binding energy).
M, unrelated to the mass of the hydrogen atom.
M = m_proton + m_electron – |V|/c² (|V| = magnitude of the electron's potential energy in the H-atom).
questions.topic: Mass-Energy Equivalence and Gravitational Mass of the H-atom
questions.explanation: By mass-energy equivalence, the total rest mass-energy of the bound hydrogen atom is less than the sum of the free proton and electron masses by exactly the binding energy B = 13.6 eV (not the potential energy magnitude |V|, which is twice as large). So M = m_proton + m_electron – B/c².

questions.text: The graph which shows the variation of the de Broglie wavelength (λ) of a particle and its associated momentum (p) is
options: λ vs p: straight line increasing
λ vs p: straight line decreasing
λ vs p: increasing curve (hyperbola-like rising)
λ vs p: decreasing curve (hyperbola, λ=h/p)
questions.explanation: λ = h/p, so λ is inversely proportional to p — a decreasing hyperbolic curve as shown in option (4).

questions.text: The calculated spin only magnetic moment of Cr2+ ion is:
questions.explanation: Cr2+ has configuration 3d4, giving 4 unpaired electrons. Spin-only magnetic moment μ = √(n(n+2)) = √(4×6) = √24 ≈ 4.90 BM.

questions.text: When light propagates through a material medium of relative permittivity εr and relative permeability μr, the velocity of light v is given by: (c: velocity of light in vacuum)
questions.topic: Velocity of Light in a Medium
questions.explanation: Refractive index n = √(εrμr) = c/v, so v = c/√(εrμr).

questions.text: The correct decreasing order of basic strength of the species H2O, NH3, OH-, and NH2- is
questions.topic: Decreasing Order of Basic Strength: H2O, NH3, OH-, NH2-
questions.explanation: Comparing the conjugate bases of very weak acids (NH3, pKa≈38, and H2O, pKa≈15.7) shows that NH2- (amide ion) is a far stronger base than OH- (hydroxide), since NH3 is a much weaker acid than H2O. Between the neutral molecules, NH3 is more basic than H2O, giving the overall order NH2- > OH- > NH3 > H2O.

questions.text: The electric field intensity produced by the radiation from a 100 W bulb at a 3 m distance is E. The electric field intensity produced by the radiation from a 50 W bulb at the same distance is
questions.topic: Electric Field Intensity vs Bulb Power
questions.explanation: The intensity of an EM wave is proportional to the square of the electric field amplitude, and intensity at a fixed distance is proportional to the source power. So E ∝ √P. Hence the field from the 50 W bulb is E×√(50/100) = E/√2.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 34 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A first-order reaction is 50% completed in 1.26×10¹⁴ s. How much time would it take for 100% completion?
questions.topic: Time for 100% Completion of a First-Order Reaction
questions.explanation: A first-order reaction follows exponential decay and, mathematically, the reactant concentration only approaches zero asymptotically but never reaches it in any finite time, so 100% completion technically requires an infinite amount of time.

questions.text: At a point A on the earth's surface the angle of dip, delta = +25 degrees. At a point B on the earth's surface the angle of dip, delta = -25 degrees. We can interpret that:
options: A is located in the northern hemisphere and B is located in the southern hemisphere
A and B are both located in the southern hemisphere.
A and B are both located in the northern hemisphere.
A is located in the southern hemisphere and B is located in the northern hemisphere.
questions.explanation: By sign convention, positive dip angle indicates the magnetic needle points towards the surface of the earth (northern hemisphere), while negative dip indicates southern hemisphere. So A (+25°) is in northern hemisphere and B (-25°) is in southern hemisphere.

questions.text: An ideal gas is made of polyatomic molecules. Each of the molecules has three translational, three rotational and f number of vibrational modes. If the ratio of heat capacities Cp/Cv of the gas is 8/7, then the value of f is:
questions.topic: Degrees of Freedom and Specific Heat Ratio
questions.explanation: Total degrees of freedom = 3 (translational) + 3 (rotational) + 2f (each vibrational mode contributes 2, for kinetic and potential energy). gamma = Cp/Cv = 1 + 2/(degrees of freedom) = 8/7, so 2/(dof) = 1/7, giving dof = 14. So 3+3+2f = 14, 2f = 8, f = 4.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides. (2) The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4. (3) Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group. (4) Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
options: Alkali metals react with water to form their hydroxides.
The oxidation number of K in KO2 is +4.
Ionisation enthalpy of alkali metals decreases from top to bottom in the group.
Lithium is the strongest reducing agent among the alkali metals.
questions.explanation: In KO2 (potassium superoxide), potassium has oxidation state +1 (not +4), since the superoxide ion O2- has an overall charge of -1. The other statements about alkali metals reacting with water, decreasing ionisation enthalpy down the group, and lithium being the strongest reducing agent are all correct.

questions.text: An electromagnetic wave of wavelength 'λ' is incident on a photosensitive surface of negligible work function. If 'm' is the mass of photoelectron emitted from the surface has de-Broglie wavelength λd, then:
questions.topic: de Broglie Wavelength and Photoelectric Effect
questions.explanation: With negligible work function, hc/λ = Kmax. Also λd = h/√(2mKmax), so Kmax = h²/(2mλd²). Equating: hc/λ = h²/(2mλd²), giving λ = (2mc/h)λd².

questions.text: Cyclohexylmagnesium bromide is treated with cyclohexylamine. One of the products formed in this reaction is:
options: 2-(cyclohexylamino)cyclohexan-1-amine type product (a C-C coupled ring with an NH2 group)
Bicyclohexyl (two cyclohexane rings joined by a C-C bond)
Dicyclohexylamine (two cyclohexyl rings joined via NH)
questions.topic: Reaction of Grignard Reagent with Active Hydrogen Compounds
questions.explanation: Cyclohexylamine has an acidic N-H proton. Grignard reagents are strong bases and react instantly with any compound having an active (acidic) hydrogen via a simple acid-base (protonation) reaction rather than nucleophilic addition, since there is no electrophilic carbon available in the amine. The Grignard's carbanion-like cyclohexyl group is protonated to form cyclohexane, while the amine is converted to its magnesium bromide salt (BrMg-NH-C6H11).

questions.text: Under isothermal condition a gas at 300 K expands from 0.1 L to 0.25 L against a constant external pressure of 2 bar. The work done by the gas is: [Given that 1 L bar = 100 J]
Two identical balls A and B having velocities of 0.5 m/s and -0.3 m/s respectively collide elastically in one dimension. The velocities of B and A after the collision respectively will be:
questions.explanation: For an elastic collision between two identical masses, the velocities are simply interchanged. So A's final velocity = -0.3 m/s, B's final velocity = 0.5 m/s. Since the question asks for B then A: 0.5 m/s and -0.3 m/s.

questions.text: The correct order of energies of molecular orbitals of N2 molecule is:
options: sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < sigma2pz < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < sigma2pz < sigma*2pz < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py)
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma2pz < sigma*2pz
sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < sigma2pz < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz
questions.explanation: For N2 (and other molecules with atomic number up to 7, where there is significant s-p mixing), the correct molecular orbital energy order is: sigma1s < sigma*1s < sigma2s < sigma*2s < (pi2px = pi2py) < sigma2pz < (pi*2px = pi*2py) < sigma*2pz. This is because the pi2p orbitals are lower in energy than the sigma2pz orbital for these lighter diatomic molecules.

questions.text: On addition of a small amount of KMnO4 to concentrated H2SO4, a green oily compound is obtained which is highly explosive in nature. Identify the compound.
questions.topic: Green Oily Explosive Compound from KMnO4 and Conc. H2SO4
questions.explanation: Concentrated H2SO4 dehydrates KMnO4 to form manganese heptoxide (Mn2O7), a green, oily, and highly explosive covalent oxide of manganese in its +7 oxidation state.

questions.text: Match List - I with List - II. List-I: A. XeO3, B. XeF2, C. XeOF4, D. XeF6. List-II: I. sp³d; linear, II. sp³; pyramidal, III. sp³d³; distorted octahedral, IV. sp³d²; square Pyramidal. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: XeO3 is sp³ hybridized, pyramidal (II). XeF2 is sp³d, linear (I). XeOF4 is sp³d², square pyramidal (IV). XeF6 is sp³d³, distorted octahedral (III). So A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.

questions.text: Using the standard electrode potentials, find out the pair between which redox reaction is not feasible: Fe3+/Fe2+ = +0.77 V; I2/I− = +0.54 V; Cu2+/Cu = +0.34 V; Ag+/Ag = +0.80 V.
questions.topic: Feasibility of Redox Reactions from E° Values
questions.explanation: For the Ag/Fe3+ pair, Ag must be oxidised (reverse of Ag+/Ag, giving −0.80 V) while Fe3+ is reduced (+0.77 V). The net cell potential = 0.77 − 0.80 = −0.03 V, which is negative, so this redox reaction is not thermodynamically feasible, unlike the other listed pairs.

questions.text: A shell of mass m is at rest initially. It explodes into three fragments having equal mass in the ratio 2:2:1. If the fragments having equal mass fly off along mutually perpendicular directions with speed v, the speed of the third (lighter) fragment is:
questions.explanation: Net linear momentum after explosion must be zero. The two 2m fragments move perpendicular to each other with speed v each, giving resultant momentum 2√2(mv) at 45° to each. This must be balanced by the m fragment: mv' = 2√2 mv ⟹ v' = 2√2 v.

questions.text: In the following reaction sequence, X and Z, respectively, are: CH3CH2CH2-OH + PCl3 → CH3CH2CH2Cl + X + HCl; Z (via alc. KOH, Δ) ← (C6H5CO)2O2/HBr ← CH3-CH-CH3(Br) [cyclohexane ring intermediate Y]
questions.topic: Identifying X and Z in reaction sequence
questions.explanation: Reaction of an alcohol with PCl3 gives the alkyl chloride plus H3PO3 (not POCl3) as the byproduct (X=H3PO3); the subsequent anti-Markovnikov HBr addition (peroxide effect) followed by dehydrohalogenation gives Z=CH3CH2CH2-Br.

questions.text: In a plane electromagnetic wave travelling in free space, the electric field component oscillates sinusoidally at a frequency of 2.0×10^10 Hz and amplitude 48Vm^-1. Then the amplitude of oscillating magnetic field is: (Speed of light in free space = 3 × 10^8 ms^-1)
questions.topic: Electric and Magnetic Field Amplitude Relation

questions.text: Which of the following units is useful in relating the concentration of a solution with its vapour pressure?
questions.topic: Concentration Unit Linked to Vapour Pressure
questions.explanation: Raoult's law relates a solution's vapour pressure directly to the mole fraction of its components, making mole fraction the natural concentration unit for this relationship.

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following: (1) All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals. (2) All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals. (3) In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state. (4) The shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx2-y2 and dz2 are similar to each other.
options: All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals.
All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals.
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy in free state.
The shapes of dxy, dyz and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx2-y2 and dz2 are similar to each other.
questions.topic: Shapes and Sizes of d Orbitals
questions.explanation: While dxy, dyz, and dzx orbitals do have similar shapes to each other (all 4-lobed, lying between axes), dx2-y2 and dz2 do NOT have similar shapes to each other: dx2-y2 has 4 lobes along the axes, while dz2 has a unique dumbbell-with-torus shape. So statement 4 is incorrect.

questions.text: For a first order reaction A -> Product, initial concentration of A is 0.1 M, which becomes 0.001 M after 5 minutes. Rate constant for the reaction in min-1 is:

A uniform conducting wire of length 12a and resistance 'R' is wound up as a current carrying coil in the shape of (i) an equilateral triangle of side 'a', (ii) a square of side 'a'. The magnetic dipole moments of the coil in each case respectively are:
questions.topic: Magnetic moment of wire coils (triangle vs square)
questions.explanation: Triangle: 4 turns of side a (12a/3a=4 turns), area=(√3/4)a², m=4×I×(√3/4)a²=√3Ia². Square: 3 turns of side a (12a/4a=3), area=a², m=3×I×a²=3Ia². So √3Ia² and 3Ia².

questions.text: Enzymes that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer require an alkaline earth metal (M) as the cofactor. M is:
questions.explanation: Mg2+ is the alkaline earth metal cofactor required by enzymes (kinases) that utilize ATP in phosphate transfer reactions, as it helps stabilize the negative charges on the phosphate groups of ATP.

questions.text: Copper crystallises in fcc unit cell with cell edge length of 3.608 x 10^-8 cm. The density of copper is 8.92 g/cm^3. Calculate the atomic mass of copper.
questions.topic: Atomic Mass from Unit Cell Density
questions.explanation: For fcc, Z=4. Using density formula d = ZM/(Na*a^3): M = d*Na*a^3/Z = (8.92 x 6.022x10^23 x (3.608x10^-8)^3)/4 = 63.1 g/mol (u).

questions.text: The rate law for the reaction A + 2B → C is found to be Rate = k[A][B]. If the concentration of reactant 'B' is doubled, keeping the concentration of 'A' constant, the value of the rate constant will be
questions.topic: Rate Constant is Independent of Concentration
questions.explanation: The rate constant k is a characteristic of the reaction at a given temperature and does not depend on the concentrations of the reactants; only the overall rate (not k itself) changes when concentrations are changed.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. Microwave, B. Visible light, C. Gamma rays, D. Infra-red rays. List II — I. Electrons in atoms emit light when they move from a higher to a lower energy level, II. Radioactive decay of nucleus, III. Vibration of atoms and molecules, IV. Klystron valve or magnetron valve.
questions.explanation: Microwave produced by klystron/magnetron (IV); visible light from electron transitions (I); gamma rays from radioactive decay (II); infra-red from vibration of atoms/molecules (III). A-IV, B-I, C-II, D-III.

questions.text: Which amongst the following will be most readily dehydrated under acidic conditions? Four substituted pentane-diol/nitro-alcohol structures are given, each bearing a NO2 group and an OH group at different positions along the chain, with structure (2) having the NO2 and OH groups positioned to form the most stable carbocation on dehydration (adjacent to a secondary carbon away from the electron-withdrawing NO2 group).
options: Structure (1): OH groups at two positions on a branched chain with no NO2 group
Structure (2): NO2 group at one end, OH at the other end, forming the most stable secondary carbocation farthest from the electron-withdrawing NO2 group
Structure (3): NO2 and OH groups adjacent, destabilizing the forming carbocation
Structure (4): NO2 and OH groups close together on adjacent carbons, destabilizing the forming carbocation
questions.explanation: Dehydration under acidic conditions proceeds via carbocation formation, and the rate depends on carbocation stability. The NO2 group is strongly electron-withdrawing and destabilizes a nearby carbocation. In structure (2), the OH group (which leaves as water) is positioned such that the resulting carbocation forms far from the NO2 group, making it the most stable carbocation among the options and hence the most readily dehydrated.

questions.text: The average thermal energy for a mono-atomic gas is: (kB is Boltzmann constant and T, absolute temperature)
questions.topic: Average thermal energy per degree of freedom for a monatomic gas
questions.explanation: A monatomic gas has 3 translational degrees of freedom, each contributing (1/2)kBT, giving total average thermal energy = (3/2)kBT.

questions.text: One end of string of length l is connected to a particle of mass 'm' and the other end is connected to a small peg on a smooth horizontal table. If the particle moves in a circle with speed 'v', the net force on the particle (directed towards center) will be (T represents the tension in the string):
questions.topic: Circular motion on a smooth horizontal table
questions.explanation: On a smooth horizontal table, tension T itself provides the entire centripetal force (T = mv²/l), so the net force directed towards the center is simply T.

questions.text: Consider the following nuclear reaction: ²³⁸U → ²³⁴Th + ⁴He. Take masses of ²³⁸U, ²³⁴Th and ⁴He as 238.050 u, 234.043 u and 4.003 u, respectively. The Q value for the reaction, in keV, is: [Given: 1 u = 931.5 MeV c⁻²]
Which of the following is an incorrect statement?
options: GeX4 (X = F, Cl, Br, I) is more stable than GeX2
questions.topic: Group 14 Elements - Stability of Oxidation States
questions.explanation: Due to the inert pair effect, Pb(II) is more stable than Pb(IV), and PbF4 is actually ionic in nature (not covalent) due to the large size and high charge density effects, making statement 3 the incorrect one.

questions.text: Match List I with List II: List I — A. C2H4, B. C2H2, C. CH4, D. NH3. List II — I. 3σ bonds, 2π bonds, II. 3σ bonds, one lone pair, III. 4σ bonds, IV. 5σ bonds, 1π bond.
questions.explanation: C2H4 (ethylene) has 5σ+1π bonds (IV); C2H2 (acetylene) has 3σ+2π bonds (I); CH4 has 4σ bonds (III); NH3 has 3σ bonds + 1 lone pair (II). A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II.

questions.text: A nucleus with mass number 240 breaks into two fragments each of mass number 120, the binding energy per nucleon of unfragmented nuclei is 7.6 MeV while that of fragments is 8.5 MeV. The total gain in the Binding Energy in the process is:
questions.topic: Binding energy gain in nuclear fission

questions.text: A galvanometer of resistance 100 Ω gives full scale deflection for a current of 1 mA. It is converted into an ammeter of range 0–10 A. The shunt required is:

A thin spherical shell is charged by some source. The potential difference between the two points C and P (in V) shown in the figure is: (Take 1/4πε₀ = 9×10⁹ SI units) [Figure: spherical shell of radius R=3cm, q=1μC, C is centre, P is a point on the shell surface]
questions.topic: Potential at Surface vs Nearby External Point of a Charged Shell
questions.explanation: For a charged spherical shell, the potential is the same at the centre (C) and at the surface (any point including P on the surface), both equal to kq/R. So VP - VC = 0.

questions.text: In which of the following devices the eddy current effect is not used?
questions.explanation: An electric heater works by simple resistive (Joule) heating, not by the eddy current effect, unlike induction furnace and magnetic braking which use eddy currents.

questions.text: A screw gauge has least count of 0.01 mm and there are 50 divisions in its circular scale. The pitch of the screw gauge is:
questions.topic: Pitch of a screw gauge from least count and divisions
questions.explanation: Pitch = Least count × number of divisions on circular scale = 0.01×50 = 0.5 mm.

questions.text: The ratio of the radius of gyration of a thin uniform disc about an axis passing through its centre and normal to its plane to the radius of gyration of the disc about its diameter is
