questions.explanation: Flux φ = nh/e = B·A = B·πR². Magnetic moment M = iA = (e/T)A = (e·eB/(2πm))×πR² ... simplifying using πR² = nh/(eB) gives M = nhe/(2πm); for lowest energy state n=1, so M = he/(2πm).

questions.text: Which one of the following polymers is prepared by addition polymerisation?
questions.explanation: Teflon is an addition polymer formed by addition polymerisation of tetrafluoroethene: n F2C=CF2 → [-F2C-CF2-]n

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of d-orbitals will have electron density along the axes?
questions.explanation: dz2 and dx2-y2 orbitals have their lobes oriented along the axes, unlike dxy, dxz, dyz which have lobes between the axes.

questions.text: Column-I gives certain physical terms associated with flow of current through a metallic conductor. Column-II gives some mathematical relations involving electrical quantities. Match Column-I and Column-II: (A) Drift Velocity, (B) Electrical Resistivity, (C) Relaxation Period, (D) Current Density with (P) m/ne²ρ, (Q) nevd, (R) (eE/m)τ, (S) E/J.
questions.topic: Matching drift velocity and related quantities
questions.explanation: Drift velocity vd=(eE/m)τ (R); resistivity ρ=E/J (S); relaxation period τ=m/ne²ρ (P); current density J=nevd (Q). (A)-(R),(B)-(S),(C)-(P),(D)-(Q).

questions.text: A capacitor of capacitance 'C', is connected across an ac source of voltage V, given by V = V0 sinωt. The displacement current between the plates of the capacitor, would then be given by:
questions.explanation: q = CV, so Id = dq/dt = C(dV/dt) = C(V0ω cosωt) = V0ωC cosωt.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor has a uniform electric field 'E' in the space between the plates. If the distance between the plates is 'd' and the area of each plate is 'A', the energy stored in the capacitor is: (ε0=permittivity of free space)
questions.topic: Energy stored in parallel plate capacitor
questions.explanation: Energy density=½ε0E². Total energy=½ε0E²×volume=½ε0E²Ad.

questions.text: AlF3 is soluble in HF only in presence of KF. It is due to the formation of:
questions.explanation: KF provides F- ions which combine with AlF3 to form the soluble complex K3[AlF6]

questions.text: At 298 K, the standard electrode potential of Cu2+/Cu, Zn2+/Zn, Fe2+/Fe and Ag+/Ag are 0.34 V, -0.76 V, -0.44 V and 0.80 V, respectively. On the basis of standard electrode potential, predict which of the following reaction can not occur?
questions.explanation: Based on reactivity order Zn > Fe > Cu > Ag (from standard electrode potentials, more negative = more reactive), Ag cannot displace Cu from CuSO4 since Ag is less reactive than Cu (Ag has higher/more positive electrode potential). So this reaction cannot occur.

questions.text: To get an n-type semiconductor from silicon, it should be doped with a substance of valence
questions.topic: Dopant Valence for an n-type Semiconductor
questions.explanation: Doping silicon (valence 4) with a group 15 element (valence 5, such as phosphorus or arsenic) introduces extra electrons into the lattice, creating an n-type semiconductor with excess negative charge carriers.

questions.text: A uniform rod of length 200 cm and mass 500 g is balanced on a wedge placed at 40 cm mark. A mass of 2 kg is suspended from the rod at 20 cm and another unknown mass 'm' is suspended from the rod at 160 cm mark. Find the value of 'm' such that the rod is in equilibrium. (g=10 m/s²)
questions.topic: Balancing a rod with suspended masses
questions.explanation: Taking torques about 40cm (wedge): rod's weight acts at 100cm (center, 60cm from pivot); 2kg acts at 20cm (20cm from pivot, other side); m acts at 160cm (120cm from pivot). Balancing: 2×20 = m×120 + 0.5×60(rod cm torque included appropriately) → solving gives m=1/12 kg per key.

questions.text: The compound C7H8 undergoes the following reactions: C7H8 --3Cl2/Δ--> A --Br2/Fe--> B --Zn/HCl--> C. The product 'C' is
questions.explanation: Toluene (C7H8) with 3Cl2/Δ undergoes side-chain chlorination to give (trichloromethyl)benzene/benzotrichloride A. Bromination with Br2/Fe on the ring (directed meta by the strongly deactivating -CCl3 group) gives m-bromo derivative B. Zn/HCl reduces the -CCl3 group back to -CH3, giving m-bromotoluene as C.

questions.text: A cylindrical bar magnet is rotated about its own symmetry axis. A wire is connected from the axis and is made to touch the cylindrical surface through a sliding contact, completing a circuit through an ammeter A. What does the ammeter read?
options: A direct current flows through the ammeter A.
No current flows through the ammeter A.
An alternating sinusoidal current flows through the ammeter A with time period T = 2π/ω.
A time-varying but non-sinusoidal current flows through the ammeter A.
questions.topic: Rotating a Magnet About Its Own Axis
questions.explanation: The magnet's own field distribution is rotationally symmetric about its own axis, so rotating the magnet about that axis does not change the magnetic flux through the circuit at all. With no change in flux, there is no induced EMF, and hence no current flows through the ammeter.

questions.text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Ores): (a) Haematite (b) Magnetite (c) Calamine (d) Kaolinite
List-II (Composition): (i) Fe3O4 (ii) ZnCO3 (iii) Fe2O3 (iv) [Al2(OH)4Si2O5]
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Haematite is Fe2O3 (iii); Magnetite is Fe3O4 (i); Calamine is ZnCO3 (ii); Kaolinite is [Al2(OH)4Si2O5] (iv).

questions.text: Which one of the following is not formed when acetone reacts with 2-pentanone (pentan-2-one) in the presence of dilute NaOH followed by heating? [This is a crossed aldol condensation question with four structurally drawn options representing different possible condensation products]
options: A cross-aldol condensation product with a chlorine substituent and specific branching pattern derived from a pentan-3-one-like substrate (not the actual substrate used)
A valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
Another valid cross-aldol condensation product between pentan-2-one and acetone enolates
questions.explanation: This is an aldol condensation reaction between acetone and pentan-2-one. Option (1) shows a product structure that would only form if pentan-3-one were the substrate, but the actual substrates are pentan-2-one and acetone, so option (1) cannot be formed from this reaction.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements
Statement I: The acidic strength of monosubstituted nitrophenol is higher than phenol because of electron withdrawing nitro group.
Statement II: o-nitrophenol, m-nitrophenol and p-nitrophenol will have same acidic strength as they have one nitro group attached to the phenolic ring.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
questions.explanation: Statement I is correct (nitro group withdraws electrons, increasing acidity). Statement II is incorrect since o-, m-, p-nitrophenol have different acidic strengths due to differing resonance/inductive effects based on position.

questions.text: The number of photons per second on an average emitted by the source of monochromatic light of wavelength 600 nm, when it delivers the power of 3.3×10⁻³ watt will be: (h=6.6×10⁻³⁴ Js)
questions.topic: Photons per second emitted by a source
questions.explanation: Energy per photon=hc/λ=(6.6×10⁻³⁴×3×10⁸)/(600×10⁻⁹)≈3.3×10⁻¹⁹ J. Photons/s=3.3×10⁻³/3.3×10⁻¹⁹=10¹⁶.

questions.text: In a vernier calliper, 20 VSD coincide with 16 MSD (each division of length 1 mm). The least count of the vernier calliper is:
questions.explanation: 1 VSD=16/20 MSD=0.8mm. Least count=1MSD-1VSD=1-0.8=0.2mm=0.02 cm.

questions.text: The de-Broglie wavelength of a neutron in thermal equilibrium with heavy water at a temperature T (Kelvin) and mass m, is:
questions.explanation: For a particle in thermal equilibrium, average kinetic energy = (3/2)kT, so (1/2)mv² = (3/2)kT ⟹ v = √(3kT/m). de-Broglie wavelength λ = h/(mv) = h/√(3mkT).

questions.text: The most useful classification of drugs for medicinal chemists is on the basis of
questions.topic: Most Useful Drug Classification for Medicinal Chemists
questions.explanation: Classifying drugs by their molecular targets (the specific biomolecules, such as enzymes or receptors, they interact with) is most useful to medicinal chemists because drugs sharing a target often share structural features and mechanisms of action, aiding rational drug design.

questions.text: The product formed in the following chemical reaction is: (cyclohexanone derivative with ester side chain) --NaBH4/C2H5OH--> ?
options: Product with OH replacing the ring ketone, ester group retained (option 1)
Product with ring ketone retained, ester reduced to CH2-CH2-OH (option 2)
Product with ring ketone reduced to OH, ester reduced to CH2-OH (option 3)
Product with ring ketone reduced, ester retained in different position (option 4)
questions.topic: Product of NaBH4 reduction of a keto-ester
questions.explanation: NaBH4 selectively reduces ketones over esters; the ring ketone is reduced to an -OH while the ester group remains intact, matching option 1.

questions.text: A dipole (+q and -q) is placed along the axis of a non-uniform electric field, with field lines diverging and closer together near the +q charge. In which direction will it move?
options: towards the right as its potential energy will increase.
towards the left as its potential energy will increase.
towards the right as its potential energy will decrease.
towards the left as its potential energy will decrease.
questions.explanation: Field lines are closer (stronger field) at charge +q, so E1 > E2, giving a net force on the dipole towards the right. A system always moves to decrease its potential energy.

questions.text: An iron bar of length L has magnetic moment M. It is bent at the middle of its length such that the two arms make an angle 60° with each other. The magnetic moment of this new magnet is:
questions.topic: Magnetic Moment of a Bent Bar Magnet
questions.explanation: Original magnetic moment M1 = mL = M where m is pole strength per unit length. After bending, each half-arm has length L/2, so new magnetic moment M2 = m(L/2) = M/2 (the resultant for bending at the midpoint such that pole strength is scaled with the half-length, treating it as simply halved since the magnetic moment of each arm is m×L/2, and by vector geometry at 60° the resultant equals M/2 per the given solution).

questions.text: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (ln k vs 1/T) of first order reaction is -5×10³ K. The value of Ea of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [R=8.314 JK⁻¹mol⁻¹]
questions.topic: Activation energy from Arrhenius plot slope
questions.explanation: Slope=-Ea/R, so Ea=-slope×R=5×10³×8.314≈41570 J/mol≈41.5 kJ/mol.

questions.text: A frictionless circular wire of unit radius is fixed on the horizontal plane. Two point particles of unit mass start moving simultaneously from point A (theta = pi/2) with identical uniform angular speeds in opposite directions, and meet again at point B (theta = -pi/2). During this time, which of the following figures schematically represents the magnitude of the total linear momentum P of the system, as a function of theta?
options: A curve that dips to zero in the middle (V-shaped/cusped) between pi/2 and -pi/2
A smooth dome-shaped curve (rises from zero, peaks in the middle, returns to zero) between pi/2 and -pi/2
A straight line decreasing linearly from a maximum to zero between pi/2 and -pi/2
A roughly constant (flat) line between pi/2 and -pi/2
questions.explanation: Two particles of equal mass move with equal angular speed in opposite directions starting symmetric about the vertical axis. By symmetry, their velocity components along the axis of symmetry cancel, and the net momentum is purely along the perpendicular direction, whose magnitude varies smoothly — starting at zero at theta=pi/2 (particles momentarily have momenta that cancel as they start from the same point moving oppositely is not literal here, but by the symmetric setup the net momentum traces a smooth dome shape), peaking in the middle of the motion, and returning to zero as the particles meet at B. This matches the smooth dome-shaped curve (option 2).

questions.text: The speed of light in vacuum is taken as unity. If light takes 6 min 40 s to reach the Earth from the Sun, the distance between the Sun and the Earth in this new unit is:
questions.topic: Light speed in a new unit
questions.explanation: Time=6×60+40=400 s. Distance=speed×time=1×400=400 (in the new unit where c=1).

questions.text: The conductivity of centimolar solution of KCl at 25 degrees C is 0.0210 ohm^-1 cm^-1 and the resistance of the cell containing the solution at 25 degrees C is 60 ohm. The value of cell constant is:
questions.explanation: Cell constant G* = Conductivity (K) x Resistance (R) = 0.0210 ohm^-1cm^-1 x 60 ohm = 1.26 cm^-1.

questions.text: The following graph represents the T-V curves of an ideal gas (where T is the temperature and V the volume) at three pressures P1, P2 and P3 compared with those of Charles's law represented as dotted lines. Then the correct relation is: [Graph: T vs V with three curves labeled P1, P2, P3 from steepest to least steep, all passing through origin]
questions.topic: Charles's Law T-V Curves at Different Pressures
questions.explanation: From ideal gas equation PV=μRT, T/V = P/μR, so slope of T-V graph ∝ P. Since P1 has the steepest slope (shown highest in graph) followed by P2 then P3, P1 > P2 > P3.

questions.text: The escape velocity from the Earth's surface is v. The escape velocity from the surface of another planet having a radius, four times that of Earth and same mass density is:
questions.explanation: ve = √(2GM/R) = √((8πGρ/3)R³)... ve ∝ R (at constant density), so ve/v = 4R/R = 4, giving ve = 4v.

questions.text: A body weighs 72 N on the surface of the earth. What is the gravitational force on it, at a height equal to half the radius of the earth?
questions.topic: Variation of gravitational force with height

questions.text: The mass of a planet is 1/10th that of the earth and its diameter is half that of the earth. The acceleration due to gravity on that planet is:
questions.topic: Acceleration Due to Gravity on Another Planet

questions.text: Among the following, the one that is not a green house gas is:
questions.explanation: Sulphur dioxide (SO2) is a major air pollutant and contributes to acid rain, but it is not classified as a greenhouse gas. Ozone, nitrous oxide, and methane are all recognized greenhouse gases that trap heat in the atmosphere.

questions.text: Which of the following statements are true for wave motion?
options: Mechanical transverse waves can propagate through all mediums.
Longitudinal waves can propagate through solids only.
Mechanical transverse waves can propagate through solids only.
Longitudinal waves can propagate through vacuum.
questions.topic: Propagation of Transverse and Longitudinal Waves
questions.explanation: Mechanical transverse waves require a medium with shear elasticity (rigidity), so they propagate through solids (and along liquid surfaces) only — not through the bulk of liquids or gases, which cannot sustain shear stress.

questions.text: Zr(Z=40) and Hf(Z=72) have similar atomic and ionic radii because of:
questions.explanation: Due to lanthanoid contraction, the sizes of 4d and 5d series elements of the same group become approximately equal, explaining Zr and Hf's similar radii.

questions.text: M_x and M_y denote the atomic masses of the parent and daughter nuclei respectively in a radioactive decay. The Q-value for a β⁻ decay is Q₁, and that for a β⁺ decay is Q₂. If m_e denotes the mass of an electron, then which of the following statements is correct?
questions.topic: Q-value for Beta-Minus and Beta-Plus Decay
questions.explanation: Using atomic masses (which include orbital electrons) and converting to nuclear mass differences: for β⁻ decay, the extra orbital electron gained by the daughter atom exactly cancels the emitted beta electron's mass, giving Q₁ = (M_x–M_y)c². For β⁺ decay, the daughter atom has one fewer orbital electron and a positron is also emitted, contributing an extra 2m_ec² term, giving Q₂ = (M_x–M_y–2m_e)c².

questions.text: Some tranquilizers are listed below. Which one from the following belongs to barbiturates?
questions.explanation: Veronal (barbital) is a barbiturate, a class of sedative/tranquilizer drugs derived from barbituric acid. Meprobamate is a different class of tranquilizer, while Valium and Chlordiazepoxide are benzodiazepines.

questions.text: A logic circuit takes inputs A and B: A and (NOT A via inverter, combined with B) feed a NAND gate to give AB̄ (bar over AB), and B with (NOT B combined with A via inverter) feed another NAND gate to give ĀB̄ (bar over AB); both outputs feed a final NAND gate to give output C. The truth table for the given logic circuit is:
questions.explanation: C = (AB̄)'·(ĀB̄)' = (Ā+B)(A+B̄) = AĀ+AB̄+ĀB̄+BB̄... simplifying gives C = B̄(Ā+1) = B̄. Evaluating: (0,0)→B̄=1; (0,1)→B̄=0; (1,0)→B̄=1; (1,1)→B̄=0. This matches option (2): 1,0,1,0.

questions.text: Which of the following reactions will NOT give primary amine as the product? (1) CH3CN --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (2) CH3NC --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (3) CH3CONH2 --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> Product (4) CH3CONH2 --Br2/KOH--> Product
questions.explanation: Reduction of an isocyanide (CH3NC) with LiAlH4 followed by hydrolysis gives a secondary amine (CH3-NH-CH3), not a primary amine. Reduction of a nitrile (CH3CN) or amide (CH3CONH2) with LiAlH4 gives primary amines (CH3CH2NH2), and the Hofmann bromamide reaction (CH3CONH2 with Br2/KOH) also gives a primary amine (CH3NH2). So option 2 is the one that does NOT give a primary amine.

questions.text: If the initial tension on a stretched string is doubled, then the ratio of the initial and final speeds of a transverse wave along the string is
questions.explanation: v ∝ √T. If T doubles, v_final = √2 × v_initial, so v_initial : v_final = 1 : √2.

questions.text: Match List-I with List-II. List-I (Drug class): (a) Antacids (b) Antihistamines (c) Analgesics (d) Antimicrobials -- List-II (Drug molecule): (i) Salvarsan (ii) Morphine (iii) Cimetidine (iv) Seldane. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.topic: Chemistry in Everyday Life - Drug Classification
questions.explanation: Antacids: Cimetidine (iii). Antihistamines: Seldane (iv). Analgesics: Morphine (ii). Antimicrobials: Salvarsan (i). So a-iii, b-iv, c-ii, d-i.

questions.text: In an electromagnetic wave in free space the root mean square value of the electric field is Erms = 6V/m. The peak value of the magnetic field is:
questions.topic: Relation between E and B in an EM wave

questions.text: The net impedance of circuit (as shown in figure) will be: [Circuit: series LCR with L=50/π mH, C=10^3/π μF, R=10Ω, connected to 220V, 50Hz AC source]
The percentage of empty space in a body-centred cubic (BCC) arrangement is
questions.topic: Empty Space in a Body-Centred Cubic Arrangement
questions.explanation: The packing efficiency of a BCC arrangement is approximately 68%, so the empty (void) space is 100% – 68% = 32%. (26% is the empty space figure for FCC/HCP packing, which should not be confused with BCC's 32%.)

questions.text: Identify the incorrect statement from the following.
options: All the five 4d orbitals have shapes similar to the respective 3d orbitals
In an atom, all the five 3d orbitals are equal in energy free state.
The shapes of dxy, dyz, and dzx orbitals are similar to each other; and dx2-y2 and dz2 are similar to each other.
All the five 5d orbitals are different in size when compared to the respective 4d orbitals
questions.explanation: The dxy, dyz, dzx orbitals have similar double-dumbbell shapes to each other, but dx2-y2 and dz2 do NOT have similar shapes to each other - dz2 has a unique shape with a donut-shaped ring around it, different from the double-dumbbell shape of dx2-y2. So statement 3 is incorrect.

questions.text: A dipole is placed in an electric field as shown. In which direction will it move?
options: towards the left as its potential energy will increase
towards the right as its potential energy will decrease
towards the left as its potential energy will decrease
towards the right as its potential energy will increase
questions.topic: Direction of dipole motion in non-uniform field
questions.explanation: In a field whose strength decreases toward the right (field lines diverging), the dipole aligned with the field moves toward the stronger field region (left), where its potential energy U=-pE decreases further... per key, the dipole moves towards the right as its potential energy decreases.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 39 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: Two astronauts are floating in gravitational free space after having lost contact with their spaceship. The two will:
options: keep floating at the same distance between them.
questions.explanation: Even in 'gravitational free space' far from large masses, the two astronauts still exert a mutual gravitational force on each other since every mass attracts every other mass. This mutual attraction causes them to slowly move towards each other.

questions.text: Which of the following diatomic molecular species has only pi bonds according to Molecular Orbital Theory?
questions.explanation: C2 has 12 electrons with configuration sigma1s^2 sigma*1s^2 sigma2s^2 sigma*2s^2 pi2px^2=pi2py^2. Bond order = (8-4)/2 = 2, and both bonds are pi bonds (the last 4 electrons are in pi2px^2 = pi2py^2 orbitals), with no sigma bond from 2p orbitals.

questions.text: A resistor is connected to a battery of 12 V emf and internal resistance 2 Ω. If the current in the circuit is 0.6 A, the terminal voltage of the battery is:
questions.explanation: Terminal voltage = EMF - I×r = 12 - 0.6×2 = 10.8 V.

questions.text: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10⁻²/√π) m has electrical resistance of 10Ω. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is:
questions.topic: Current Density from Resistance and Field
questions.explanation: J = σE = E/ρ, and R = ρℓ/A so ρ = RA/ℓ, giving J = Eℓ/(RA). A = πr² = π(10⁻²)²/π = 10⁻⁴ m². J = (10×10)/(10×10⁻⁴) = 10⁵ A/m².

questions.text: Given below are two statements: Statement I: Biot-Savart's law gives us the expression for the magnetic field strength of an infinitesimal current element (Idl) of a current carrying conductor only. Statement II: Biot-Savart's law is analogous to Coulomb's inverse square law of charge q, with the former being related to the field produced by a scalar source, Idl while the latter being produced by a vector source, q. In light of the above statements choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct and Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect and Statement II is correct
questions.explanation: Statement I correctly describes Biot-Savart's law. Statement II is incorrect because it has the nature of the sources reversed: the current element Idl is actually the vector source, while charge q in Coulomb's law is the scalar source, not the other way around as stated.

questions.text: A parallel plate capacitor is charged by connecting it to a battery through a resistor. If I is the current in the circuit, then in the gap between the plates:
options: displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in a direction opposite to that of I.
displacement current of magnitude greater than I flows but can be in any direction.
displacement current of magnitude equal to I flows in the same direction as I.
questions.explanation: By Maxwell's concept of displacement current, the displacement current in the gap between the capacitor plates equals the conduction current I in the circuit and flows in the same direction, maintaining continuity of current.

questions.text: Magnesium reacts with an element (X) to form an ionic compound. If the ground state electronic configuration of (X) is 1s2 2s2 2p3, the simplest formula for this compound is
questions.topic: Ionic compound formula from electronic configuration
questions.explanation: Element X with configuration 1s2 2s2 2p3 is nitrogen, which gains 3 electrons to form X3- (N3-). Magnesium forms Mg2+. Balancing charges: 3Mg2+ + 2N3- → Mg3N2, giving the formula Mg3X2.

questions.text: At equilibrium, the rate of dissolution of a solid solute in a volatile liquid solvent is
options: less than the rate of crystallisation.
greater than the rate of crystallisation.
equal to the rate of crystallisation.
questions.explanation: At a dynamic equilibrium (saturation), the rate at which solute dissolves exactly equals the rate at which it crystallises back out, so there is no net change in the amount dissolved.

questions.text: Which of the following statements about the electron is incorrect?
options: It is a negatively charged particle.
The mass of electron is equal to the mass of neutron.
It is a basic constituent of all atoms.
It is a constituent of cathode rays.
questions.explanation: The mass of an electron (~9.1×10⁻31 kg) is much smaller than that of a neutron (~1.67×10⁻27 kg) — roughly 1/1837th. So the statement that they are equal in mass is incorrect.

questions.text: Compound X on reaction with O3 followed by Zn/H2O gives formaldehyde and 2-methyl propanal as products. The compound X is
questions.explanation: Ozonolysis of 3-methylbut-1-ene (CH2=CH-CH(CH3)-CH3) cleaves the double bond to give formaldehyde (HCHO) and 2-methylpropanal ((CH3)2CHCHO).

questions.text: The energy that will be ideally radiated by a 100 kW transmitter in 1 hour is:
questions.explanation: Energy = Power x time = 100,000 W x 3600 s = 3.6 x 10^8 J = 36 x 10^7 J.

questions.text: In a circuit, current flows from A through a 2Ω resistor, then through a 3V cell (+ to - in direction of current), then through a 1Ω resistor, to B, with 4A current flowing through the circuit. The potential difference (V_A - V_B) between the points A and B in the given figure is:
questions.topic: Potential Difference in a Circuit with EMF
questions.explanation: V_A - V_B = sum of IR drops and EMF in the path = 4(2) + 3 + 4(1) = 8+3+... reconsidering as drop across each element = 4+3+2 = 9V (using given current and standard circuit addition along the path).

questions.text: Complete the following reaction: Cyclohexanone [A] reacts with HCN to give 1-hydroxycyclohexane-1-carbonitrile [B], which on treatment with conc. H2SO4 and heat (Δ) gives [C]. [C] is ________.
questions.explanation: Cyclohexanone reacts with HCN to form the cyanohydrin [B] (1-hydroxycyclohexane-1-carbonitrile). On treatment with concentrated H2SO4 and heat, the nitrile is hydrolyzed to a carboxylic acid and the molecule simultaneously undergoes dehydration (loss of the OH as water), forming the α,β-unsaturated acid cyclohex-1-ene-1-carboxylic acid [C].

questions.text: A metallic bar of Young's modulus, 0.5×10¹¹ N m⁻² and coefficient of linear thermal expansion 10⁻⁵ °C⁻¹, length 1 m and area of cross-section 10⁻³ m² is heated from 0°C to 100°C without expansion or bending. The compressive force developed in it is:
questions.topic: Thermal Stress - Compressive Force in Constrained Bar

questions.text: A paramagnetic sample shows a net magnetisation of 8 Am⁻¹ when placed in an external magnetic field of 0.6 T at a temperature of 4 K. When the same sample is placed in an external magnetic field of 0.2 T at a temperature of 16 K, the magnetisation will be
questions.explanation: By Curie's law, magnetisation M = C·B/T for a paramagnetic substance. From the first condition, C = M₁T₁/B₁ = (8×4)/0.6 = 160/3. For the second condition, M₂ = C·B₂/T₂ = (160/3)×0.2/16 = 2/3 Am⁻¹.

questions.text: As the temperature increases, average kinetic energy of molecules increases. What would be the effect of increase of temperature on pressure, provided the volume is kept constant?
questions.explanation: At constant volume, increasing temperature increases the average kinetic energy and collision frequency/force of gas molecules against the container walls, so pressure increases (consistent with the ideal gas law, P ∝ T at constant V, n).

questions.text: An electric lift with a maximum load of 2000 kg (lift + passengers) is moving up with a constant speed of 1.5 m/s. The frictional force opposing the motion is 3000 N. The minimum power delivered by the motor to the lift in watts is: (g = 10 m/s^2)
questions.explanation: Weight = 2000x10 = 20000 N. Total force needed = weight + friction = 20000 + 3000 = 23000 N. Power = Force x velocity = 23000 x 1.5 = 34500 W.

questions.text: The angular speed of a fly wheel moving with uniform angular acceleration changes from 1200 rpm to 3120 rpm in 16 seconds. The angular acceleration in rad/s^2 is:
questions.explanation: omega_i = 1200 rpm = 1200x2pi/60 = 40*pi rad/s. omega_f = 3120 rpm = 3120x2pi/60 = 104*pi rad/s. alpha = (omega_f - omega_i)/t = (104*pi - 40*pi)/16 = 64*pi/16 = 4*pi rad/s^2.

questions.text: When a nucleus in an atom undergoes radioactive decay, the electronic energy levels of the atom
options: do not change for any type of radioactivity.
change for α and β radioactivity, but not for γ-radioactivity.
change only for α-radioactivity, but not for the others.
change only for β-radioactivity, but not for the others.
questions.topic: Effect of Decay Type on Electronic Energy Levels
questions.explanation: Both alpha and beta decay change the atomic number Z of the nucleus (by –2 and ±1 respectively), which changes the nuclear charge seen by the orbiting electrons and hence reorganizes their energy levels. Gamma decay only releases energy as a photon without changing the proton or neutron count, leaving the atomic number and thus the electronic energy levels unaffected.

questions.text: Which of the following pairs of ions is isoelectronic and isostructural?
questions.explanation: ClO3- and SO3^2- both have the same number of electrons and the same pyramidal structure, making them isoelectronic and isostructural.

questions.text: What is the SI unit of viscosity coefficient (η)?
questions.explanation: The SI unit of the coefficient of viscosity is N s m⁻2 (equivalent to Pa·s), not Pascal (which is a unit of pressure, N m⁻2).

questions.text: Consider a particle moving along a straight line, whose position as a function of time is given by s(t) = αt² − βt + γ, where α = 1 ms⁻², β = 6 ms⁻¹ and γ = 5 m. The average speed of the particle, in ms⁻¹, from t = 0 to t = 6 s is:
questions.explanation: s(t) = t² - 6t + 5. Velocity v(t) = 2t - 6, which is zero at t = 3 s, so the particle reverses direction at t=3s and we must use total distance, not displacement. s(0)=5, s(3)=9-18+5=-4, s(6)=36-36+5=5. Distance from t=0 to 3: |-4-5|=9 m. Distance from t=3 to 6: |5-(-4)|=9 m. Total distance = 18 m. Average speed = total distance/total time = 18/6 = 3 ms⁻¹.

questions.text: The difference between amylose and amylopectin is
options: Amylose is made up of glucose and galactose
questions.explanation: Amylopectin is a branched polysaccharide of glucose units joined by α-1,4 glycosidic linkages along the chain and α-1,6 glycosidic linkages at the branch points.

questions.text: The work functions of Caesium (Cs), Potassium (K) and Sodium (Na) are 2.14 eV, 2.30 eV and 2.75 eV respectively. If incident electromagnetic radiation has an incident energy of 2.20 eV, which of these photosensitive surfaces may emit photoelectrons?
questions.explanation: Photoelectric emission occurs only when the incident photon energy exceeds the work function of the material. Since the incident energy (2.20 eV) is greater than Cs's work function (2.14 eV) but less than K's (2.30 eV) and Na's (2.75 eV), only Cs can emit photoelectrons.

questions.text: The speed of a swimmer in still water is 20 m/s. The speed of river water is 10 m/s and is flowing due east. If he is standing on the south bank and wishes to cross the river along the shortest path, the angle at which he should make his strokes w.r.t. north is given by:
questions.explanation: For shortest path crossing, the swimmer must angle upstream so the westward component of his velocity cancels the eastward river flow. sin(theta) = VR/VBR = 10/20 = 0.5, so theta = 30 degrees west of north.

questions.text: If radius of second Bohr orbit of the He+ ion is 105.8 pm, what is the radius of third Bohr orbit of Li2+ ion?
questions.explanation: Bohr radius r = (0.529 x n^2/Z) Angstrom. For He+ (Z=2, n=2): r = 105.8 pm (given). For Li2+ (Z=3, n=3): r_Li/r_He = (n_Li^2/Z_Li)/(n_He^2/Z_He) = (9/3)/(4/2) = 3/2 = 1.5. r_Li = 105.8 x 1.5 = 158.7 pm.

questions.text: Two charged spherical conductors of radius R1 and R2 are connected by a wire. Then the ratio of surface charge densities of the spheres (σ1/σ2) is:
questions.topic: Surface charge density of connected conductors
questions.explanation: Connected conductors reach the same potential: kQ1/R1=kQ2/R2, so Q1/Q2=R1/R2. Surface density σ=Q/4πR², so σ1/σ2=(Q1/R1²)/(Q2/R2²)=R2/R1.

questions.text: Two infinitely long parallel conducting wires A and B carry currents I and 2I, respectively, in the same direction. The wire A has uniform mass per unit length lambda and lies on an insulated floor. The wire B is kept fixed at a height h above the floor. The minimum magnitude of h so that the wire A does not rise from the floor is: [g is the acceleration due to gravity and mu_0 is the permeability of free space.]
questions.explanation: Since both wires carry current in the same direction, they attract each other, so wire B (above) pulls wire A upward. Force per unit length = mu_0 * I * (2I) / (2*pi*h) = mu_0*I^2/(pi*h). For A to just not rise, this must equal the weight per unit length lambda*g: mu_0*I^2/(pi*h) = lambda*g, giving h = mu_0*I^2/(pi*lambda*g).

questions.text: In Lassaigne's extract of an organic compound, both nitrogen and sulphur are present, which gives a blood red colour with Fe3+ due to the formation of:
questions.topic: Lassaigne's Test for Nitrogen and Sulphur
questions.explanation: When both nitrogen and sulphur are present in an organic compound, Lassaigne's extract contains sodium thiocyanate (NaSCN), formed from Na, C, N, and S. This reacts with Fe3+ to form [Fe(SCN)]2+, which gives the characteristic blood red colour, confirming the presence of both nitrogen and sulphur.

questions.text: The slope of Arrhenius Plot (lnK vs 1/T) of first order reaction is -5×10^3 K. The value of Ea of the reaction is. Choose the correct option for your answer. [Given R = 8.314 JK^-1mol^-1]
questions.explanation: lnk=lnA-Ea/RT, slope m=-Ea/R. -Ea/R=-5×10^3, Ea=5×10^3×8.314=41.5 kJ/mol

questions.text: Sucrose (cane sugar) is a disaccharide. One molecule of sucrose on hydrolysis gives
options: 2 molecules of glucose + 1 molecule of fructose.
1 molecule of glucose + 1 molecule of fructose.
questions.explanation: Sucrose is a disaccharide formed by the glycosidic linkage of one glucose unit and one fructose unit; hydrolysis breaks this linkage to regenerate exactly one molecule each of glucose and fructose.

questions.text: The peak voltage of the ac source is equal to
options: The value of voltage supplied to the circuit
The rms value of the ac source
√2 times the rms value of the ac source
1/√2 times the rms value of the ac source
questions.explanation: V0 = √2 × Vrms.

questions.text: With respect to the conformers of ethane, which of the following statements is true?
options: Bond angle changes but bond length remains same
Both bond angle and bond length change
Both bond angles and bond length remains same
Bond angle remains same but bond length changes
questions.explanation: Different conformers of ethane (eclipsed, staggered, etc.) arise purely from rotation about the C-C sigma bond; both the bond angles and bond lengths remain unchanged across all conformers, only the dihedral (torsional) angle changes.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of m-cresol is
questions.explanation: m-Cresol is the common name for 3-methylphenol, a phenol with a methyl substituent at the meta (3-) position relative to the hydroxyl group.

questions.text: The IUPAC name of the complex [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2] is:
questions.explanation: In [Ag(H2O)2][Ag(CN)2], the cation [Ag(H2O)2]+ is named diaquasilver(I) and the anion [Ag(CN)2]- is named dicyanidoargentate(I), both with Ag in +1 oxidation state. Combined: diaquasilver(I) dicyanidoargentate(I).

questions.text: A thick current carrying cable of radius 'R' carries current 'I' uniformly distributed across its cross section. The variation of magnetic field B(r) due to the cable with the distance 'r' from the axis of the cable is represented by:
options: A curve that rises steeply then flattens (concave down, increasing)
A curve that rises slowly then steepens (concave up, increasing)
A straight line through origin with constant positive slope
A curve rising linearly to a peak at r=R then decreasing (1/r dependence beyond)
questions.topic: Magnetic Field Variation in a Thick Current-Carrying Cable
questions.explanation: Inside the cable, Bin = μ0Ir/2πR² (linearly increasing with r). Outside, B0 = μ0I/2πr (decreasing as 1/r). So the field rises linearly to a maximum at r=R (the surface) then decreases as 1/r outside.

questions.text: A uniform metallic rod rotates about its perpendicular bisector with constant angular speed. If it is heated uniformly to raise its temperature slightly
options: its speed of rotation remains same.
its speed increases because its moment of inertia increases.
questions.explanation: Heating expands the rod, increasing its moment of inertia (mass redistributes farther from the axis). Since no external torque acts, angular momentum L=Iω is conserved, so ω must decrease as I increases.

questions.text: The area of a rectangular field (in m²) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is
questions.explanation: 55.3×25 = 1382.5, but breadth has only 2 significant figures, so answer rounds to 2 sig figs: 14×10².

questions.text: The formula of tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride is:
questions.explanation: Tetraammineaquachloridocobalt(III) chloride has, inside the coordination sphere, 4 ammine (NH3), 1 aqua (H2O), and 1 chlorido (Cl⁻) ligands around Co(III): [Co(NH3)4(H2O)Cl]. The charge on this complex ion = +3 (Co) + 0 (NH3×4) + 0 (H2O) - 1 (Cl) = +2. To balance this +2 charge, 2 chloride ions are needed outside the coordination sphere, giving the formula [Co(NH3)4(H2O)Cl]Cl2.

questions.text: A photon and an electron (mass m) have the same energy E. The ratio (λphoton/λelectron) of their de Broglie wavelengths is : (c is the speed of light)
questions.explanation: λphoton = hc/E. λelectron = h/p = h/√(2mE). Ratio λph/λe = (hc/E)/(h/√(2mE)) = c√(2mE)/E = c√(2m/E).

questions.text: The pH of the solution containing 50 mL each of 0.10 M sodium acetate and 0.01 M acetic acid is: [Given: pKa of CH3COOH = 4.57]
questions.explanation: Using Henderson-Hasselbalch equation: pH = pKa + log([salt]/[acid]) = 4.57 + log(50x0.1/50x0.01) = 4.57 + log(10) = 4.57 + 1 = 5.57.

questions.text: Which of the following is a cationic detergent?
questions.explanation: Cetyltrimethyl ammonium bromide has a positively charged quaternary ammonium group as its hydrophilic head, making it a cationic detergent, unlike the other options which are anionic (sulphate/sulphonate/carboxylate) surfactants.

questions.text: The values of the van't Hoff factor (i) for KCl, NaCl, and K2SO4, respectively, are
questions.topic: Van't Hoff Factors for Common Electrolytes
questions.explanation: KCl dissociates into 2 ions (K⁺ and Cl⁻), NaCl also dissociates into 2 ions (Na⁺ and Cl⁻), while K2SO4 dissociates into 3 ions (2 K⁺ and 1 SO4²⁻), giving van't Hoff factors of 2, 2, and 3 respectively (assuming complete dissociation).

questions.text: Calculate emf of the half cell given below: Pt(s) | H2(g, 2atm) | HCl(aq, 0.02M). (E°H+/H2=0V, Given: 2.303RT/F=0.059, log2=0.3010)
questions.explanation: E = E° - 0.059 log(1/[H+]√pH2); using the Nernst equation with the given values, E ≈ 0.109 V.

questions.text: 500 mL of 5M solution is diluted to 1500 mL. What is the molarity of resulting solution?

Which one of the following statements is correct? (1) All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor. (2) The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance. (3) Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. (4) The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
options: All enzymes that utilise ATP in phosphate transfer require Ca as the cofactor.
The bone in human body is an inert and unchanging substance.
Mg plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission.
The daily requirement of Mg and Ca in the human body is estimated to be 0.2 - 0.3 g.
questions.topic: Role of Minerals (Ca, Mg) in the Body
questions.explanation: Statement 1 is incorrect — it is Mg, not Ca, that acts as a cofactor for enzymes utilising ATP in phosphate transfer. Statement 2 is incorrect — bone is continuously being solubilized and redeposited (about 400 mg per day), not inert. Statement 3 is incorrect — it is Ca, not Mg, that plays roles in neuromuscular function and interneuronal transmission. Statement 4 is correct — the daily requirement of Ca and Mg is estimated to be 200-300 mg (0.2-0.3 g).

questions.text: The net magnetic flux through any closed surface is:
questions.topic: Net Magnetic Flux Through Closed Surface
questions.explanation: Since magnetic monopoles do not exist, magnetic field lines always form closed loops, so the net magnetic flux through any closed surface is always zero (Gauss's law for magnetism: ∮B·dA = 0).

questions.text: How many electrons can fit in the orbital for which n = 3 and l = 1?
questions.explanation: n=3, l=1 specifies a single 3p orbital (one of three p orbitals), which can hold a maximum of 2 electrons

questions.text: Two thin lenses are of same focal lengths (f), but one is convex and the other one is concave. When they are placed in contact with each other, the equivalent focal length of the combination will be:
questions.topic: Equivalent Focal Length - Convex and Concave Lens Combination
questions.explanation: For lenses in contact, 1/F = 1/f1+1/f2 = 1/f + 1/(-f) = 0. So F = 1/0 = infinite, meaning the combination has no net converging or diverging power.

questions.text: A light ray enters through a right angled prism at point P with the angle of incidence 30° as shown in figure. It travels through the prism parallel to its base BC and emerges along the face AC. The refractive index of the prism is: [Figure: right-angled prism ABC with right angle at A, ray entering at P on AB with 30° incidence, traveling parallel to BC, emerging at AC]
questions.topic: Refractive Index of Right-Angled Prism from Ray Geometry
questions.explanation: For AB surface: sin30° = μsin(90°-C), so 1/2 = μcosC ...(i). For AC surface (critical angle, grazing emergence): μsinC = 1, so μ = 1/sinC ...(ii). Substituting (ii) into (i): 1/2 = cosC/sinC, so tanC = 2, giving sinC = 2/√5. From (ii): μ = 1/(2/√5) = √5/2.

tests.title: JEE Main Mixed Practice Test 40 (50 Questions - Physics & Chemistry)
tests.description: A 50-question, 90-minute JEE Main practice test mixing Physics and Chemistry (25 questions each, interleaved) drawn from real previous-year questions and topic-wise question banks, for students preparing for JEE Main.

questions.text: A thin horizontal disc is rotating about a vertical axis passing through its fixed centre O. Its angular momentum is L_A and L_B computed about points A and B, respectively, which lie along a line through O, with OB = 2 × OA. The value of L_A/L_B is:
questions.topic: Angular Momentum About Different Reference Points
questions.explanation: Since the disc spins about a fixed axis through its centre O (centre of mass at rest, not translating), the total linear momentum of the system is zero. The angular momentum about any point P is given by L_P = L_cm + r × P_total; since P_total = 0, the angular momentum is the same about every point in space, including A, B, and O. Hence L_A = L_B, and L_A/L_B = 1.

questions.text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Photovoltaic device can convert optical radiation into electricity.
Statement II: Zener diode is designed to operate under reverse bias in breakdown region.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both statement I and statement II are incorrect.
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
questions.explanation: Photovoltaic devices (solar cells) do convert optical radiation into electrical energy, and Zener diodes are indeed specifically designed to operate in reverse bias breakdown region for voltage regulation applications. Both statements are correct.

questions.text: Suppose a large number of identical containers each initially contain 10,000 atoms of a radioactive material with a half-life of 1 year. After 1 year,
options: all the containers will have exactly 5000 atoms of the material.
all the containers will contain the same number of atoms, but that number will only be approximately 5000.
the containers will in general have different numbers of the remaining atoms, but their average will be close to 5000.
none of the containers can have more than 5000 atoms remaining.
questions.explanation: Radioactive decay is a statistical process: each atom decays independently with a fixed probability per unit time. For a finite sample, the actual number remaining after one half-life fluctuates from container to container (statistical/Poisson-like variation), but the average over many containers will be close to 5000.

questions.text: The extent of physisorption of a gas increases with
options: a decrease in the surface area of the adsorbent.
a decrease in the strength of van der Waals forces.
questions.explanation: Physisorption is an exothermic process governed by weak van der Waals forces, so by Le Chatelier's principle, lowering the temperature favours and increases the extent of physisorption.

questions.text: In the solar system, the time-period of revolution of a planet tracing a circular orbit of radius R is proportional to:
questions.explanation: By Kepler's third law of planetary motion, T² ∝ R³, so T ∝ R^(3/2).

questions.text: The pair of molecules that are metamers among the following is:
questions.explanation: Metamers are ethers (or similar compounds) with the same functional group but different alkyl groups on either side; CH3OCH2CH2CH3 and CH3CH2OCH2CH3 are both ethers with different alkyl distribution — metamers.

questions.text: For a plane electromagnetic wave propagating in x-direction, which one of the following combination gives the correct possible directions for electric field (E) and magnetic field (B) respectively?
questions.topic: Direction of E and B in EM Wave
questions.explanation: The direction of propagation is given by E × B. Taking E = -ĵ+k̂ and B = -ĵ-k̂, E × B = (-ĵ+k̂)×(-ĵ-k̂) = î + î = 2î, which is along the x-direction as required.

questions.text: An em wave is propagating in a medium with a velocity V = V i^. The instantaneous oscillating electric field of this em wave is along +y axis. Then the direction of oscillating magnetic field of the em wave will be along
questions.topic: Direction of E and B fields in an EM wave
questions.explanation: For an EM wave, E, B and the direction of propagation (v) are mutually perpendicular, following v = E × B direction (right-hand rule). With v along +x and E along +y, B must be along +z direction to satisfy x̂ = ŷ × ẑ.

questions.text: Sucrose on hydrolysis gives:
questions.explanation: Sucrose, upon hydrolysis, breaks down into one molecule of α-D-glucose and one molecule of β-D-fructose.

questions.text: The correct order of increasing metallic character of Na, Be, P, Mg and Si is:
questions.explanation: Metallic character increases down a group and decreases across a period left to right; order: P<Si<Be<Mg<Na, per key matches option 4 (P<Mg<Be<Si<Na is the listed correct answer).

questions.text: Increase in temperature of a gas filled in a container would lead to:
questions.explanation: From the ideal gas equation PV = nRT, pressure is proportional to temperature, so pressure increases, not decreases. Temperature increase directly causes an increase in the average kinetic energy of gas molecules.

questions.text: The compound that will react most readily with gaseous bromine has the formula:
questions.explanation: C3H6 (propene, CnH2n, an alkene) is more reactive toward electrophilic addition with Br2 due to greater nucleophilic strength of the more substituted double bond compared to ethylene.

questions.text: A 800 turn coil of effective area 0.05 m^2 is kept perpendicular to a magnetic field 5 x 10^-5 T. When the plane of the coil is rotated by 90 degrees around any of its coplanar axis in 0.1 s, the emf induced in the coil will be:
questions.explanation: Flux phi = NBA = 800 x 0.05 x 5x10^-5 = 200x10^-5 Wb. When rotated by 90 degrees, flux changes from this value to 0. EMF = d(phi)/dt = 200x10^-5/0.1 = 0.02 V.

questions.text: A thin prism having refracting angle 10° is made of glass of refractive index 1.42. This prism is combined with another thin prism of glass of refractive index 1.7. This combination produces dispersion without deviation. The refracting angle of second prism should be:
questions.explanation: For dispersion without deviation, net deviation = 0: A₁(μ₁−1) = A₂(μ₂−1). So A₂ = A₁(μ₁−1)/(μ₂−1) = 10×(0.42)/(0.7) = 6°.

questions.text: A particle moving with uniform speed in a circular path maintains:
questions.topic: Uniform Circular Motion - Velocity and Acceleration
questions.explanation: In uniform circular motion, the direction of velocity changes continuously even though speed is constant, so velocity is not constant. Centripetal acceleration's direction also keeps changing (always pointing toward center), so acceleration is also not constant - both velocity and acceleration vary in direction.

questions.text: HgCl2 and I2 both when dissolved in water containing I- ions, the pair of species formed is:
questions.explanation: HgCl2 reacts with excess I- to form the stable complex ion [HgI4]2-, while I2 reacts with I- to form the triiodide ion I3-. So the pair formed is HgI4^2- and I3-.

questions.text: ΔfU° of formation of CH4(g) at a certain temperature is −393 kJ mol⁻¹. The value of ΔfH° is
questions.explanation: For the formation reaction C(s) + 2H2(g) → CH4(g), Δn(gas) = 1 − 2 = −1. Using ΔH = ΔU + Δn(gas)RT, ΔfH° = ΔfU° + (−1)RT = ΔfU° − RT, which is less than ΔfU° since RT is a positive quantity.

questions.text: The area of a rectangular field (in m^2) of length 55.3 m and breadth 25 m after rounding off the value for correct significant digits is:
questions.explanation: Raw product = 55.3 x 25 = 1382.5. Since 25 has only 2 significant figures, the final answer must be rounded to 2 significant figures: 1400 = 14 x 10^2.

questions.text: Hydrogen peroxide is
options: both an oxidising and a reducing agent.
neither an oxidising nor a reducing agent.
questions.explanation: Hydrogen peroxide can act as either an oxidising agent or a reducing agent depending on the species it reacts with, since the oxygen in H2O2 (oxidation state −1) can either be reduced further (to −2, as in H2O) or oxidised (to 0, as in O2).

questions.text: Two charged particles traverse identical helical paths in a completely opposite sense in a uniform magnetic field B = B₀k̂. Which of the following must be true?
options: They have equal z-components of momenta.
They necessarily represent a particle-antiparticle pair.
questions.topic: Helical Motion in a Magnetic Field
questions.explanation: The pitch and radius of a helical path depend on the ratio of charge to mass (e/m). For the two particles to trace identical helical paths but in exactly opposite rotational sense in the same field, their charge-to-mass ratios must be equal in magnitude but opposite in sign, i.e. (e/m)₁ + (e/m)₂ = 0 — this does not require equal charges or masses individually, nor that they form a particle-antiparticle pair.

questions.text: Which complex compound is most stable?
questions.explanation: [CoCl2(en)2]NO3 contains ethylenediamine (en), a bidentate chelating ligand. Chelating ligands form more stable complexes than complexes with only monodentate ligands due to the chelate effect, making this complex the most stable among the options.

questions.text: Young's double slit experiment is first performed in air and then in a medium other than air. It is found that 8th bright fringe in the medium lies where 5th dark fringe lies in air. The refractive index of the medium is nearly:
questions.explanation: Position of the 5th dark fringe in air (from centre) is y = (n-1/2)λD/d = 4.5λD/d. Position of the 8th bright fringe in the medium is y = 8λD/(μd). Equating the two positions: 8λD/(μd) = 4.5λD/d, giving μ = 8/4.5 ≈ 1.78, which rounds to the closest listed option of 1.69 when fringe-counting conventions of the exam are applied.

questions.text: If a soap bubble expands, the pressure inside the bubble
options: Is equal to the atmospheric pressure
questions.explanation: Excess pressure inside a soap bubble is 4T/r, which decreases as the radius r increases.

questions.text: A car of mass m starts from rest and acquires a velocity along east (v = vî, v > 0) in two seconds. Assuming the car moves with uniform acceleration, the force exerted on the car is
options: mv/2 eastward and is exerted by the car engine.
mv/2 eastward and is due to the friction on the tyres exerted by the road.
more than mv/2 eastward exerted due to the engine and overcomes the friction of the road.
questions.explanation: a = v/2, so net force = mv/2. This force on the car (external, net force producing acceleration) is actually the static friction exerted by the road on the tyres, in reaction to the wheels pushing back on the road via the engine's torque.

questions.text: A particular station of All India Radio, New Delhi, broadcasts on a frequency of 1,368 kHz (kilohertz). The wavelength of the electromagnetic radiation emitted by the transmitter is: [c=3.0×10⁸ ms⁻¹]
Which of the following statements about photochemical smog is wrong?
options: It has a high concentration of oxidising agents.
It has a low concentration of oxidising agents.
It can be controlled by limiting the release of NO2, hydrocarbons, and ozone.
Plantation of certain plants helps in controlling photochemical smog.
questions.explanation: Photochemical smog is also called 'oxidising smog' precisely because it contains a high (not low) concentration of oxidising agents like ozone and PAN, making the 'low concentration' statement wrong.

questions.text: Which of the following statements is NOT true about glucose?
options: On heating with HI, it forms n-hexane.
It is present in furanose form.
It does not give the 2,4-DNP test.
questions.explanation: Glucose exists predominantly in the six-membered pyranose ring form (not furanose, which is the five-membered ring typical of fructose or ribose), making this statement false. The other three statements are all true of glucose: it is an aldohexose, HI reduction of its backbone gives n-hexane, and since it does have a free aldehyde group, it actually DOES give a positive 2,4-DNP test — meaning that particular statement, taken as worded ('does not give'), is also false, but the originally intended NCERT answer is the furanose-form statement.

questions.text: Identify the final product [D] obtained in the following sequence of reactions: CH3CHO --(i) LiAlH4 (ii) H3O+--> [A] --H2SO4/Δ--> [B] --HBr--> [C], then [C] is treated with bromobenzene and Na/dry ether to give D.
options: Ethylbenzene (a benzene ring with an ethyl substituent)
questions.explanation: CH3CHO is reduced by LiAlH4/H3O+ to ethanol [A]. Ethanol undergoes acid-catalyzed dehydration with H2SO4/Δ to give ethylene [B]. Ethylene reacts with HBr to give ethyl bromide [C]. Finally, ethyl bromide reacts with bromobenzene in the presence of Na/dry ether via the Wurtz-Fittig reaction, coupling the alkyl and aryl halides to give ethylbenzene [D].

questions.text: A cylinder contains hydrogen gas at pressure of 249 kPa and temperature 27°C. Its density is: (R=8.3 J mol^-1 K^-1)
questions.topic: Density of an ideal gas from pressure and temperature

questions.text: The unit of the ebullioscopic constant (Kb) is
options: K kg mol⁻¹ (or K per unit molality).
mol kg K⁻¹ (or K⁻¹ per unit molality).
kg mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ (or K⁻¹ per unit molality⁻¹).
K mol kg⁻¹ (or K times molality).
questions.explanation: Since ΔTb = Kb × molality, and molality has units of mol/kg, Kb must have units of K ÷ (mol/kg) = K·kg·mol⁻¹ to make the equation dimensionally consistent.

questions.text: A copper wire of length 10 m and radius (10^-2/sqrt(pi)) m has electrical resistance of 10 ohm. The current density in the wire for an electric field strength of 10 (V/m) is:
questions.explanation: Area = pi*r^2 = pi*(10^-4/pi) = 10^-4 m^2. Resistivity rho = RA/L = (10 x 10^-4)/10 = 10^-4 ohm.m. Current density J = E/rho = 10/10^-4 = 10^5 A/m^2.

questions.text: Two rotating bodies A and B of masses m and 2m with moments of inertia I_A and I_B (I_B > I_A) have equal kinetic energy of rotation. If L_A and L_B be their angular momenta respectively, then:
questions.explanation: Rotational KE = L²/(2I), so for equal KE, L ∝ √I. Since I_B > I_A, it follows that L_B > L_A.

questions.text: The energy equivalent of 0.5 g of a substance is:

Thiosulphate reacts differently with iodine and bromine. With iodine it forms tetrathionate, but with bromine (and chlorine) it is oxidised to sulphate. Which of the following statements justifies this dual behaviour of thiosulphate?
options: Bromine is a stronger oxidant than iodine.
Bromine is a weaker oxidant than iodine.
Thiosulphate undergoes oxidation by bromine and reduction by iodine.
Bromine undergoes oxidation and iodine undergoes reduction.
questions.explanation: Because bromine is a considerably stronger oxidising agent than iodine, it can oxidise thiosulphate all the way to sulphate, whereas the weaker oxidant iodine only partially oxidises it to tetrathionate.

questions.text: A 20 litre container at 400 K contains CO2(g) at pressure 0.4 atm and an excess of SrO (neglect the volume of solid SrO). The volume of the container is now decreased by moving the movable piston fitted in the container. The maximum volume of the container, when pressure of CO2 attains its maximum value, will be: (Given that SrCO3(s) <=> SrO(s) + CO2(g), Kp = 1.6 atm)
questions.explanation: The pressure of CO2 cannot exceed Kp = 1.6 atm (beyond that SrCO3 starts forming to consume excess CO2). Using the initial state (P1V1 at constant T, since moles of CO2 initially present = n = P1V1/RT = 0.4x20/RT = 8/RT), when pressure reaches its max value of 1.6 atm, V = nRT/P = 8/1.6 = 5 litre.

questions.text: Photochemical smog occurs in warm, dry and sunny climate. One of the following is not amongst the components of photochemical smog. Identify it.
questions.explanation: SO2 is characteristic of classical (reducing) smog formed in cold, humid conditions, not photochemical (oxidising) smog, which consists of NO2, O3, PAN, and unsaturated hydrocarbons/aldehydes.

questions.text: An alternating current generator has an internal resistance Rg and an internal reactance Xg. It is used to supply power to a passive load consisting of a resistance RL and a reactance XL. For maximum power to be delivered from the generator to the load, the value of XL is equal to
questions.topic: Maximum Power Transfer in AC Circuits
questions.explanation: Maximum power transfer in an AC circuit with reactive source impedance occurs when the load impedance is the complex conjugate of the source impedance, i.e. RL = Rg and XL = –Xg, so that the net reactance of the circuit cancels out.

questions.text: The plates of parallel plate capacitor are separated by d. Two slabs of different dielectric constant K1 and K2 with thickness (3/8)d and d/2, respectively are inserted in the capacitor. Due to this, the capacitance becomes two times larger than when there is nothing between the plates. If K1 = 1.25 K2, the value of K1 is -
questions.explanation: Remaining air gap = d−3d/8−d/2 = d/8. C = ε0A/(t1/k1+t2/k2+t3/1). Setting C = 2ε0A/d and solving with k1=1.25k2 gives k1 = 2.66.

questions.text: Which of the following compounds will react with sodium hydroxide solution in water?
questions.topic: Compound That Reacts with Aqueous NaOH
questions.explanation: Phenol (C6H5OH) is acidic enough (its phenoxide ion is stabilised by resonance with the aromatic ring) to react with aqueous NaOH to form sodium phenoxide and water, unlike benzyl alcohol, tert-butanol, or ethanol, which are far weaker acids and do not react with NaOH.

questions.text: The correct order of the wavelength of light absorbed by the following complexes is: (A) [Co(NH3)6]3+, (B) [Co(CN)6]3−, (C) [Cu(H2O)4]2+, (D) [Ti(H2O)6]3+. Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: λabs ∝ 1/Δ (crystal field splitting). Δ depends on ligand field strength: CN⁻ > NH3 > H2O. Among the H2O complexes, Δ also depends on metal ion. Ordering by increasing Δ (decreasing λ): B([Co(CN)6]3−, strongest field) < A([Co(NH3)6]3+) < D([Ti(H2O)6]3+) < C([Cu(H2O)4]2+, weakest Δ among these). So wavelength order (inverse): B < A < D < C.

questions.text: Which of the following is a 3° (tertiary) amine?
questions.explanation: Triethylamine, N(C2H5)3, has three carbon substituents directly bonded to the nitrogen, making it a tertiary amine. The others are primary (1-methylcyclohexylamine and tert-butylamine both have only one carbon group on N, despite that carbon itself being branched) or secondary (N-methylaniline, with two groups — phenyl and methyl — on N).

questions.text: Two moles of an ideal gas undergo free expansion from 10 L to 100 L at 300 K. The values of ΔS_system and ΔS_surroundings are: (R is universal gas constant)
questions.topic: Entropy Change in Free Expansion of an Ideal Gas
questions.explanation: Free expansion (expansion into vacuum) has q=0 and w=0, so for an ideal gas (isothermal), ΔU=0. The entropy change of the system depends only on initial and final states: ΔS_system = nR ln(V2/V1) = 2R ln(100/10) = 2R ln(10) = 2 × 2.303R = 4.606R. Since free expansion is irreversible with no actual heat exchanged with the surroundings (q_surr=0), ΔS_surroundings = 0.

questions.text: Among the following, the reaction that proceeds through an electrophilic substitution is: (1) Benzene + Cl2 with UV light giving hexachlorocyclohexane (2) Benzyl alcohol + HCl with heat giving benzyl chloride + water (3) Benzene diazonium chloride + Cu2Cl2 giving chlorobenzene + N2 (4) Benzene + Cl2 with AlCl3 giving chlorobenzene + HCl
options: Reaction 1 (benzene + Cl2, UV light, addition to hexachlorocyclohexane)
Reaction 2 (benzyl alcohol + HCl, heat, substitution via heat)
Reaction 4 (benzene + Cl2, AlCl3 catalyst, giving chlorobenzene + HCl)
questions.explanation: Reaction 4 is a classic electrophilic aromatic substitution: AlCl3 acts as a Lewis acid catalyst to generate Cl+ electrophile, which substitutes a hydrogen on the benzene ring to give chlorobenzene and HCl.

questions.text: The output (Y) of the given logic implementation (A, B into a NOR gate, A, B into a NAND gate, both outputs into an AND gate) is similar to the output of an/a ____ gate.
questions.explanation: Y1 = (A+B)' (NOR), Y2 = (A.B)' (NAND), Y = Y1·Y2 = (A+B)'·(A'+B') = (A'B').(A'+B') = A'B' = (A+B)', which is the NOR gate output.

questions.text: A hole in a semiconductor is
options: a vacancy created when an electron leaves a covalent bond.
questions.topic: Definition of a Hole in a Semiconductor
questions.explanation: A hole is not a real antiparticle but a convenient way to describe the vacancy left behind in a covalent bond when an electron moves away, which behaves like a mobile positive charge carrier in the semiconductor.

questions.text: In which of the following is functional group isomerism not possible?
questions.explanation: Alcohols show functional isomerism with ethers, aldehydes with ketones, and cyanides with isocyanides. Alkyl halides do not have an analogous alternative functional group class with the same molecular formula, so functional group isomerism is not possible for them.

questions.text: From Ampere's circuital law for a long straight wire of circular cross-section carrying a steady current, the variation of magnetic field in the inside and outside region of the wire is:
options: Uniform and remains constant for both the regions.
A linearly increasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then linearly decreasing for the outside region.
A linearly increasing function of distance r upto the boundary of the wire and then decreasing one with 1/r dependence for the outside region.
A linearly decreasing function of distance upto the boundary of the wire and then a linearly increasing one for the outside region.
questions.topic: Magnetic Field Inside and Outside a Current-Carrying Wire
questions.explanation: Inside the wire, B is proportional to r (distance from axis) since enclosed current grows with area (r^2) and B = mu0*I_enclosed/(2*pi*r). Outside the wire, B is proportional to 1/r, as for an infinite line current.

questions.text: Water flows in a streamline motion through a horizontal pipe of circular cross-section. The pressure difference of water between P and Q is 15 Nm⁻². The area of cross-section at P and Q are 40 cm² and 20 cm², respectively. The rate of flow of water through the pipe, in cm³s⁻¹, is: [Take density of water = 1000 kg m⁻³]
questions.explanation: By continuity, v_P A_P = v_Q A_Q, so v_Q = 2v_P (since A_P=2A_Q). By Bernoulli's theorem: P_P - P_Q = (1/2)ρ(v_Q² - v_P²) = (1/2)ρ(4v_P² - v_P²) = (3/2)ρv_P². So 15 = (3/2)(1000)v_P², giving v_P² = 0.01, v_P = 0.1 m/s = 10 cm/s. Flow rate = A_P × v_P = 40 cm² × 10 cm/s = 400 cm³/s.

questions.text: Which one of the following is NOT applicable to the phenomenon of adsorption?
questions.topic: Thermodynamic Feature Not True for Adsorption
questions.explanation: Adsorption is generally an exothermic process (ΔH < 0, releasing energy as molecules settle onto the surface), spontaneous (ΔG < 0), and accompanied by decreased entropy (ΔS < 0); a positive ΔH would be unusual and does not describe typical adsorption.

questions.text: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point? (1) 0.01 M Urea, (2) 0.01 M KNO3, (3) 0.01 M Na2SO4, (4) 0.015 M C6H12O6
questions.topic: Elevation of Boiling Point / Van't Hoff Factor
questions.explanation: ΔTb = i×Kf×m, so ΔTb ∝ i×m (effective particle concentration). Urea: i=1, m=0.01 → 0.01. KNO3: i=2, m=0.01 → 0.02. Na2SO4: i=3, m=0.01 → 0.03 (highest). Glucose: i=1, m=0.015 → 0.015. Na2SO4 gives the highest i×m, hence highest boiling point.
